## Common chart props

Every chart built with `defineChart` accepts these on top of its own props. HTML components (big-number, callout, ...) do not. All are JSON-serialisable except the callbacks (`onSelect`, `onEvents`, `onReady`) and the function forms of `data`, `transform`, `format` and `option`. Generated from `CommonChartProps` in `packages/insightcharts/src/core/define.tsx`.

| Prop | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `data` | `DataInput` | Rows, CSV text, a URL, `{ url, path }`, an async function, or an Arrow-style table. Omit inside `<InsightData>`. |
| `transform` | `Transform \| Transform[]` | A pipeline of transforms applied before drawing. |
| `title` | `string` | The title. One plain statement of what the data shows, with the number and the period ("Monthly churn fell from 4.2% to 2.1% in 2024"), or a plain label ("Monthly churn, 2024"). One clause, no figures of speech. |
| `subtitle` | `string` | Measure, unit, population, period. |
| `source` | `string` | Data source, shown as "Source: ...". |
| `note` | `string` | Method notes or caveats. |
| `height` | `number \| string` | CSS height of the plot. Default 360. |
| `aspect` | `number` | Width / height. Overrides `height`. |
| `highlight` | `string \| string[]` | The entity (or entities) the title is about. Every other series is drawn in grey. |
| `annotations` | `Annotation[]` | Reference lines, shaded bands and callouts, in data coordinates. |
| `format` | `FormatSpec` | How to print values: `"compact"`, `"percent"`, `"currency:USD"`, `"{value} kg"`, Intl options, or a function. |
| `legend` | `boolean` | Show the legend. Default: shown when there are two or more series. |
| `select` | `boolean \| string` | Make marks clickable to filter. Inside `<InsightData>` the selection filters every other chart. Pass a field name, or `true` to use the chart's category field. |
| `onSelect` | `(values: string[], field: string) => void` | Called with the selected values whenever the selection changes. |
| `option` | `EChartsOption \| ((option: EChartsOption, ctx: BuildContext) => EChartsOption)` | Deep-merged over the generated ECharts option, or a function that receives and returns it. Use it for ECharts settings no prop covers. |
| `theme` | `ThemeInput` | A built-in theme name (`"editorial"`, `"ledger"`, `"noir"`...), or a theme object. A named theme paints its own background behind the chart. |
| `frame` | `boolean` | Paint the theme's background behind the chart. Default: on for a named theme with its own surface. |
| `mode` | `ModeInput` | `"auto"` (default) follows the page, `"system"` follows the OS, or force `"light"` / `"dark"`. |
| `renderer` | `RendererInput` | `"auto"` (default) uses SVG for light charts and canvas for heavy ones. |
| `animate` | `boolean` | Set false to disable animation for this chart. Reduced-motion preferences are always respected. |
| `lazy` | `boolean` | Mount the chart only when it scrolls within 200px of the viewport. Default true (from `InsightProvider`). |
| `group` | `string` | Link tooltips with other charts sharing this group id. |
| `exportable` | `boolean \| ExportFormat[]` | Show an export menu: `true` or a list of formats from png, jpeg, svg, pdf, csv, json. |
| `table` | `boolean` | Show a collapsible "View data" table under the chart. |
| `alt` | `string` | Accessible description: the chart type and measures, then the main pattern and the notable values. |
| `id` | `string` | Stable id for this chart's selection in the shared store. |
| `onEvents` | `Record<string, ChartEventHandler>` | ECharts event handlers: `{ click: (params, chart) => {} }`. |
| `onReady` | `(chart: EChartsInstance) => void` | Called with the ECharts instance once it is initialised. |
| `className` | `string` | Class on the figure element. |
| `style` | `CSSProperties` | Inline style on the figure element. |

---

## Data

Charts work on an array of plain row objects. The `data` prop accepts many shapes and normalises them to rows; `transform` then reshapes those rows. Both are JSON-serialisable, so a whole pipeline can live in a spec.

### Accepted `data` shapes

| Shape | Example | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Row objects | `[{ year: 2020, value: 1 }]` | The native form. |
| Array of arrays | `[["year", "value"], [2020, 1]]` | The first array is the header. |
| Array of primitives | `[3, 5, 8]` | Becomes `{ index, value }` rows. |
| Columnar object | `{ year: [2020, 2021], value: [1, 2] }` | Every value must be an array or typed array. |
| Table object | Apache Arrow table, DuckDB result, Arquero table | Anything with `toArray()`. Rows with `toJSON()` are converted. |
| API envelope | `{ data: [...] }` | An array under `data`, `rows`, `results`, `items` or `records` is found automatically. |
| CSV text | `"year,value\n2020,1"` | Any string that is not a URL. Delimiter is detected from `,` tab `;` and the pipe character. |
| URL string | `"/data/energy.csv"` | A single-line string with no comma that starts with `http://`, `https://`, `/`, `./`, `../` or `data:`. |
| Remote source | `{ url, format, path, init, refresh }` | `format`: `csv`, `tsv`, `json`, `ndjson` (otherwise inferred from the extension, then the content type, then the content). `path`: dot path to the rows inside a JSON response, e.g. `"data.results"`. `init`: passed to `fetch`. `refresh`: re-fetch interval in ms. |
| Inline CSV | `{ csv: "...", delimiter: ";" }` | |
| Inline JSON | `{ json: anything, path: "a.b" }` | |
| Function or promise | `() => fetchRows()` or a `Promise` | Resolves to any shape above. Not JSON; client components only. |

Omit `data` on a chart inside `<InsightData>` and it reads the shared rows.

If no row array can be found, the chart shows an error telling you to pass `path`.

#### CSV type inference

CSV cells are converted: numbers (including `1,234` thousands separators), `true`/`false`, and `42%` (becomes `0.42`). Empty cells, `NA`, `N/A`, `null` and `NaN` become `null`. Values with a leading zero (`007`, zip codes) stay strings. Dates stay strings; ISO date strings (`2024-03-01`, `2024-03`) are recognised by charts as temporal. Use the `parse` transform to force a type.

#### Loading behaviour

- In-memory data resolves synchronously: no loading flash.
- URLs, functions and promises load asynchronously; the chart shows a skeleton, then the chart, or an error message with the HTTP status.
- URL loads are de-duplicated and cached for the page's lifetime, unless the source has `init` or `refresh`.
- Inline literals written in JSX are compared by content, so `data={[...]}` does not reload on every render. Arrays over 500 rows are compared by identity: keep a stable reference (a module constant or `useMemo`).

On the server, or anywhere outside React:

```ts
import { loadData, transformRows, parseCsv } from "insightcharts/data";

const rows = transformRows(await loadData({ url: "https://example.com/api", path: "data.results" }), [
  { type: "filter", field: "year", op: ">=", value: 2015 },
]);
```

### Wide and long data

Charts with `x`, `y` and `series` accept both layouts:

```tsx
// Wide: one column per series
<LineChart data={[{ year: "2022", solar: 4.6, wind: 7.3 }]} x="year" y={["solar", "wind"]} />

// Long: one row per series per x
<LineChart data={[{ year: "2022", source: "solar", share: 4.6 }, { year: "2022", source: "wind", share: 7.3 }]} x="year" y="share" series="source" />
```

In wide data the series keys are the field names (`"solar"`); in long data they are the values of the `series` field. Those keys are what `highlight` and `names` refer to.

### Transforms

`transform` takes one transform or an array applied in order. Each is a JSON object with a `type`; a function `(rows) => rows` is also accepted in JSX.

| Transform | Fields | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `"filter"` | `field`, `op` (default `==`), `value` | Keep rows that match. |
| `"aggregate"` | `groupBy` (field or fields, optional), `measures: { name: { op, field } }` | One row per group. Omit `field` for `count`. |
| `"sort"` | `by`, `order` (`"asc"` default, or `"desc"`) | |
| `"limit"` | `n`, `offset` | Slice. |
| `"top"` | `n`, `by`, `other`, `label` | Keep the top `n` rows by `by`. To fold the rest into one row, pass both `other` (the text, e.g. `"Other"`) and `label` (the field that text goes in); the folded row's `by` value is the sum. |
| `"fold"` | `fields`, `key` (default `"key"`), `value` (default `"value"`) | Wide to long. |
| `"pivot"` | `index`, `key`, `value`, `op` (default `sum`) | Long to wide: one row per `index`, one column per distinct `key`. |
| `"bin"` | `field`, `step` or `bins`, `as` (default `<field>_bin`) | Adds the bin start as `as` and the bin end as `<as>_end`. |
| `"derive"` | `as`, `op`, `fields`, `groupBy`, `base` | Adds a computed column; see below. |
| `"rename"` | `fields: { old: "new" }` | |
| `"select"` | `fields` | Keep only these columns. |
| `"parse"` | `fields: { name: "number" \| "date" \| "string" \| "boolean" }` | Coerce types. `number` strips `,`, `$`, `%` and spaces. |

Filter ops: `==`, `!=`, `>`, `>=`, `<`, `<=`, `in` (value is an array), `not-in`, `between` (value is `[low, high]`, inclusive), `contains` (case-insensitive substring), `exists` (non-null and non-empty; pass `value: false` to invert).

Aggregate ops: `sum`, `mean`, `median`, `min`, `max`, `count`, `distinct`, `first`, `last`.

Derive ops:

- Arithmetic on two fields: `add`, `subtract`, `multiply`, `divide` (`fields: ["a", "b"]`).
- Running, on one field in row order, restarting per `groupBy` group: `percent-of-total`, `cumulative`, `rank` (1 is the largest), `change` (difference from the previous row), `percent-change`, `index` (rebased so the first row equals `base`, default 100).

#### Examples

Top five plus "Other":

```json
[
  { "type": "aggregate", "groupBy": "category", "measures": { "revenue": { "op": "sum", "field": "amount" } } },
  { "type": "top", "n": 5, "by": "revenue", "other": "Other", "label": "category" }
]
```

Index several series to 100 at the start so growth is comparable (say "Indexed, 2019 = 100" in the subtitle):

```json
{ "type": "derive", "as": "indexed", "op": "index", "fields": ["value"], "groupBy": "country" }
```

Wide to long:

```json
{ "type": "fold", "fields": ["solar", "wind"], "key": "source", "value": "share" }
```

### Order of operations

Standalone chart: load `data`, then the chart's `transform`.

Inside `<InsightData>`: load the shared `data`, apply the store's `transform`, filter by the other charts' selections, then apply the chart's own `transform`.

---

## Theming and dark mode

### The default theme

With no configuration, charts inherit the page font and read shadcn/ui's `--background`, `--foreground` and `--muted-foreground` variables when they exist, with neutral fallbacks when they do not. The series colours are InsightCharts' own palette, whose order is chosen so neighbouring colours stay distinguishable under colour-vision deficiency. Keep the order if you re-skin.

### Three ways to theme

#### 1. CSS variables

Every colour token of the default theme reads an `--ic-*` variable first. Set them in your stylesheet, globally or on any ancestor:

```css
:root {
  --ic-accent: #7c3aed;
  --ic-series-1: #7c3aed;
  --ic-font-display: "Fraunces", serif;
}
.dark {
  --ic-accent: #a78bfa;
  --ic-series-1: #a78bfa;
}
```

`npx shadcn@latest add @insightcharts/theme` writes the full set with their default values into your global CSS so you can edit them in place.

| CSS variable | Token | Light default | Dark default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--ic-surface` | `surface` | `var(--background, #fcfcfb)` | `var(--background, #1a1a19)` |
| `--ic-ink` | `ink` | `var(--foreground, #0b0b0b)` | `var(--foreground, #f0efec)` |
| `--ic-ink-secondary` | `inkSecondary` | `#52514e` | `#c3c2b7` |
| `--ic-muted` | `muted` | `var(--muted-foreground, #898781)` | `var(--muted-foreground, #898781)` |
| `--ic-grid` | `grid` | `#e1e0d9` | `#2c2c2a` |
| `--ic-axis` | `axis` | `#c3c2b7` | `#383835` |
| `--ic-accent` | `accent` | `#2a78d6` | `#3987e5` |
| `--ic-context` | `context` | `#c3c2b7` | `#52514e` |
| `--ic-positive` | `positive` | `#0ca30c` | `#0ca30c` |
| `--ic-negative` | `negative` | `#d03b3b` | `#e66767` |
| `--ic-series-1` | `categorical[0]` | `#2a78d6` | `#3987e5` |
| `--ic-series-2` | `categorical[1]` | `#eb6834` | `#d95926` |
| `--ic-series-3` | `categorical[2]` | `#1baf7a` | `#199e70` |
| `--ic-series-4` | `categorical[3]` | `#eda100` | `#c98500` |
| `--ic-series-5` | `categorical[4]` | `#e87ba4` | `#d55181` |
| `--ic-series-6` | `categorical[5]` | `#008300` | `#0ca30c` |
| `--ic-series-7` | `categorical[6]` | `#6250d6` | `#9085e9` |
| `--ic-series-8` | `categorical[7]` | `#e34948` | `#e66767` |
| `--ic-font` | `fontFamily` | `inherit` | `inherit` |
| `--ic-font-display` | `displayFamily` | `var(--ic-font, inherit)` | `var(--ic-font, inherit)` |

The `sequential` and `diverging` ramps, `fontSize`, `radius` and `lineWidth` have no CSS variable; set them with the `theme` prop.

#### 2. The `theme` prop

On any chart, on `InsightProvider`, or on HTML components that declare it. It accepts:

- flat tokens, applied to both modes: `theme={{ accent: "#7c3aed", radius: 2 }}`
- per-mode tokens: `theme={{ light: { accent: "#7c3aed" }, dark: { accent: "#a78bfa" } }}`
- a full theme object from `createTheme(input, base?)`

A chart's `theme` is merged over the surrounding provider's. Token values may be literals or CSS variable references (`"var(--brand, #2a78d6)"`); they are resolved against the chart's own DOM node, so scoped overrides work.

Tokens: `surface`, `ink`, `inkSecondary`, `muted`, `grid`, `axis`, `accent`, `context`, `positive`, `negative`, `categorical[]`, `sequential[]`, `diverging[]`, `fontFamily`, `displayFamily`, `fontSize`, `radius`, `lineWidth`.

#### 3. The shadcn preset

```tsx
import { InsightProvider } from "insightcharts";
import { shadcnTheme } from "insightcharts/themes";

<InsightProvider theme={shadcnTheme}>{children}</InsightProvider>
```

`shadcnTheme` takes series colours from `--chart-1` to `--chart-5`, the accent from `--chart-1` (falling back to `--primary`) and gridlines from `--border`. shadcn's stock chart colours are not ordered for colour-vision-deficiency separation, so keep direct labels or legends on. `insightcharts/themes` also exports `defaultTheme`, `createTheme`, six presets and the `themes` record that holds all of them by name.

### Presets

`editorialTheme`, `ledgerTheme`, `monoTheme`, `earthTheme`, `scienceTheme` and `posterTheme` each define a light and a dark token set, with categorical palettes checked for colour-vision-deficiency separation in both modes. Unlike `insight` and `shadcn`, which follow the host page, a preset paints for its own surface: put it in a container with the matching background, which `themeSurfaces[name]` gives you as `{ light, dark }`.

```tsx
import { InsightProvider } from "insightcharts";
import { editorialTheme, themeSurfaces } from "insightcharts/themes";

<div style={{ background: themeSurfaces.editorial.light, padding: 24 }}>
  <InsightProvider theme={editorialTheme} mode="light">{children}</InsightProvider>
</div>
```

### Dark mode

`mode` is a prop on every chart and on `InsightProvider`:

- `"auto"` (default): match what the page looks like. In order: the nearest ancestor with a `.dark` / `.light` class or a `data-theme`, `data-mode`, `data-color-mode` or `data-color-scheme` attribute; otherwise the luminance of the nearest painted background; otherwise the page's `color-scheme` and the OS preference.
- `"system"`: follow the OS preference.
- `"light"` / `"dark"`: force it.

Charts re-resolve their colours when the root's class or theme attributes change, so toggles such as next-themes work without a remount. Each component root carries `data-ic-mode="light|dark"`.

### Restyling the chrome

The title, subtitle, legend and source line are HTML elements, each with a `data-slot` attribute: `ic-figure`, `ic-header`, `ic-title`, `ic-subtitle`, `ic-legend`, `ic-plot`, `ic-source`, `ic-table`, `ic-actions`, `ic-menu`, `ic-skeleton`, `ic-state`. HTML components add their own (for example `ic-big-number-value`). Target them from CSS:

```css
[data-slot="ic-title"] { font-size: 1.5rem; }
```

`className` and `style` on a chart apply to its `figure` element.

---

## Crossfiltering with InsightData

`InsightData` loads data once and shares it. Charts inside it that do not pass their own `data` read the shared rows, and any chart with `select` filters all the others when the reader clicks a mark.

```tsx
"use client";
import { BarChart, InsightData, LineChart } from "insightcharts";

export function Sales({ rows }: { rows: Record<string, unknown>[] }) {
  return (
    <InsightData data={rows}>
      <BarChart
        id="by-region"
        select
        transform={{ type: "aggregate", groupBy: "region", measures: { revenue: { op: "sum", field: "revenue" } } }}
        x="region"
        y="revenue"
        title="Revenue by region"
      />
      <LineChart
        transform={{ type: "aggregate", groupBy: "month", measures: { revenue: { op: "sum", field: "revenue" } } }}
        x="month"
        y="revenue"
        title="Revenue by month"
        subtitle="Click a region above to filter"
      />
    </InsightData>
  );
}
```

### How it behaves

- `select` makes marks clickable. `select={true}` uses the chart's own category field (for `bar-chart` that is `x`; for `line-chart` it is `series`). `select="field"` names the field explicitly.
- A click toggles that value in the chart's selection; several values can be selected. A click on empty plot area clears it.
- A selection filters every other chart, never the chart that made it. The selecting chart keeps its full domain and fades the unselected marks.
- Each chart's own `transform` runs after the shared filter, so charts can aggregate the filtered rows differently.
- A chart that passes its own `data` inside `InsightData` is not filtered, but its selection still filters the others.
- Without an `InsightData` ancestor, `select` still works locally: the chart fades unselected marks and calls `onSelect`.

### Props

`InsightData`:

| Prop | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `data` | `DataInput` | Shared data, any accepted shape. |
| `transform` | `Transform \| Transform[]` | Applied once to the shared rows, before filtering. |
| `selections` | `Record<string, Selection>` | Controlled selections, keyed by chart id. |
| `onSelectionsChange` | `(selections) => void` | Called on every change. |

On charts: `select`, `onSelect(values, field)`, and `id` (a stable key for the chart's selection; set it when you control or persist selections, otherwise a generated id is used).

A `Selection` is `{ field, values?: string[], range?: [min, max] }`. Clicks produce `values`; `range` can be set programmatically and filters with an inclusive between.

### Reading or driving the store

```tsx
import { useInsightData } from "insightcharts";

function ClearFilters() {
  const store = useInsightData(); // null outside <InsightData>
  if (!store || Object.keys(store.selections).length === 0) return null;
  return <button onClick={() => store.clear()}>Clear filters</button>;
}
```

The store exposes `all` (unfiltered rows), `rows`, `status`, `error`, `selections`, `select(owner, selection | null)`, `clear()` and `rowsFor(owner?)` (rows filtered by every selection except `owner`'s).

### Linked tooltips

Separately from filtering, charts that share a `group` id link their tooltips and axis pointers: `group="sales"` on each.

### Design notes

- Tell the reader the charts are linked, with a subtitle such as "Click a bar to filter".
- The charts must show their main fact before the reader clicks anything.

---

## Scroll and swipe stories with Scrolly

`Scrolly` pins a graphic and changes its state as the reader moves through a list of steps. Because the same chart receives new props at each step, ECharts animates between the states.

```tsx
"use client";
import { LineChart, Scrolly } from "insightcharts";

const data = [
  { year: "2019", solar: 2.7, wind: 5.3 },
  { year: "2021", solar: 3.7, wind: 6.5 },
  { year: "2023", solar: 5.5, wind: 7.8 },
];

const steps = [
  { id: "both", content: "Solar and wind share of global electricity generation, 2019 to 2023.", highlight: [] as string[] },
  { id: "wind", content: "Wind's share rose from 5.3% in 2019 to 7.8% in 2023.", highlight: ["wind"] },
  { id: "solar", content: "Solar's share rose from 2.7% in 2019 to 5.5% in 2023.", highlight: ["solar"] },
];

export function EnergyStory() {
  return (
    <Scrolly steps={steps}>
      {({ step }) => (
        <LineChart
          data={data}
          x="year"
          y={["solar", "wind"]}
          format="{value}%"
          highlight={step.highlight}
          title="Solar and wind share of electricity, 2019 to 2023"
          subtitle="Share of global electricity generation"
          source="Ember"
        />
      )}
    </Scrolly>
  );
}
```

### Steps and state

Each step is `{ id?, content, ...yourKeys }`. `content` is the text for the step (a sentence or two). Any other keys are yours: the state the graphic should be in. `id` is also set as the step element's `id`, so it works as a link anchor.

`children` is a function that receives `{ index, step, progress, count }` and returns the graphic. `progress` runs 0 to 1 through the active step in scroll mode and is 0 in the other modes.

`children` is a function, so `Scrolly` must be used from a client component.

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `steps` | `StoryStep[]` | | The steps. |
| `children` | `(state) => ReactNode` | | Renders the graphic for the active step. |
| `mode` | `"auto" \| "scroll" \| "swipe" \| "steps"` | `"auto"` | See below. |
| `side` | `"left" \| "right"` | `"left"` | Which side the text column sits on in scroll mode. |
| `stickyTop` | `number \| string` | `0` | Offset from the top of the viewport at which the graphic pins; set it to the height of a fixed header. |
| `stepHeight` | `string` | `"80vh"` | Scroll distance per step. |
| `index` | `number` | | Controlled active step. |
| `onStepChange` | `(index, step) => void` | | Called when the active step changes. |
| `theme` | `ThemeInput` | | Theme for the step cards. |
| `colorMode` | `"auto" \| "system" \| "light" \| "dark"` | provider's | Colour mode for the step cards. Named `colorMode` because `mode` is the interaction mode. |
| `className`, `style` | | | On the root element. |

### Modes

- `"scroll"`: the graphic is sticky and the steps scroll past; the step crossing the middle of the viewport is active. When the container is narrower than 768px the steps overlay the graphic as cards instead of sitting beside it.
- `"swipe"`: the graphic sits on top and the steps are cards that swipe horizontally, with Previous and Next buttons.
- `"steps"`: one card at a time with Previous and Next buttons. No scroll hijacking; suitable for embeds.
- `"auto"`: swipe when the container is under 640px wide on a coarse-pointer (touch) device, scroll otherwise.

In swipe and steps modes the left and right arrow keys move between steps. In scroll and swipe modes all step text is in the document.

### Writing steps

- Change one thing per step: the data, the highlight or the encoding.
- Keep the same chart component in the same position across steps and change its props. Swapping to a different component, or changing its `key`, remounts it and loses the transition.
- Use three to seven steps. Each step is one or two plain sentences.
- Each step states one fact about what the chart shows at that step, with the number from the data: "Solar's share rose from 2.7% in 2019 to 5.5% in 2023." Do not start a step with "But" or "And" to link it to the previous one.
- The first step shows all of the data with no highlight.
- Give the chart a `title` that is true at every step (a plain label works), or set the title per step from the step's keys.
- Step text follows the same writing rules as titles. See "Choosing a form".

---

## Infographics

An infographic is a template with `category: "infographic"`. It draws one designed sheet, called a poster: a painted background, a large title, little other text, and one large graphic or several graphics laid out together. Every infographic is composed on the `poster` molecule from atoms with `category: "poster"`, called poster primitives.

### When to choose a poster

| The piece is | Use |
|---|---|
| One image that is read in a few seconds and shared as a picture | An infographic template |
| One image with a layout no infographic template has | The `poster` molecule with your own panels |
| One fact at a fixed social size (1:1, 4:5, 16:9, 9:16) | `social-card` |
| A page with paragraphs, a method note, recommendations or charts with axes | A report-style template such as `executive-brief`, `report-page` or `visual-essay` |
| A dashboard the reader filters | `data-explorer` |

A poster suits large counts, rankings, shares, flows and scales that read from the size of the marks. It does not suit dense time series or anything that needs axes and gridlines to be read.

### The infographic templates

Pick the template from the decision table in "Choosing a form" (rows with the job "Lay out a whole poster"). Each template's page lists its regions and has a complete example.

### Writing an infographic spec

```json
{
  "type": "count-poster",
  "theme": "noir",
  "kicker": "Education",
  "title": "Norland's schools taught 1.84 million pupils in 2025",
  "subtitle": "Pupils enrolled in state schools by stage, autumn term 2025.",
  "unit": 1000,
  "unitLabel": "1,000 people",
  "hero": {
    "data": [
      { "stage": "Primary", "pupils": 820000 },
      { "stage": "Lower secondary", "pupils": 480000 },
      { "stage": "Upper secondary", "pupils": 390000 },
      { "stage": "Vocational", "pupils": 170000 }
    ],
    "name": "stage",
    "value": "pupils",
    "title": "820,000 pupils were in primary school"
  },
  "sources": "Norland Ministry of Education, school census 2025",
  "note": "Norland is an invented country. All figures are illustrative."
}
```

Render it with `<Insight spec={spec} />`.

- `title` is required. It is the poster's one fact, as a plain sentence with its number. `kicker` is a short topic label and `subtitle` names the measure, population and period.
- `theme` is a poster theme name. Each template has its own default.
- Each template has named region props (`hero`, `reference`, `area`, `bars` and `shares` on `count-poster`; `scale`, `figures` and `side` on `scale-poster`). Read the template's page for its regions.
- A region takes a compact config: `data` rows, the field names, and any other prop of the primitive that draws the region. A `title`, `subtitle`, `source` or `note` in the config becomes the heading and source line of that panel.
- A region also takes a full spec with its own `type`. That replaces the primitive the template would have drawn.
- `sources`, `note` and `credit` are the footer. Always set `sources`. Say in `note` when data is illustrative.
- `linked: true` makes marks clickable. A click highlights the same name in every other graphic that has it and filters graphics that read the shared `data` prop.
- `download: true` adds a "Download PNG" control under the poster.
- `maxWidth` limits the width. `mode` is `"light"` by default and a poster does not follow the page's colour mode.

Keep names identical across regions (the same spelling of each entity) so `linked` can join them.

### Composing a poster with the poster frame

Use `poster` when no template has the layout.

```json
{
  "type": "poster",
  "theme": "forest",
  "kicker": "Transport",
  "title": "Tarn Valley buses carried 9.6 million passengers in 2025",
  "subtitle": "Passengers on the valley's seven bus routes, January to December 2025.",
  "panels": [
    { "span": 5, "valign": "center", "content": { "type": "big-number", "size": "hero", "value": "9.6 million", "label": "Passengers in 2025", "context": "8.9 million in 2024" } },
    {
      "span": 7,
      "title": "Route 4 carried 2.3 million passengers",
      "subtitle": "Passengers by route, thousands, 2025",
      "content": { "type": "pill-rank", "data": [{ "route": "Route 4", "k": 2300 }, { "route": "Route 1", "k": 1900 }, { "route": "Route 7", "k": 1500 }], "name": "route", "value": "k", "format": "{value}k", "highlight": "Route 4" }
    },
    {
      "title": "Passenger numbers were 6.1 million in 2021",
      "content": { "type": "block-bar", "data": [{ "year": "2021", "m": 6.1 }, { "year": "2023", "m": 8.2 }, { "year": "2025", "m": 9.6 }], "name": "year", "value": "m", "format": "{value}m" }
    }
  ],
  "sources": "Tarn Valley Transport Authority",
  "note": "Tarn Valley is an invented place. All figures are illustrative."
}
```

- `panels` is required. Each panel is `{ content, title?, subtitle?, span?, rowSpan?, source?, note?, align?, valign?, bleed?, id? }`.
- `content` is a component spec. Put the panel's heading in the panel's `title`, not in the chart's `title`. Every panel heading is then set in the same type.
- `columns` is 12 by default. `span` is in those units and defaults to the full width. `span: 5` beside `span: 7` makes one row. `columns: 2` or `columns: 3` gives a simple grid.
- `aspect` fixes the shape (`"4:5"`, `"16:9"`, `0.75`). The poster still grows when its content needs more height.
- `rules` is `"dotted"` (default), `"solid"` or `"none"`.
- The frame passes its theme and colour mode to everything inside. Do not set `theme` or `mode` on a chart in a panel.
- Use at most about six panels. Give charts in panels a `height` when they do not size themselves (`bar-chart`, `donut-chart`, `treemap`). Poster primitives size themselves.

### Poster themes

Eight themes, passed by name as `theme`.

| Name | Ground | Marks |
|---|---|---|
| `noir` | Near-black `#0d0d0f` | Yellow, sky blue, coral, off-white, green. White type. |
| `magenta` | Magenta `#c2006b` | Pale pink, near-black, cyan, yellow. White type. |
| `dusk` | Violet gradient, `#24104f` to `#5e2067` | Orange, pale yellow, pink, lilac, mint. White type. |
| `paper` | Off-white `#f3ecdf` | Red, ink black, warm grey, blue. Black type. `mode: "dark"` gives the same design on charcoal `#1d1b18`. |
| `ocean` | Navy to teal gradient, `#041c3a` to `#084c5c` | Aqua, coral, sand, blue. White type. |
| `forest` | Dark green `#0f3d2a` | Lime, orange, cream, light blue. Cream type. |
| `blueprint` | Cobalt `#1447c8` | Yellow, white, salmon, pale blue. White type. Monospace display face. |
| `sunrise` | Cream to peach gradient, `#fff1e0` to `#ffdfc6` | Plum, tangerine, teal, blue. Plum type. |

- Seven themes have one look: the same tokens in light and dark. Only `paper` has a different dark variant.
- A poster theme has 4 or 5 categorical colours. Fold further entities into "Other" or shade by value.
- `posterThemes` and `posterBackgrounds` are exported from `insightcharts/themes`. `posterBackgrounds[name].light` is the CSS background, which is a gradient for `dusk`, `ocean` and `sunrise`.
- Do not hard-code colours in a spec. Pick a theme.

### Poster primitives

The data job to primitive table is in "Choosing a form" under "Poster primitives". A primitive is a chart built with `defineChart` and accepts the common chart props (`data`, `transform`, `title`, `highlight`, `format`, `select`, ...). It prints names and values on or beside its marks, has no axes by default and sets its own height. It works in any theme and outside a poster.

Any other atom also fits a panel. `big-number` (with `size: "hero"`), `pictogram-chart`, `treemap`, `waffle-chart`, `segmented-bar`, `donut-chart`, `bar-chart` and `icon-stat` are used in the `poster` examples.

### Icons

An icon prop (`icon`, `icons`, `iconField` values) takes a built-in name or a custom single path written as `"path://M0 0..."` on a 24 by 24 grid. Use only these names:

- People: `person`, `woman`, `child`, `baby`, `group`
- Home and buildings: `house`, `building`, `factory`, `hospital`, `school`, `shop`
- Transport: `car`, `bus`, `train`, `bike`, `plane`, `ship`, `truck`, `rocket`
- Nature and energy: `tree`, `leaf`, `sun`, `cloud`, `rain`, `drop`, `snow`, `wind-turbine`, `solar-panel`, `flame`, `bolt`, `battery`, `barrel`, `plug`, `mountain`, `wave`, `globe`
- Food and farming: `wheat`, `bread`, `apple`, `carrot`, `fish`, `cow`, `chicken`, `milk-bottle`, `cup`, `bottle`, `fork-knife`
- Money and shopping: `coin`, `banknote`, `cart`, `bag`, `bin`
- Objects: `phone`, `laptop`, `book`, `lightbulb`, `heart`, `cross`, `pill`, `syringe`, `clock`, `calendar`, `flag`, `star`, `pin`, `lock`, `satellite`
- Shapes: `circle`, `square`

An unknown name falls back to another icon without an error. Check every icon name against this list. `icons`, `iconNames`, `iconGroups`, `resolveIcon` and `iconSymbol` are exported from `insightcharts` and `insightcharts/core`. The `Icon` component draws one icon as inline SVG and takes `name`, `size`, `color`, `title` and `fallback`.

### PNG download

- `download: true` on `poster` or on any infographic adds a "Download PNG" control under the sheet. The image is the whole sheet without the control.
- On `poster`, `exportWidth` sets the image width (default 2400), `filename` the file name (default: a slug of the title), `downloadLabel` the label and `onExport` receives the `Blob`. The infographic templates take `download` only.
- With `download` set, every chart in the poster mounts at once instead of lazily.
- From code: `rasterize(element, pixelWidth)` and `canvasToBlob(canvas)` from `insightcharts/core` paint any element to a PNG, and `downloadBlob(blob, name)` saves it. The poster sheet is the element with `data-slot="ic-poster"`.
- The painter draws backgrounds including linear and radial gradients, borders, radii, clipping, text, inline SVG and canvases. It does not draw outer or blurred shadows, CSS transforms, conic or repeating gradients or `url()` backgrounds.

### Phone layout

A poster lays out from its own width, not the viewport.

| Poster width | Layout |
|---|---|
| 760px and wider | The grid as written. |
| 600 to 759px | Two columns. On a 12-unit grid a panel with `span` up to 6 takes one column and a wider panel takes both. |
| Under 600px | One column, every panel full width, in the order of `panels`. |

Under 600px the padding is 20px, the gap is 28px and a fixed `aspect` is dropped. Order `panels` so the poster reads correctly as one column. Poster primitives lay themselves out again for the narrow width.

### Checklist

- The `title` is one clause with its number and period.
- Every panel heading is one fact about that panel or a plain label.
- `sources` is set.
- Every icon name is in the list above.
- Entity names are spelt the same in every region.
- There are at most about six panels.
- No chart in a panel sets its own `theme` or `mode`.

---

## Export

### The export menu

```tsx
<BarChart data={data} x="country" y="share" title="Renewable share of electricity by country" exportable />
```

`exportable` adds an "Export" menu at the top right of the figure (visible on hover or keyboard focus). `true` offers PNG, SVG, PDF and CSV. Pass a list to choose from all six formats: `exportable={["png", "jpeg", "svg", "pdf", "csv", "json"]}`. Set it once for every chart with `<InsightProvider exportable>`.

### Formats

| Format | Contents |
|---|---|
| `png`, `jpeg` | The chart re-rendered off-screen at `pixelRatio` (default 2), with the title, subtitle and source line drawn in, on the theme's surface colour. |
| `svg` | A standalone SVG with the same chrome as text elements. |
| `pdf` | A single page containing the image. |
| `csv`, `json` | The rows the chart drew, after loading, crossfilter and `transform`. |

Image exports use the chart's current size, theme and colour mode, and never have a transparent background unless you pass one.

### Programmatic export

Every chart forwards a ref with `export(options)`, `getInstance()` and `getOption()`.

```tsx
"use client";
import { useRef } from "react";
import { LineChart } from "insightcharts";
import type { ChartHandle } from "insightcharts";

export function Downloadable({ data }: { data: Record<string, unknown>[] }) {
  const chart = useRef<ChartHandle>(null);
  return (
    <>
      <LineChart ref={chart} data={data} x="year" y="solar" title="Solar generation by year" />
      <button onClick={() => chart.current?.export({ format: "png", filename: "solar" })}>Download PNG</button>
    </>
  );
}
```

Options:

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `format` | `"png"` | `png`, `jpeg`, `svg`, `pdf`, `csv` or `json`. |
| `filename` | slug of the title | Without extension. |
| `pixelRatio` | `2` | Raster scale. |
| `chrome` | `true` | Include the title, subtitle and source line in image exports. |
| `background` | theme surface | Background colour. |
| `download` | `true` | Set false to get the `Blob` back without triggering a download. |

`export()` always resolves to the `Blob`. Export runs in the browser; there is no server-side image rendering in the package.

### The data table

`table` adds a collapsible "View data" table under the chart with the same rows. Screen-reader users and readers who need exact values can use it.

Lower-level functions (`exportChart`, `toSvgString`, `toCanvas`, `downloadBlob`) are exported from `insightcharts/core` for custom charts built on `Chart`.

---

## The JSON spec

A spec is a component described as plain JSON: `type` is the component's kebab-case name, every other key is a prop.

```json
{
  "type": "line-chart",
  "data": { "url": "/data/energy.csv" },
  "transform": [{ "type": "filter", "field": "year", "op": ">=", "value": 2015 }],
  "x": "year",
  "y": ["solar", "wind"],
  "highlight": "solar",
  "annotations": [{ "type": "line", "axis": "x", "value": "2020", "label": "Pandemic" }],
  "title": "Solar and wind share of electricity since 2015",
  "subtitle": "Share of global electricity generation, %",
  "source": "Ember"
}
```

```tsx
import { Insight } from "insightcharts";

<Insight spec={spec} />
```

### When to use a spec

- The chart is chosen at runtime: by an AI agent, a CMS field, an API response.
- You need to store, diff or validate charts as data.

When you are writing a page by hand, JSX with named imports is the better choice: it is type-checked and only bundles what you import (the package ships one module per component). Rendering `Insight` registers, and therefore bundles, every component.

### Rules

- `type` must be a component name from the manifest. An unknown type renders a visible message listing the available types; it does not throw.
- Props are the same as in JSX. Field names are strings in both.
- Specs nest. Wherever a molecule or template takes content (a slot), it accepts text or another spec.
- Everything is expressible except functions: no callbacks (`onSelect`, `onEvents`, `onReady`), and no function forms of `data`, `transform`, `format` or `option`. Use the string and object forms: URLs and `{ url, path }` for data, transform objects, format strings such as `"percent"` or `"{value} kg"`, and an `option` object for ECharts overrides.

### Validate before rendering

The schema is generated from the component metadata:

- `https://insightcharts.dev/schema/insight-spec.json`

It is a `oneOf` over component types. Each type lists the component's own props (plus the common chart props for charts, or `className`, `style`, `theme` and `mode` for HTML components) and rejects unknown keys, which catches misspelt and invented props. Use any JSON Schema (draft-07) validator. The component manifest, with every component's description, props and example, is at `https://insightcharts.dev/schema/manifest.json` and ships in the package as `insightcharts/manifest.json`.

### Formats and annotations in JSON

`format`: `"auto"`, `"compact"` (12.9K), `"percent"` (0.42 becomes 42%), `"percent-raw"` (42 becomes 42%), `"integer"`, `"signed"`, `"year"`, `"currency:USD"`, `"decimal:2"`, a template containing `{value}` such as `"{value} kg"`, or an `Intl.NumberFormat` options object.

`annotations` (cartesian charts), positioned in data coordinates:

```json
[
  { "type": "line", "axis": "y", "value": 50, "label": "Target", "dashed": true },
  { "type": "band", "axis": "x", "from": "2020", "to": "2021", "label": "Lockdowns" },
  { "type": "point", "x": "2023", "y": 5.5, "label": "5.5% in 2023", "position": "top" }
]
```

`line` also takes `emphasis` (draw in ink rather than muted). `point` takes `dot: false` to hide the marker; its `label` supports `\n` line breaks.

### Registering your own components

`Insight` and nested slots look components up by `meta.name`. To make a spec resolve to your own component, or to a registry copy you have customised, register it:

```tsx
import { registerComponents } from "insightcharts";
import { BarChart } from "@/components/insightcharts/atoms/bar-chart";

registerComponents({ BarChart }); // the last registration for a name wins
```

`listComponents()` returns the metadata of everything registered, and `getComponent(type)` returns one component.

---

## Recipes

Each recipe uses `bar-chart`, `line-chart` and `big-number`, which are the reference components. Check the component catalogue for more specific forms before settling on these.

Where a recipe shows its rows, the title states a fact from those rows. Where the rows are not shown (`data={rows}`), the title is a plain label. When you have the data, replace the label with one fact and its number, following the writing rules in "Choosing a form".

### Ranked bars with one highlighted

```tsx
const rows = [
  { country: "Norway", share: 98 },
  { country: "Brazil", share: 89 },
  { country: "Canada", share: 68 },
  { country: "Germany", share: 52 },
];

<BarChart
  data={rows}
  x="country"
  y="share"
  format="{value}%"
  highlight="Brazil"
  title="Renewables supplied 89% of Brazil's electricity in 2023"
  subtitle="Share of electricity from renewables, 2023"
  source="Ember"
/>
```

A single-series bar chart sorts descending and labels each bar, so there is no value axis to read. `highlight` takes the category label.

### Top five plus Other

```tsx
<BarChart
  data={orders}
  transform={[
    { type: "aggregate", groupBy: "category", measures: { revenue: { op: "sum", field: "amount" } } },
    { type: "top", n: 5, by: "revenue", other: "Other", label: "category" },
  ]}
  x="category"
  y="revenue"
  format="currency:USD"
  title="Revenue by category"
/>
```

### Highlight one line among several

```tsx
<LineChart
  data={long}
  x="year"
  y="share"
  series="country"
  highlight="Denmark"
  format="percent"
  title="Wind share of electricity by country"
  subtitle="Wind as a share of electricity generation"
  source="Ember"
/>
```

Long data: one row per country per year. Every country other than Denmark is drawn in the context grey.

### Annotate a date, a period and a value

```tsx
<LineChart
  data={monthly}
  x="month"
  y="signups"
  annotations={[
    { type: "line", axis: "x", value: "2024-03", label: "Pricing change" },
    { type: "band", axis: "x", from: "2024-07", to: "2024-08", label: "Outage" },
    { type: "point", x: "2024-11", y: 4210, label: "4,210 in November" },
  ]}
  title="Signups reached 4,210 in November 2024"
  subtitle="New accounts per month, 2024"
  source="Internal analytics"
/>
```

Annotation `value`, `from`, `to` and `x` must match the x values in the data.

### Compare growth with an index

```tsx
<LineChart
  data={long}
  transform={{ type: "derive", as: "indexed", op: "index", fields: ["value"], groupBy: "country" }}
  x="year"
  y="indexed"
  series="country"
  title="GDP by country since 2019"
  subtitle="GDP index, 2019 = 100"
/>
```

The rebasing must be stated in the subtitle. Rows must already be in time order within each group.

### A big number with context

```tsx
<BigNumber
  value={0.317}
  format="percent"
  label="Share of global electricity from renewables"
  delta={0.021}
  deltaLabel="vs 2023"
  context="Up from 19% in 2010"
  size="hero"
/>
```

Numeric `delta` values are fractions rendered as signed percentages (`0.021` is +2.1%). Pass `upIsGood={false}` when an increase is bad.

### Stat row above a chart

Until a molecule covers your case, compose atoms with ordinary layout. Use container-friendly CSS (`minmax(0, 1fr)`, `minWidth: 0`) so charts can shrink.

```tsx
<section style={{ display: "grid", gap: "2rem" }}>
  <div style={{ display: "grid", gridTemplateColumns: "repeat(auto-fit, minmax(160px, 1fr))", gap: "1.5rem" }}>
    <BigNumber value={1240000} format="compact" label="Active users" delta={0.12} deltaLabel="vs last quarter" />
    <BigNumber value={0.043} format="percent" label="Monthly churn" delta={-0.008} deltaLabel="vs last quarter" upIsGood={false} />
    <BigNumber value={38} format="{value} min" label="Median session" context="Also 38 min in January" />
  </div>
  <LineChart data={weekly} x="week" y="active" title="Weekly active users" source="Product analytics" />
</section>
```

### Load from an API on the server

```tsx
import { loadData } from "insightcharts/data";
import { BarChart } from "insightcharts";

export default async function Page() {
  const rows = await loadData({ url: "https://api.example.com/v1/emissions", path: "data.results" });
  return <BarChart data={rows} x="sector" y="mt_co2" format="{value} Mt" title="CO2 emissions by sector" source="Example API" />;
}
```

In a client-only app, pass the same `{ url, path }` object straight to `data`. The chart shows a skeleton while it loads.

### A JSON spec

```json
{
  "type": "bar-chart",
  "data": [
    { "country": "Norway", "share": 98 },
    { "country": "Brazil", "share": 89 },
    { "country": "Canada", "share": 68 }
  ],
  "x": "country",
  "y": "share",
  "format": "{value}%",
  "highlight": "Norway",
  "title": "Renewables supplied 98% of Norway's electricity in 2023",
  "subtitle": "Share of electricity generation from renewables, 2023",
  "source": "Ember"
}
```

Render with `<Insight spec={spec} />` and validate against `https://insightcharts.dev/schema/insight-spec.json`. `data` can also be a URL with a `transform`:

```json
{
  "type": "bar-chart",
  "data": { "url": "/data/renewables.csv" },
  "transform": [{ "type": "filter", "field": "year", "op": "==", "value": 2023 }],
  "x": "country",
  "y": "share",
  "title": "Renewable share of electricity by country, 2023"
}
```

### Override one ECharts setting

```tsx
<LineChart data={rows} x="date" y="price" option={{ yAxis: { min: 0, max: 200 } }} title="Daily price" />
```

`option` is deep-merged over what the component generates. Use a prop when one exists, and `option` only when none does.

## Arc diagram (`arc-diagram`)

> Places entities in order on a line and joins each related pair with a semicircular arc whose thickness is the value of the connection; dots are sized by each entity's total.

- Component: `ArcDiagram` (import from `insightcharts`)
- Spec type: `"arc-diagram"`
- Level: atom. Category: poster.
- An ECharts chart built with `defineChart`: accepts every common chart prop (data, transform, title, highlight, annotations, ...).

### When to use

Connections among up to about 20 entities that have a meaningful order (stops on a line, chapters, age groups, teams by size): trips between stations, trade between neighbours, characters sharing scenes.

### Avoid

Flows with a direction through stages (use sankey-chart); one source splitting into parts (use fan-flow); a full matrix of every pair where exact values matter (use heatmap); more than about 20 entities or 60 connections (use heatmap).

### Install

From npm (the component ships in the package):

```bash
npm install insightcharts echarts
```

Or copy the source into your project with the shadcn CLI, so you can edit it (the engine still comes from the `insightcharts` package):

```bash
npx shadcn@latest registry add @insightcharts=https://insightcharts.dev/r/{name}.json   # once per project
npx shadcn@latest add @insightcharts/arc-diagram
```

The file lands at `components/insightcharts/atoms/arc-diagram.tsx`. `@insightcharts/arc-diagram-demo` adds a ready-made example next to it.

### Usage

```tsx
import { ArcDiagram } from "insightcharts";

const data = [
  { a: "Harbour", b: "Market", trips: 4200 },
  { a: "Harbour", b: "Quay", trips: 900 },
  { a: "Quay", b: "Market", trips: 1300 },
  { a: "Market", b: "Town Hall", trips: 2600 },
  { a: "Market", b: "University", trips: 3100 },
  { a: "Town Hall", b: "University", trips: 1500 },
  { a: "Town Hall", b: "Hospital", trips: 1100 },
  { a: "University", b: "Park", trips: 800 },
  { a: "University", b: "Airport", trips: 1900 },
  { a: "Park", b: "Hospital", trips: 600 },
  { a: "Hospital", b: "Stadium", trips: 700 },
  { a: "Stadium", b: "Airport", trips: 1200 },
  { a: "Harbour", b: "Airport", trips: 2300 },
  { a: "Market", b: "Stadium", trips: 1700 },
  { a: "Quay", b: "University", trips: 500 },
];

<ArcDiagram
  theme="dusk"
  data={data}
  from="a"
  to="b"
  value="trips"
  order={["Harbour", "Quay", "Market", "Town Hall", "University", "Park", "Hospital", "Stadium", "Airport"]}
  colorBy="none"
  format="integer"
  title="Harbour and Market stations exchanged 4,200 trips a day"
  subtitle="Daily trips between pairs of stations on one tram line, both directions; dots show each station's total"
  note="Illustrative figures for an invented line."
/>
```

### JSON spec

The same thing as data, rendered with `<Insight spec={spec} />`:

```json
{
  "type": "arc-diagram",
  "theme": "dusk",
  "data": [
    { "a": "Harbour", "b": "Market", "trips": 4200 },
    { "a": "Harbour", "b": "Quay", "trips": 900 },
    { "a": "Quay", "b": "Market", "trips": 1300 },
    { "a": "Market", "b": "Town Hall", "trips": 2600 },
    { "a": "Market", "b": "University", "trips": 3100 },
    { "a": "Town Hall", "b": "University", "trips": 1500 },
    { "a": "Town Hall", "b": "Hospital", "trips": 1100 },
    { "a": "University", "b": "Park", "trips": 800 },
    { "a": "University", "b": "Airport", "trips": 1900 },
    { "a": "Park", "b": "Hospital", "trips": 600 },
    { "a": "Hospital", "b": "Stadium", "trips": 700 },
    { "a": "Stadium", "b": "Airport", "trips": 1200 },
    { "a": "Harbour", "b": "Airport", "trips": 2300 },
    { "a": "Market", "b": "Stadium", "trips": 1700 },
    { "a": "Quay", "b": "University", "trips": 500 }
  ],
  "from": "a",
  "to": "b",
  "value": "trips",
  "order": ["Harbour", "Quay", "Market", "Town Hall", "University", "Park", "Hospital", "Stadium", "Airport"],
  "colorBy": "none",
  "format": "integer",
  "title": "Harbour and Market stations exchanged 4,200 trips a day",
  "subtitle": "Daily trips between pairs of stations on one tram line, both directions; dots show each station's total",
  "note": "Illustrative figures for an invented line."
}
```

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `from` (required) | `string` |  | Field naming one end of each connection. With `select: true` a click selects the entity under this field name, so inside `<InsightData>` other charts are filtered on `from`; pass `select: "<field>"` to link on the field that holds the entity in the shared rows. |
| `to` (required) | `string` |  | Field naming the other end. |
| `value` | `string` |  | Value field: arc thickness. Omit to count rows. Rows joining the same pair are summed, in either direction. |
| `order` | `string[]` |  | Entity names in the order they sit on the line. Entities not listed follow in data order. |
| `orientation` | `"auto" \| "horizontal" \| "vertical"` | `"auto"` | Line along the bottom with arcs above, or down the left with arcs to the right. Auto turns vertical on narrow screens. |
| `colorBy` | `"series" \| "none"` |  | `series`: each arc in the colour of its first entity; past the size of the theme's palette the extra colours are derived from the theme's own. `none`: every arc in the accent. Default: series while the entities fit the palette (at most 8), none beyond. |
| `arcLabels` | `boolean` | `true` | Print values at the top of the arcs, largest first, wherever they do not collide. The values that do not fit are printed while their entity is hovered or selected, and every value is in the tooltip. |
| `names` | `Record<string, string>` |  | Display names for entity keys. |

### Common props

Also accepts every prop in the "Common chart props" section of this file.

### Composition

- Composes: nothing (it is a primitive)
- Used by: [network-poster](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/network-poster.md)

## Area chart (`area-chart`)

> Shows a quantity over time as a filled area from zero: one series, stacked series, shares of 100%, or a streamgraph.

- Component: `AreaChart` (import from `insightcharts`)
- Spec type: `"area-chart"`
- Level: atom. Category: trend.
- An ECharts chart built with `defineChart`: accepts every common chart prop (data, transform, title, highlight, annotations, ...).

### When to use

A volume or cumulative quantity over time where the filled magnitude matters; stacked when the total and its composition both matter; percent when only the mix matters; stream for the changing mix of many series over a long period.

### Avoid

Comparing the trajectories of several series against each other (use line-chart: only the bottom band of a stack has a flat baseline); a few time points (use bar-chart with stack); more than about 6 bands.

### Install

From npm (the component ships in the package):

```bash
npm install insightcharts echarts
```

Or copy the source into your project with the shadcn CLI, so you can edit it (the engine still comes from the `insightcharts` package):

```bash
npx shadcn@latest registry add @insightcharts=https://insightcharts.dev/r/{name}.json   # once per project
npx shadcn@latest add @insightcharts/area-chart
```

The file lands at `components/insightcharts/atoms/area-chart.tsx`. `@insightcharts/area-chart-demo` adds a ready-made example next to it.

### Usage

```tsx
import { AreaChart } from "insightcharts";

const data = [
  { year: "2014", gw: 180 },
  { year: "2015", gw: 229 },
  { year: "2016", gw: 306 },
  { year: "2017", gw: 405 },
  { year: "2018", gw: 512 },
  { year: "2019", gw: 633 },
  { year: "2020", gw: 774 },
  { year: "2021", gw: 945 },
  { year: "2022", gw: 1177 },
  { year: "2023", gw: 1610 },
];

<AreaChart
  data={data}
  x="year"
  y="gw"
  names={{ gw: "Installed solar capacity" }}
  format="{value} GW"
  title="World solar capacity rose from 180 GW in 2014 to 1,610 GW in 2023"
  subtitle="Cumulative installed solar PV capacity, gigawatts"
  source="IRENA, Renewable Capacity Statistics (rounded)"
  note="Figures are approximate, for illustration"
/>
```

### JSON spec

The same thing as data, rendered with `<Insight spec={spec} />`:

```json
{
  "type": "area-chart",
  "data": [
    { "year": "2014", "gw": 180 },
    { "year": "2015", "gw": 229 },
    { "year": "2016", "gw": 306 },
    { "year": "2017", "gw": 405 },
    { "year": "2018", "gw": 512 },
    { "year": "2019", "gw": 633 },
    { "year": "2020", "gw": 774 },
    { "year": "2021", "gw": 945 },
    { "year": "2022", "gw": 1177 },
    { "year": "2023", "gw": 1610 }
  ],
  "x": "year",
  "y": "gw",
  "names": { "gw": "Installed solar capacity" },
  "format": "{value} GW",
  "title": "World solar capacity rose from 180 GW in 2014 to 1,610 GW in 2023",
  "subtitle": "Cumulative installed solar PV capacity, gigawatts",
  "source": "IRENA, Renewable Capacity Statistics (rounded)",
  "note": "Figures are approximate, for illustration"
}
```

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `x` (required) | `string` |  | Time or ordered category field. ISO dates are placed on a true time axis. |
| `y` (required) | `string \| string[]` |  | Value field, or several (one area each). |
| `series` | `string` |  | Field that splits rows into areas (long data). |
| `stack` | `boolean \| "percent"` | `false` | Stack the areas; `percent` normalises every x position to 100%. |
| `stream` | `boolean` | `false` | Streamgraph: stack around a centred baseline. The value axis is dropped because only band thickness is readable. |
| `curve` | `"linear" \| "smooth" \| "step"` | `"linear"` | Edge shape. A streamgraph defaults to smooth. |
| `labels` | `boolean` |  | Name each band inside itself where it fits; the rest go to the legend. Default: on when stacked. |
| `names` | `Record<string, string>` |  | Display names for series keys. |

### Common props

Also accepts every prop in the "Common chart props" section of this file.

### Composition

- Composes: nothing (it is a primitive)
- Used by: [section](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/section.md), [atlas-poster](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/atlas-poster.md), [social-card](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/social-card.md)

## Arrow chart (`arrow-chart`)

> Draws an arrow per category from a start value to an end value, showing the direction and size of each shift.

- Component: `ArrowChart` (import from `insightcharts`)
- Spec type: `"arrow-chart"`
- Level: atom. Category: comparison.
- An ECharts chart built with `defineChart`: accepts every common chart prop (data, transform, title, highlight, annotations, ...).

### When to use

Shifts between two moments across up to about 25 categories when some rise and some fall: swings between elections, before / after a policy.

### Avoid

When both levels matter more than the direction (use dumbbell-chart); more than two points in time (use slope-chart or line-chart); a single value per category (use bar-chart).

### Install

From npm (the component ships in the package):

```bash
npm install insightcharts echarts
```

Or copy the source into your project with the shadcn CLI, so you can edit it (the engine still comes from the `insightcharts` package):

```bash
npx shadcn@latest registry add @insightcharts=https://insightcharts.dev/r/{name}.json   # once per project
npx shadcn@latest add @insightcharts/arrow-chart
```

The file lands at `components/insightcharts/atoms/arrow-chart.tsx`. `@insightcharts/arrow-chart-demo` adds a ready-made example next to it.

### Usage

```tsx
import { ArrowChart } from "insightcharts";

const data = [
  { group: "Under 30", y2019: 62, y2024: 71 },
  { group: "30 to 44", y2019: 58, y2024: 63 },
  { group: "45 to 64", y2019: 49, y2024: 47 },
  { group: "65 and over", y2019: 41, y2024: 34 },
];

<ArrowChart
  theme="editorial"
  data={data}
  category="group"
  from="y2019"
  to="y2024"
  names={{ y2019: "2019", y2024: "2024" }}
  format="{value}%"
  changeLabel="Change"
  height={220}
  title="Support among under-30s rose from 62% in 2019 to 71% in 2024"
  subtitle="Share in favour of the congestion charge, by age group, 2019 to 2024"
  source="City residents survey"
  note="Illustrative figures."
/>
```

### JSON spec

The same thing as data, rendered with `<Insight spec={spec} />`:

```json
{
  "type": "arrow-chart",
  "theme": "editorial",
  "data": [
    { "group": "Under 30", "y2019": 62, "y2024": 71 },
    { "group": "30 to 44", "y2019": 58, "y2024": 63 },
    { "group": "45 to 64", "y2019": 49, "y2024": 47 },
    { "group": "65 and over", "y2019": 41, "y2024": 34 }
  ],
  "category": "group",
  "from": "y2019",
  "to": "y2024",
  "names": { "y2019": "2019", "y2024": "2024" },
  "format": "{value}%",
  "changeLabel": "Change",
  "height": 220,
  "title": "Support among under-30s rose from 62% in 2019 to 71% in 2024",
  "subtitle": "Share in favour of the congestion charge, by age group, 2019 to 2024",
  "source": "City residents survey",
  "note": "Illustrative figures."
}
```

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `category` (required) | `string` |  | Category field: one arrow each. |
| `from` (required) | `string` |  | Field with the start value, or (long data) the `series` value that marks it. |
| `to` (required) | `string` |  | Field with the end value, or (long data) the `series` value that marks it. |
| `series` | `string` |  | Long data: the field whose values are `from` and `to`. |
| `value` | `string` | `"value"` | Long data: the measure field. |
| `good` | `"up" \| "down" \| "none"` | `"up"` | Direction drawn in the positive colour. `none` uses the accent for every arrow. |
| `sort` | `"change" \| "from" \| "to" \| "none"` | `"change"` | Row order. |
| `order` | `"desc" \| "asc"` | `"desc"` | Sort direction. |
| `labels` | `boolean` |  | Start and end values at the tail and head. Default: on for up to 14 rows; otherwise a value axis is drawn. |
| `changeLabel` | `boolean \| string` | `false` | Print the signed change in a right-hand column; a string sets the column header. |
| `zero` | `boolean` | `false` | Start the value axis at zero. |
| `names` | `Record<string, string>` |  | Display names for the `from` and `to` keys. |

### Common props

Also accepts every prop in the "Common chart props" section of this file.

### Composition

- Composes: nothing (it is a primitive)
- Used by: no molecule or template yet

### More examples

#### Lower is better, one row highlighted

```tsx

  { country: "Austria", before: 5.3, after: 5.2 },
  { country: "Luxembourg", before: 5.9, after: 6.1 },

  data={data}
  category="country"
  from="before"
  to="after"
  names={{ before: "2013", after: "2024" }}
  good="down"
  highlight="Greece"
  sort="change"
  order="asc"
  format="{value}%"
  title="Greek unemployment fell from 27.5% in 2013 to 10.1% in 2024"
  subtitle="Unemployment rate, 2013 to 2024"
  source="Eurostat (rounded)"
  note="Figures are approximate, for illustration"
```

## Bar chart (`bar-chart`)

> Compares a value across categories with bars from a zero baseline.

- Component: `BarChart` (import from `insightcharts`)
- Spec type: `"bar-chart"`
- Level: atom. Category: comparison.
- An ECharts chart built with `defineChart`: accepts every common chart prop (data, transform, title, highlight, annotations, ...).

### When to use

Ranking or comparing up to about 20 categories; grouped for a few series, stacked when the total and its composition both matter.

### Avoid

Change over many time points (use line-chart); two values per category (use dumbbell-chart); more than about 5 stacked segments.

### Install

From npm (the component ships in the package):

```bash
npm install insightcharts echarts
```

Or copy the source into your project with the shadcn CLI, so you can edit it (the engine still comes from the `insightcharts` package):

```bash
npx shadcn@latest registry add @insightcharts=https://insightcharts.dev/r/{name}.json   # once per project
npx shadcn@latest add @insightcharts/bar-chart
```

The file lands at `components/insightcharts/atoms/bar-chart.tsx`. `@insightcharts/bar-chart-demo` adds a ready-made example next to it.

### Usage

```tsx
import { BarChart } from "insightcharts";

const data = [
  { country: "Norway", share: 98 },
  { country: "Brazil", share: 89 },
  { country: "Canada", share: 68 },
];

<BarChart
  data={data}
  x="country"
  y="share"
  format="{value}%"
  title="Renewables supplied 98% of Norway's electricity in 2023"
  theme="ledger"
/>
```

### JSON spec

The same thing as data, rendered with `<Insight spec={spec} />`:

```json
{
  "type": "bar-chart",
  "data": [
    { "country": "Norway", "share": 98 },
    { "country": "Brazil", "share": 89 },
    { "country": "Canada", "share": 68 }
  ],
  "x": "country",
  "y": "share",
  "format": "{value}%",
  "title": "Renewables supplied 98% of Norway's electricity in 2023",
  "theme": "ledger"

```

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `x` (required) | `string` |  | Category field. |
| `y` (required) | `string \| string[]` |  | Value field, or several for grouped / stacked bars. |
| `series` | `string` |  | Field that splits rows into series (long data). |
| `orientation` | `"auto" \| "horizontal" \| "vertical"` | `"auto"` | Horizontal for rankings and long labels, vertical for time. |
| `sort` | `"none" \| "asc" \| "desc"` |  | Bar order. Default: descending for rankings, data order for time. |
| `stack` | `boolean \| "percent"` | `false` | Stack series; `percent` normalises to 100%. |
| `labels` | `boolean` |  | Value labels at bar ends. Default: on for one series of up to 12 bars. |
| `names` | `Record<string, string>` |  | Display names for series keys. |

### Common props

Also accepts every prop in the "Common chart props" section of this file.

### Composition

- Composes: nothing (it is a primitive)
- Used by: [before-after](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/before-after.md), [chart-callout](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/chart-callout.md), [chart-tabs](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/chart-tabs.md), [linked-charts](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/linked-charts.md), [poster](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/poster.md), [scrolly-chart](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/scrolly-chart.md), [section](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/section.md), [small-multiple-grid](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/small-multiple-grid.md), [comparison-brief](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/comparison-brief.md), [data-explorer](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/data-explorer.md), [executive-brief](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/executive-brief.md), [explainer](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/explainer.md), [report-page](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/report-page.md), [scorecard](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/scorecard.md), [social-card](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/social-card.md), [story-deck](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/story-deck.md), [timeline-story](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/timeline-story.md), [visual-essay](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/visual-essay.md)

## Beeswarm chart (`beeswarm-chart`)

> Shows a distribution as one dot per row along a value axis, with dots stacked sideways where they would collide.

- Component: `BeeswarmChart` (import from `insightcharts`)
- Spec type: `"beeswarm-chart"`
- Level: atom. Category: distribution.
- An ECharts chart built with `defineChart`: accepts every common chart prop (data, transform, title, highlight, annotations, ...).

### When to use

Showing a distribution while keeping every individual visible: 30 to about 2,000 named things (countries, players, schools), optionally in a few rows by group, with one or two highlighted.

### Avoid

More than about 2,000 rows or when only the summary matters (use histogram or box-plot); many groups with few rows each (use strip-plot); two numeric measures (use scatter-chart).

### Install

From npm (the component ships in the package):

```bash
npm install insightcharts echarts
```

Or copy the source into your project with the shadcn CLI, so you can edit it (the engine still comes from the `insightcharts` package):

```bash
npx shadcn@latest registry add @insightcharts=https://insightcharts.dev/r/{name}.json   # once per project
npx shadcn@latest add @insightcharts/beeswarm-chart
```

The file lands at `components/insightcharts/atoms/beeswarm-chart.tsx`. `@insightcharts/beeswarm-chart-demo` adds a ready-made example next to it.

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `value` (required) | `string` |  | Numeric field that positions each dot along the axis. |
| `group` | `string` |  | Field that splits the dots into rows, one swarm per group. |
| `series` | `string` |  | Field that colours dots by category. Beyond 6 categories the rest turn grey. |
| `label` | `string` |  | Field naming each dot, for tooltips, `highlight` and labels on highlighted dots. |
| `radius` | `number` |  | Dot radius in px. Default 5 down to 3 by row count; shrinks if a swarm would overflow its row. |
| `median` | `boolean` | `false` | Mark each row's median with a vertical tick. |
| `names` | `Record<string, string>` |  | Display names for series keys. |

### Common props

Also accepts every prop in the "Common chart props" section of this file.

### Composition

- Composes: nothing (it is a primitive)
- Used by: no molecule or template yet

```tsx
  data={data}

  median

```

## Big number (`big-number`)

> A featured statistic with its label, change and the context that gives it meaning.

- Component: `BigNumber` (import from `insightcharts`)
- Spec type: `"big-number"`
- Level: atom. Category: figure.
- An HTML component: it takes only the props listed below, plus `theme`, `mode`, `className` and `style` where its source declares them. It does not take the common chart props.

### When to use

A single headline figure, or a row of three or four key numbers. Always give it context: a comparison, a denominator or a period.

### Avoid

Showing a number with no comparison; using a gauge or a one-slice donut for the same job.

### Install

From npm (the component ships in the package):

```bash
npm install insightcharts echarts
```

Or copy the source into your project with the shadcn CLI, so you can edit it (the engine still comes from the `insightcharts` package):

```bash
npx shadcn@latest registry add @insightcharts=https://insightcharts.dev/r/{name}.json   # once per project
npx shadcn@latest add @insightcharts/big-number
```

The file lands at `components/insightcharts/atoms/big-number.tsx`. `@insightcharts/big-number-demo` adds a ready-made example next to it.

### Usage

```tsx
import { BigNumber } from "insightcharts";

<BigNumber
  value={0.317}
  format="percent"
  label="Share of global electricity from renewables"
  delta={0.021}
  deltaLabel="vs 2023"
  context="Up from 19% in 2010"
/>
```

### JSON spec

The same thing as data, rendered with `<Insight spec={spec} />`:

```json
{
  "type": "big-number",
  "value": 0.317,
  "format": "percent",
  "label": "Share of global electricity from renewables",
  "delta": 0.021,
  "deltaLabel": "vs 2023",
  "context": "Up from 19% in 2010"
}
```

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `value` (required) | `number \| string` |  | The figure. Numbers are formatted with `format`. |
| `label` (required) | `string` |  | What it measures, sentence case. |
| `context` | `string` |  | The comparison, denominator or period that gives it meaning. |
| `delta` | `number \| string` |  | Change against a baseline. Numbers render as signed percentages (0.12 is +12%). |
| `deltaLabel` | `string` |  | What the delta is against, e.g. "vs last quarter". |
| `upIsGood` | `boolean` | `true` | Whether an increase is good news; decides the delta colour. |
| `format` | `FormatSpec` | `"auto"` | Number format. |
| `size` | `"hero" \| "stat"` | `"stat"` | `hero` for the one number a piece leads with. |
| `align` | `"left" \| "center"` | `"left"` | Text alignment. |
| `variant` | `"plain" \| "filled" \| "tinted" \| "with-icon" \| "with-ring" \| "with-trend"` | `"plain"` | The display: `filled` (a solid ground in the tone with contrasting ink), `tinted` (a 10% wash), `with-icon` (needs `icon`: a tinted badge above the label), `with-ring` (needs `target` or `max`, or a share from 0 to 1: a progress ring beside the figure), `with-trend` (needs `series`: a line under the figure). A variant whose data is missing renders as `plain`. |
| `tone` | `"neutral" \| "accent" \| "positive" \| "negative" \| number` | `"accent"` | Colour of the ground or graphic. A number picks from the theme's categorical palette, 0-based. |
| `icon` | `IconInput` |  | A built-in icon name or `path://...`, for `with-icon`. |
| `series` | `number[]` |  | Past values in time order, oldest first, ending with the current value, for `with-trend`. |
| `target` | `number` |  | The goal for `value`, for `with-ring`. |
| `max` | `number` |  | End of the ring's scale. Default: the target, or 1 for a share. |
| `theme` | `ThemeInput` |  | A theme name such as `"editorial"`, or token overrides. A named theme paints its own ground. |
| `frame` | `boolean` |  | Set false to stop a named theme painting its ground. |

### Composition

- Composes: nothing (it is a primitive)
- Used by: [annotated-timeline](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/annotated-timeline.md), [before-after](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/before-after.md), [hero-figure](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/hero-figure.md), [metric-breakdown](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/metric-breakdown.md), [poster](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/poster.md), [quote-figure](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/quote-figure.md), [stat-row](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/stat-row.md), [explainer](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/explainer.md), [social-card](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/social-card.md), [story-deck](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/story-deck.md), [timeline-story](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/timeline-story.md)

## Block bars (`block-bar`)

> Compares 3 to 12 values as thick rounded bars from a zero baseline, with each value printed inside the end of its bar and the category beneath.

- Component: `BlockBar` (import from `insightcharts`)
- Spec type: `"block-bar"`
- Level: atom. Category: poster.
- An ECharts chart built with `defineChart`: accepts every common chart prop (data, transform, title, highlight, annotations, ...).

### When to use

A short series or ranking that should read as a bold graphic with no axis: ticket sales in each of six years, two paired measures in five regions. Add `detail` for a second small figure above each bar and `marker` for an event between two bars.

### Avoid

More than 12 bars, more than two series or stacked parts (use bar-chart); negative values (use diverging-bar-chart); a long time series (use line-chart); values that differ by more than about 50 times, where the short bars vanish (use proportional-area).

### Install

From npm (the component ships in the package):

```bash
npm install insightcharts echarts
```

Or copy the source into your project with the shadcn CLI, so you can edit it (the engine still comes from the `insightcharts` package):

```bash
npx shadcn@latest registry add @insightcharts=https://insightcharts.dev/r/{name}.json   # once per project
npx shadcn@latest add @insightcharts/block-bar
```

The file lands at `components/insightcharts/atoms/block-bar.tsx`. `@insightcharts/block-bar-demo` adds a ready-made example next to it.

### Usage

```tsx
import { BlockBar } from "insightcharts";

const data = [
  { year: "2020", tickets: 18400, seats: "41% of seats" },
  { year: "2021", tickets: 22900, seats: "49% of seats" },
  { year: "2022", tickets: 31200, seats: "58% of seats" },
  { year: "2023", tickets: 36800, seats: "64% of seats" },
  { year: "2024", tickets: 41500, seats: "69% of seats" },
  { year: "2025", tickets: 48200, seats: "74% of seats" },
];

<BlockBar
  theme="noir"
  data={data}
  name="year"
  value="tickets"
  detail="seats"
  format="integer"
  marker={{ after: "2021", label: "Second screen opened" }}
  title="The Portholm Film Festival sold 48,200 tickets in 2025"
  subtitle="Tickets sold per year and share of available seats filled, 2020 to 2025"
  source="Illustrative data"
  note="Invented figures for a fictional festival"
/>
```

### JSON spec

The same thing as data, rendered with `<Insight spec={spec} />`:

```json
{
  "type": "block-bar",
  "theme": "noir",
  "data": [
    { "year": "2020", "tickets": 18400, "seats": "41% of seats" },
    { "year": "2021", "tickets": 22900, "seats": "49% of seats" },
    { "year": "2022", "tickets": 31200, "seats": "58% of seats" },
    { "year": "2023", "tickets": 36800, "seats": "64% of seats" },
    { "year": "2024", "tickets": 41500, "seats": "69% of seats" },
    { "year": "2025", "tickets": 48200, "seats": "74% of seats" }
  ],
  "name": "year",
  "value": "tickets",
  "detail": "seats",
  "format": "integer",
  "marker": { "after": "2021", "label": "Second screen opened" },
  "title": "The Portholm Film Festival sold 48,200 tickets in 2025",
  "subtitle": "Tickets sold per year and share of available seats filled, 2020 to 2025",
  "source": "Illustrative data",
  "note": "Invented figures for a fictional festival"
}
```

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` (required) | `string` |  | Category field: one bar (or one pair of bars) per value. |
| `value` (required) | `string \| string[]` |  | Value field, or two fields for paired bars. |
| `series` | `string` |  | Field that splits long-format rows into paired series. |
| `detail` | `string` |  | Field holding a short secondary label printed above each bar, e.g. "3.5% of GDP". |
| `marker` | `{ after: string; label?: string }` |  | A dotted line after the named category, marking an event, with an optional label. |
| `orientation` | `"auto" \| "vertical" \| "horizontal"` | `"auto"` | `auto` draws columns and switches to horizontal bars on narrow widths. |
| `names` | `Record<string, string>` |  | Display names for series keys. |

### Common props

Also accepts every prop in the "Common chart props" section of this file.

### Composition

- Composes: nothing (it is a primitive)
- Used by: [count-poster](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/count-poster.md), [timeline-poster](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/timeline-poster.md)

### More examples

#### Paired series

```tsx
import { BlockBar } from "insightcharts";

const data = [
  { line: "Coast line", weekday: 41200, weekend: 26800 },
  { line: "Valley line", weekday: 33500, weekend: 12900 },
  { line: "Airport link", weekday: 27100, weekend: 29400 },
  { line: "Harbour loop", weekday: 15800, weekend: 9200 },
];

<BlockBar
  theme="magenta"
  data={data}
  name="line"
  value={["weekday", "weekend"]}
  names={{ weekday: "Weekday", weekend: "Weekend day" }}
  format="compact"
  title="The Airport link carried 29,400 passengers on a weekend day"
  subtitle="Average daily passengers by rail line, weekdays and weekend days, 2025"
  source="Illustrative data"
  note="Invented figures for a fictional network"
/>
```

#### Highlight, click to select

```tsx

  { country: "Norway", share: 89 },
  { country: "Sweden", share: 58 },
  { country: "Netherlands", share: 35 },
  { country: "Germany", share: 19 },
  { country: "Spain", share: 9 },

<BlockBar
  data={data}
  name="country"
  value="share"
  format="{value}%"

  select

  subtitle="Battery electric share of new passenger car sales, five countries, 2025"

/>
```

#### Stress: twelve bars, long labels, uneven values

```tsx

  { port: "Greater Northern Container Terminal", teu: 9400, d: "31% of total" },
  { port: "Southport", teu: 6100, d: "20%" },
  { port: "Marlow Quay", teu: 4300, d: "14%" },

  { port: "Old Harbour", teu: 1100, d: "4%" },
  { port: "Tidewater", teu: 800, d: "3%" },
  // ... 4 more rows

<BlockBar
  theme="sunrise"
  data={data}
  name="port"
  value="teu"
  detail="d"
  format="integer"
  title="Greater Northern handled 9,400 thousand containers in 2025"
  subtitle="Container throughput by port, thousand TEU, 2025"
  source="Illustrative data"
  note="Invented figures for a fictional country"
/>
```
