## Box plot (`box-plot`)

> Summarises a numeric field per group as median, quartile box, whiskers and outlier dots, computed from raw rows.

- Component: `BoxPlot` (import from `insightcharts`)
- Spec type: `"box-plot"`
- Level: atom. Category: distribution.
- An ECharts chart built with `defineChart`: accepts every common chart prop (data, transform, title, highlight, annotations, ...).

### When to use

Comparing the centre and spread of a numeric value across several groups, especially with many rows per group and an audience comfortable with quartiles.

### Avoid

A general audience or fewer than about 20 rows per group (use strip-plot or beeswarm-chart, which show the observations themselves); one group whose shape matters, such as two peaks, which a box hides (use histogram).

### Install

From npm (the component ships in the package):

```bash
npm install insightcharts echarts
```

Or copy the source into your project with the shadcn CLI, so you can edit it (the engine still comes from the `insightcharts` package):

```bash
npx shadcn@latest registry add @insightcharts=https://insightcharts.dev/r/{name}.json   # once per project
npx shadcn@latest add @insightcharts/box-plot
```

The file lands at `components/insightcharts/atoms/box-plot.tsx`. `@insightcharts/box-plot-demo` adds a ready-made example next to it.

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `value` (required) | `string` |  | Numeric field to summarise. Pass raw rows; quartiles are computed in the chart. |
| `group` | `string` |  | Category field: one box per distinct value. Omit for a single box. |
| `label` | `string` |  | Field naming each row, shown when hovering an outlier. |
| `orientation` | `"horizontal" \| "vertical"` | `"horizontal"` | Horizontal leaves room for long names; vertical suits ordered categories. |
| `whiskers` | `"tukey" \| "minmax"` | `"tukey"` | `tukey`: furthest point within 1.5 × IQR, the rest drawn as outliers. `minmax`: the extremes. |
| `sort` | `"none" \| "asc" \| "desc"` | `"none"` | Order boxes by median. |

### Common props

Also accepts every prop in the "Common chart props" section of this file.

### Composition

- Composes: nothing (it is a primitive)
- Used by: no molecule or template yet

## Bubble network (`bubble-network`)

> Draws a small set of circles sized by value and joined by thin lines, with one circle highlighted and tagged.

- Component: `BubbleNetwork` (import from `insightcharts`)
- Spec type: `"bubble-network"`
- Level: atom. Category: poster.
- An ECharts chart built with `defineChart`: accepts every common chart prop (data, transform, title, highlight, annotations, ...).

### When to use

Showing which of up to about 12 named things are connected, and how big each is: trade blocs, route maps between hubs, partnerships, shared ownership. Give `x` and `y` to place the circles by hand, for example roughly geographically.

### Avoid

Flows with magnitudes between stages (use sankey-chart); more than about 12 circles or a dense web of links (use heatmap as a matrix, or data-table); comparison of the sizes alone (use bar-chart or circle-pack).

### Install

From npm (the component ships in the package):

```bash
npm install insightcharts echarts
```

Or copy the source into your project with the shadcn CLI, so you can edit it (the engine still comes from the `insightcharts` package):

```bash
npx shadcn@latest registry add @insightcharts=https://insightcharts.dev/r/{name}.json   # once per project
npx shadcn@latest add @insightcharts/bubble-network
```

The file lands at `components/insightcharts/atoms/bubble-network.tsx`. `@insightcharts/bubble-network-demo` adds a ready-made example next to it.

### Usage

```tsx
import { BubbleNetwork } from "insightcharts";

const data = [
  { airport: "Lisbon", m: 34 },
  { airport: "Madrid", m: 60 },
  { airport: "Paris", m: 67 },
  { airport: "Frankfurt", m: 59 },
  { airport: "Rome", m: 41 },
  { airport: "Athens", m: 28 },
  { airport: "Istanbul", m: 76 },
];

<BubbleNetwork
  theme="ocean"
  data={data}
  name="airport"
  value="m"
  links={[
    { from: "Istanbul", to: "Frankfurt" },
    { from: "Istanbul", to: "Paris" },
    { from: "Istanbul", to: "Rome" },
    { from: "Istanbul", to: "Athens" },
    { from: "Istanbul", to: "Madrid" },
    { from: "Istanbul", to: "Lisbon" },
    { from: "Madrid", to: "Lisbon" },
    { from: "Paris", to: "Frankfurt" },
    { from: "Rome", to: "Athens" },
  ]}
  highlight="Istanbul"
  tag="Busiest"
  format="{value}m"
  title="Istanbul handled 76 million passengers in 2023"
  subtitle="Passengers at seven airports, millions, 2023. Lines show the routes in this example."
  note="Rounded passenger figures; the routes drawn are illustrative"
/>
```

### JSON spec

```json
    { "from": "Istanbul", "to": "Athens" },
    { "from": "Istanbul", "to": "Madrid" },

  "highlight": "Istanbul",
```

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` (required) | `string` |  | Name field: one circle per row. |
| `value` (required) | `string` |  | Value field: circle area. |
| `x` | `string` |  | Horizontal position field, 0 (left) to 100 (right). With `y`, places the circles by hand. |
| `y` | `string` |  | Vertical position field, 0 (top) to 100 (bottom). |
| `links` | `{ from: string; to: string; value?: number }[]` |  | Lines between circles, by name. `value` sets the line width and is printed on the line. |
| `tag` | `string` |  | Short tag attached to the highlighted circle, e.g. "Joined 2024". |
| `linkFormat` | `FormatSpec` |  | How to print link values. |
| `linkLabels` | `boolean` |  | Print link values on the lines. Default: on when any link has a value. |
| `layout` | `"ring" \| "hub"` |  | Without `x` and `y`: "ring" spaces the circles round an ellipse in data order, "hub" also moves the most-connected circle to the middle. Default: "hub" when one circle links to most of the others. |

### Common props

Also accepts every prop in the "Common chart props" section of this file.

### Composition

- Composes: nothing (it is a primitive)
- Used by: [atlas-poster](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/atlas-poster.md), [network-poster](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/network-poster.md)

## Bubble scale (`bubble-scale`)

> Places circles sized by one measure along a single value scale set by another, spread sideways so none overlap, with boxed scale marks instead of an axis.

- Component: `BubbleScale` (import from `insightcharts`)
- Spec type: `"bubble-scale"`
- Level: atom. Category: poster.
- An ECharts chart built with `defineChart`: accepts every common chart prop (data, transform, title, highlight, annotations, ...).

### When to use

A poster answer to "where does each one sit on this scale, and how big is it": 5 to about 40 named things with a rate or score (the scale) and a magnitude (the area), such as import dependency against share of demand.

### Avoid

Two measures that should be read against each other on two axes (use scatter-chart); one measure only (use beeswarm-chart or strip-plot); precise comparison of the sizes (use bar-chart); more than about 60 rows (use beeswarm-chart).

### Install

From npm (the component ships in the package):

```bash
npm install insightcharts echarts
```

Or copy the source into your project with the shadcn CLI, so you can edit it (the engine still comes from the `insightcharts` package):

```bash
npx shadcn@latest registry add @insightcharts=https://insightcharts.dev/r/{name}.json   # once per project
npx shadcn@latest add @insightcharts/bubble-scale
```

The file lands at `components/insightcharts/atoms/bubble-scale.tsx`. `@insightcharts/bubble-scale-demo` adds a ready-made example next to it.

### Usage

```tsx
import { BubbleScale } from "insightcharts";

const data = [
  { material: "Lithium", imported: 100, kt: 38 },
  { material: "Cobalt", imported: 86, kt: 21 },
  { material: "Graphite", imported: 98, kt: 96 },
  { material: "Nickel", imported: 71, kt: 164 },
  { material: "Manganese", imported: 96, kt: 52 },
  { material: "Copper", imported: 48, kt: 410 },
  { material: "Aluminium", imported: 59, kt: 290 },
  { material: "Rare earths", imported: 100, kt: 9 },
  { material: "Silicon metal", imported: 64, kt: 73 },
  { material: "Zinc", imported: 22, kt: 118 },
  { material: "Steel scrap", imported: 4, kt: 520 },
  { material: "Tin", imported: 78, kt: 14 },
];

<BubbleScale
  theme="sunrise"
  data={data}
  name="material"
  value="imported"
  size="kt"
  format="{value}%"
  sizeFormat="{value} kt"
  domain={[0, 100]}
  ticks={[0, 20, 40, 60, 80, 100]}
  scaleLabel="Imported"
  title="Imports supply between 4% and 100% of the region's demand for 12 materials"
  subtitle="Share of each material imported (position) and annual demand in thousand tonnes (area), 12 battery and grid materials"
  note="Illustrative figures for an invented region"
/>
```

```json
    { "material": "Silicon metal", "imported": 64, "kt": 73 },
    { "material": "Zinc", "imported": 22, "kt": 118 },
    { "material": "Steel scrap", "imported": 4, "kt": 520 },

```

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` (required) | `string` |  | Name field: one circle per row. |
| `value` (required) | `string` |  | Numeric field that positions each circle along the scale. Printed with `format`. |
| `size` (required) | `string` |  | Numeric field for circle area. Printed inside or beside each circle with `sizeFormat`. |
| `series` | `string` |  | Field that colours circles by category. Default: circles are shaded along the scale with the sequential ramp. |
| `orientation` | `"vertical" \| "horizontal"` | `"vertical"` | Direction of the scale. Narrow containers always use vertical. |
| `domain` | `[number, number]` |  | Scale range. Default: the data extent rounded out to the tick step. |
| `ticks` | `number[]` |  | Values to mark on the scale. Default: about five round values. |
| `scaleLabel` | `string` |  | Short name of the scale measure, printed at the head of the scale. |
| `sizeFormat` | `FormatSpec` |  | How to print the size measure. |
| `guides` | `boolean` | `true` | Thin dotted guide line at each scale mark. |
| `names` | `Record<string, string>` |  | Display names for series keys. |

### Common props

Also accepts every prop in the "Common chart props" section of this file.

### Composition

- Composes: nothing (it is a primitive)
- Used by: [flow-poster](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/flow-poster.md)

```tsx
  { fund: "Fund G", fee: 0.23, bn: 33 },
  { fund: "Fund H", fee: 0.12, bn: 24 },
  // ... 32 more rows
];

<BubbleScale
  theme="forest"
  data={data}
  name="fund"
  value="fee"
  size="bn"
  format="{value}%"
  sizeFormat="${value}bn"

  subtitle="Annual fee (position) and assets in $ billion (area), 40 index and active funds"
  note="Illustrative figures for invented funds"
/>
```

## Bullet chart (`bullet-chart`)

> Compares one measure per row with its target, optionally against qualitative bands such as poor / fair / good.

- Component: `BulletChart` (import from `insightcharts`)
- Spec type: `"bullet-chart"`
- Level: atom. Category: comparison.
- An ECharts chart built with `defineChart`: accepts every common chart prop (data, transform, title, highlight, annotations, ...).

### When to use

Progress against a target or budget for one to about 10 measures, including measures in different units (`scale: "independent"`); a compact scorecard instead of a row of gauges.

### Avoid

No target or thresholds to compare with (use bar-chart); a single share of a whole (use progress-meter); change over time (use line-chart).

### Install

From npm (the component ships in the package):

```bash
npm install insightcharts echarts
```

Or copy the source into your project with the shadcn CLI, so you can edit it (the engine still comes from the `insightcharts` package):

```bash
npx shadcn@latest registry add @insightcharts=https://insightcharts.dev/r/{name}.json   # once per project
npx shadcn@latest add @insightcharts/bullet-chart
```

The file lands at `components/insightcharts/atoms/bullet-chart.tsx`. `@insightcharts/bullet-chart-demo` adds a ready-made example next to it.

### Usage

```tsx
import { BulletChart } from "insightcharts";

const data = [
  { region: "North America", sales: 94, target: 80 },
  { region: "Europe", sales: 71, target: 85 },
  { region: "Asia Pacific", sales: 63, target: 60 },
  { region: "Latin America", sales: 38, target: 55 },
];

<BulletChart
  theme="mono"
  data={data}
  category="region"
  value="sales"
  target="target"
  bands={[50, 75, 110]}
  bandNames={["Below plan", "On plan", "Stretch"]}
  names={{ sales: "Sales", target: "Target" }}
  format="currency:USD"
  height={240}
  title="Europe sold $71 million against a target of $85 million in 2024"
  subtitle="Sales against target by region, $ millions, 2024"
  source="Company accounts"
  note="Illustrative figures."
/>
```

### JSON spec

The same thing as data, rendered with `<Insight spec={spec} />`:

```json
{
  "type": "bullet-chart",
  "theme": "mono",
  "data": [
    { "region": "North America", "sales": 94, "target": 80 },
    { "region": "Europe", "sales": 71, "target": 85 },
    { "region": "Asia Pacific", "sales": 63, "target": 60 },
    { "region": "Latin America", "sales": 38, "target": 55 }
  ],
  "category": "region",
  "value": "sales",
  "target": "target",
  "bands": [50, 75, 110],
  "bandNames": ["Below plan", "On plan", "Stretch"],
  "names": { "sales": "Sales", "target": "Target" },
  "format": "currency:USD",
  "height": 240,
  "title": "Europe sold $71 million against a target of $85 million in 2024",
  "subtitle": "Sales against target by region, $ millions, 2024",
  "source": "Company accounts",
  "note": "Illustrative figures."
}
```

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `category` (required) | `string` |  | Field naming each row. |
| `value` (required) | `string` |  | Field with the measured value. Values below zero are not supported. |
| `target` | `string` |  | Field with the target, drawn as a tick across the bar. |
| `bands` | `number[] \| string[]` |  | Ascending upper bounds of qualitative bands, or the fields holding them per row. Omit unless the thresholds are real. |
| `bandNames` | `string[]` |  | Band names, lowest first, for the legend and tooltip. |
| `max` | `number \| string` |  | End of the scale: a number or a per-row field. Default: just past the largest value, target or band. |
| `scale` | `"shared" \| "independent"` | `"shared"` | One axis for all rows, or each row on its own scale (different units). |
| `formatField` | `string` |  | Field holding a format spec per row, for mixed units. |
| `names` | `Record<string, string>` |  | Display names for the value and target fields. |

### Common props

Also accepts every prop in the "Common chart props" section of this file.

### Composition

- Composes: nothing (it is a primitive)
- Used by: [scorecard](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/scorecard.md)

### More examples

#### Scorecard with a separate scale per row

```tsx
import { BulletChart } from "insightcharts";

const data = [
  { kpi: "Revenue", actual: 4.6, goal: 5, low: 3.5, mid: 4.5, high: 6, unit: "${value}m" },
  { kpi: "Gross margin", actual: 41, goal: 38, low: 25, mid: 35, high: 50, unit: "{value}%" },
  {
    kpi: "New customers",
    actual: 1320,
    goal: 1500,
    low: 900,
    mid: 1300,
    high: 1800,
    unit: "integer",
  },
  {
    kpi: "Customer satisfaction",
    actual: 4.4,
    goal: 4.5,
    low: 3.5,
    mid: 4.2,
    high: 5,
    unit: "decimal:1",
  },
  {
    kpi: "Average order value",
    actual: 58,
    goal: 52,
    low: 40,
    mid: 50,
    high: 65,
    unit: "currency:EUR",
  },
];

<BulletChart
  theme="ledger"
  data={data}
  category="kpi"
  value="actual"
  target="goal"
  bands={["low", "mid", "high"]}
  bandNames={["Poor", "Acceptable", "Good"]}
  scale="independent"
  formatField="unit"
  names={{ actual: "Actual", goal: "Target" }}
  height={300}
  title="Third-quarter revenue was $4.6 million against a target of $5.0 million"
  subtitle="Third-quarter results against target"
  note="Illustrative figures."
/>
```

#### No thresholds, one row highlighted


## Bump chart (`bump-chart`)

> Shows how the ranking of entities changes over time, with rank 1 at the top and each line named at its end.

- Component: `BumpChart` (import from `insightcharts`)
- Spec type: `"bump-chart"`
- Level: atom. Category: trend.
- An ECharts chart built with `defineChart`: accepts every common chart prop (data, transform, title, highlight, annotations, ...).

### When to use

League tables over 3 to about 15 periods for up to about 12 entities, when the order and the changes in rank are what matter and the underlying values differ too much (or too little) to share an axis.

### Avoid

When the size of the values matters (use line-chart); only two periods (use slope-chart); a single ranking (use bar-chart or lollipop-chart).

### Install

From npm (the component ships in the package):

```bash
npm install insightcharts echarts
```

Or copy the source into your project with the shadcn CLI, so you can edit it (the engine still comes from the `insightcharts` package):

```bash
npx shadcn@latest registry add @insightcharts=https://insightcharts.dev/r/{name}.json   # once per project
npx shadcn@latest add @insightcharts/bump-chart
```

The file lands at `components/insightcharts/atoms/bump-chart.tsx`. `@insightcharts/bump-chart-demo` adds a ready-made example next to it.

### Usage

```tsx
import { BumpChart } from "insightcharts";

const data = [
  { year: "2019", Tesla: 0.37, BYD: 0.23, SAIC: 0.16, Volkswagen: 0.14, Hyundai: 0.13, Geely: 0.12 },
  { year: "2020", Tesla: 0.5, BYD: 0.18, SAIC: 0.27, Volkswagen: 0.42, Hyundai: 0.2, Geely: 0.1 },
  { year: "2021", Tesla: 0.94, BYD: 0.6, SAIC: 0.68, Volkswagen: 0.76, Hyundai: 0.35, Geely: 0.2 },
  { year: "2022", Tesla: 1.31, BYD: 1.86, SAIC: 0.72, Volkswagen: 0.83, Hyundai: 0.51, Geely: 0.65 },
  { year: "2023", Tesla: 1.81, BYD: 3.02, SAIC: 0.79, Volkswagen: 1, Hyundai: 0.57, Geely: 0.93 },
  { year: "2024", Tesla: 1.79, BYD: 4.27, SAIC: 0.9, Volkswagen: 1.04, Hyundai: 0.56, Geely: 1.39 },
];

<BumpChart
  theme="poster"
  data={data}
  x="year"
  y={["Tesla", "BYD", "SAIC", "Volkswagen", "Hyundai", "Geely"]}
  highlight="BYD"
  format="{value}m"
  height={300}
  title="BYD rose from fifth in 2020 to first in 2022"
  subtitle="Rank among six carmakers by plug-in vehicles sold worldwide, 2019 to 2024"
  source="Company reports"
  note="Approximate figures."
/>
```

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `x` (required) | `string` |  | Time or ordered category field. |
| `y` (required) | `string \| string[]` |  | Value field to rank by, or several (one line each). |
| `series` | `string` |  | Field that splits rows into entities (long data). |
| `ranked` | `boolean` | `false` | The values are already ranks (1 = best) and are plotted as given. |
| `order` | `"desc" \| "asc"` | `"desc"` | Which values rank first when ranks are computed: largest (`desc`) or smallest (`asc`). |
| `startLabels` | `boolean` |  | Name lines at the start as well as the end. Default: on when the chart is wide enough. |
| `names` | `Record<string, string>` |  | Display names for series keys. |

### Common props

Also accepts every prop in the "Common chart props" section of this file.

### Composition

- Composes: nothing (it is a primitive)
- Used by: no molecule or template yet

### More examples

## Calendar heatmap (`calendar-heatmap`)

> Colours every day of one or more years by a value, laid out as a grid of weeks.

- Component: `CalendarHeatmap` (import from `insightcharts`)
- Spec type: `"calendar-heatmap"`
- Level: atom. Category: trend.
- An ECharts chart built with `defineChart`: accepts every common chart prop (data, transform, title, highlight, annotations, ...).

### When to use

Daily data over months or years where weekly rhythm, seasonality, streaks and gaps matter: activity, sales, incidents, habits.

### Avoid

Reading the trend or exact values (use line-chart); fewer than about three months of days (use bar-chart); a non-daily grain such as hour by weekday (use heatmap).

### Install

From npm (the component ships in the package):

```bash
npm install insightcharts echarts
```

Or copy the source into your project with the shadcn CLI, so you can edit it (the engine still comes from the `insightcharts` package):

```bash
npx shadcn@latest registry add @insightcharts=https://insightcharts.dev/r/{name}.json   # once per project
npx shadcn@latest add @insightcharts/calendar-heatmap
```

The file lands at `components/insightcharts/atoms/calendar-heatmap.tsx`. `@insightcharts/calendar-heatmap-demo` adds a ready-made example next to it.

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `date` (required) | `string` |  | Date field: ISO strings, Dates or epoch milliseconds. One cell per calendar day. |
| `value` (required) | `string` |  | Numeric field that colours each day. Rows sharing a day are summed. |
| `orientation` | `"auto" \| "horizontal" \| "vertical"` | `"auto"` | Weeks left to right, or top to bottom. `auto` goes vertical under 480px. |
| `weekStart` | `"monday" \| "sunday"` | `"monday"` | First day of the week. |
| `domain` | `[number, number]` |  | Fix the ends of the colour scale. Default: 0 to the maximum. |
| `height` | `number \| string` |  | Common prop, but note the default: when omitted the height follows the cell size, which follows the width, so cells stay square. |

### Common props

Also accepts every prop in the "Common chart props" section of this file.

### Composition

- Composes: nothing (it is a primitive)
- Used by: no molecule or template yet

### More examples

#### Three years, with a gap in the record

```tsx
import { CalendarHeatmap } from "insightcharts";

const data = [
  { day: "2022-01-01", steps: 3996 },
  { day: "2022-01-02", steps: 1946 },
  { day: "2022-01-03", steps: 3651 },
  { day: "2022-01-04", steps: 4872 },
  { day: "2022-01-05", steps: 2206 },
  { day: "2022-01-06", steps: 1736 },
  { day: "2022-01-07", steps: 4042 },
  { day: "2022-01-08", steps: 5780 },
  // ... 1058 more rows
];

<CalendarHeatmap
  data={data}
  date="day"
  value="steps"
  format="compact"
  title="Steps per day, 2022 to 2024"
  subtitle="Daily step count. There is no data for April 2023."
  note="Illustrative data"
/>
```

## Callout (`callout`)

> A boxed statement of fact with a short bold lead and a sentence of explanation. The tone is marked by icon and tint.

- Component: `Callout` (import from `insightcharts`)
- Spec type: `"callout"`
- Level: atom. Category: text.
- An HTML component: it takes only the props listed below, plus `theme`, `mode`, `className` and `style` where its source declares them. It does not take the common chart props.

### When to use

Beside or under a chart, to state its main fact in words, with the number. Also for a caveat the reader must not miss (`negative`).

### Avoid

Long narration (use `prose`), a featured number (use `big-number` or `stat-tile`), or more than one callout per chart.

### Install

From npm (the component ships in the package):

```bash
npm install insightcharts echarts
```

Or copy the source into your project with the shadcn CLI, so you can edit it (the engine still comes from the `insightcharts` package):

```bash
npx shadcn@latest registry add @insightcharts=https://insightcharts.dev/r/{name}.json   # once per project
npx shadcn@latest add @insightcharts/callout
```

The file lands at `components/insightcharts/atoms/callout.tsx`. `@insightcharts/callout-demo` adds a ready-made example next to it.

### Usage

```tsx
import { Callout } from "insightcharts";

<Callout
  tone="accent"
  label="Summary"
  lead="Solar supplied more than half of demand on 4 in 10 summer afternoons in 2024"
  text="Wholesale prices were below zero on those afternoons."
/>
```

### JSON spec

The same thing as data, rendered with `<Insight spec={spec} />`:

```json
{
  "type": "callout",
  "tone": "accent",
  "label": "Summary",
  "lead": "Solar supplied more than half of demand on 4 in 10 summer afternoons in 2024",
  "text": "Wholesale prices were below zero on those afternoons."
}
```

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `lead` | `string` |  | The fact in a few bold words. State it with its number. |
| `text` | `string` |  | One sentence of explanation or evidence. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` |  | JSX alternative to `text`. |
| `tone` | `"neutral" \| "positive" \| "negative" \| "accent"` | `"neutral"` | Sets the icon shape and the tint together. |
| `label` | `string` |  | Small label above the lead, e.g. "Summary". |
| `variant` | `"soft" \| "outline" \| "plain"` | `"soft"` | Tinted box, bordered box, or no box. |
| `frame` | `boolean` |  | Paint a named theme's background behind the callout, with padding and rounded corners. On by default for a named theme with its own surface; `false` turns it off. |

### Composition

- Composes: nothing (it is a primitive)
- Used by: [chart-callout](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/chart-callout.md), [comparison-brief](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/comparison-brief.md), [data-explorer](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/data-explorer.md), [explainer](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/explainer.md)

### More examples

#### Positive

```tsx
import { Callout } from "insightcharts";

<Callout
  theme="editorial"
  tone="positive"
  lead="Monthly churn fell from 4.2% to 2.1% between January and June"
  text="It has stayed at 2.1% for two quarters since."
/>
```

#### Negative caveat, outline

```tsx
import { Callout } from "insightcharts";

<Callout
  theme="ledger"
  tone="negative"
  variant="outline"
  label="Caveat"
  lead="2020 figures are not comparable"
  text="The survey moved online during lockdown. Response rates among over-75s fell by a third. Treat 2020 as a break in the series."
/>
```

#### Neutral, plain

```tsx
import { Callout } from "insightcharts";

<Callout
  theme="blueprint"
  tone="neutral"
  variant="plain"
  text="Figures are provisional until the statistical office publishes its annual revision in September."
/>
```

#### One token overridden

```tsx
import { Callout } from "insightcharts";

<Callout
  theme={{ accent: "#b4237a" }}
  tone="accent"
  label="Key point"
  lead="Night buses carried 18% of all weekend journeys in 2024"
  text="The share was 11% in 2019. Illustrative figures."
/>
```

#### Accent on a painted ground

```tsx
import { Callout } from "insightcharts";

<Callout
  theme="forest"
  tone="accent"
  variant="outline"
  lead="Tree cover in the city rose from 14% to 19% between 2010 and 2024"
  text="The target for 2030 is 25%. Illustrative figures."
/>
```

- Choosing a form: https://insightcharts.dev/llms/guides/choosing-a-form.md

## Choropleth map (`choropleth-map`)

> Colours the regions of a map by a normalised value, from GeoJSON you supply.

- Component: `ChoroplethMap` (import from `insightcharts`)
- Spec type: `"choropleth-map"`
- Level: atom. Category: geo.
- An ECharts chart built with `defineChart`: accepts every common chart prop (data, transform, title, highlight, annotations, ...).

### When to use

A rate, share or per-capita figure that varies by place, where the geographic pattern (a north-south divide, a cluster) is what the reader needs to see. Use a diverging scale for change or for values either side of a meaningful midpoint.

### Avoid

Raw counts, which mostly map population (normalise first, or use bar-chart); ranking regions precisely (use bar-chart); a handful of regions with no spatial pattern (use bar-chart); regions so different in size that small ones vanish (use a tile-grid GeoJSON).

### Install

From npm (the component ships in the package):

```bash
npm install insightcharts echarts
```

Or copy the source into your project with the shadcn CLI, so you can edit it (the engine still comes from the `insightcharts` package):

```bash
npx shadcn@latest registry add @insightcharts=https://insightcharts.dev/r/{name}.json   # once per project
npx shadcn@latest add @insightcharts/choropleth-map
```

The file lands at `components/insightcharts/atoms/choropleth-map.tsx`. `@insightcharts/choropleth-map-demo` adds a ready-made example next to it.

### Usage

```tsx
import { ChoroplethMap } from "insightcharts";

const data = [
  { state: "Queensland", share: 45 },
  { state: "South Australia", share: 47 },
  { state: "Western Australia", share: 39 },
  { state: "New South Wales", share: 31 },
  { state: "Australian Capital Territory", share: 29 },
  { state: "Victoria", share: 26 },
  { state: "Northern Territory", share: 22 },
  { state: "Tasmania", share: 19 },
];

<ChoroplethMap
  theme="earth"
  geo={{
    type: "FeatureCollection",
    features: [
      {
        type: "Feature",
        properties: { name: "Western Australia", code: "WA" },
        geometry: { type: "Polygon", coordinates: [[[0, 1], [4, 1], [4, 6], [0, 6], [0, 1]]] },
      },
      {
        type: "Feature",
        properties: { name: "Northern Territory", code: "NT" },
        geometry: { type: "Polygon", coordinates: [[[4, 3.5], [6.5, 3.5], [6.5, 6.5], [4, 6.5], [4, 3.5]]] },
      },
      {
        type: "Feature",
        properties: { name: "South Australia", code: "SA" },
        geometry: { type: "Polygon", coordinates: [[[4, 1], [6.5, 1], [6.5, 3.5], [4, 3.5], [4, 1]]] },
      },
      {
        type: "Feature",
        properties: { name: "Queensland", code: "Qld" },
        geometry: {
          type: "Polygon",
          coordinates: [
            [
              [6.5, 3],
              [10, 3],
              [10, 5.2],
              [8.6, 5.2],
              [8.6, 7.2],
              [7.6, 7.2],
              [7.6, 6.2],
              [6.5, 6.2],
              [6.5, 3],
            ],
          ],
        },
      },
      {
        type: "Feature",
        properties: { name: "New South Wales", code: "NSW" },
        geometry: {
          type: "Polygon",
          coordinates: [
            [[6.5, 1.4], [10, 1.4], [10, 3], [6.5, 3], [6.5, 1.4]],
            [[8.7, 1.8], [8.7, 2.4], [9.4, 2.4], [9.4, 1.8], [8.7, 1.8]],
          ],
        },
      },
      {
        type: "Feature",
        properties: { name: "Australian Capital Territory", code: "ACT" },
        geometry: {
          type: "Polygon",
          coordinates: [[[8.7, 1.8], [9.4, 1.8], [9.4, 2.4], [8.7, 2.4], [8.7, 1.8]]],
        },
      },
      {
        type: "Feature",
        properties: { name: "Victoria", code: "Vic" },
        geometry: {
          type: "Polygon",
          coordinates: [[[6.5, 0.3], [9.2, 0.3], [9.2, 1.4], [6.5, 1.4], [6.5, 0.3]]],
        },
      },
      {
        type: "Feature",
        properties: { name: "Tasmania", code: "Tas" },
        geometry: {
          type: "Polygon",
          coordinates: [[[7.6, -1.1], [8.7, -1.1], [8.7, -0.3], [7.6, -0.3], [7.6, -1.1]]],
        },
      },
    ],
  }}
  data={data}
  region="state"
  value="share"
  format="{value}%"
  aspectScale={1}
  labels
  labelProperty="code"
  height={380}
  title="47% of homes in South Australia had rooftop solar in 2023"
  subtitle="Share of dwellings with a solar installation, by state and territory, 2023"
  source="Australian PV Institute"
  note="Approximate figures on a simplified block map"
/>
```

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `geo` (required) | `GeoJSON FeatureCollection \| string` |  | The map: a GeoJSON object, or a URL to fetch one from. Registered with ECharts automatically. |
| `region` (required) | `string` |  | Row field holding the region name that joins to the GeoJSON. |
| `value` (required) | `string` |  | Row field holding the value. Use a rate or share, not a raw count. |
| `nameProperty` | `string` | `"name"` | GeoJSON feature property holding each region's name. |
| `scale` | `"sequential" \| "diverging"` | `"sequential"` | Sequential for magnitude; diverging for values either side of a midpoint. |
| `midpoint` | `number` | `0` | Centre of the diverging scale. |
| `domain` | `[number, number]` |  | Fix the colour scale instead of using the data's range. |
| `labels` | `boolean \| "value"` | `false` | Print region names on the map; `"value"` adds the value on a second line. |
| `labelProperty` | `string` |  | GeoJSON feature property to print instead of the full name, e.g. a postal or ISO code. |
| `missingLabel` | `string` | `"No data"` | Legend text for regions without a value. |
| `aspectScale` | `number` | `0.75` | Horizontal stretch for longitude; 1 for tile maps and projected coordinates. |

### Common props

Also accepts every prop in the "Common chart props" section of this file.

### Composition

- Composes: nothing (it is a primitive)
- Used by: [atlas-poster](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/atlas-poster.md)

### More examples

#### Diverging, with missing regions

```tsx
import { ChoroplethMap } from "insightcharts";

const data = [
  { state: "Queensland", net: 3.1 },
  { state: "Western Australia", net: 1.9 },
  { state: "South Australia", net: -0.2 },
  { state: "New South Wales", net: -3.4 },
  { state: "Victoria", net: -0.9 },
  { state: "Tasmania", net: -1.6 },
];

  geo={{
    type: "FeatureCollection",
    features: [

        type: "Feature",
```

#### Diverging on a tile grid


## Circle pack (`circle-pack`)

> Shows parts as tightly packed circles sized by value, optionally clustered into groups, with the value and name printed inside each circle.

- Component: `CirclePack` (import from `insightcharts`)
- Spec type: `"circle-pack"`
- Level: atom. Category: poster.
- An ECharts chart built with `defineChart`: accepts every common chart prop (data, transform, title, highlight, annotations, ...).

### When to use

A poster view of 5 to about 60 parts of very different sizes where the reader should see the largest ones and their rough proportions at once: budgets by programme, emissions by source, users by product. One level of grouping is supported.

### Avoid

Values that need precise comparison (use bar-chart, where bars share a baseline); parts that must visibly add up to a whole (use treemap or waffle-chart); more than about 80 parts (use treemap); negative values (use diverging-bar-chart).

### Install

From npm (the component ships in the package):

```bash
npm install insightcharts echarts
```

Or copy the source into your project with the shadcn CLI, so you can edit it (the engine still comes from the `insightcharts` package):

```bash
npx shadcn@latest registry add @insightcharts=https://insightcharts.dev/r/{name}.json   # once per project
npx shadcn@latest add @insightcharts/circle-pack
```

The file lands at `components/insightcharts/atoms/circle-pack.tsx`. `@insightcharts/circle-pack-demo` adds a ready-made example next to it.

### Usage

```tsx
import { CirclePack } from "insightcharts";

const data = [
  { crop: "Maize", group: "Cereals", mt: 1160 },
  { crop: "Wheat", group: "Cereals", mt: 780 },
  { crop: "Rice", group: "Cereals", mt: 790 },
  { crop: "Barley", group: "Cereals", mt: 150 },
  { crop: "Sorghum", group: "Cereals", mt: 60 },
  { crop: "Potatoes", group: "Roots", mt: 375 },
  { crop: "Cassava", group: "Roots", mt: 330 },
  { crop: "Sweet potatoes", group: "Roots", mt: 90 },
  { crop: "Yams", group: "Roots", mt: 85 },
  { crop: "Soybeans", group: "Oil crops", mt: 350 },
  { crop: "Oil palm fruit", group: "Oil crops", mt: 420 },
  { crop: "Rapeseed", group: "Oil crops", mt: 87 },
  { crop: "Sunflower seed", group: "Oil crops", mt: 54 },
];

<CirclePack
  theme="magenta"
  data={data}
  name="crop"
  value="mt"
  group="group"
  format="{value} Mt"
  title="The world harvested 1,160 million tonnes of maize in 2022"
  subtitle="Harvest of 13 major crops by group, million tonnes, 2022"
  source="FAOSTAT"
  note="Rounded, approximate figures for illustration"
/>
```

### JSON spec

The same thing as data, rendered with `<Insight spec={spec} />`:

```json
{
  "type": "circle-pack",
  "theme": "magenta",
  "data": [
    { "crop": "Maize", "group": "Cereals", "mt": 1160 },
    { "crop": "Wheat", "group": "Cereals", "mt": 780 },
    { "crop": "Rice", "group": "Cereals", "mt": 790 },
    { "crop": "Barley", "group": "Cereals", "mt": 150 },
    { "crop": "Sorghum", "group": "Cereals", "mt": 60 },
    { "crop": "Potatoes", "group": "Roots", "mt": 375 },
    { "crop": "Cassava", "group": "Roots", "mt": 330 },
    { "crop": "Sweet potatoes", "group": "Roots", "mt": 90 },
    { "crop": "Yams", "group": "Roots", "mt": 85 },
    { "crop": "Soybeans", "group": "Oil crops", "mt": 350 },
    { "crop": "Oil palm fruit", "group": "Oil crops", "mt": 420 },
    { "crop": "Rapeseed", "group": "Oil crops", "mt": 87 },
    { "crop": "Sunflower seed", "group": "Oil crops", "mt": 54 }
  ],
  "name": "crop",
  "value": "mt",
  "group": "group",
  "format": "{value} Mt",
  "title": "The world harvested 1,160 million tonnes of maize in 2022",
  "subtitle": "Harvest of 13 major crops by group, million tonnes, 2022",
  "source": "FAOSTAT",
  "note": "Rounded, approximate figures for illustration"
}
```

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` (required) | `string` |  | Name field: one circle per row. |
| `value` (required) | `string` |  | Value field: circle area. Non-positive values are dropped. |
| `group` | `string` |  | Parent field. Circles sharing a group sit together and share a colour. |
| `ring` | `"none" \| "group" \| "all"` |  | Thin dotted enclosing ring: one per group with its name and total, or one around the whole pack. Default "group" when `group` is set, else "none". |
| `colorBy` | `"group" \| "value" \| "single"` |  | Colour by group, shade by value along the sequential ramp, or use the accent for every circle. Default "group" when `group` is set, else "single". |
| `icon` | `string \| Record<string, string>` |  | Icon drawn above the number in large circles: one for all, or a map from circle or group name to icon. Built-in name or `path://`. |
| `sizeLegend` | `boolean \| number[]` | `false` | Size key of nested reference circles. `true` picks round values; an array sets them. |
| `labels` | `boolean` | `true` | Print names and values inside circles, and beside the ones too small to hold them. |
| `names` | `Record<string, string>` |  | Display names for group keys. |

### Common props

Also accepts every prop in the "Common chart props" section of this file.

### Composition

- Composes: nothing (it is a primitive)
- Used by: [ranking-poster](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/ranking-poster.md)

### More examples

#### Flat, with highlight, icons and a size key

```tsx
  data={data}
  name="service"
  value="m"
  format="${value}m"

  sizeLegend
  select
  title="Schools take $412 million of the city's $1,627 million budget"
  subtitle="Annual spending by service, $ million. Click a circle to select it."
  note="Illustrative figures for an invented city"
/>
```

## Curve rank (`curve-rank`)

> Places each entity on two parallel scales, one per measure, and joins its two positions with a smooth S-curve labelled with the name and both values.

- Component: `CurveRank` (import from `insightcharts`)
- Spec type: `"curve-rank"`
- Level: atom. Category: poster.
- An ECharts chart built with `defineChart`: accepts every common chart prop (data, transform, title, highlight, annotations, ...).

### When to use

Two different measures of the same 4 to about 15 entities, when the point is how standing on one relates to standing on the other: price against sales, staff against output, cost against usage. Each side has its own scale, stated in its heading.

### Avoid

The same measure at two moments (use slope-chart); ranks across many periods (use bump-chart); more than about 15 entities or a statistical relationship (use scatter-chart); exact comparison on one measure (use bar-chart).

### Install

From npm (the component ships in the package):

```bash
npm install insightcharts echarts
```

Or copy the source into your project with the shadcn CLI, so you can edit it (the engine still comes from the `insightcharts` package):

```bash
npx shadcn@latest registry add @insightcharts=https://insightcharts.dev/r/{name}.json   # once per project
npx shadcn@latest add @insightcharts/curve-rank
```

The file lands at `components/insightcharts/atoms/curve-rank.tsx`. `@insightcharts/curve-rank-demo` adds a ready-made example next to it.

### Usage

```tsx
import { CurveRank } from "insightcharts";

const data = [
  { drink: "Filter coffee", price: 2.4, cups: 310 },
  { drink: "Espresso", price: 2.6, cups: 145 },
  { drink: "Flat white", price: 3.6, cups: 260 },
  { drink: "Iced latte", price: 4.2, cups: 180 },
  { drink: "Matcha latte", price: 4.8, cups: 75 },
  { drink: "Hot chocolate", price: 3.9, cups: 40 },
];

<CurveRank
  theme="blueprint"
  data={data}
  name="drink"
  left="price"
  right="cups"
  leftLabel="Price per cup"
  rightLabel="Cups sold a day"
  leftFormat={{ style: "currency", currency: "GBP" }}
  leftTop="low"
  title="Filter coffee sold 310 cups a day at £2.40 a cup"
  subtitle="Price per cup and cups sold per day for six drinks at one café, cheapest at the top"
  note="Illustrative figures."
/>
```

### JSON spec

The same thing as data, rendered with `<Insight spec={spec} />`:

```json
{
  "type": "curve-rank",
  "theme": "blueprint",
  "data": [
    { "drink": "Filter coffee", "price": 2.4, "cups": 310 },
    { "drink": "Espresso", "price": 2.6, "cups": 145 },
    { "drink": "Flat white", "price": 3.6, "cups": 260 },
    { "drink": "Iced latte", "price": 4.2, "cups": 180 },
    { "drink": "Matcha latte", "price": 4.8, "cups": 75 },
    { "drink": "Hot chocolate", "price": 3.9, "cups": 40 }
  ],
  "name": "drink",
  "left": "price",
  "right": "cups",
  "leftLabel": "Price per cup",
  "rightLabel": "Cups sold a day",
  "leftFormat": { "style": "currency", "currency": "GBP" },
  "leftTop": "low",
  "title": "Filter coffee sold 310 cups a day at £2.40 a cup",
  "subtitle": "Price per cup and cups sold per day for six drinks at one café, cheapest at the top",
  "note": "Illustrative figures."
}
```

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` (required) | `string` |  | Entity field: one curve per row. |
| `left` (required) | `string` |  | Field for the left-hand measure. |
| `right` (required) | `string` |  | Field for the right-hand measure. |
| `leftLabel` | `string` |  | Heading over the left rule: the measure and its unit. Defaults to the field name. |
| `rightLabel` | `string` |  | Heading over the right rule. Defaults to the field name. |
| `leftScale` | `"linear" \| "log"` | `"linear"` | Scale of the left measure. A log scale is stated in the heading. |
| `rightScale` | `"linear" \| "log"` | `"linear"` | Scale of the right measure. |
| `leftTop` | `"high" \| "low"` | `"high"` | Which end of the left measure sits at the top. |
| `rightTop` | `"high" \| "low"` | `"high"` | Which end of the right measure sits at the top. |
| `leftFormat` | `FormatSpec` |  | How to print left values. Defaults to `format`. |
| `rightFormat` | `FormatSpec` |  | How to print right values. Defaults to `format`. |
| `order` | `string[]` |  | Entity names in the order that assigns colours. Pass the same list to glyph-table to match its row colours. |
| `colorBy` | `"series" \| "none"` |  | `series`: one colour per entity; past the size of the theme's palette the extra colours are derived from the theme's own (glyph-table derives the same ones). `none`: every curve in the accent. Default: series while the entities fit the palette (at most 8), none beyond. |
| `names` | `Record<string, string>` |  | Display names for entity keys. |

### Common props

Also accepts every prop in the "Common chart props" section of this file.

### Composition

- Composes: nothing (it is a primitive)
- Used by: [matrix-poster](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/matrix-poster.md)

## Data table (`data-table`)

> A restrained editorial table from rows and a column config: aligned tabular numbers, an optional in-cell bar, row highlight and click-to-sort headers.

- Component: `DataTable` (import from `insightcharts`)
- Spec type: `"data-table"`
- Level: atom. Category: figure.
- An HTML component: it takes only the props listed below, plus `theme`, `mode`, `className` and `style` where its source declares them. It does not take the common chart props.

### When to use

When readers need to look up exact values, or compare a handful of entities across several measures with different units. Sort it by the column the caption refers to and highlight the row it names.

### Avoid

Showing a trend or a single comparison (use `line-chart` or `bar-chart`); more than about 7 columns or 30 rows without `maxHeight`.

### Install

From npm (the component ships in the package):

```bash
npm install insightcharts echarts
```

Or copy the source into your project with the shadcn CLI, so you can edit it (the engine still comes from the `insightcharts` package):

```bash
npx shadcn@latest registry add @insightcharts=https://insightcharts.dev/r/{name}.json   # once per project
npx shadcn@latest add @insightcharts/data-table
```

The file lands at `components/insightcharts/atoms/data-table.tsx`. `@insightcharts/data-table-demo` adds a ready-made example next to it.

### Usage

```tsx
import { DataTable } from "insightcharts";

<DataTable
  theme="editorial"
  caption="Wind and solar supplied 67% of Denmark's electricity in 2024"
  subtitle="Electricity generation by country, 2024"
  source="Ember (illustrative figures)"
  highlight="Denmark"
  sort={{ key: "share", direction: "desc" }}
  columns={[
    { key: "country", label: "Country" },
    { key: "share", label: "Wind and solar share", format: "percent", bar: true, width: "38%" },
    { key: "twh", label: "Generation, TWh", format: "decimal:1" },
    {
      key: "change",
      label: "Change vs 2023",
      format: { style: "percent", signDisplay: "exceptZero", maximumFractionDigits: 1 },
    },
  ]}
  rows={[
    { country: "Germany", share: 0.43, twh: 209.4, change: 0.031 },
    { country: "Spain", share: 0.42, twh: 112.8, change: 0.044 },
    { country: "Denmark", share: 0.67, twh: 23.1, change: 0.012 },
    { country: "Netherlands", share: 0.41, twh: 49.6, change: 0.058 },
    { country: "Portugal", share: 0.46, twh: 22.9, change: 0.027 },
    { country: "France", share: 0.14, twh: 73.5, change: 0.009 },
    { country: "Poland", share: 0.24, twh: 40.2, change: -0.004 },
  ]}
/>
```

### JSON spec

The same thing as data, rendered with `<Insight spec={spec} />`:

```json
{
  "type": "data-table",
  "theme": "editorial",
  "caption": "Wind and solar supplied 67% of Denmark's electricity in 2024",
  "subtitle": "Electricity generation by country, 2024",
  "source": "Ember (illustrative figures)",
  "highlight": "Denmark",
  "sort": { "key": "share", "direction": "desc" },
  "columns": [
    { "key": "country", "label": "Country" },
    {
      "key": "share",
      "label": "Wind and solar share",
      "format": "percent",
      "bar": true,
      "width": "38%"
    },
    { "key": "twh", "label": "Generation, TWh", "format": "decimal:1" },
    {
      "key": "change",
      "label": "Change vs 2023",
      "format": { "style": "percent", "signDisplay": "exceptZero", "maximumFractionDigits": 1 }
    }
  ],
  "rows": [
    { "country": "Germany", "share": 0.43, "twh": 209.4, "change": 0.031 },
    { "country": "Spain", "share": 0.42, "twh": 112.8, "change": 0.044 },
    { "country": "Denmark", "share": 0.67, "twh": 23.1, "change": 0.012 },
    { "country": "Netherlands", "share": 0.41, "twh": 49.6, "change": 0.058 },
    { "country": "Portugal", "share": 0.46, "twh": 22.9, "change": 0.027 },
    { "country": "France", "share": 0.14, "twh": 73.5, "change": 0.009 },
    { "country": "Poland", "share": 0.24, "twh": 40.2, "change": -0.004 }
  ]
}
```

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rows` (required) | `Row[]` |  | One object per row. |
| `columns` | `(string \| { key, label?, format?, align?, bar?, sortable?, width? })[]` |  | Columns in order. Defaults to every key of the first row. Numeric columns are right-aligned. |
| `caption` | `string` |  | The table's title, as a real `<caption>`. |
| `subtitle` | `string` |  | Units and period, under the caption. |
| `source` | `string` |  | Shown under the table as "Source: ...". |
| `highlight` | `string \| number \| (string \| number)[]` |  | Rows to emphasise, matched on the first column (or `highlightKey`). |
| `highlightKey` | `string` |  | Field `highlight` matches against. |
| `sort` | `{ key, direction?: "asc" \| "desc" }` |  | Initial sort. |
| `sortable` | `boolean` | `true` | Click or press Enter on a header to sort; a third press restores the original order. |
| `maxHeight` | `number \| string` |  | Height before the body scrolls under the sticky header. |
| `density` | `"comfortable" \| "compact"` | `"comfortable"` | Row padding. |
| `frame` | `boolean` |  | Paint a named theme's background behind the table, with padding and rounded corners. On by default for a named theme with its own surface; `false` turns it off. |

### Composition

- Composes: nothing (it is a primitive)
- Used by: [data-explorer](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/data-explorer.md)

## Delta (`delta`)

> An inline change indicator: direction arrow, signed value and an optional baseline label.

- Component: `Delta` (import from `insightcharts`)
- Spec type: `"delta"`
- Level: atom. Category: figure.
- An HTML component: it takes only the props listed below, plus `theme`, `mode`, `className` and `style` where its source declares them. It does not take the common chart props.

### When to use

Next to a figure, in a sentence, a table cell or a tile, to say how much it changed and against what. Set `upIsGood: false` for measures where a fall is the good news (churn, emissions, wait times).

### Avoid

Standing alone as the main figure (use `big-number` or `stat-tile`, which include a delta). Do not omit the baseline label unless the surrounding text names it.

### Install

From npm (the component ships in the package):

```bash
npm install insightcharts echarts
```

Or copy the source into your project with the shadcn CLI, so you can edit it (the engine still comes from the `insightcharts` package):

```bash
npx shadcn@latest registry add @insightcharts=https://insightcharts.dev/r/{name}.json   # once per project
npx shadcn@latest add @insightcharts/delta
```

The file lands at `components/insightcharts/atoms/delta.tsx`. `@insightcharts/delta-demo` adds a ready-made example next to it.

### Usage

```tsx
import { Delta } from "insightcharts";

<Delta value={0.124} label="vs last quarter" size="md" />
```

### JSON spec

The same thing as data, rendered with `<Insight spec={spec} />`:

```json
{ "type": "delta", "value": 0.124, "label": "vs last quarter", "size": "md" }
```

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `value` (required) | `number \| string` |  | The change. Numbers format as signed percentages by default (0.12 is +12%). |
| `label` | `string` |  | The baseline, e.g. "vs last quarter". |
| `upIsGood` | `boolean` | `true` | Whether an increase is good news; decides the colour only. |
| `direction` | `"up" \| "down" \| "flat"` |  | Override the direction inferred from the sign. |
| `format` | `FormatSpec` | `signed percent` | Number format, e.g. `"signed"` for absolute changes or `"{value} pts"`. |
| `size` | `"sm" \| "md" \| "lg" \| "xl"` |  | 12, 14, 16 or 20px. Inherits the surrounding size when omitted. |
| `variant` | `"text" \| "pill" \| "solid"` | `"text"` | `pill` adds a tinted capsule behind the value; `solid` fills the capsule and sets the value in the surface colour. |
| `tone` | `"auto" \| "neutral" \| "accent" \| "positive" \| "negative" \| "inherit"` | `"auto"` | Colour of the value. `auto` follows the direction and `upIsGood`; `inherit` takes the surrounding text colour, for a coloured ground. |
| `theme` | `ThemeInput` |  | A theme name such as `"ledger"`, or token overrides. A named theme paints its own ground. |
| `frame` | `boolean` |  | Set false to stop a named theme painting its ground. |

### Composition

- Composes: nothing (it is a primitive)
- Used by: [before-after](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/before-after.md), [comparison-table](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/comparison-table.md), [ranked-list](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/ranked-list.md)

### More examples

#### Down is good (churn)

```tsx
import { Delta } from "insightcharts";

<Delta value={-0.021} label="monthly churn vs January" upIsGood={false} size="md" />
```

#### Down is bad, pill

```tsx
import { Delta } from "insightcharts";

<Delta value={-1840} format="signed" label="net subscribers this month" variant="pill" size="md" />
```

#### No change

```tsx
import { Delta } from "insightcharts";

<Delta value={0} label="vs 2023" size="md" />
```

#### String value, large pill

```tsx
import { Delta } from "insightcharts";

<Delta value="3 places" direction="up" label="in the regional ranking" variant="pill" size="lg" />
```

#### Solid capsule, extra large

```tsx
import { Delta } from "insightcharts";

<Delta value={0.33} label="solar capacity added vs 2023" variant="solid" size="xl" />
```

#### Solid, down is good, editorial

```tsx

  theme="editorial"
  value="−2.1 pts"
  label="monthly churn vs January"
  upIsGood={false}

  size="lg"
/>
```

#### Accent tone, ledger

```tsx

  theme="ledger"
  value={0.43}
  label="recurring revenue vs January"
  tone="accent"
  variant="pill"
  size="lg"
/>
```

#### Neutral tone

```tsx

```

#### Pill on a poster ground, noir

```tsx

  theme="noir"
  value="2 places"
  direction="up"
  label="since matchday 20"
  variant="pill"

```

#### Solid, magenta

```tsx

  theme="magenta"
  value={0.152}
  label="tickets sold vs the 2023 final"
  variant="solid"

  size="xl"
/>
```

## Diverging bar chart (`diverging-bar-chart`)

> Draws bars either side of a centre line: positive against negative values, or stacked agree / disagree responses around a neutral midpoint.

- Component: `DivergingBarChart` (import from `insightcharts`)
- Spec type: `"diverging-bar-chart"`
- Level: atom. Category: comparison.
- An ECharts chart built with `defineChart`: accepts every common chart prop (data, transform, title, highlight, annotations, ...).

### When to use

Values that can be above or below zero (net change, balance, deviation from average); survey scales where the split between the two sides matters; two opposed groups back to back.

### Avoid

Values that are all positive (use bar-chart); parts that do not have a natural two-sided order (use a stacked bar-chart); change between two dates (use arrow-chart or dumbbell-chart).

### Install

From npm (the component ships in the package):

```bash
npm install insightcharts echarts
```

Or copy the source into your project with the shadcn CLI, so you can edit it (the engine still comes from the `insightcharts` package):

```bash
npx shadcn@latest registry add @insightcharts=https://insightcharts.dev/r/{name}.json   # once per project
npx shadcn@latest add @insightcharts/diverging-bar-chart
```

The file lands at `components/insightcharts/atoms/diverging-bar-chart.tsx`. `@insightcharts/diverging-bar-chart-demo` adds a ready-made example next to it.

### Usage

```tsx
import { DivergingBarChart } from "insightcharts";

const data = [
  { city: "Austin", change: 21.3 },
  { city: "Phoenix", change: 11.2 },
  { city: "Seattle", change: 8.1 },
  { city: "Chicago", change: -2.9 },
  { city: "San Francisco", change: -7.4 },
  { city: "St. Louis", change: -11.6 },
];

<DivergingBarChart
  data={data}
  x="city"
  y="change"
  format="{value}%"
  height={260}
  title="Austin's population grew 21.3% between 2010 and 2020"
  subtitle="Population change, 2010 to 2020"
  note="Illustrative figures."
/>
```

### JSON spec

The same thing as data, rendered with `<Insight spec={spec} />`:

```json
{
  "type": "diverging-bar-chart",
  "data": [
    { "city": "Austin", "change": 21.3 },
    { "city": "Phoenix", "change": 11.2 },
    { "city": "Seattle", "change": 8.1 },
    { "city": "Chicago", "change": -2.9 },
    { "city": "San Francisco", "change": -7.4 },
    { "city": "St. Louis", "change": -11.6 }
  ],
  "x": "city",
  "y": "change",
  "format": "{value}%",
  "height": 260,
  "title": "Austin's population grew 21.3% between 2010 and 2020",
  "subtitle": "Population change, 2010 to 2020",
  "note": "Illustrative figures."
}
```

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `x` (required) | `string` |  | Category field. |
| `y` (required) | `string \| string[]` |  | One signed value field, or several fields ordered from most negative to most positive. |
| `series` | `string` |  | Field that splits rows into ordered series (long data). |
| `neutral` | `string \| false` |  | Series centred on the midline. Default: the middle one of an odd number of series. |
| `percent` | `boolean` | `false` | Normalise each row to 100% (stacked series). |
| `colors` | `"polarity" \| "sentiment"` | `"polarity"` | Single series: diverging poles, or the positive / negative colours when one side is good and the other bad. |
| `sort` | `"none" \| "asc" \| "desc"` |  | Row order. Default: descending by value or by the positive side; data order for dates. |
| `orientation` | `"auto" \| "horizontal" \| "vertical"` | `"auto"` | Horizontal, except vertical for a single series over dates. |
| `labels` | `boolean` |  | Values at bar ends (single) or inside segments (stacked). Default: on when there is room. |
| `names` | `Record<string, string>` |  | Display names for series keys. |

### Common props

Also accepts every prop in the "Common chart props" section of this file.

### Composition

- Composes: nothing (it is a primitive)
- Used by: [executive-brief](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/executive-brief.md), [report-page](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/report-page.md)

### More examples

```tsx
  theme="science"
```

## Donut chart (`donut-chart`)

> Shows how 2 to 5 parts make up one whole, with each slice labelled by name and share.

- Component: `DonutChart` (import from `insightcharts`)
- Spec type: `"donut-chart"`
- Level: atom. Category: part-to-whole.
- An ECharts chart built with `defineChart`: accepts every common chart prop (data, transform, title, highlight, annotations, ...).

### When to use

A simple composition with one dominant part, or one part the title is about, where the total itself is worth printing in the centre.

### Avoid

More than 5 categories or parts of similar size that must be ranked (use bar-chart); a single figure (use big-number); composition compared across groups or time (use bar-chart with stack "percent"); a compact card (use segmented-bar).

### Install

From npm (the component ships in the package):

```bash
npm install insightcharts echarts
```

Or copy the source into your project with the shadcn CLI, so you can edit it (the engine still comes from the `insightcharts` package):

```bash
npx shadcn@latest registry add @insightcharts=https://insightcharts.dev/r/{name}.json   # once per project
npx shadcn@latest add @insightcharts/donut-chart
```

The file lands at `components/insightcharts/atoms/donut-chart.tsx`. `@insightcharts/donut-chart-demo` adds a ready-made example next to it.

### Usage

```tsx
import { DonutChart } from "insightcharts";

const data = [
  { tenure: "Own outright", households: 8.8 },
  { tenure: "Own with a mortgage", households: 7.4 },
  { tenure: "Rent privately", households: 4.9 },
  { tenure: "Rent social housing", households: 4.1 },
];

<DonutChart
  theme="paper"
  data={data}
  name="tenure"
  value="households"
  format="{value}m"
  centerLabel="households"
  highlight="Rent privately"
  title="4.9 million households in England rented privately in 2022-23"
  subtitle="Households by tenure, England, 2022-23"
  source="English Housing Survey"
  note="Figures are approximate, for illustration"
/>
```

### JSON spec

The same thing as data, rendered with `<Insight spec={spec} />`:

```json
{
  "type": "donut-chart",
  "theme": "paper",
  "data": [
    { "tenure": "Own outright", "households": 8.8 },
    { "tenure": "Own with a mortgage", "households": 7.4 },
    { "tenure": "Rent privately", "households": 4.9 },
    { "tenure": "Rent social housing", "households": 4.1 }
  ],
  "name": "tenure",
  "value": "households",
  "format": "{value}m",
  "centerLabel": "households",
  "highlight": "Rent privately",
  "title": "4.9 million households in England rented privately in 2022-23",
  "subtitle": "Households by tenure, England, 2022-23",
  "source": "English Housing Survey",
  "note": "Figures are approximate, for illustration"
}
```

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` (required) | `string` |  | Category field: one slice per distinct value. |
| `value` (required) | `string` |  | Value field. |
| `maxSlices` | `number` | `5` | Most slices drawn, including "Other"; smaller categories are folded. |
| `centerLabel` | `string` |  | Small label in the hole, e.g. "Total". Turns the centre text on. |
| `centerValue` | `string \| number` |  | Big text in the hole. Default: the formatted total when `centerLabel` is set. |
| `otherLabel` | `string` | `"Other"` | Name of the folded slice. |
| `names` | `Record<string, string>` |  | Display names for category keys. |

### Common props

Also accepts every prop in the "Common chart props" section of this file.

### Composition

- Composes: nothing (it is a primitive)
- Used by: [poster](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/poster.md), [data-explorer](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/data-explorer.md), [explainer](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/explainer.md)

### More examples


```tsx
  // ... 1 more rows
```

#### Stress: long names and a sliver

```tsx
  title="Staff costs made up 68% of the departmental budget"
  subtitle="Departmental spending by category, £ thousands"
  source="Illustrative data"
/>
```

## Dumbbell chart (`dumbbell-chart`)

> Shows two values per category as dots joined by a line, so the length of the line shows the difference.

- Component: `DumbbellChart` (import from `insightcharts`)
- Spec type: `"dumbbell-chart"`
- Level: atom. Category: comparison.
- An ECharts chart built with `defineChart`: accepts every common chart prop (data, transform, title, highlight, annotations, ...).

### When to use

Before / after or group A / group B across up to about 20 categories, when the size of the difference is what the reader needs.

### Avoid

A single value per category (use lollipop-chart or bar-chart); when the direction of change matters more than the two levels (use arrow-chart); more than two points in time (use slope-chart or line-chart).

### Install

From npm (the component ships in the package):

```bash
npm install insightcharts echarts
```

Or copy the source into your project with the shadcn CLI, so you can edit it (the engine still comes from the `insightcharts` package):

```bash
npx shadcn@latest registry add @insightcharts=https://insightcharts.dev/r/{name}.json   # once per project
npx shadcn@latest add @insightcharts/dumbbell-chart
```

The file lands at `components/insightcharts/atoms/dumbbell-chart.tsx`. `@insightcharts/dumbbell-chart-demo` adds a ready-made example next to it.

### Usage

```tsx
import { DumbbellChart } from "insightcharts";

const data = [
  { country: "South Korea", y2000: 76, y2023: 83.6 },
  { country: "Turkey", y2000: 71.1, y2023: 77.3 },
  { country: "Poland", y2000: 73.8, y2023: 78.6 },
  { country: "Japan", y2000: 81.2, y2023: 84.1 },
  { country: "Germany", y2000: 78.2, y2023: 81.2 },
  { country: "United States", y2000: 76.7, y2023: 78.4 },
];

<DumbbellChart
  theme="science"
  data={data}
  category="country"
  from="y2000"
  to="y2023"
  names={{ y2000: "2000", y2023: "2023" }}
  gapLabel="Gain"
  format="decimal:1"
  height={280}
  title="Life expectancy in South Korea rose from 76.0 years in 2000 to 83.6 in 2023"
  subtitle="Life expectancy at birth, years, 2000 and 2023"
  source="OECD Health Statistics (rounded)"
  note="Figures are approximate, for illustration"
/>
```

### JSON spec

The same thing as data, rendered with `<Insight spec={spec} />`:

```json
{
  "type": "dumbbell-chart",
  "theme": "science",
  "data": [
    { "country": "South Korea", "y2000": 76, "y2023": 83.6 },
    { "country": "Turkey", "y2000": 71.1, "y2023": 77.3 },
    { "country": "Poland", "y2000": 73.8, "y2023": 78.6 },
    { "country": "Japan", "y2000": 81.2, "y2023": 84.1 },
    { "country": "Germany", "y2000": 78.2, "y2023": 81.2 },
    { "country": "United States", "y2000": 76.7, "y2023": 78.4 }
  ],
  "category": "country",
  "from": "y2000",
  "to": "y2023",
  "names": { "y2000": "2000", "y2023": "2023" },
  "gapLabel": "Gain",
  "format": "decimal:1",
  "height": 280,
  "title": "Life expectancy in South Korea rose from 76.0 years in 2000 to 83.6 in 2023",
  "subtitle": "Life expectancy at birth, years, 2000 and 2023",
  "source": "OECD Health Statistics (rounded)",
  "note": "Figures are approximate, for illustration"
}
```

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `category` (required) | `string` |  | Category field: one row of the chart each. |
| `from` (required) | `string` |  | Field with the first value, or (long data) the `series` value that marks it. |
| `to` (required) | `string` |  | Field with the second value, or (long data) the `series` value that marks it. |
| `series` | `string` |  | Long data: the field whose values are `from` and `to`. |
| `value` | `string` | `"value"` | Long data: the measure field. |
| `kind` | `"change" \| "groups"` | `"change"` | `change` draws a tint then the accent (before / after); `groups` uses two hues (two peers). |
| `sort` | `"gap" \| "from" \| "to" \| "none"` | `"gap"` | Row order. |
| `order` | `"desc" \| "asc"` | `"desc"` | Sort direction. |
| `labels` | `boolean` |  | Value labels beside both dots. Default: on for up to 14 rows; otherwise a value axis is drawn. |
| `gapLabel` | `boolean \| string` | `false` | Print the gap in a right-hand column; a string sets the column header. |
| `zero` | `boolean` | `false` | Start the value axis at zero. |
| `names` | `Record<string, string>` |  | Display names for the `from` and `to` keys. |

### Common props

Also accepts every prop in the "Common chart props" section of this file.

### Composition

- Composes: nothing (it is a primitive)
- Used by: [chart-callout](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/chart-callout.md), [hero-figure](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/hero-figure.md), [small-multiple-grid](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/small-multiple-grid.md), [executive-brief](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/executive-brief.md), [report-page](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/report-page.md), [visual-essay](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/visual-essay.md)

### More examples

## Fan flow (`fan-flow`)

> One solid block that splits into curved ribbons, each as thick as its value, ending at an aligned column of names, values and shares.

- Component: `FanFlow` (import from `insightcharts`)
- Spec type: `"fan-flow"`
- Level: atom. Category: poster.
- An ECharts chart built with `defineChart`: accepts every common chart prop (data, transform, title, highlight, annotations, ...).

### When to use

One total divided among 4 to about 14 destinations (or collected from that many origins, with `direction: "in"`) when the picture of the split is the point: where a budget goes, what a day's water is used for, which sources feed one total.

### Avoid

Flows with more than one stage or several sources (use sankey-chart); precise comparison of the parts (use bar-chart); 2 to 4 parts (use segmented-bar or donut-chart); values that can be negative (use bar-chart).

### Install

From npm (the component ships in the package):

```bash
npm install insightcharts echarts
```

Or copy the source into your project with the shadcn CLI, so you can edit it (the engine still comes from the `insightcharts` package):

```bash
npx shadcn@latest registry add @insightcharts=https://insightcharts.dev/r/{name}.json   # once per project
npx shadcn@latest add @insightcharts/fan-flow
```

The file lands at `components/insightcharts/atoms/fan-flow.tsx`. `@insightcharts/fan-flow-demo` adds a ready-made example next to it.

### Usage

```tsx
import { FanFlow } from "insightcharts";

const data = [
  { use: "Shower", litres: 128 },
  { use: "Toilet", litres: 97 },
  { use: "Washing machine", litres: 62 },
  { use: "Kitchen tap", litres: 45 },
  { use: "Dishwasher", litres: 24 },
  { use: "Garden", litres: 21 },
  { use: "Bathroom tap", litres: 19 },
  { use: "Leaks", litres: 16 },
];

<FanFlow
  theme="forest"
  data={data}
  name="use"
  value="litres"
  trunk="Litres a day"
  tagged={["Shower", "Washing machine", "Dishwasher"]}
  tagLabel="Uses heated water"
  title="Showers used 128 of a household's 412 litres of water a day"
  subtitle="Daily water use of one four-person household by use, litres"
  note="Illustrative figures."
/>
```

### JSON spec

The same thing as data, rendered with `<Insight spec={spec} />`:

```json
{
  "type": "fan-flow",
  "theme": "forest",
  "data": [
    { "use": "Shower", "litres": 128 },
    { "use": "Toilet", "litres": 97 },
    { "use": "Washing machine", "litres": 62 },
    { "use": "Kitchen tap", "litres": 45 },
    { "use": "Dishwasher", "litres": 24 },
    { "use": "Garden", "litres": 21 },
    { "use": "Bathroom tap", "litres": 19 },
    { "use": "Leaks", "litres": 16 }
  ],
  "name": "use",
  "value": "litres",
  "trunk": "Litres a day",
  "tagged": ["Shower", "Washing machine", "Dishwasher"],
  "tagLabel": "Uses heated water",
  "title": "Showers used 128 of a household's 412 litres of water a day",
  "subtitle": "Daily water use of one four-person household by use, litres",
  "note": "Illustrative figures."
}
```

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` (required) | `string` |  | Destination field: one ribbon per distinct value. |
| `value` (required) | `string` |  | Value field: ribbon thickness. Rows sharing a name are summed; non-positive values are dropped. |
| `trunk` | `string` |  | Label printed in the single block, with the total. |
| `direction` | `"out" \| "in"` | `"out"` | `out`: one block fans out to many labels on the right. `in`: many labels on the left flow into one block. |
| `maxItems` | `number` | `12` | Ribbons to keep; the rest are summed into the remainder ribbon. |
| `otherLabel` | `string` | `"Other"` | Name of the remainder ribbon, drawn in the context colour. A row with this name is treated as the remainder. |
| `tagged` | `string[]` |  | Destinations marked with a dotted outline around the name. |
| `tagLabel` | `string` |  | What the dotted outline means, printed in the key. Needed for `tagged` to be drawn. |
| `share` | `boolean` | `true` | Print each ribbon's share of the total. Dropped on narrow screens. |
| `colorBy` | `"series" \| "none"` |  | `series`: one colour per destination; past the size of the theme's palette the extra colours are derived from the theme's own. `none`: every ribbon in the accent. Default: series while the destinations fit the palette (at most 8), none beyond. |
| `sort` | `"value" \| "none"` | `"value"` | Largest first, or the data order. |

### Common props

Also accepts every prop in the "Common chart props" section of this file.

### Composition

- Composes: nothing (it is a primitive)
- Used by: [flow-poster](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/flow-poster.md)

### More examples

#### Many into one, with highlight

## Funnel chart (`funnel-chart`)

> Shows how many remain at each step of a sequence, with conversion and drop-off between steps.

- Component: `FunnelChart` (import from `insightcharts`)
- Spec type: `"funnel-chart"`
- Level: atom. Category: flow.
- An ECharts chart built with `defineChart`: accepts every common chart prop (data, transform, title, highlight, annotations, ...).

### When to use

A strict sequence where each stage is a subset of the one before: sign-up flows, hiring pipelines, sales stages, applications to admissions. 3 to 7 stages.

### Avoid

Stages that are not sequential subsets, or categories with no order (use bar-chart); flows that split to several destinations (use sankey-chart); conversion tracked over time (use line-chart).

### Install

From npm (the component ships in the package):

```bash
npm install insightcharts echarts
```

Or copy the source into your project with the shadcn CLI, so you can edit it (the engine still comes from the `insightcharts` package):

```bash
npx shadcn@latest registry add @insightcharts=https://insightcharts.dev/r/{name}.json   # once per project
npx shadcn@latest add @insightcharts/funnel-chart
```

The file lands at `components/insightcharts/atoms/funnel-chart.tsx`. `@insightcharts/funnel-chart-demo` adds a ready-made example next to it.

### Usage

```tsx
import { FunnelChart } from "insightcharts";

const data = [
  { step: "Visited the pricing page", users: 48200 },
  { step: "Started a free trial", users: 9640 },
  { step: "Connected a data source", users: 5310 },
  { step: "Invited a teammate", users: 2230 },
  { step: "Became a paying customer", users: 1480 },
];

<FunnelChart
  data={data}
  stage="step"
  value="users"
  format="integer"
  title="20% of pricing-page visitors started a free trial"
  subtitle="Users reaching each step of the sign-up funnel, last 90 days"
  source="Product analytics"
  note="Illustrative data"
/>
```

### JSON spec

The same thing as data, rendered with `<Insight spec={spec} />`:

```json
{
  "type": "funnel-chart",
  "data": [
    { "step": "Visited the pricing page", "users": 48200 },
    { "step": "Started a free trial", "users": 9640 },
    { "step": "Connected a data source", "users": 5310 },
    { "step": "Invited a teammate", "users": 2230 },
    { "step": "Became a paying customer", "users": 1480 }
  ],
  "stage": "step",
  "value": "users",
  "format": "integer",
  "title": "20% of pricing-page visitors started a free trial",
  "subtitle": "Users reaching each step of the sign-up funnel, last 90 days",
  "source": "Product analytics",
  "note": "Illustrative data"
}
```

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `stage` (required) | `string` |  | Stage field. Rows are read in data order; the first row is the top of the funnel. |
| `value` (required) | `string` |  | Count field. |
| `dropoff` | `boolean` | `true` | State the drop-off between consecutive stages. |
| `dropoffLabel` | `string` | `"dropped off"` | Word for what is lost between stages. |

### Common props

Also accepts every prop in the "Common chart props" section of this file.

### Composition

- Composes: nothing (it is a primitive)
- Used by: no molecule or template yet

### More examples

## Glyph table (`glyph-table`)

> A table with one row per entity in which every number is drawn as a small form chosen per column (counted dots, squares or icons, a ring, a sized circle, a bar) with the value printed beside it.

- Component: `GlyphTable` (import from `insightcharts`)
- Spec type: `"glyph-table"`
- Level: atom. Category: poster.
- An HTML component: it takes only the props listed below, plus `theme`, `mode`, `className` and `style` where its source declares them. It does not take the common chart props.

### When to use

Comparing 3 to about 12 entities across 2 to 5 measures with different units, when the table should read as a graphic: profiles of products, cities, teams or species. Pair it with curve-rank by passing both the same `order`.

### Avoid

Looking up many exact values, sorting, or more than about 12 rows (use data-table); one measure across entities (use bar-chart or pictogram-chart); a trend over time (use line-chart or small-multiples).

### Install

From npm (the component ships in the package):

```bash
npm install insightcharts echarts
```

Or copy the source into your project with the shadcn CLI, so you can edit it (the engine still comes from the `insightcharts` package):

```bash
npx shadcn@latest registry add @insightcharts=https://insightcharts.dev/r/{name}.json   # once per project
npx shadcn@latest add @insightcharts/glyph-table
```

The file lands at `components/insightcharts/atoms/glyph-table.tsx`. `@insightcharts/glyph-table-demo` adds a ready-made example next to it.

### Usage

```tsx
import { GlyphTable } from "insightcharts";

<GlyphTable
  theme="noir"
  caption="Filter coffee sold 310 cups a day at £2.40 a cup"
  subtitle="Six drinks at one café: price, cups sold per day, share ordered with oat milk, seconds to prepare and caffeine"
  note="Illustrative figures."
  name="drink"
  nameLabel="Drink"
  columns={[
    {
      field: "price",
      label: "Price per cup",
      glyph: "bar",
      format: { style: "currency", currency: "GBP" },
      max: 5,
    },
    { field: "cups", label: "Cups sold a day", glyph: "dots", unit: 10 },
    { field: "oat", label: "With oat milk", glyph: "ring", format: "{value}%" },
    { field: "seconds", label: "Seconds to prepare", glyph: "blocks", unit: 10 },
    { field: "caffeine", label: "Caffeine, mg", glyph: "circle" },
  ]}
  rows={[
    { drink: "Filter coffee", price: 2.4, cups: 310, oat: 8, seconds: 15, caffeine: 140 },
    { drink: "Espresso", price: 2.6, cups: 145, oat: null, seconds: 30, caffeine: 65 },
    { drink: "Flat white", price: 3.6, cups: 260, oat: 34, seconds: 95, caffeine: 130 },
    { drink: "Iced latte", price: 4.2, cups: 180, oat: 41, seconds: 70, caffeine: 130 },
    { drink: "Matcha latte", price: 4.8, cups: 75, oat: 57, seconds: 110, caffeine: 70 },
    { drink: "Hot chocolate", price: 3.9, cups: 40, oat: 22, seconds: 85, caffeine: 10 },
  ]}
/>
```

```json
      "max": 5

  ]
```
