
### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rows` (required) | `Row[]` |  | One object per entity. |
| `name` | `string` |  | Field holding the entity name. Defaults to the first key of the first row. |
| `nameLabel` | `string` |  | Heading of the name column. |
| `columns` (required) | `{ field, label?, glyph?: "dots" \| "blocks" \| "ring" \| "circle" \| "bar" \| "icons" \| "text", unit?, format?, max?, icon? }[]` |  | Glyph columns in order. `dots`, `blocks` and `icons` draw one mark per `unit` (default 1, raised to a round number when the largest value would not fit, and stated in the heading). `ring` fills to `max` (default 100, or 1 for fractions). `circle` is sized by area and `bar` by length against `max` (default: the column's largest value). `text` prints the value alone. |
| `order` | `string[]` |  | Entity names in display order; also assigns colours. Pass the same list to curve-rank to match its curve colours. |
| `highlight` | `string \| string[]` |  | Entities drawn in colour; every other row turns grey. |
| `colorBy` | `"series" \| "none"` |  | `series`: one colour per entity; past the size of the theme's palette the extra colours are derived from the theme's own (curve-rank derives the same ones). `none`: every row in the accent. Default: series while the rows fit the palette (at most 8), none beyond. |
| `caption` | `string` |  | The table's title, as a real `<caption>`. |
| `subtitle` | `string` |  | Measures, units and period, under the caption. |
| `source` | `string` |  | Shown under the table as "Source: ...". |
| `note` | `string` |  | Method notes or caveats, shown under the table. |
| `select` | `boolean` |  | Let readers click a row (or press Enter on it) to select it; the other rows fade. |
| `onSelect` | `(values: string[]) => void` |  | Called with the selected entity names whenever the selection changes. |
| `selected` | `string[]` |  | Controlled selection: the entity names currently selected. When given, the table shows exactly this list and a click only calls `onSelect`. Omit it and the table keeps its own selection. |
| `frame` | `boolean` |  | Paint a named theme's background behind the block, with padding and rounded corners. On by default for a named theme with its own surface; `false` turns it off. |

### Composition

- Composes: nothing (it is a primitive)
- Used by: [matrix-poster](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/matrix-poster.md), [profile-poster](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/profile-poster.md)

## Headline (`headline`)

> The opening block of a piece or section: kicker, title, one-sentence deck and a byline/date line.

- Component: `Headline` (import from `insightcharts`)
- Spec type: `"headline"`
- Level: atom. Category: text.
- An HTML component: it takes only the props listed below, plus `theme`, `mode`, `className` and `style` where its source declares them. It does not take the common chart props.

### When to use

At the top of a data story (`page`), at the start of each chapter (`section`), or as the heading of a tile (`card`). Write the title as one plain fact with its number. Write the deck as a second plain sentence.

### Avoid

Titling a single chart: charts carry their own `title` and `subtitle`. For numbered chapters use `step-marker`.

### Install

From npm (the component ships in the package):

```bash
npm install insightcharts echarts
```

Or copy the source into your project with the shadcn CLI, so you can edit it (the engine still comes from the `insightcharts` package):

```bash
npx shadcn@latest registry add @insightcharts=https://insightcharts.dev/r/{name}.json   # once per project
npx shadcn@latest add @insightcharts/headline
```

The file lands at `components/insightcharts/atoms/headline.tsx`. `@insightcharts/headline-demo` adds a ready-made example next to it.

### Usage

```tsx
import { Headline } from "insightcharts";

<Headline
  theme="ledger"
  size="page"
  kicker="Energy transition"
  title="Solar generated more electricity than coal in Europe in 2024"
  deck="Solar was the continent's second-largest source of electricity that year."
  byline="By Ana Ruiz and Tom Okafor"
  date="2025-03-14"
/>
```

### JSON spec

The same thing as data, rendered with `<Insight spec={spec} />`:

```json
{
  "type": "headline",
  "theme": "ledger",
  "size": "page",
  "kicker": "Energy transition",
  "title": "Solar generated more electricity than coal in Europe in 2024",
  "deck": "Solar was the continent's second-largest source of electricity that year.",
  "byline": "By Ana Ruiz and Tom Okafor",
  "date": "2025-03-14"
}
```

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `title` (required) | `string` |  | One fact with its number, as a plain sentence. Wraps balanced. |
| `kicker` | `string` |  | Small label above the title: section, series or topic. Sentence case. |
| `deck` | `string` |  | One-sentence standfirst. |
| `byline` | `string` |  | Author line, shown as written, e.g. "By Ana Ruiz". |
| `date` | `string` |  | ISO dates are formatted for the locale and wrapped in `<time>`; other strings are shown as written. |
| `size` | `"page" \| "section" \| "card"` | `"section"` | Type scale. Titles step down automatically in narrow containers. |
| `level` | `1 \| 2 \| 3 \| 4 \| 5 \| 6` |  | Heading level. Defaults to 1 (page), 2 (section), 3 (card). |
| `align` | `"left" \| "center"` | `"left"` | Text alignment. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` |  | Extra content under the byline. |
| `frame` | `boolean` |  | Paint a named theme's background behind the block, with padding and rounded corners. On by default for a named theme with its own surface; `false` turns it off. |

### Composition

- Composes: nothing (it is a primitive)
- Used by: [hero-figure](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/hero-figure.md), [section](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/section.md), [comparison-brief](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/comparison-brief.md), [data-explorer](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/data-explorer.md), [executive-brief](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/executive-brief.md), [explainer](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/explainer.md), [report-page](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/report-page.md), [scorecard](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/scorecard.md), [timeline-story](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/timeline-story.md), [visual-essay](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/visual-essay.md)

### More examples

#### Section

```tsx
import { Headline } from "insightcharts";

<Headline
  size="section"
  kicker="Chapter 2"
  title="Germany and the Netherlands have more solar installations per person than Spain"
  deck="Solar installations per person, by country."
/>
```

#### Card

```tsx

<Headline
  theme="paper"
  size="card"
  title="Wholesale electricity prices by hour, summer 2024"
  deck="Median day-ahead price for each hour of the day."
  date="Updated June 2024"
/>
```

#### Centered page, long title

```tsx

  theme="dusk"
  size="page"
  align="center"
  title="Household energy bills in January 2025 were one third higher than before the price shock three years earlier"
  deck="Bills have fallen more slowly than forecast."
  byline="By the data desk"

/>
```

## Heatmap (`heatmap`)

> Colours a category-by-category (or time-by-category) grid by a numeric value, using a sequential or diverging scale.

- Component: `Heatmap` (import from `insightcharts`)
- Spec type: `"heatmap"`
- Level: atom. Category: comparison.
- An ECharts chart built with `defineChart`: accepts every common chart prop (data, transform, title, highlight, annotations, ...).

### When to use

Finding patterns across two dimensions at once: hour by weekday, cohort by month, product by region. Good when there are too many series for lines or bars and the overall pattern matters more than exact values.

### Avoid

Precise comparison of a few values (use bar-chart); a single series over time (use line-chart); a daily value across a year (use calendar-heatmap).

### Install

From npm (the component ships in the package):

```bash
npm install insightcharts echarts
```

Or copy the source into your project with the shadcn CLI, so you can edit it (the engine still comes from the `insightcharts` package):

```bash
npx shadcn@latest registry add @insightcharts=https://insightcharts.dev/r/{name}.json   # once per project
npx shadcn@latest add @insightcharts/heatmap
```

The file lands at `components/insightcharts/atoms/heatmap.tsx`. `@insightcharts/heatmap-demo` adds a ready-made example next to it.

### Usage


### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `x` (required) | `string` |  | Column field: a category or a date. |
| `y` (required) | `string` |  | Row field. |
| `value` (required) | `string` |  | Numeric field that colours each cell. One data row per cell. |
| `diverging` | `boolean` | `false` | Diverging palette centred on `midpoint`, for values with a meaningful middle. |
| `midpoint` | `number` | `0` | Centre of the diverging scale. |
| `labels` | `boolean` |  | Print the value in each cell. Default: on when cells are large enough. |
| `sort` | `"none" \| "asc" \| "desc"` | `"none"` | Order rows by their total. |
| `domain` | `[number, number]` |  | Fix the ends of the colour scale. |

### Common props

Also accepts every prop in the "Common chart props" section of this file.

### Composition

- Composes: nothing (it is a primitive)
- Used by: [executive-brief](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/executive-brief.md), [visual-essay](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/visual-essay.md)

### More examples

#### Missing cells (cohort triangle)

```tsx
import { Heatmap } from "insightcharts";

const data = [
  { cohort: "Jan cohort", month: "M0", retained: 1 },
  { cohort: "Jan cohort", month: "M1", retained: 0.64 },
```

## Histogram (`histogram`)

> Bins a numeric field and shows how many rows fall in each bin, as touching bars on a continuous axis.

- Component: `Histogram` (import from `insightcharts`)
- Spec type: `"histogram"`
- Level: atom. Category: distribution.
- An ECharts chart built with `defineChart`: accepts every common chart prop (data, transform, title, highlight, annotations, ...).

### When to use

Showing the shape of a distribution for one numeric variable with roughly 50 rows or more: its centre, spread, skew, gaps and multiple peaks.

### Avoid

Comparing distributions across several groups (use box-plot or beeswarm-chart); under about 50 rows, where every observation can be shown (use strip-plot or beeswarm-chart); counts by category (use bar-chart).

### Install

From npm (the component ships in the package):

```bash
npm install insightcharts echarts
```

Or copy the source into your project with the shadcn CLI, so you can edit it (the engine still comes from the `insightcharts` package):

```bash
npx shadcn@latest registry add @insightcharts=https://insightcharts.dev/r/{name}.json   # once per project
npx shadcn@latest add @insightcharts/histogram
```

The file lands at `components/insightcharts/atoms/histogram.tsx`. `@insightcharts/histogram-demo` adds a ready-made example next to it.

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `value` (required) | `string` |  | Numeric field to bin. |
| `bins` | `number` |  | Approximate number of bins; the width is rounded to a tidy step. Default: from the row count. |
| `step` | `number` |  | Exact bin width in value units. Overrides `bins`. |
| `median` | `boolean` | `false` | Vertical marker at the median. |
| `mean` | `boolean` | `false` | Vertical marker at the mean. |
| `normalize` | `boolean` | `false` | Share of rows per bin instead of a count. |
| `countLabel` | `string` |  | Title for the count axis, e.g. "Runners". |

### Common props

Also accepts every prop in the "Common chart props" section of this file.

### Composition

- Composes: nothing (it is a primitive)
- Used by: [report-page](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/report-page.md)

## Icon array grid (`icon-array-grid`)

> Compares many counts as a grid of labelled tiles, each holding an array of N icons with its name and number.

- Component: `IconArrayGrid` (import from `insightcharts`)
- Spec type: `"icon-array-grid"`
- Level: atom. Category: poster.
- An ECharts chart built with `defineChart`: accepts every common chart prop (data, transform, title, highlight, annotations, ...).

### When to use

Counts of up to about 150 in 4 to 24 categories, especially rates per 100 or per 1,000: cars per 100 households in 12 districts. Set `total` so every tile shows the same full array with the uncounted icons as ghosts.

### Avoid

Counts in the thousands (use unit-blocks); two to six categories where one row of icons each is enough (use pictogram-chart); values that need precise comparison or ranking (use block-bar or bar-chart); one share of one whole (use waffle-chart).

### Install

From npm (the component ships in the package):

```bash
npm install insightcharts echarts
```

Or copy the source into your project with the shadcn CLI, so you can edit it (the engine still comes from the `insightcharts` package):

```bash
npx shadcn@latest registry add @insightcharts=https://insightcharts.dev/r/{name}.json   # once per project
npx shadcn@latest add @insightcharts/icon-array-grid
```

The file lands at `components/insightcharts/atoms/icon-array-grid.tsx`. `@insightcharts/icon-array-grid-demo` adds a ready-made example next to it.

### Usage

```tsx
import { IconArrayGrid } from "insightcharts";

const data = [
  { district: "Ashby", cars: 118 },
  { district: "Brook End", cars: 104 },
  { district: "Castle Hill", cars: 97 },
  { district: "Dockside", cars: 41 },
  { district: "Eastfield", cars: 88 },
  { district: "Fairmile", cars: 126 },
  { district: "Greenway", cars: 73 },
  { district: "Hollins", cars: 110 },
  { district: "Old Town", cars: 36 },
  { district: "Priory", cars: 92 },
  { district: "Riverside", cars: 58 },
  { district: "Station Quarter", cars: 29 },
];

<IconArrayGrid
  theme="sunrise"
  data={data}
  name="district"
  value="cars"
  icon="car"
  unitLabel="1 car per 100 households"
  columns={4}
  title="Fairmile had 126 cars per 100 households in 2025"
  subtitle="Cars per 100 households in 12 districts of Port Aldwin, 2025"
  source="Illustrative data"
  note="Invented figures for a fictional city"
/>
```

### JSON spec

The same thing as data, rendered with `<Insight spec={spec} />`:

```json
{
  "type": "icon-array-grid",
  "theme": "sunrise",
  "data": [
    { "district": "Ashby", "cars": 118 },
    { "district": "Brook End", "cars": 104 },
    { "district": "Castle Hill", "cars": 97 },
    { "district": "Dockside", "cars": 41 },
    { "district": "Eastfield", "cars": 88 },
    { "district": "Fairmile", "cars": 126 },
    { "district": "Greenway", "cars": 73 },
    { "district": "Hollins", "cars": 110 },
    { "district": "Old Town", "cars": 36 },
    { "district": "Priory", "cars": 92 },
    { "district": "Riverside", "cars": 58 },
    { "district": "Station Quarter", "cars": 29 }
  ],
  "name": "district",
  "value": "cars",
  "icon": "car",
  "unitLabel": "1 car per 100 households",
  "columns": 4,
  "title": "Fairmile had 126 cars per 100 households in 2025",
  "subtitle": "Cars per 100 households in 12 districts of Port Aldwin, 2025",
  "source": "Illustrative data",
  "note": "Invented figures for a fictional city"
}
```

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` (required) | `string` |  | Category field: one tile per row. |
| `value` (required) | `string` |  | Value field: the count each tile shows. |
| `unit` | `number` | `1` | Units per icon. |
| `unitLabel` | `string` |  | What one icon stands for, for the key line, e.g. "1 car". |
| `total` | `number` |  | Draw every tile out of this many units, with uncounted icons as ghosts: 100 for a rate per 100. |
| `icon` | `IconName \| "path://..."` | `"circle"` | Built-in icon name or a custom single SVG path. |
| `perRow` | `number` | `10` | Icons per line inside a tile. |
| `columns` | `number` |  | Most tiles per line. Default: as many as fit at a readable size. Narrow containers use fewer. |
| `sort` | `"none" \| "asc" \| "desc"` | `"none"` | Order of the tiles. |

### Common props

Also accepts every prop in the "Common chart props" section of this file.

### Composition

- Composes: nothing (it is a primitive)
- Used by: no molecule or template yet

### More examples

## Icon stat (`icon-stat`)

> A "1 in 4"-style statement: a row or grid of simple glyphs with some filled, and the sentence they illustrate.

- Component: `IconStat` (import from `insightcharts`)
- Spec type: `"icon-stat"`
- Level: atom. Category: figure.
- An HTML component: it takes only the props listed below, plus `theme`, `mode`, `className` and `style` where its source declares them. It does not take the common chart props.

### When to use

A single proportion that is easier to read as people or units than as a percentage: 1 in 4, 3 in 10, 37 of 100. Round to a small denominator first.

### Avoid

Comparing several proportions (use `bar-chart`), precise percentages (use `big-number`), or fractions that need more than 100 units.

### Install

From npm (the component ships in the package):

```bash
npm install insightcharts echarts
```

Or copy the source into your project with the shadcn CLI, so you can edit it (the engine still comes from the `insightcharts` package):

```bash
npx shadcn@latest registry add @insightcharts=https://insightcharts.dev/r/{name}.json   # once per project
npx shadcn@latest add @insightcharts/icon-stat
```

The file lands at `components/insightcharts/atoms/icon-stat.tsx`. `@insightcharts/icon-stat-demo` adds a ready-made example next to it.

### Usage

```tsx
import { IconStat } from "insightcharts";

<IconStat
  icon="person"
  count={1}
  total={4}
  text="households could not cover an unexpected bill of €500 without borrowing."
/>
```

### JSON spec

The same thing as data, rendered with `<Insight spec={spec} />`:

```json
{
  "type": "icon-stat",
  "icon": "person",
  "count": 1,
  "total": 4,
  "text": "households could not cover an unexpected bill of €500 without borrowing."
}
```

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `count` (required) | `number` |  | How many glyphs are filled. |
| `total` | `number` | `10` | How many glyphs are drawn. Capped at 100. |
| `text` | `string` |  | The sentence completing the figure. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` |  | JSX alternative to `text`. |
| `value` | `string \| false` |  | The figure as words. Defaults to "{count} in {total}"; `false` hides it. |
| `icon` | `"circle" \| "person" \| "square" \| IconName` | `"circle"` | Glyph per unit. Filled units are solid, the rest outlined. Any other icon name from `core/icons.ts` also works; its unfilled units are faded instead of outlined. |
| `columns` | `number` |  | Glyphs per row. Defaults to `total`, at most 10. |
| `size` | `number` |  | Glyph height in px; shrinks to fit narrow containers. |
| `tone` | `"accent" \| "positive" \| "negative" \| "neutral"` | `"accent"` | Fill colour by meaning. |
| `align` | `"left" \| "center"` | `"left"` | Alignment. |
| `frame` | `boolean` |  | Paint a named theme's background behind the block, with padding and rounded corners. On by default for a named theme with its own surface; `false` turns it off. |

### Composition

- Composes: nothing (it is a primitive)
- Used by: [poster](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/poster.md), [proportion-statement](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/proportion-statement.md), [atlas-poster](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/atlas-poster.md), [explainer](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/explainer.md)

### More examples

#### Circles, 3 in 10

```tsx
import { IconStat } from "insightcharts";

<IconStat theme="forest" count={3} total={10} text="new cars sold in Europe in 2024 had a plug." />
```

## Legend key (`legend-key`)

> A standalone colour key: categorical swatches, or a sequential/diverging ramp with end labels.

- Component: `LegendKey` (import from `insightcharts`)
- Spec type: `"legend-key"`
- Level: atom. Category: figure.
- An HTML component: it takes only the props listed below, plus `theme`, `mode`, `className` and `style` where its source declares them. It does not take the common chart props.

### When to use

When several charts (small multiples, a map and a bar chart, a dashboard row) share one colour encoding, show the key once above them and turn their own legends off.

### Avoid

A single chart: its built-in legend or, better, direct labels already do this. Do not list more than eight categories.

### Install

From npm (the component ships in the package):

```bash
npm install insightcharts echarts
```

Or copy the source into your project with the shadcn CLI, so you can edit it (the engine still comes from the `insightcharts` package):

```bash
npx shadcn@latest registry add @insightcharts=https://insightcharts.dev/r/{name}.json   # once per project
npx shadcn@latest add @insightcharts/legend-key
```

The file lands at `components/insightcharts/atoms/legend-key.tsx`. `@insightcharts/legend-key-demo` adds a ready-made example next to it.

### Usage

```tsx
import { LegendKey } from "insightcharts";

<LegendKey
  theme="poster"
  title="Source of electricity"
  items={["Solar", "Wind", "Hydro", "Gas", { label: "Other", muted: true }]}
/>
```

### JSON spec

The same thing as data, rendered with `<Insight spec={spec} />`:

```json
{
  "type": "legend-key",
  "theme": "poster",
  "title": "Source of electricity",
  "items": ["Solar", "Wind", "Hydro", "Gas", { "label": "Other", "muted": true }]
}
```

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `scale` | `"categorical" \| "sequential" \| "diverging"` |  | Defaults to `categorical` when `items` is given, otherwise `sequential`. |
| `items` | `(string \| { label, color?, index?, shape?, muted? })[]` |  | Categorical entries. Colours come from the theme's categorical order by position (or `index`) unless given. |
| `labels` | `string[]` |  | Ramp end labels: `[low, high]` or `[low, middle, high]`. |
| `colors` | `string[]` |  | Ramp colours, low to high. Defaults to the theme's sequential or diverging ramp. |
| `stepped` | `boolean` | `false` | Discrete steps instead of a continuous gradient, for binned scales. |
| `title` | `string` |  | What the key encodes. |
| `shape` | `"square" \| "line" \| "dot"` | `"square"` | Default swatch shape: match the marks. |
| `orientation` | `"horizontal" \| "vertical"` | `"horizontal"` | Categorical layout. |
| `width` | `number` | `240` | Ramp width in px, capped at the container. |
| `align` | `"left" \| "center"` | `"left"` | Alignment within the container. |
| `frame` | `boolean` |  | Paint a named theme's background behind the block, with padding and rounded corners. On by default for a named theme with its own surface; `false` turns it off. |

### Composition

- Composes: nothing (it is a primitive)
- Used by: [small-multiple-grid](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/small-multiple-grid.md)

### More examples

#### Sequential ramp

```tsx
import { LegendKey } from "insightcharts";

<LegendKey
  scale="sequential"
  title="Share of electricity from renewables"
  labels={["0%", "100%"]}
/>
```

#### Diverging, stepped

```tsx
import { LegendKey } from "insightcharts";

<LegendKey
  theme="editorial"
  scale="diverging"
  stepped
  title="Change in house prices, 2019 to 2024"
  labels={["−20%", "No change", "+20%"]}
  width={300}
/>
```

#### Lines, vertical, explicit order

```tsx
import { LegendKey } from "insightcharts";

<LegendKey
  theme="ocean"
  orientation="vertical"
  shape="line"
  items={[
    { label: "Germany", index: 0 },
    { label: "Spain", index: 3 },
    { label: "EU average", muted: true },
  ]}
/>
```

## Line chart (`line-chart`)

> Shows how one or more values change over time or another ordered dimension.

- Component: `LineChart` (import from `insightcharts`)
- Spec type: `"line-chart"`
- Level: atom. Category: trend.
- An ECharts chart built with `defineChart`: accepts every common chart prop (data, transform, title, highlight, annotations, ...).

### When to use

Trends over time with roughly 5 or more points; comparing the trajectories of a few series; one highlighted series against many context series.

### Avoid

Unordered categories (use bar-chart); only two time points (use slope-chart); more than about 6 equally important lines (use small-multiples).

### Install

From npm (the component ships in the package):

```bash
npm install insightcharts echarts
```

Or copy the source into your project with the shadcn CLI, so you can edit it (the engine still comes from the `insightcharts` package):

```bash
npx shadcn@latest registry add @insightcharts=https://insightcharts.dev/r/{name}.json   # once per project
npx shadcn@latest add @insightcharts/line-chart
```

The file lands at `components/insightcharts/atoms/line-chart.tsx`. `@insightcharts/line-chart-demo` adds a ready-made example next to it.

### Usage

```tsx
import { LineChart } from "insightcharts";

const data = [
  { year: "2019", solar: 2.7, wind: 5.3 },
  { year: "2020", solar: 3.2, wind: 5.9 },
  { year: "2021", solar: 3.7, wind: 6.5 },
  { year: "2022", solar: 4.6, wind: 7.3 },
  { year: "2023", solar: 5.5, wind: 7.8 },
];

<LineChart
  data={data}
  x="year"
  y={["solar", "wind"]}
  format="{value}%"
  title="Solar's share rose from 2.7% to 5.5% between 2019 and 2023"
/>
```

### JSON spec

The same thing as data, rendered with `<Insight spec={spec} />`:

```json
{
  "type": "line-chart",
  "data": [
    { "year": "2019", "solar": 2.7, "wind": 5.3 },
    { "year": "2020", "solar": 3.2, "wind": 5.9 },
    { "year": "2021", "solar": 3.7, "wind": 6.5 },
    { "year": "2022", "solar": 4.6, "wind": 7.3 },
    { "year": "2023", "solar": 5.5, "wind": 7.8 }
  ],
  "x": "year",
  "y": ["solar", "wind"],
  "format": "{value}%",
  "title": "Solar's share rose from 2.7% to 5.5% between 2019 and 2023"
}
```

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `x` (required) | `string` |  | Time or ordered category field. ISO dates are placed on a true time axis. |
| `y` (required) | `string \| string[]` |  | Value field, or several (one line each). |
| `series` | `string` |  | Field that splits rows into lines (long data). |
| `curve` | `"linear" \| "smooth" \| "step"` | `"linear"` | Line shape. |
| `area` | `boolean` | `false` | Light fill under the line; forces a zero baseline. |
| `endLabels` | `boolean` |  | Name each line at its end. Default: on for up to 6 lines. |
| `points` | `boolean` |  | Marker on every point. Default: on for 12 points or fewer. |
| `zero` | `boolean` | `false` | Start the value axis at zero. |
| `log` | `boolean` | `false` | Logarithmic value axis. |
| `names` | `Record<string, string>` |  | Display names for series keys. |
| `contextLabels` | `boolean \| string` | `false` | With `highlight`: name the grey context lines. `true` adds a muted end label to each when they all fit; a string such as `"Other cities"` adds one muted legend entry instead. On narrow charts the legend already lists every line. |

### Common props

Also accepts every prop in the "Common chart props" section of this file.

### Composition

- Composes: nothing (it is a primitive)
- Used by: [chart-callout](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/chart-callout.md), [chart-tabs](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/chart-tabs.md), [hero-figure](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/hero-figure.md), [linked-charts](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/linked-charts.md), [scrolly-chart](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/scrolly-chart.md), [section](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/section.md), [comparison-brief](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/comparison-brief.md), [executive-brief](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/executive-brief.md), [explainer](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/explainer.md), [report-page](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/report-page.md), [scorecard](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/scorecard.md), [story-deck](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/story-deck.md), [timeline-story](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/timeline-story.md), [visual-essay](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/visual-essay.md)

### More examples

## Lollipop chart (`lollipop-chart`)

> Ranks categories with a dot on a thin stem from zero, or as a stemless dot plot on a free scale.

- Component: `LollipopChart` (import from `insightcharts`)
- Spec type: `"lollipop-chart"`
- Level: atom. Category: comparison.
- An ECharts chart built with `defineChart`: accepts every common chart prop (data, transform, title, highlight, annotations, ...).

### When to use

Rankings of 8 to 30 categories where bars would be too heavy; dot plot mode when the values sit far from zero and the differences between them matter, or to compare a few series per row.

### Avoid

Fewer than about 6 categories or part-to-whole stacks (use bar-chart); exactly two values per row where the difference between them matters (use dumbbell-chart); change over time (use line-chart).

### Install

From npm (the component ships in the package):

```bash
npm install insightcharts echarts
```

Or copy the source into your project with the shadcn CLI, so you can edit it (the engine still comes from the `insightcharts` package):

```bash
npx shadcn@latest registry add @insightcharts=https://insightcharts.dev/r/{name}.json   # once per project
npx shadcn@latest add @insightcharts/lollipop-chart
```

The file lands at `components/insightcharts/atoms/lollipop-chart.tsx`. `@insightcharts/lollipop-chart-demo` adds a ready-made example next to it.

### Usage

```tsx
import { LollipopChart } from "insightcharts";

const data = [
  { country: "Netherlands", share: 27 },
  { country: "Denmark", share: 19 },
  { country: "Germany", share: 10 },
  { country: "Sweden", share: 9 },
  { country: "Japan", share: 8 },
  { country: "France", share: 4 },
  { country: "United Kingdom", share: 2 },
  { country: "United States", share: 1 },
];

<LollipopChart
  theme="mono"
  data={data}
  x="country"
  y="share"
  format="{value}%"
  height={300}
  title="27% of trips in the Netherlands are made by bike"
  subtitle="Share of all trips made by bicycle"
  source="National travel surveys, latest available year (rounded)"
  note="Figures are approximate, for illustration"
/>
```

### JSON spec

The same thing as data, rendered with `<Insight spec={spec} />`:

```json
{
  "type": "lollipop-chart",
  "theme": "mono",
  "data": [
    { "country": "Netherlands", "share": 27 },
    { "country": "Denmark", "share": 19 },
    { "country": "Germany", "share": 10 },
    { "country": "Sweden", "share": 9 },
    { "country": "Japan", "share": 8 },
    { "country": "France", "share": 4 },
    { "country": "United Kingdom", "share": 2 },
    { "country": "United States", "share": 1 }
  ],
  "x": "country",
  "y": "share",
  "format": "{value}%",
  "height": 300,
  "title": "27% of trips in the Netherlands are made by bike",
  "subtitle": "Share of all trips made by bicycle",
  "source": "National travel surveys, latest available year (rounded)",
  "note": "Figures are approximate, for illustration"
}
```

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `x` (required) | `string` |  | Category field. |
| `y` (required) | `string \| string[]` |  | Value field. Several fields draw several dots per row (dot plot). |
| `series` | `string` |  | Field that splits rows into series (long data). Forces the dot plot. |
| `stem` | `boolean` | `true` | Stem from zero. `false` draws a dot plot whose scale need not start at zero. |
| `orientation` | `"auto" \| "horizontal" \| "vertical"` | `"auto"` | Horizontal for rankings, vertical for dates. |
| `sort` | `"none" \| "asc" \| "desc"` |  | Row order. Default: descending for rankings, data order for dates. |
| `labels` | `boolean` |  | Value beside each dot. Default: on for one series of up to 16 rows. |
| `names` | `Record<string, string>` |  | Display names for series keys. |

### Common props

Also accepts every prop in the "Common chart props" section of this file.

### Composition

- Composes: nothing (it is a primitive)
- Used by: [data-explorer](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/data-explorer.md), [explainer](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/explainer.md)

```tsx
  data={data}

  y="years"
  stem={false}
```

## Nested shares (`nested-shares`)

> Shows several shares of the same whole, such as one share at five dates, as outlines nested from one corner of a square, each enclosing an area equal to its share.

- Component: `NestedShares` (import from `insightcharts`)
- Spec type: `"nested-shares"`
- Level: atom. Category: poster.
- An ECharts chart built with `defineChart`: accepts every common chart prop (data, transform, title, highlight, annotations, ...).

### When to use

How much of one whole something was at 2 to 8 dates or in 2 to 8 categories, when the growth of a share is the point: bicycles made 4% of trips in 2005 and 27% in 2025.

### Avoid

Shares that are parts of each other and should add up (use waffle-chart or treemap); more than 8 items or precise reading of a trend (use line-chart); shares within a point or two of each other, where outlines coincide (use block-bar).

### Install

From npm (the component ships in the package):

```bash
npm install insightcharts echarts
```

Or copy the source into your project with the shadcn CLI, so you can edit it (the engine still comes from the `insightcharts` package):

```bash
npx shadcn@latest registry add @insightcharts=https://insightcharts.dev/r/{name}.json   # once per project
npx shadcn@latest add @insightcharts/nested-shares
```

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` (required) | `string` |  | Field naming each share: a period ("2025") or a category. |
| `value` (required) | `string` |  | Value field: each row's share of the whole. |
| `total` | `number` |  | The whole. Default: 1 when every value is at most 1, otherwise 100. |
| `wholeLabel` | `string` |  | What the outer square stands for, printed under it, e.g. "All trips". |
| `corner` | `"bottom-left" \| "top-left"` | `"bottom-left"` | The corner every outline grows from. |

### Common props

## Orbit chart (`orbit-chart`)

> Places items as dots on concentric rings round a centre, one ring per category, level or period, with a key that explains rings, angle and dot area.

- Component: `OrbitChart` (import from `insightcharts`)
- Spec type: `"orbit-chart"`
- Level: atom. Category: poster.
- An ECharts chart built with `defineChart`: accepts every common chart prop (data, transform, title, highlight, annotations, ...).

### When to use

A designed alternative to a table for 6 to about 40 named things grouped by distance, level or era from one centre: suppliers by tier, moons by planet-distance band, releases by decade, stakeholders by closeness. One item can be highlighted.

### Avoid

A numeric distance that must be read exactly (use strip-plot or scatter-chart); comparison of the dot values (use bar-chart); more than about 6 rings or 40 items (use data-table); hierarchy with sizes that add up (use treemap or circle-pack).

### Install

From npm (the component ships in the package):

```bash
npm install insightcharts echarts
```

Or copy the source into your project with the shadcn CLI, so you can edit it (the engine still comes from the `insightcharts` package):

```bash
npx shadcn@latest registry add @insightcharts=https://insightcharts.dev/r/{name}.json   # once per project
npx shadcn@latest add @insightcharts/orbit-chart
```

The file lands at `components/insightcharts/atoms/orbit-chart.tsx`. `@insightcharts/orbit-chart-demo` adds a ready-made example next to it.

### Usage

```tsx
import { OrbitChart } from "insightcharts";

const data = [
  { supplier: "Halden Cells", tier: "Tier 1", spend: 84 },
  { supplier: "Orrin Motors", tier: "Tier 1", spend: 61 },
  { supplier: "Vale Castings", tier: "Tier 1", spend: 37 },
  { supplier: "Kestrel Wiring", tier: "Tier 2", spend: 22 },
  { supplier: "Brask Cathodes", tier: "Tier 2", spend: 48 },
  { supplier: "Lumen Glass", tier: "Tier 2", spend: 15 },
  { supplier: "Pell Magnets", tier: "Tier 2", spend: 29 },
  { supplier: "Tarn Lithium", tier: "Tier 3", spend: 33 },
  { supplier: "Iver Copper", tier: "Tier 3", spend: 19 },
  { supplier: "Sorrel Graphite", tier: "Tier 3", spend: 12 },
  { supplier: "Moss Resins", tier: "Tier 3", spend: 6 },
  { supplier: "Dunmore Nickel", tier: "Tier 3", spend: 26 },
];

<OrbitChart
  theme="noir"
  data={data}
  name="supplier"
  ring="tier"
  value="spend"
  format="${value}m"
  centerLabel="Car plant"
  highlight="Brask Cathodes"
  ringLabel="Tier 1 sells to the plant, each further ring sells to the ring inside it"
  sizeLabel="annual spend"
  title="Brask Cathodes is a tier 2 supplier with $48 million of annual spend"
  subtitle="12 suppliers to one car plant by supply-chain tier, annual spend in $ million"
  note="Illustrative figures for invented companies"
/>
```

```json
  "sizeLabel": "annual spend",
  "title": "Brask Cathodes is a tier 2 supplier with $48 million of annual spend",
  "subtitle": "12 suppliers to one car plant by supply-chain tier, annual spend in $ million",
  "note": "Illustrative figures for invented companies"
}
```

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` (required) | `string` |  | Name field: one dot per row. |
| `ring` (required) | `string` |  | Field naming the ring each dot sits on: a category, level or period. |
| `rings` | `string[]` |  | Ring order from the centre outward. Default: first appearance in the data. |
| `value` | `string` |  | Value field: dot area. Without it every dot is the same size. |
| `angle` | `string` |  | Numeric field that sets the angle round the ring. Without it dots are spaced evenly. |
| `angleDomain` | `[number, number]` | `[0, 360]` | Values of `angle` that map to a full turn, clockwise from 12 o'clock. |
| `ringLabel` | `string` |  | What the rings mean, for the key. Default: the `ring` field name. |
| `angleLabel` | `string` |  | What the angle means, for the key, e.g. "Clockwise from the top: month of launch". |
| `sizeLabel` | `string` |  | What dot area means, for the key. Default: the `value` field name. |
| `icon` | `string` |  | Icon in the centre disc: a built-in name or `path://`. |
| `centerLabel` | `string` |  | Short text in the centre disc, used when there is no `icon`. |
| `colorBy` | `"ring" \| "single"` | `"ring"` | A colour per ring, or the accent for every dot. |
| `showKey` | `boolean` | `true` | Show the key that explains rings, angle and dot area. |

### Common props

Also accepts every prop in the "Common chart props" section of this file.

### Composition

- Composes: nothing (it is a primitive)
- Used by: [radial-poster](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/radial-poster.md)

## Pictogram chart (`pictogram-chart`)

> Compares quantities with rows of repeated icons, each icon standing for a fixed number of units.

- Component: `PictogramChart` (import from `insightcharts`)
- Spec type: `"pictogram-chart"`
- Level: atom. Category: comparison.
- An ECharts chart built with `defineChart`: accepts every common chart prop (data, transform, title, highlight, annotations, ...).

### When to use

A few categories (2 to 6) of countable things, people, homes, vehicles, where making the quantity concrete matters more than reading precise values.

### Avoid

More than about 8 categories or values that need precise comparison (use bar-chart); a share of one whole (use waffle-chart); values that would need more than about 60 icons in a row (raise `unit`, or use bar-chart).

### Install

From npm (the component ships in the package):

```bash
npm install insightcharts echarts
```

Or copy the source into your project with the shadcn CLI, so you can edit it (the engine still comes from the `insightcharts` package):

```bash
npx shadcn@latest registry add @insightcharts=https://insightcharts.dev/r/{name}.json   # once per project
npx shadcn@latest add @insightcharts/pictogram-chart
```

The file lands at `components/insightcharts/atoms/pictogram-chart.tsx`. `@insightcharts/pictogram-chart-demo` adds a ready-made example next to it.

### Usage

```tsx
import { PictogramChart } from "insightcharts";

const data = [
  { city: "Tokyo", people: 37.1 },
  { city: "Delhi", people: 33.8 },
  { city: "Shanghai", people: 29.9 },
  { city: "São Paulo", people: 22.8 },
  { city: "Mexico City", people: 22.5 },
];

<PictogramChart
  theme="magenta"
  data={data}
  name="city"
  value="people"
  unit={2}
  unitLabel="2 million people"
  format="{value}m"
  highlight="Delhi"
  title="Delhi had 33.8 million people in 2024, 3.3 million fewer than Tokyo"
  subtitle="Population of the five largest urban agglomerations, 2024"
  source="UN World Urbanization Prospects"
  note="Figures are approximate, for illustration"
/>
```

### JSON spec

The same thing as data, rendered with `<Insight spec={spec} />`:

```json
{
  "type": "pictogram-chart",
  "theme": "magenta",
  "data": [
    { "city": "Tokyo", "people": 37.1 },
    { "city": "Delhi", "people": 33.8 },
    { "city": "Shanghai", "people": 29.9 },
    { "city": "São Paulo", "people": 22.8 },
    { "city": "Mexico City", "people": 22.5 }
  ],
  "name": "city",
  "value": "people",
  "unit": 2,
  "unitLabel": "2 million people",
  "format": "{value}m",
  "highlight": "Delhi",
  "title": "Delhi had 33.8 million people in 2024, 3.3 million fewer than Tokyo",
  "subtitle": "Population of the five largest urban agglomerations, 2024",
  "source": "UN World Urbanization Prospects",
  "note": "Figures are approximate, for illustration"
}
```

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` (required) | `string` |  | Category field: one row of icons per category. |
| `value` (required) | `string` |  | Value field. |
| `unit` | `number` |  | Units per icon. Default: a round number giving the largest row about ten icons. |
| `unitLabel` | `string` |  | What one icon stands for, for the key line, e.g. "1 million people". |
| `icon` | `IconName \| "path://..."` | `"person"` | Built-in icon name from `core/icons.ts` ("person", "house", "car", "tree", "coin", "drop", "bolt", "wind-turbine", "wheat" and about 60 more) or a custom single SVG path. |
| `icons` | `Record<string, string>` |  | Icon per category key; falls back to `icon`. |
| `perRow` | `number` |  | Wrap rows after this many icons. Default: as many as fit. |
| `labels` | `boolean` | `true` | Print the value after each row. |
| `sort` | `"none" \| "asc" \| "desc"` | `"none"` | Row order. |

### Common props

Also accepts every prop in the "Common chart props" section of this file.

### Composition

- Composes: nothing (it is a primitive)
- Used by: [poster](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/poster.md), [explainer](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/explainer.md)

## Pill rank (`pill-rank`)

> Shows a ranked list as horizontally centred rounded bars, with each name in capitals on its pill, the value at the left edge and the rank at the right.

- Component: `PillRank` (import from `insightcharts`)
- Spec type: `"pill-rank"`
- Level: atom. Category: poster.
- An ECharts chart built with `defineChart`: accepts every common chart prop (data, transform, title, highlight, annotations, ...).

### When to use

A poster ranking of 4 to about 20 named things where the order and the overall silhouette matter more than fine differences: top cities, largest employers, league tables, with one row highlighted and optional reference rows set apart below.

### Avoid

Precise comparison of values (use bar-chart, where bars share a baseline); negative values (use diverging-bar-chart); change in rank over time (use bump-chart); more than about 25 rows (use data-table).

### Install

From npm (the component ships in the package):

```bash
npm install insightcharts echarts
```

Or copy the source into your project with the shadcn CLI, so you can edit it (the engine still comes from the `insightcharts` package):

```bash
npx shadcn@latest registry add @insightcharts=https://insightcharts.dev/r/{name}.json   # once per project
npx shadcn@latest add @insightcharts/pill-rank
```

The file lands at `components/insightcharts/atoms/pill-rank.tsx`. `@insightcharts/pill-rank-demo` adds a ready-made example next to it.

### Usage

```tsx
import { PillRank } from "insightcharts";

const data = [
  { river: "Nile", km: 6650 },
  { river: "Amazon", km: 6400 },
  { river: "Yangtze", km: 6300 },
  { river: "Mississippi-Missouri", km: 6275 },
  { river: "Yenisei", km: 5539 },
  { river: "Yellow River", km: 5464 },
  { river: "Ob-Irtysh", km: 5410 },
  { river: "Congo", km: 4700 },
  { river: "Danube", km: 2850 },
  { river: "Rhine", km: 1230 },
];

<PillRank
  theme="paper"
  data={data}
  name="river"
  value="km"
  format="{value} km"
  highlight="Congo"
  compare={["Danube", "Rhine"]}
  compareLabel="Europe, for comparison"
  title="The Congo is 4,700 km long"
  subtitle="Length of eight major river systems and two European rivers, kilometres"
  source="Encyclopaedia Britannica"
  note="Lengths of river systems are approximate and vary by source"
/>
```

### JSON spec

The same thing as data, rendered with `<Insight spec={spec} />`:

```json
{
  "type": "pill-rank",
  "theme": "paper",
  "data": [
    { "river": "Nile", "km": 6650 },
    { "river": "Amazon", "km": 6400 },
    { "river": "Yangtze", "km": 6300 },
    { "river": "Mississippi-Missouri", "km": 6275 },
    { "river": "Yenisei", "km": 5539 },
    { "river": "Yellow River", "km": 5464 },
    { "river": "Ob-Irtysh", "km": 5410 },
    { "river": "Congo", "km": 4700 },
    { "river": "Danube", "km": 2850 },
    { "river": "Rhine", "km": 1230 }
  ],
  "name": "river",
  "value": "km",
  "format": "{value} km",
  "highlight": "Congo",
  "compare": ["Danube", "Rhine"],
  "compareLabel": "Europe, for comparison",
  "title": "The Congo is 4,700 km long",
  "subtitle": "Length of eight major river systems and two European rivers, kilometres",
  "source": "Encyclopaedia Britannica",
  "note": "Lengths of river systems are approximate and vary by source"
}
```

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` (required) | `string` |  | Name field: one row per data row. |
| `value` (required) | `string` |  | Value field: pill width. Non-positive values are dropped. |
| `sort` | `boolean` | `true` | Sort rows largest first. Set false to keep the data order. |
| `compare` | `string[]` |  | Names of rows that are not ranked: drawn below a dotted rule, without a rank number. |
| `compareLabel` | `string` |  | Short heading over the comparison rows, e.g. "For comparison". |
| `max` | `number` |  | Value that fills the full pill width. Default: the largest value. |
| `ranks` | `boolean` | `true` | Show the rank number at the right edge. |

### Common props

Also accepts every prop in the "Common chart props" section of this file.

### Composition

- Composes: nothing (it is a primitive)
- Used by: [atlas-poster](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/atlas-poster.md), [network-poster](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/network-poster.md), [radial-poster](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/radial-poster.md), [ranking-poster](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/ranking-poster.md)

### More examples

## Progress meter (`progress-meter`)

> A labelled horizontal meter of one value against a maximum or target, with the target marked and the value printed.

- Component: `ProgressMeter` (import from `insightcharts`)
- Spec type: `"progress-meter"`
- Level: atom. Category: figure.
- An HTML component: it takes only the props listed below, plus `theme`, `mode`, `className` and `style` where its source declares them. It does not take the common chart props.

### When to use

Progress toward a goal, a quota or a capacity: funds raised, budget spent, share of a target reached. Stack several with `size: "sm"` to compare progress across a few items.

### Avoid

Comparing more than a handful of items (use `bar-chart`), anything without a meaningful end point (use `big-number`), or a gauge dial.

### Install

From npm (the component ships in the package):

```bash
npm install insightcharts echarts
```

Or copy the source into your project with the shadcn CLI, so you can edit it (the engine still comes from the `insightcharts` package):

```bash
npx shadcn@latest registry add @insightcharts=https://insightcharts.dev/r/{name}.json   # once per project
npx shadcn@latest add @insightcharts/progress-meter
```

The file lands at `components/insightcharts/atoms/progress-meter.tsx`. `@insightcharts/progress-meter-demo` adds a ready-made example next to it.

### Usage

```tsx
import { ProgressMeter } from "insightcharts";

<ProgressMeter
  label="Homes with a heat pump or district heating"
  value={0.46}
  max={1}
  showMax={false}
  target={0.7}
  targetLabel="2030 target"
  context="Up from 31% in 2020. At the current rate the target is reached in 2033."
/>
```

### JSON spec

The same thing as data, rendered with `<Insight spec={spec} />`:

```json
{
  "type": "progress-meter",
  "label": "Homes with a heat pump or district heating",
  "value": 0.46,
  "max": 1,
  "showMax": false,
  "target": 0.7,
  "targetLabel": "2030 target",
  "context": "Up from 31% in 2020. At the current rate the target is reached in 2033."
}
```

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `value` (required) | `number` |  | The current value. |
| `label` (required) | `string` |  | What is measured, sentence case. |
| `max` | `number` |  | End of the track. Defaults to the target, or 1 with no target. |
| `min` | `number` | `0` | Start of the track. |
| `target` | `number` |  | A goal or threshold, drawn as a tick and labelled. |
| `targetLabel` | `string` | `"Target"` | Name for the target tick. |
| `showMax` | `boolean` |  | Print "of {max}" after the value. Default: only when `max` is given. |
| `context` | `string` |  | A line under the meter that gives the number meaning. |
| `format` | `FormatSpec` |  | Number format. Defaults to `"percent"` when the track ends at 1 or less, otherwise `"auto"`. |
| `tone` | `"accent" \| "positive" \| "negative" \| "neutral" \| number` | `"accent"` | Fill colour by meaning. A number picks from the theme's categorical palette, 0-based, for a stack of meters that name different entities. |
| `size` | `"sm" \| "md" \| "lg"` | `"md"` | Track of 6, 8 or 12px. `sm` for dense stacks, `lg` for a single featured meter. |
| `detail` | `string` |  | A short muted note after the value, e.g. a share of the total ("26%"). |
| `theme` | `ThemeInput` |  | A theme name such as `"science"`, or token overrides. A named theme paints its own ground. |
| `frame` | `boolean` |  | Set false to stop a named theme painting its ground. |

### Composition

- Composes: nothing (it is a primitive)
- Used by: [metric-breakdown](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/metric-breakdown.md), [quote-figure](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/quote-figure.md), [report-page](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/report-page.md)

### More examples

#### Against a maximum

```tsx
/>
```

## Proportional area (`proportional-area`)

> Compares two to eight values as squares or circles whose areas are proportional to the values, each printed with its name and number.

- Component: `ProportionalArea` (import from `insightcharts`)
- Spec type: `"proportional-area"`
- Level: atom. Category: poster.
- An ECharts chart built with `defineChart`: accepts every common chart prop (data, transform, title, highlight, annotations, ...).

### When to use

A few quantities that differ a lot (2 times to 100 times), where the reader should feel the difference in size: lake areas, budgets, market sizes. Nest them to show one quantity inside another.

### Avoid

Values within about 30% of each other, where areas look the same (use block-bar or bar-chart); more than 8 values (use treemap or bar-chart); parts of one whole (use treemap or waffle-chart); negative values.

### Install

From npm (the component ships in the package):

```bash
npm install insightcharts echarts
```

Or copy the source into your project with the shadcn CLI, so you can edit it (the engine still comes from the `insightcharts` package):

```bash
npx shadcn@latest registry add @insightcharts=https://insightcharts.dev/r/{name}.json   # once per project
npx shadcn@latest add @insightcharts/proportional-area
```

The file lands at `components/insightcharts/atoms/proportional-area.tsx`. `@insightcharts/proportional-area-demo` adds a ready-made example next to it.

### Usage

```tsx
import { ProportionalArea } from "insightcharts";

const data = [
  { lake: "Superior", area: 82100 },
  { lake: "Victoria", area: 68900 },
  { lake: "Tanganyika", area: 32900 },
  { lake: "Erie", area: 25700 },
  { lake: "Titicaca", area: 8370 },
];

<ProportionalArea
  theme="blueprint"
  data={data}
  name="lake"
  value="area"
  format="integer"
  ratio
  title="Lake Superior covers 82,100 km², 9.8 times Lake Titicaca"
  subtitle="Surface area of five lakes, square kilometres"
  source="Approximate published figures"
  note="Rounded, for illustration"
/>
```

### JSON spec

The same thing as data, rendered with `<Insight spec={spec} />`:

```json
{
  "type": "proportional-area",
  "theme": "blueprint",
  "data": [
    { "lake": "Superior", "area": 82100 },
    { "lake": "Victoria", "area": 68900 },
    { "lake": "Tanganyika", "area": 32900 },
    { "lake": "Erie", "area": 25700 },
    { "lake": "Titicaca", "area": 8370 }
  ],
  "name": "lake",
  "value": "area",
  "format": "integer",
  "ratio": true,
  "title": "Lake Superior covers 82,100 km², 9.8 times Lake Titicaca",
  "subtitle": "Surface area of five lakes, square kilometres",
  "source": "Approximate published figures",
  "note": "Rounded, for illustration"
}
```

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` (required) | `string` |  | Category field: one shape per row. |
| `value` (required) | `string` |  | Value field. Each shape's area is proportional to it. |
| `shape` | `"square" \| "circle"` | `"square"` | Squares or circles. |
| `layout` | `"row" \| "nested" \| "packed"` | `"row"` | `row`: side by side on a common baseline. `nested`: inside one another from a shared corner (squares) or lowest point (circles). `packed`: clustered together. |
| `ratio` | `boolean \| string` |  | Print how many times the largest value is the smallest. `true` for "{largest} is {ratio} times {smallest}", or a template with those placeholders. |
| `sort` | `"none" \| "asc" \| "desc"` | `"none"` | Order of the shapes in the row layout. Nested and packed always draw largest first. |

### Common props

Also accepts every prop in the "Common chart props" section of this file.

### Composition

- Composes: nothing (it is a primitive)
- Used by: [atlas-poster](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/atlas-poster.md), [count-poster](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/count-poster.md)

### More examples

#### Nested squares, highlight, click to select

```tsx

  { market: "All groceries", sales: 412 },
  { market: "Fresh produce", sales: 96 },
  { market: "Organic produce", sales: 21 },
  { market: "Organic berries", sales: 3.4 },
];

<ProportionalArea
  data={data}
  name="market"
  value="sales"
  layout="nested"
  format="£{value}m"
  highlight="Organic produce"
  select
  ratio="{largest} is {ratio} times {smallest}"
  title="Organic produce took £21m of £412m grocery sales in 2025"
  subtitle="Annual sales of one regional grocer by category, £ million, 2025"
  source="Illustrative data"
  note="Invented figures"
/>
```

#### Circles in a row

```tsx
  { reactor: "Test unit", output: 40 },

  subtitle="Generating capacity of four power stations, megawatts"
```

## Prose (`prose`)

> A readable block of narration at a 45-75 character measure, for the text between charts.

- Component: `Prose` (import from `insightcharts`)
- Spec type: `"prose"`
- Level: atom. Category: text.
- An HTML component: it takes only the props listed below, plus `theme`, `mode`, `className` and `style` where its source declares them. It does not take the common chart props.

### When to use

To say what a chart showed and introduce the next one. Use two or three short paragraphs at a time.

### Avoid

A single statement of fact (use `callout`), a quotation (use `pull-quote`), or sourcing and method notes (use `source-note`).

### Install

From npm (the component ships in the package):

```bash
npm install insightcharts echarts
```

Or copy the source into your project with the shadcn CLI, so you can edit it (the engine still comes from the `insightcharts` package):

```bash
npx shadcn@latest registry add @insightcharts=https://insightcharts.dev/r/{name}.json   # once per project
npx shadcn@latest add @insightcharts/prose
```

The file lands at `components/insightcharts/atoms/prose.tsx`. `@insightcharts/prose-demo` adds a ready-made example next to it.

### Usage

```tsx
import { Prose } from "insightcharts";

<Prose
  text={"In 2015 solar supplied **3% of Europe's electricity**. Hydro supplied more than three times as much.\n\nPanel prices fell by about 80% in the years that followed. In 2024 solar generated more electricity than coal across the EU, according to [Ember's annual review](https://ember-energy.org).\n\nSolar's share differs by country. The next chart shows it for each EU member state."}
/>
```

### JSON spec

The same thing as data, rendered with `<Insight spec={spec} />`:

```json
{
  "type": "prose",
  "text": "In 2015 solar supplied **3% of Europe's electricity**. Hydro supplied more than three times as much.\n\nPanel prices fell by about 80% in the years that followed. In 2024 solar generated more electricity than coal across the EU, according to [Ember's annual review](https://ember-energy.org).\n\nSolar's share differs by country. The next chart shows it for each EU member state."
}
```

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `text` | `string \| string[]` |  | Narration. Blank lines separate paragraphs. Supports `**bold**`, `*italic*` and `[link](url)`. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` |  | JSX alternative to `text`. |
| `size` | `"sm" \| "md" \| "lg"` | `"md"` | Body size: 14, 16 or 18px. |
| `measure` | `number` | `65` | Line length in characters, clamped to 45-75. |
| `lead` | `boolean` | `false` | Set the first paragraph a step larger. |
| `tone` | `"default" \| "muted"` | `"default"` | `muted` for secondary narration. |
| `align` | `"left" \| "center"` | `"left"` | Centres the block (text stays left-aligned). |
| `frame` | `boolean` |  | Paint a named theme's background behind the block, with padding and rounded corners. On by default for a named theme with its own surface; `false` turns it off. |

### Composition

- Composes: nothing (it is a primitive)
- Used by: [annotated-timeline](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/annotated-timeline.md), [scrolly-chart](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/scrolly-chart.md), [section](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/section.md), [comparison-brief](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/comparison-brief.md), [executive-brief](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/executive-brief.md), [explainer](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/explainer.md), [report-page](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/report-page.md), [scorecard](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/scorecard.md), [story-deck](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/story-deck.md), [timeline-story](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/timeline-story.md), [visual-essay](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/visual-essay.md)

### More examples

#### Lead paragraph, large

```tsx
import { Prose } from "insightcharts";

<Prose
  theme="editorial"
  size="lg"
  lead
  text={[
    "The typical household energy bill almost doubled between the winter of 2020 and the winter of 2022.",
    "Wholesale prices have fallen since then. Standing charges and network costs have not fallen. The average bill is still about a third higher than it was in 2020.",
  ]}
/>
```

#### Muted aside, narrow measure

```tsx
import { Prose } from "insightcharts";

<Prose
  theme="sunrise"
  size="sm"
  tone="muted"
  measure={48}
  text="*How to read this section.* Each dot is one local authority. Dots further right have more installed capacity per person. The vertical position shows median household income."
/>
```

## Pull quote (`pull-quote`)

> A large quotation with its attribution.

- Component: `PullQuote` (import from `insightcharts`)
- Spec type: `"pull-quote"`
- Level: atom. Category: text.
- An HTML component: it takes only the props listed below, plus `theme`, `mode`, `className` and `style` where its source declares them. It does not take the common chart props.

### When to use

To quote a person on a finding the charts have already shown, or to break up a long run of charts. One per section at most.

### Avoid

Restating a number (use `big-number`) or the main fact of a chart (use `callout`). Never quote without attribution.

### Install

From npm (the component ships in the package):

```bash
npm install insightcharts echarts
```

Or copy the source into your project with the shadcn CLI, so you can edit it (the engine still comes from the `insightcharts` package):

```bash
npx shadcn@latest registry add @insightcharts=https://insightcharts.dev/r/{name}.json   # once per project
npx shadcn@latest add @insightcharts/pull-quote
```

The file lands at `components/insightcharts/atoms/pull-quote.tsx`. `@insightcharts/pull-quote-demo` adds a ready-made example next to it.

### Usage

```tsx
import { PullQuote } from "insightcharts";

<PullQuote
  theme="editorial"
  quote="Solar set the midday wholesale price on most days in 2023. Our plans had assumed that would happen in the 2030s."
  attribution="Marit de Vries"
  role="Head of system operations, Dutch grid operator"
/>
```

### JSON spec

The same thing as data, rendered with `<Insight spec={spec} />`:

```json
{
  "type": "pull-quote",
  "theme": "editorial",
  "quote": "Solar set the midday wholesale price on most days in 2023. Our plans had assumed that would happen in the 2030s.",
  "attribution": "Marit de Vries",
  "role": "Head of system operations, Dutch grid operator"
}
```

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `quote` | `string` |  | The words quoted, without quotation marks. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` |  | JSX alternative to `quote`. |
| `attribution` | `string` |  | Who said it. |
| `role` | `string` |  | Their role, or where it was said. |
| `cite` | `string` |  | Source URL: set as the blockquote `cite` and linked from the attribution. |
| `size` | `"md" \| "lg"` | `"lg"` | `lg` anchors a section; `md` sits inside a column. |
| `align` | `"left" \| "center"` | `"left"` | Left-aligned quotes carry a side rule; centred ones do not. |
| `frame` | `boolean` |  | Paint a named theme's background behind the block, with padding and rounded corners. On by default for a named theme with its own surface; `false` turns it off. |

### Composition

- Composes: nothing (it is a primitive)
- Used by: [quote-figure](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/quote-figure.md), [story-deck](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/story-deck.md), [visual-essay](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/visual-essay.md)

## Radial bar chart (`radial-bar-chart`)

> Draws bars around a circle for data that repeats in a cycle, such as hours of the day or months of the year.

- Component: `RadialBarChart` (import from `insightcharts`)
- Spec type: `"radial-bar-chart"`
- Level: atom. Category: trend.
- An ECharts chart built with `defineChart`: accepts every common chart prop (data, transform, title, highlight, annotations, ...).

### When to use

Only when the dimension is cyclical and the wrap-around matters: activity by hour of day, seasonality by month, wind by compass direction. The first category is placed at 12 o'clock.

### Avoid

Any dimension that does not wrap around: categories, rankings, years (use bar-chart); precise comparison of values, since bars further out look bigger (use bar-chart or line-chart); more than about 3 stacked series.

### Install

From npm (the component ships in the package):

```bash
npm install insightcharts echarts
```

Or copy the source into your project with the shadcn CLI, so you can edit it (the engine still comes from the `insightcharts` package):

```bash
npx shadcn@latest registry add @insightcharts=https://insightcharts.dev/r/{name}.json   # once per project
npx shadcn@latest add @insightcharts/radial-bar-chart
```

The file lands at `components/insightcharts/atoms/radial-bar-chart.tsx`. `@insightcharts/radial-bar-chart-demo` adds a ready-made example next to it.

### Usage

```tsx
import { RadialBarChart } from "insightcharts";

const data = [
  { hour: "00:00", trips: 2.1 },
  { hour: "01:00", trips: 1.2 },
  { hour: "02:00", trips: 0.8 },
  { hour: "03:00", trips: 0.6 },
  { hour: "04:00", trips: 0.7 },
  { hour: "05:00", trips: 1.4 },
  { hour: "06:00", trips: 3.6 },
  { hour: "07:00", trips: 6.9 },
  { hour: "08:00", trips: 8.8 },
  { hour: "09:00", trips: 6.4 },
  { hour: "10:00", trips: 5.1 },
  { hour: "11:00", trips: 5.3 },
  { hour: "12:00", trips: 5.9 },
  { hour: "13:00", trips: 5.6 },
  { hour: "14:00", trips: 5.4 },
  { hour: "15:00", trips: 6 },
  { hour: "16:00", trips: 7.4 },
  { hour: "17:00", trips: 9.2 },
  { hour: "18:00", trips: 8.1 },
  { hour: "19:00", trips: 6 },
  { hour: "20:00", trips: 4.6 },
  { hour: "21:00", trips: 3.9 },
  { hour: "22:00", trips: 3.3 },
  { hour: "23:00", trips: 2.7 },
];

<RadialBarChart
  theme="dusk"
  data={data}
  x="hour"
  y="trips"
  format="{value}%"
  centerLabel="24 hours"
  highlight={["08:00", "17:00"]}
  title="Weekday bike-share trips peak at 9.2% in the 5pm hour and 8.8% in the 8am hour"
  subtitle="Share of daily bike-share trips starting in each hour, weekdays"
  source="Illustrative bike-share data"
/>
```

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `x` (required) | `string` |  | The cyclical category field, in cycle order. |
| `y` (required) | `string \| string[]` |  | Value field, or several to stack. |
| `series` | `string` |  | Field that splits rows into stacked series (long data). |
| `labelEvery` | `number` |  | Label every nth category around the rim. Default: chosen to avoid crowding. |
| `labels` | `boolean` |  | Print the value on the tallest bar. Default: on for a single series. |
| `centerFirst` | `boolean` | `false` | Centre the first category on 12 o'clock (compass directions) instead of starting its band there (hours). |
| `centerLabel` | `string` |  | Text in the centre of the ring, e.g. "24 hours". |
| `names` | `Record<string, string>` |  | Display names for series keys. |

### Common props

Also accepts every prop in the "Common chart props" section of this file.

### Composition

- Composes: nothing (it is a primitive)
- Used by: [story-deck](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/story-deck.md)

## Radial spokes (`radial-spokes`)

> Draws one spoke per row radiating from a centre disc, each as long as its value, with the name and value set on an outer ring.

- Component: `RadialSpokes` (import from `insightcharts`)
- Spec type: `"radial-spokes"`
- Level: atom. Category: poster.
- An ECharts chart built with `defineChart`: accepts every common chart prop (data, transform, title, highlight, annotations, ...).

### When to use

A poster of 4 to 12 effects, causes or attributes of one subject, which sits in the centre as an icon or a short label: what a household's energy goes on, the side effects of one drug, the scores of one product.

### Avoid

Precise comparison or a ranking (use bar-chart or pill-rank); a dimension that is a cycle, such as hours or months (use radial-bar-chart); more than 12 rows (use bar-chart); several subjects compared on the same attributes (use small-multiples or heatmap).

### Install

From npm (the component ships in the package):

```bash
npm install insightcharts echarts
```

Or copy the source into your project with the shadcn CLI, so you can edit it (the engine still comes from the `insightcharts` package):

```bash
npx shadcn@latest registry add @insightcharts=https://insightcharts.dev/r/{name}.json   # once per project
npx shadcn@latest add @insightcharts/radial-spokes
```

The file lands at `components/insightcharts/atoms/radial-spokes.tsx`. `@insightcharts/radial-spokes-demo` adds a ready-made example next to it.

### Usage

```tsx
import { RadialSpokes } from "insightcharts";

const data = [
  { use: "Space heating", share: 42 },
  { use: "Hot water", share: 17 },
  { use: "Cooking", share: 6 },
  { use: "Fridge and freezer", share: 8 },
  { use: "Laundry", share: 7 },
  { use: "Lighting", share: 5 },
  { use: "Screens and computers", share: 9 },
  { use: "Everything else", share: 6 },
];

<RadialSpokes
  theme="forest"
  data={data}
  name="use"
  value="share"
  format="{value}%"
  icon="house"
  highlight="Space heating"
  title="Space heating uses 42% of a home's energy"
  subtitle="Share of household energy by end use, a typical home in a cool climate"
  note="Illustrative figures"
/>
```

### JSON spec

The same thing as data, rendered with `<Insight spec={spec} />`:

```json
{
  "theme": "forest",
  "type": "radial-spokes",
  "data": [
    { "use": "Space heating", "share": 42 },
    { "use": "Hot water", "share": 17 },
    { "use": "Cooking", "share": 6 },
    { "use": "Fridge and freezer", "share": 8 },
    { "use": "Laundry", "share": 7 },
    { "use": "Lighting", "share": 5 },
    { "use": "Screens and computers", "share": 9 },
    { "use": "Everything else", "share": 6 }
  ],
  "name": "use",
  "value": "share",
  "format": "{value}%",
  "icon": "house",
  "highlight": "Space heating",
  "title": "Space heating uses 42% of a home's energy",
  "subtitle": "Share of household energy by end use, a typical home in a cool climate",
  "note": "Illustrative figures"
}
```

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` (required) | `string` |  | Name field: one spoke per row, in data order, clockwise. |
| `value` (required) | `string` |  | Value field: spoke length from the centre disc. |
| `shape` | `"bar" \| "line"` | `"bar"` | A thick tapered bar with a round head, or a thin line ending in a dot. |
| `icon` | `string` |  | Icon in the centre disc: a built-in name or `path://`. |
| `centerLabel` | `string` |  | Short text in the centre disc, used when there is no `icon`. |
| `ring` | `boolean` | `true` | Dotted outer ring at the scale maximum, where the labels sit. |
| `max` | `number` |  | Value that reaches the outer ring. Default: the largest value. |
| `startAngle` | `number` | `0` | Angle of the first spoke in degrees clockwise from 12 o'clock. |
| `sweep` | `number` | `360` | Arc the spokes are spread over, in degrees. 180 makes a fan. |
| `colorBy` | `"single" \| "value"` | `"single"` | The accent for every spoke, or a shade by value along the sequential ramp. |

### Common props

Also accepts every prop in the "Common chart props" section of this file.

### Composition

- Composes: nothing (it is a primitive)
- Used by: [atlas-poster](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/atlas-poster.md), [radial-poster](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/radial-poster.md)

### More examples

#### Thin lines, centre label, click to select

```tsx
  { aspect: "Battery life", score: 8.6 },
  { aspect: "Camera", score: 7.1 },
  { aspect: "Screen", score: 9 },
  { aspect: "Speed", score: 6.4 },
  { aspect: "Build", score: 7.8 },
  { aspect: "Value", score: 5.2 },
];

<RadialSpokes
  data={data}
  name="aspect"
  value="score"
  shape="line"
  max={10}
  format={{ minimumFractionDigits: 1 }}
  centerLabel="Model K phone"
  select
  title="Reviewers scored the Model K's screen 9.0 out of 10"
  subtitle="Average review score by aspect, out of 10. The ring marks 10."
  note="Illustrative scores for an invented phone"
/>
```

#### Fan over 180 degrees, shaded by value

## Ribbon chart (`ribbon-chart`)

> One filled band per entity across periods: its thickness is its value in each period and its vertical position is its rank, so bands cross as the order changes.

- Component: `RibbonChart` (import from `insightcharts`)
- Spec type: `"ribbon-chart"`
- Level: atom. Category: poster.
- An ECharts chart built with `defineChart`: accepts every common chart prop (data, transform, title, highlight, annotations, ...).

### When to use

4 to 8 entities over 4 to 10 periods when both the size of each and the changing order matter, and the graphic should read as one flowing form: market shares, harvests, medal tables, budget lines.

### Avoid

Totals that matter more than order, or a smooth centred stream of many periods (use area-chart, which has stacked and stream modes); rank alone (use bump-chart); more than 8 entities or 10 periods (use line-chart or small-multiples); values that can be negative (use line-chart).

### Install

From npm (the component ships in the package):

```bash
npm install insightcharts echarts
```

Or copy the source into your project with the shadcn CLI, so you can edit it (the engine still comes from the `insightcharts` package):

```bash
npx shadcn@latest registry add @insightcharts=https://insightcharts.dev/r/{name}.json   # once per project
npx shadcn@latest add @insightcharts/ribbon-chart
```

The file lands at `components/insightcharts/atoms/ribbon-chart.tsx`. `@insightcharts/ribbon-chart-demo` adds a ready-made example next to it.

### Usage

```tsx
import { RibbonChart } from "insightcharts";

const data = [
  { year: "2019", Potatoes: 7.4, Carrots: 5.1, Onions: 4.2, Beans: 2.6, Squash: 1.2 },
  { year: "2020", Potatoes: 6.9, Carrots: 5.6, Onions: 3.8, Beans: 3.1, Squash: 2.3 },
  { year: "2021", Potatoes: 6.1, Carrots: 5.9, Onions: 3.1, Beans: 3.4, Squash: 3.9 },
  { year: "2022", Potatoes: 5.2, Carrots: 6.3, Onions: 2.9, Beans: 3.2, Squash: 5 },
  { year: "2023", Potatoes: 4.8, Carrots: 6, Onions: 2.4, Beans: 3.6, Squash: 6.1 },
  { year: "2024", Potatoes: 4.1, Carrots: 6.2, Onions: 2.2, Beans: 3.5, Squash: 6.8 },
];

<RibbonChart
  theme="sunrise"
  data={data}
  x="year"
  y={["Potatoes", "Carrots", "Onions", "Beans", "Squash"]}
  format="{value} t"
  title="The squash harvest rose from 1.2 to 6.8 tonnes between 2019 and 2024"
  subtitle="Harvest of five crops at one community farm, tonnes, 2019 to 2024, largest at the top each year"
  note="Illustrative figures."
/>
```

### JSON spec

The same thing as data, rendered with `<Insight spec={spec} />`:

```json
{
  "theme": "sunrise",
  "type": "ribbon-chart",
  "data": [
    { "year": "2019", "Potatoes": 7.4, "Carrots": 5.1, "Onions": 4.2, "Beans": 2.6, "Squash": 1.2 },
    { "year": "2020", "Potatoes": 6.9, "Carrots": 5.6, "Onions": 3.8, "Beans": 3.1, "Squash": 2.3 },
    { "year": "2021", "Potatoes": 6.1, "Carrots": 5.9, "Onions": 3.1, "Beans": 3.4, "Squash": 3.9 },
    { "year": "2022", "Potatoes": 5.2, "Carrots": 6.3, "Onions": 2.9, "Beans": 3.2, "Squash": 5 },
    { "year": "2023", "Potatoes": 4.8, "Carrots": 6, "Onions": 2.4, "Beans": 3.6, "Squash": 6.1 },
    { "year": "2024", "Potatoes": 4.1, "Carrots": 6.2, "Onions": 2.2, "Beans": 3.5, "Squash": 6.8 }
  ],
  "x": "year",
  "y": ["Potatoes", "Carrots", "Onions", "Beans", "Squash"],
  "format": "{value} t",
  "title": "The squash harvest rose from 1.2 to 6.8 tonnes between 2019 and 2024",
  "subtitle": "Harvest of five crops at one community farm, tonnes, 2019 to 2024, largest at the top each year",
  "note": "Illustrative figures."
}
```

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `x` (required) | `string` |  | Period field: one column of the ribbon per distinct value, in data order. |
| `y` (required) | `string \| string[]` |  | Value field (long data), or one column per entity (wide data). Band thickness; negative values are drawn as zero. |
| `series` | `string` |  | Entity field, for long data. |
| `values` | `boolean` | `true` | Print each value inside its band at every period where it fits. |
| `labels` | `"both" \| "end"` |  | Entity names at both ends, or only at the end. Default: both, end only on narrow screens. |
| `names` | `Record<string, string>` |  | Display names for entity keys. |
| `colorBy` | `"auto" \| "series" \| "none"` | `"auto"` | `auto`: the largest entities take the theme's colours and any past the palette size (at most 8) are grey. `series`: every band gets its own colour, the extra ones derived from the theme's own. `none`: every band in the accent. |

### Common props

Also accepts every prop in the "Common chart props" section of this file.

### Composition

- Composes: nothing (it is a primitive)
- Used by: [timeline-poster](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/timeline-poster.md)

### More examples
