## Sankey chart (`sankey-chart`)

> Shows how a quantity flows from sources through stages to destinations, with link width proportional to the flow.

- Component: `SankeyChart` (import from `insightcharts`)
- Spec type: `"sankey-chart"`
- Level: atom. Category: flow.
- An ECharts chart built with `defineChart`: accepts every common chart prop (data, transform, title, highlight, annotations, ...).

### When to use

Where things come from and where they go: energy from fuel to end use, budget from revenue to spending, users from channel to outcome. Works best with 2 to 4 stages and up to about 20 nodes.

### Avoid

A single sequence of steps with drop-off (use funnel-chart); comparing a few totals (use bar-chart); flows that loop back (cycles cannot be drawn and are dropped); more than about 40 links.

### Install

From npm (the component ships in the package):

```bash
npm install insightcharts echarts
```

Or copy the source into your project with the shadcn CLI, so you can edit it (the engine still comes from the `insightcharts` package):

```bash
npx shadcn@latest registry add @insightcharts=https://insightcharts.dev/r/{name}.json   # once per project
npx shadcn@latest add @insightcharts/sankey-chart
```

The file lands at `components/insightcharts/atoms/sankey-chart.tsx`. `@insightcharts/sankey-chart-demo` adds a ready-made example next to it.

### Usage

```tsx
import { SankeyChart } from "insightcharts";

const data = [
  { from: "Coal", to: "Electricity", twh: 290 },
  { from: "Gas", to: "Electricity", twh: 210 },
  { from: "Gas", to: "Heat", twh: 330 },
  { from: "Wind and solar", to: "Electricity", twh: 240 },
  { from: "Nuclear", to: "Electricity", twh: 120 },
  { from: "Oil", to: "Transport", twh: 560 },
  { from: "Oil", to: "Heat", twh: 90 },
  { from: "Electricity", to: "Homes", twh: 280 },
  { from: "Electricity", to: "Industry", twh: 330 },
  { from: "Electricity", to: "Transport", twh: 30 },
  { from: "Electricity", to: "Losses", twh: 220 },
  { from: "Heat", to: "Homes", twh: 270 },
  { from: "Heat", to: "Industry", twh: 150 },
];

<SankeyChart
  theme="noir"
  data={data}
  from="from"
  to="to"
  value="twh"
  format="{value} TWh"
  title="220 TWh of the 860 TWh used to generate electricity was lost"
  subtitle="Energy flows from fuel to end use, terawatt-hours per year"
  source="Illustrative national energy balance"
/>
```

### JSON spec

The same thing as data, rendered with `<Insight spec={spec} />`:

```json
{
  "theme": "noir",
  "type": "sankey-chart",
  "data": [
    { "from": "Coal", "to": "Electricity", "twh": 290 },
    { "from": "Gas", "to": "Electricity", "twh": 210 },
    { "from": "Gas", "to": "Heat", "twh": 330 },
    { "from": "Wind and solar", "to": "Electricity", "twh": 240 },
    { "from": "Nuclear", "to": "Electricity", "twh": 120 },
    { "from": "Oil", "to": "Transport", "twh": 560 },
    { "from": "Oil", "to": "Heat", "twh": 90 },
    { "from": "Electricity", "to": "Homes", "twh": 280 },
    { "from": "Electricity", "to": "Industry", "twh": 330 },
    { "from": "Electricity", "to": "Transport", "twh": 30 },
    { "from": "Electricity", "to": "Losses", "twh": 220 },
    { "from": "Heat", "to": "Homes", "twh": 270 },
    { "from": "Heat", "to": "Industry", "twh": 150 }
  ],
  "from": "from",
  "to": "to",
  "value": "twh",
  "format": "{value} TWh",
  "title": "220 TWh of the 860 TWh used to generate electricity was lost",
  "subtitle": "Energy flows from fuel to end use, terawatt-hours per year",
  "source": "Illustrative national energy balance"
}
```

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `from` | `string` | `"source"` | Field naming where each flow starts. Not called `source` because that is the figure's source line. |
| `to` | `string` | `"target"` | Field naming where each flow ends. |
| `value` | `string` | `"value"` | Flow size field. Non-positive flows are dropped. |
| `orientation` | `"auto" \| "horizontal" \| "vertical"` | `"auto"` | Left to right, or top to bottom for narrow columns with short names. |
| `labels` | `boolean` | `true` | Print each node's total after its name. |
| `names` | `Record<string, string>` |  | Display names for node keys. |

### Common props

Also accepts every prop in the "Common chart props" section of this file.

### Composition

- Composes: nothing (it is a primitive)
- Used by: no molecule or template yet

### More examples

## Scale ladder (`scale-ladder`)

> A tall vertical band graded along one scale (linear or log, running up or down) with each item placed at its true position and labelled with an icon, its name and its value on alternating sides.

- Component: `ScaleLadder` (import from `insightcharts`)
- Spec type: `"scale-ladder"`
- Level: atom. Category: poster.
- An ECharts chart built with `defineChart`: accepts every common chart prop (data, transform, title, highlight, annotations, ...).

### When to use

Answering how deep, how high, how hot, how old or how far each of 4 to about 20 things is on one shared scale, when the reader needs the positions themselves: depths, altitudes, temperatures, ages, distances. Use `zones` to name ranges along the scale.

### Avoid

Comparing sizes rather than positions (use bar-chart or lollipop-chart); events with start and end dates (use timeline-chart); a distribution of many unnamed values (use strip-plot or histogram).

### Install

From npm (the component ships in the package):

```bash
npm install insightcharts echarts
```

Or copy the source into your project with the shadcn CLI, so you can edit it (the engine still comes from the `insightcharts` package):

```bash
npx shadcn@latest registry add @insightcharts=https://insightcharts.dev/r/{name}.json   # once per project
npx shadcn@latest add @insightcharts/scale-ladder
```

The file lands at `components/insightcharts/atoms/scale-ladder.tsx`. `@insightcharts/scale-ladder-demo` adds a ready-made example next to it.

### Usage

```tsx
import { ScaleLadder } from "insightcharts";

const data = [
  { thing: "Fridge", c: 4 },
  { thing: "Chocolate melts", c: 34 },
  { thing: "Egg white sets", c: 62 },
  { thing: "Water boils", c: 100, icon: "drop" },
  { thing: "Sugar caramelises", c: 170 },
  { thing: "Deep-frying oil", c: 180, icon: "drop" },
  { thing: "Bread bakes", c: 220 },
  { thing: "Home oven at full heat", c: 250 },
  { thing: "Wood-fired pizza oven", c: 450 },
];

<ScaleLadder
  theme="magenta"
  data={data}
  name="thing"
  value="c"
  iconField="icon"
  format="{value}°C"
  scaleLabel="Temperature"
  min={0}
  max={500}
  zones={[
    { from: 0, to: 100, label: "Below boiling" },
    { from: 100, to: 250, label: "Home oven range" },
    { from: 250, to: 500, label: "Wood-fired oven range" },
  ]}
  title="Nine kitchen temperatures from 4°C to 450°C"
  subtitle="Typical temperatures in a kitchen, degrees Celsius"
  note="Approximate, rounded figures."
/>
```

### JSON spec

The same thing as data, rendered with `<Insight spec={spec} />`:

```json
{
  "theme": "magenta",
  "type": "scale-ladder",
  "data": [
    { "thing": "Fridge", "c": 4 },
    { "thing": "Chocolate melts", "c": 34 },
    { "thing": "Egg white sets", "c": 62 },
    { "thing": "Water boils", "c": 100, "icon": "drop" },
    { "thing": "Sugar caramelises", "c": 170 },
    { "thing": "Deep-frying oil", "c": 180, "icon": "drop" },
    { "thing": "Bread bakes", "c": 220 },
    { "thing": "Home oven at full heat", "c": 250 },
    { "thing": "Wood-fired pizza oven", "c": 450 }
  ],
  "name": "thing",
  "value": "c",
  "iconField": "icon",
  "format": "{value}°C",
  "scaleLabel": "Temperature",
  "min": 0,
  "max": 500,
  "zones": [
    { "from": 0, "to": 100, "label": "Below boiling" },
    { "from": 100, "to": 250, "label": "Home oven range" },
    { "from": 250, "to": 500, "label": "Wood-fired oven range" }
  ],
  "title": "Nine kitchen temperatures from 4°C to 450°C",
  "subtitle": "Typical temperatures in a kitchen, degrees Celsius",
  "note": "Approximate, rounded figures."
}
```

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` (required) | `string` |  | Field holding each item's name. |
| `value` (required) | `string` |  | Field holding each item's position on the scale. |
| `icon` | `IconInput` |  | One icon for every item: a built-in name or a `path://` string. Items without an icon get a dot. |
| `iconField` | `string` |  | Field holding a per-item icon name or `path://` string. Overrides `icon`. |
| `scale` | `"linear" \| "log"` | `"linear"` | Log spaces the scale by powers of ten; the heading over the band says so. |
| `direction` | `"up" \| "down"` | `"up"` | `up`: larger values higher (height, temperature). `down`: larger values lower (depth, age). |
| `min` | `number` |  | Start of the scale. Default: a round number at or below the smallest value. |
| `max` | `number` |  | End of the scale. Default: a round number at or above the largest value. |
| `ticks` | `number[]` |  | Values that get a boxed label on the band. Default: round steps, or powers of ten on a log scale. |
| `zones` | `{ from: number; to: number; label: string }[]` |  | Named ranges along the scale, shaded across the graphic and named along its outer edge. |
| `scaleLabel` | `string` |  | Heading over the band: the measure and its unit, e.g. "Depth, metres". |
| `names` | `Record<string, string>` |  | Display names for item keys. |
| `bandWidth` | `number` |  | Width of the band in px, at most 40% of the plot width. Default 60, or 46 on narrow screens. |

### Common props

Also accepts every prop in the "Common chart props" section of this file.

### Composition

- Composes: nothing (it is a primitive)
- Used by: [profile-poster](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/profile-poster.md), [scale-poster](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/scale-poster.md)

### More examples

## Scatter chart (`scatter-chart`)

> Plots two numeric measures against each other, one dot per row, with optional bubble size, group colour, selective labels and a trend line.

- Component: `ScatterChart` (import from `insightcharts`)
- Spec type: `"scatter-chart"`
- Level: atom. Category: relationship.
- An ECharts chart built with `defineChart`: accepts every common chart prop (data, transform, title, highlight, annotations, ...).

### When to use

Showing whether and how two measures move together, spotting clusters and outliers, and placing named entities in a two-dimensional space (with quadrant lines via `annotations`).

### Avoid

A measure over time (use line-chart); one numeric measure by category (use beeswarm-chart or strip-plot); fewer than about 8 points (use bar-chart or a table); more than 4 colour groups (facet with small-multiples).

### Install

From npm (the component ships in the package):

```bash
npm install insightcharts echarts
```

Or copy the source into your project with the shadcn CLI, so you can edit it (the engine still comes from the `insightcharts` package):

```bash
npx shadcn@latest registry add @insightcharts=https://insightcharts.dev/r/{name}.json   # once per project
npx shadcn@latest add @insightcharts/scatter-chart
```

The file lands at `components/insightcharts/atoms/scatter-chart.tsx`. `@insightcharts/scatter-chart-demo` adds a ready-made example next to it.

### Usage

```tsx

  { country: "United States", spend: 12555, life: 77.5 },
```

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `x` (required) | `string` |  | Numeric field on the horizontal axis. |
| `y` (required) | `string` |  | Numeric field on the vertical axis. |
| `size` | `string` |  | Numeric field for bubble size; area is proportional to the value. |
| `series` | `string` |  | Field that colours points by group. Beyond 4 groups the smallest fold into a grey Other. |
| `label` | `string` |  | Field naming each point, for tooltips, direct labels and `highlight`. |
| `labels` | `"auto" \| "all" \| "none" \| string[]` | `"auto"` | Which points are labelled. `auto`: highlighted points, or the outliers when nothing is highlighted. Overlapping labels are hidden. |
| `trend` | `boolean` | `false` | Least-squares line of best fit through all points. |
| `logX` | `boolean` | `false` | Logarithmic x axis. |
| `logY` | `boolean` | `false` | Logarithmic y axis. |
| `xLabel` | `string` |  | x axis title. Defaults to the field name. |
| `yLabel` | `string` |  | y axis title. Defaults to the field name. |
| `xFormat` | `FormatSpec` |  | Format for x values; `format` applies to y. |
| `opacity` | `number` |  | Point opacity. Default falls as the point count rises. |
| `names` | `Record<string, string>` |  | Display names for series keys. |

### Common props

Also accepts every prop in the "Common chart props" section of this file.

### Composition

- Composes: nothing (it is a primitive)
- Used by: no molecule or template yet

## Segmented bar (`segmented-bar`)

> Splits one whole into proportional segments along a single horizontal bar.

- Component: `SegmentedBar` (import from `insightcharts`)
- Spec type: `"segmented-bar"`
- Level: atom. Category: part-to-whole.
- An ECharts chart built with `defineChart`: accepts every common chart prop (data, transform, title, highlight, annotations, ...).

### When to use

A compact part-to-whole for cards, table cells and stat rows: budget split, device mix, vote share. The legend carries names in block order.

### Avoid

Comparing compositions across several groups (use bar-chart with stack "percent"); more than about 6 parts or many slivers (use bar-chart); when the reader should count units (use waffle-chart).

### Install

From npm (the component ships in the package):

```bash
npm install insightcharts echarts
```

Or copy the source into your project with the shadcn CLI, so you can edit it (the engine still comes from the `insightcharts` package):

```bash
npx shadcn@latest registry add @insightcharts=https://insightcharts.dev/r/{name}.json   # once per project
npx shadcn@latest add @insightcharts/segmented-bar
```

The file lands at `components/insightcharts/atoms/segmented-bar.tsx`. `@insightcharts/segmented-bar-demo` adds a ready-made example next to it.

### Usage

```tsx
import { SegmentedBar } from "insightcharts";

const data = [
  { party: "Labour", seats: 411 },
  { party: "Conservative", seats: 121 },
  { party: "Liberal Democrat", seats: 72 },
  { party: "SNP", seats: 9 },
  { party: "Others", seats: 37 },
];

<SegmentedBar
  theme="ledger"
  data={data}
  name="party"
  value="seats"
  title="Labour won 411 of 650 seats in the 2024 general election"
  subtitle="Seats in the House of Commons by party after the 2024 general election"
  source="House of Commons Library"
  note="Figures are approximate, for illustration"
/>
```

### JSON spec

The same thing as data, rendered with `<Insight spec={spec} />`:

```json
{
  "theme": "ledger",
  "type": "segmented-bar",
  "data": [
    { "party": "Labour", "seats": 411 },
    { "party": "Conservative", "seats": 121 },
    { "party": "Liberal Democrat", "seats": 72 },
    { "party": "SNP", "seats": 9 },
    { "party": "Others", "seats": 37 }
  ],
  "name": "party",
  "value": "seats",
  "title": "Labour won 411 of 650 seats in the 2024 general election",
  "subtitle": "Seats in the House of Commons by party after the 2024 general election",
  "source": "House of Commons Library",
  "note": "Figures are approximate, for illustration"
}
```

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` (required) | `string` |  | Category field: one segment per distinct value. |
| `value` (required) | `string` |  | Value field. |
| `size` | `"tall" \| "thin"` | `"tall"` | 28px with shares printed inside where they fit, or 8px unlabelled. |
| `sort` | `"none" \| "desc"` | `"none"` | Segment order; the legend follows it. |
| `names` | `Record<string, string>` |  | Display names for category keys. |

### Common props

Also accepts every prop in the "Common chart props" section of this file.

### Composition

- Composes: nothing (it is a primitive)
- Used by: [metric-breakdown](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/metric-breakdown.md), [poster](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/poster.md), [comparison-brief](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/comparison-brief.md), [data-explorer](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/data-explorer.md), [explainer](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/explainer.md)

### More examples

## Shape fill (`shape-fill`)

> Shows one or more percentages as icon silhouettes filled from the bottom to that level, with the number printed large beside each.

- Component: `ShapeFill` (import from `insightcharts`)
- Spec type: `"shape-fill"`
- Level: atom. Category: poster.
- An ECharts chart built with `defineChart`: accepts every common chart prop (data, transform, title, highlight, annotations, ...).

### When to use

One to six shares of a full amount where the object itself says what is measured: how full a reservoir is, how charged a fleet is, what share of homes have a heat pump.

### Avoid

The fill height only approximates the share, because an irregular silhouette holds less area at its narrow end, so the number must always stay printed; for values to be compared precisely use block-bar or bar-chart, for a counted share use waffle-chart, for a compact inline meter use progress-meter.

### Install

From npm (the component ships in the package):

```bash
npm install insightcharts echarts
```

Or copy the source into your project with the shadcn CLI, so you can edit it (the engine still comes from the `insightcharts` package):

```bash
npx shadcn@latest registry add @insightcharts=https://insightcharts.dev/r/{name}.json   # once per project
npx shadcn@latest add @insightcharts/shape-fill
```

The file lands at `components/insightcharts/atoms/shape-fill.tsx`. `@insightcharts/shape-fill-demo` adds a ready-made example next to it.

### Usage

```tsx
import { ShapeFill } from "insightcharts";

const data = [
  { reservoir: "Carrow", level: 63 },
  { reservoir: "Upper Fen", level: 41 },
  { reservoir: "Stonebeck", level: 88 },
];

<ShapeFill
  theme="blueprint"
  data={data}
  name="reservoir"
  value="level"
  icon="drop"
  format="{value}%"
  title="Carrow Reservoir was 63% full on 1 September 2025"
  subtitle="Water stored as a share of capacity, three reservoirs, 1 September 2025"
  source="Illustrative data"
  note="Invented figures for fictional reservoirs"
/>
```

### JSON spec

The same thing as data, rendered with `<Insight spec={spec} />`:

```json
{
  "theme": "blueprint",
  "type": "shape-fill",
  "data": [
    { "reservoir": "Carrow", "level": 63 },
    { "reservoir": "Upper Fen", "level": 41 },
    { "reservoir": "Stonebeck", "level": 88 }
  ],
  "name": "reservoir",
  "value": "level",
  "icon": "drop",
  "format": "{value}%",
  "title": "Carrow Reservoir was 63% full on 1 September 2025",
  "subtitle": "Water stored as a share of capacity, three reservoirs, 1 September 2025",
  "source": "Illustrative data",
  "note": "Invented figures for fictional reservoirs"
}
```

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` (required) | `string` |  | Label field: one silhouette per row. |
| `value` (required) | `string` |  | Value field: how full each silhouette is, against `max`. |
| `max` | `number` |  | The value that fills a silhouette completely. Default: 1 when every value is at most 1, otherwise 100. |
| `icon` | `IconName \| "path://..."` | `"drop"` | Built-in icon name or a custom single SVG path. |
| `icons` | `Record<string, string>` |  | Icon per label; falls back to `icon`. |
| `columns` | `number` |  | Silhouettes per line. Default: up to four, two on a phone. |
| `colorBy` | `"single" \| "item"` | `"single"` | `single`: every silhouette in the accent colour. `item`: one colour per row. |
| `iconSize` | `number` |  | Silhouette height in px. Default: sized to the width, or grown to fill the box when the `height` prop or `aspect` is given, so one silhouette can be the main figure of a poster. |

### Common props

Also accepts every prop in the "Common chart props" section of this file.

### Composition

- Composes: nothing (it is a primitive)
- Used by: [count-poster](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/count-poster.md), [profile-poster](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/profile-poster.md), [ranking-poster](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/ranking-poster.md)

### More examples

#### One silhouette

```tsx
  title="18% of homes in Eastvale had a heat pump in 2025"

  note="Invented figure for a fictional town"
/>
```

## Slope chart (`slope-chart`)

> Connects each entity's value at two (or a few) points with a straight line, labelled with name and value at both ends.

- Component: `SlopeChart` (import from `insightcharts`)
- Spec type: `"slope-chart"`
- Level: atom. Category: trend.
- An ECharts chart built with `defineChart`: accepts every common chart prop (data, transform, title, highlight, annotations, ...).

### When to use

Before / after for 3 to about 15 entities when the change in level and in ordering both matter; pair with `highlight` to emphasise one line.

### Avoid

Five or more time points (use line-chart); when only the ordering matters (use bump-chart); when only the size of each gap matters (use dumbbell-chart or arrow-chart).

### Install

From npm (the component ships in the package):

```bash
npm install insightcharts echarts
```

Or copy the source into your project with the shadcn CLI, so you can edit it (the engine still comes from the `insightcharts` package):

```bash
npx shadcn@latest registry add @insightcharts=https://insightcharts.dev/r/{name}.json   # once per project
npx shadcn@latest add @insightcharts/slope-chart
```

The file lands at `components/insightcharts/atoms/slope-chart.tsx`. `@insightcharts/slope-chart-demo` adds a ready-made example next to it.

### Usage

```tsx
import { SlopeChart } from "insightcharts";

const data = [
  { country: "United Kingdom", y2012: 39, y2023: 1 },
  { country: "Germany", y2012: 44, y2023: 26 },
  { country: "United States", y2012: 37, y2023: 16 },
  { country: "Poland", y2012: 84, y2023: 61 },
  { country: "India", y2012: 71, y2023: 75 },
  { country: "Japan", y2012: 29, y2023: 32 },
];

<SlopeChart
  data={data}
  series="country"
  y={["y2012", "y2023"]}
  names={{ y2012: "2012", y2023: "2023" }}
  highlight="United Kingdom"
  format="{value}%"
  title="The UK's coal share of electricity fell from 39% to 1% between 2012 and 2023"
  subtitle="Share of electricity generated from coal, 2012 and 2023"
  source="Ember (rounded)"
  note="Figures are approximate, for illustration"
/>
```

### JSON spec

The same thing as data, rendered with `<Insight spec={spec} />`:

```json
{
  "type": "slope-chart",
  "data": [
    { "country": "United Kingdom", "y2012": 39, "y2023": 1 },
    { "country": "Germany", "y2012": 44, "y2023": 26 },
    { "country": "United States", "y2012": 37, "y2023": 16 },
    { "country": "Poland", "y2012": 84, "y2023": 61 },
    { "country": "India", "y2012": 71, "y2023": 75 },
    { "country": "Japan", "y2012": 29, "y2023": 32 }
  ],
  "series": "country",
  "y": ["y2012", "y2023"],
  "names": { "y2012": "2012", "y2023": "2023" },
  "highlight": "United Kingdom",
  "format": "{value}%",
  "title": "The UK's coal share of electricity fell from 39% to 1% between 2012 and 2023",
  "subtitle": "Share of electricity generated from coal, 2012 and 2023",
  "source": "Ember (rounded)",
  "note": "Figures are approximate, for illustration"
}
```

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `series` (required) | `string` |  | Entity field: one line each. |
| `x` | `string` |  | Period field for long data. Omit when each row is an entity with one column per period. |
| `y` (required) | `string \| string[]` |  | Value field (long data), or the period columns in order (one row per entity). |
| `colorBy` | `"none" \| "direction" \| "series"` | `"none"` | Accent for all lines, positive / negative by direction, or one hue per entity (up to 8). |
| `good` | `"up" \| "down"` | `"up"` | Direction that takes the positive colour when colouring by direction. |
| `labels` | `"both" \| "end"` |  | Entity names at both ends or only the end. Default: both; end only on narrow screens. |
| `names` | `Record<string, string>` |  | Display names for entity keys and period columns. |

### Common props

Also accepts every prop in the "Common chart props" section of this file.

### Composition

- Composes: nothing (it is a primitive)
- Used by: [chart-callout](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/chart-callout.md), [atlas-poster](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/atlas-poster.md), [executive-brief](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/executive-brief.md)

### More examples

#### Coloured by direction

```tsx
import { SlopeChart } from "insightcharts";

const data = [
  { region: "North East", before: 71.2, after: 68.4 },
  { region: "London", before: 68.9, after: 75.1 },
  { region: "South West", before: 76, after: 77.8 },
  { region: "Wales", before: 69.5, after: 72.6 },
  { region: "Scotland", before: 73.4, after: 73.1 },
  { region: "West Midlands", before: 70.1, after: 73.9 },
];

<SlopeChart
  theme="editorial"
  data={data}
  series="region"
  y={["before", "after"]}
  names={{ before: "2014", after: "2024" }}
  colorBy="direction"
  format="{value}%"
  title="London's employment rate rose from 68.9% to 75.1% between 2014 and 2024"
  subtitle="Employment rate, ages 16 to 64, 2014 and 2024"
  note="Illustrative figures."
/>
```

## Small multiples (`small-multiples`)

> Repeats one small line, area or bar chart per value of a facet field on a shared scale, each panel titled.

- Component: `SmallMultiples` (import from `insightcharts`)
- Spec type: `"small-multiples"`
- Level: atom. Category: trend.
- An ECharts chart built with `defineChart`: accepts every common chart prop (data, transform, title, highlight, annotations, ...).

### When to use

The same measure for 4 to about 24 entities when one chart would have too many overlapping lines; pair with `highlight` to pick out one panel, or `context` to show every other line faintly behind each.

### Avoid

Three or fewer series (use line-chart with direct labels); when exact comparison between two entities matters most (use line-chart with `highlight`); a single value per entity (use bar-chart).

### Install

From npm (the component ships in the package):

```bash
npm install insightcharts echarts
```

Or copy the source into your project with the shadcn CLI, so you can edit it (the engine still comes from the `insightcharts` package):

```bash
npx shadcn@latest registry add @insightcharts=https://insightcharts.dev/r/{name}.json   # once per project
npx shadcn@latest add @insightcharts/small-multiples
```

The file lands at `components/insightcharts/atoms/small-multiples.tsx`. `@insightcharts/small-multiples-demo` adds a ready-made example next to it.

### Usage

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `facet` (required) | `string` |  | Field whose values each get a panel. |
| `x` (required) | `string` |  | Time or ordered category field, shared by every panel. |
| `y` (required) | `string \| string[]` |  | Value field, or several (one series each in every panel). |
| `series` | `string` |  | Field that splits rows into series inside each panel (long data). |
| `kind` | `"line" \| "area" \| "bar"` | `"line"` | What each panel draws. Area and bar panels start at zero. |
| `columns` | `number` |  | Preferred number of columns; reduced automatically on narrow containers. |
| `scales` | `"shared" \| "free"` | `"shared"` | Shared value scale across panels, or each panel on its own (say so in the subtitle). |
| `context` | `boolean` | `false` | Draw every other panel's line faintly behind each panel's own. |
| `latest` | `boolean` |  | Print the latest value beside each panel title. Default: on for a single series. |
| `names` | `Record<string, string>` |  | Display names for facet values and series keys. |

### Common props

Also accepts every prop in the "Common chart props" section of this file.

### Composition

- Composes: nothing (it is a primitive)
- Used by: [visual-essay](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/visual-essay.md)

## Source note (`source-note`)

> A sourcing footer for a whole piece: sources with optional links, the period covered, method, caveats and credit.

- Component: `SourceNote` (import from `insightcharts`)
- Spec type: `"source-note"`
- Level: atom. Category: text.
- An HTML component: it takes only the props listed below, plus `theme`, `mode`, `className` and `style` where its source declares them. It does not take the common chart props.

### When to use

Once, at the end of a story or dashboard, to say where every number came from and how it was produced.

### Avoid

Sourcing a single chart: use that chart's own `source` and `note` props so the citation travels with its export.

### Install

From npm (the component ships in the package):

```bash
npm install insightcharts echarts
```

Or copy the source into your project with the shadcn CLI, so you can edit it (the engine still comes from the `insightcharts` package):

```bash
npx shadcn@latest registry add @insightcharts=https://insightcharts.dev/r/{name}.json   # once per project
npx shadcn@latest add @insightcharts/source-note
```

The file lands at `components/insightcharts/atoms/source-note.tsx`. `@insightcharts/source-note-demo` adds a ready-made example next to it.

### Usage

```tsx
import { SourceNote } from "insightcharts";

<SourceNote
  theme="earth"
  sources={[
    { name: "Ember, European Electricity Review 2025", url: "https://ember-energy.org" },
    { name: "ENTSO-E Transparency Platform", url: "https://transparency.entsoe.eu" },
  ]}
  note="Figures are approximate, for illustration"
  period="January 2015 to December 2024, monthly"
  method="Generation shares are net of pumped-storage consumption. Figures for 2024 are provisional and exclude Malta and Cyprus."
  credit="Analysis and charts by the data desk"
/>
```

### JSON spec

The same thing as data, rendered with `<Insight spec={spec} />`:

```json
{
  "type": "source-note",
  "theme": "earth",
  "sources": [
    { "name": "Ember, European Electricity Review 2025", "url": "https://ember-energy.org" },
    { "name": "ENTSO-E Transparency Platform", "url": "https://transparency.entsoe.eu" }
  ],
  "note": "Figures are approximate, for illustration",
  "period": "January 2015 to December 2024, monthly",
  "method": "Generation shares are net of pumped-storage consumption. Figures for 2024 are provisional and exclude Malta and Cyprus.",
  "credit": "Analysis and charts by the data desk"
}
```

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sources` | `string \| { name, url? } \| (string \| { name, url? })[]` |  | Where the data comes from. Entries with a `url` are linked. |
| `period` | `string` |  | The period the data covers, e.g. "2015 to 2024". Shown as "Data". |
| `method` | `string` |  | How the numbers were produced: definitions, adjustments, exclusions. |
| `note` | `string` |  | Caveats the reader should know. |
| `credit` | `string` |  | Who made the piece. |
| `layout` | `"list" \| "inline"` | `"list"` | Labelled list, or one running paragraph. |
| `rule` | `boolean` | `true` | Hairline above the note. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` |  | Extra content after the rows. |
| `frame` | `boolean` |  | Paint a named theme's background behind the block, with padding and rounded corners. On by default for a named theme with its own surface; `false` turns it off. |

### Composition

- Composes: nothing (it is a primitive)
- Used by: [hero-figure](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/hero-figure.md), [comparison-brief](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/comparison-brief.md), [data-explorer](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/data-explorer.md), [executive-brief](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/executive-brief.md), [explainer](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/explainer.md), [report-page](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/report-page.md), [scorecard](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/scorecard.md), [social-card](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/social-card.md), [story-deck](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/story-deck.md), [timeline-story](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/timeline-story.md), [visual-essay](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/visual-essay.md)

### More examples

#### Inline

```tsx
import { SourceNote } from "insightcharts";

<SourceNote
  layout="inline"
  sources={["Office for National Statistics", "Ofgem price cap tables"]}
  note="Figures are approximate, for illustration"
  period="Q1 2019 to Q4 2024"
  method="Bills are for a typical dual-fuel household paying by direct debit, in 2024 prices"
  credit="Chart design: A. Ruiz"
/>
```

#### Single source, no rule

```tsx
import { SourceNote } from "insightcharts";

<SourceNote
  theme="noir"
  rule={false}
  sources="World Bank, World Development Indicators"
  note="Illustrative data for the gallery."
/>
```

## Sparkline (`sparkline`)

> A word-sized line or bar series without axes, with the latest point marked.

- Component: `Sparkline` (import from `insightcharts`)
- Spec type: `"sparkline"`
- Level: atom. Category: trend.
- An ECharts chart built with `defineChart`: accepts every common chart prop (data, transform, title, highlight, annotations, ...).

### When to use

Showing the recent history of a number inside a stat tile, a table cell or a sentence, where the shape of the trend matters and exact values do not.

### Avoid

Anything the reader must read values from or compare across series (use line-chart); fewer than about 5 points (state the change in words or use big-number with a delta).

### Install

From npm (the component ships in the package):

```bash
npm install insightcharts echarts
```

Or copy the source into your project with the shadcn CLI, so you can edit it (the engine still comes from the `insightcharts` package):

```bash
npx shadcn@latest registry add @insightcharts=https://insightcharts.dev/r/{name}.json   # once per project
npx shadcn@latest add @insightcharts/sparkline
```

The file lands at `components/insightcharts/atoms/sparkline.tsx`. `@insightcharts/sparkline-demo` adds a ready-made example next to it.

### Usage

```tsx
import { Sparkline } from "insightcharts";

const data = [
  { month: "2023-07", rate: 3.9 },
  { month: "2023-08", rate: 3.8 },
  { month: "2023-09", rate: 3.8 },
  { month: "2023-10", rate: 3.6 },
  { month: "2023-11", rate: 3.5 },
  { month: "2023-12", rate: 3.6 },
  { month: "2024-01", rate: 3.4 },
  { month: "2024-02", rate: 3.7 },
  { month: "2024-03", rate: 3.8 },
  { month: "2024-04", rate: 3.9 },
  { month: "2024-05", rate: 4.1 },
  { month: "2024-06", rate: 4.3 },
  { month: "2024-07", rate: 4.2 },
  { month: "2024-08", rate: 4.1 },
  { month: "2024-09", rate: 4.2 },
  { month: "2024-10", rate: 4.4 },
];

<Sparkline
  data={data}
  x="month"
  y="rate"
  format="{value}%"
  showValue
  extremes
  style={{ maxWidth: 220 }}
  alt="Sparkline of the unemployment rate over 16 months, July 2023 to October 2024. It started at 3.9%, fell to 3.4% in January 2024 and ended at 4.4%, the highest in the period."
/>
```

### JSON spec

The same thing as data, rendered with `<Insight spec={spec} />`:

```json
{
  "type": "sparkline",
  "data": [
    { "month": "2023-07", "rate": 3.9 },
    { "month": "2023-08", "rate": 3.8 },
    { "month": "2023-09", "rate": 3.8 },
    { "month": "2023-10", "rate": 3.6 },
    { "month": "2023-11", "rate": 3.5 },
    { "month": "2023-12", "rate": 3.6 },
    { "month": "2024-01", "rate": 3.4 },
    { "month": "2024-02", "rate": 3.7 },
    { "month": "2024-03", "rate": 3.8 },
    { "month": "2024-04", "rate": 3.9 },
    { "month": "2024-05", "rate": 4.1 },
    { "month": "2024-06", "rate": 4.3 },
    { "month": "2024-07", "rate": 4.2 },
    { "month": "2024-08", "rate": 4.1 },
    { "month": "2024-09", "rate": 4.2 },
    { "month": "2024-10", "rate": 4.4 }
  ],
  "x": "month",
  "y": "rate",
  "format": "{value}%",
  "showValue": true,
  "extremes": true,
  "style": { "maxWidth": 220 },
  "alt": "Sparkline of the unemployment rate over 16 months, July 2023 to October 2024. It started at 3.9%, fell to 3.4% in January 2024 and ended at 4.4%, the highest in the period."
}
```

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `y` (required) | `string` |  | Value field. |
| `x` | `string` |  | Time or label field, used in the tooltip and alt text. Rows are drawn in data order. |
| `mark` | `"line" \| "bar"` | `"line"` | Line for a trend, bars for discrete counts or gains and losses (negative bars take the negative colour). |
| `extremes` | `boolean` | `false` | Mark the lowest and highest points with small dots. |
| `band` | `[number, number]` |  | Shaded reference range in value units, e.g. a normal range. |
| `area` | `boolean` | `false` | Light fill under the line; forces a zero baseline. |
| `showValue` | `boolean` | `false` | Print the last value after the line. |
| `zero` | `boolean` |  | Include zero in the scale. Default: off for lines, always on for bars. |

### Common props

Also accepts every prop in the "Common chart props" section of this file.

### Composition

- Composes: nothing (it is a primitive)
- Used by: [annotated-timeline](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/annotated-timeline.md), [before-after](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/before-after.md), [comparison-table](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/comparison-table.md), [quote-figure](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/quote-figure.md), [trend-card](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/trend-card.md)

## Stat circles (`stat-circles`)

> Shows a few related magnitudes as plain circles sized by area, each with its number set large and a short label.

- Component: `StatCircles` (import from `insightcharts`)
- Spec type: `"stat-circles"`
- Level: atom. Category: poster.
- An ECharts chart built with `defineChart`: accepts every common chart prop (data, transform, title, highlight, annotations, ...).

### When to use

The poster way to show two to six related magnitudes whose rough proportion is the point: kilograms per person in three countries, the same quantity in three years, a total and its parts set side by side.

### Avoid

More than six values or values that need precise comparison (use bar-chart); a single number (use big-number); many circles of one whole (use circle-pack); values close together, where areas look the same (use bar-chart or dumbbell-chart).

### Install

From npm (the component ships in the package):

```bash
npm install insightcharts echarts
```

Or copy the source into your project with the shadcn CLI, so you can edit it (the engine still comes from the `insightcharts` package):

```bash
npx shadcn@latest registry add @insightcharts=https://insightcharts.dev/r/{name}.json   # once per project
npx shadcn@latest add @insightcharts/stat-circles
```

The file lands at `components/insightcharts/atoms/stat-circles.tsx`. `@insightcharts/stat-circles-demo` adds a ready-made example next to it.

### Usage

```tsx
import { StatCircles } from "insightcharts";

const data = [
  { who: "per person in the United States", kg: 124 },
  { who: "per person in Brazil", kg: 100 },
  { who: "per person in China", kg: 63 },
  { who: "per person in India", kg: 6 },
];

<StatCircles
  theme="dusk"
  data={data}
  name="who"
  value="kg"
  unit="kg"
  title="Meat supply in the United States was 124 kg per person in 2021"
  subtitle="Meat supply per person per year, kilograms, 2021"
  source="FAO food balance sheets"
  note="Rounded, approximate figures for illustration"
/>
```

### JSON spec

The same thing as data, rendered with `<Insight spec={spec} />`:

```json
{
  "theme": "dusk",
  "type": "stat-circles",
  "data": [
    { "who": "per person in the United States", "kg": 124 },
    { "who": "per person in Brazil", "kg": 100 },
    { "who": "per person in China", "kg": 63 },
    { "who": "per person in India", "kg": 6 }
  ],
  "name": "who",
  "value": "kg",
  "unit": "kg",
  "title": "Meat supply in the United States was 124 kg per person in 2021",
  "subtitle": "Meat supply per person per year, kilograms, 2021",
  "source": "FAO food balance sheets",
  "note": "Rounded, approximate figures for illustration"
}
```

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` (required) | `string` |  | Label field: the short text under or beside each circle. |
| `value` (required) | `string` |  | Value field: circle area, and the number printed large. Non-positive values are dropped. |
| `unit` | `string` |  | Unit printed small after each number, e.g. "kg". Leave out when `format` already includes it. |
| `layout` | `"row" \| "steps" \| "nested"` | `"row"` | Circles centred on one line, standing on a shared baseline, or drawn inside each other from a shared lowest point. Narrow containers stack a row or steps into a column. |
| `colorBy` | `"item" \| "value" \| "single"` | `"item"` | A colour per circle, a shade by value along the sequential ramp, or the accent for all. |
| `icon` | `string \| Record<string, string>` |  | Icon above the number in large circles: one for all, or a map from label to icon. Built-in name or `path://`. |

### Common props

Also accepts every prop in the "Common chart props" section of this file.

### Composition

- Composes: nothing (it is a primitive)
- Used by: [atlas-poster](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/atlas-poster.md), [ranking-poster](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/ranking-poster.md), [scale-poster](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/scale-poster.md)

### More examples

#### Nested, shaded by value

```tsx

  { what: "litres to grow one kilogram of beef", litres: 15400 },
  { what: "litres for one kilogram of cheese", litres: 5060 },
  { what: "litres for one kilogram of rice", litres: 2500 },
  { what: "litres for one kilogram of potatoes", litres: 290 },
];

<StatCircles
  data={data}
  name="what"
  value="litres"
  layout="nested"
  colorBy="value"
  format="integer"
  title="One kilogram of beef takes 15,400 litres of water to produce"
  subtitle="Water footprint of four foods, litres per kilogram, global average"
  source="Water Footprint Network"
  note="Rounded, approximate figures for illustration"
/>
```

#### Steps, with icons, highlight and click to select

```tsx

  { year: "trees planted in 2021", trees: 1200 },
  { year: "trees planted in 2022", trees: 2900 },
  { year: "trees planted in 2023", trees: 5100 },
  { year: "trees planted in 2024", trees: 8400 },
```

```tsx
    item: "tonnes of household waste collected at the kerbside each week across the whole metropolitan area",

  },

  subtitle="Household waste by destination, tonnes per week"
  note="Illustrative figures for an invented city"
/>
```

## Stat tile (`stat-tile`)

> A compact KPI tile: label, value, change against a baseline and an optional graphic. Twenty variants display the same data as a card, a trend, progress toward a target, a comparison, a breakdown, a rank or a count of icons.

- Component: `StatTile` (import from `insightcharts`)
- Spec type: `"stat-tile"`
- Level: atom. Category: figure.
- An HTML component: it takes only the props listed below, plus `theme`, `mode`, `className` and `style` where its source declares them. It does not take the common chart props.

### When to use

Dashboard grids and KPI rows of three to six figures. Pass the data once (`value`, `delta`, `series`, `target`, `parts`, `icon`) and choose the display with `variant`; change `surface`, `tone` and `size` to set emphasis. Give every tile a delta or a context line.

### Avoid

The single number a story leads with (use `big-number` with `size: "hero"`). Do not put a full chart with axes in the trend slot. Use `unit` only for counts up to 60 icons.

### Install

From npm (the component ships in the package):

```bash
npm install insightcharts echarts
```

Or copy the source into your project with the shadcn CLI, so you can edit it (the engine still comes from the `insightcharts` package):

```bash
npx shadcn@latest registry add @insightcharts=https://insightcharts.dev/r/{name}.json   # once per project
npx shadcn@latest add @insightcharts/stat-tile
```

The file lands at `components/insightcharts/atoms/stat-tile.tsx`. `@insightcharts/stat-tile-demo` adds a ready-made example next to it.

### Usage

```tsx
import { StatTile } from "insightcharts";

<StatTile
  label="Monthly active users"
  value={48210}
  format="compact"
  delta={0.083}
  deltaLabel="vs September"
  trend={[38.1, 39.4, 39, 40.8, 42.2, 41.9, 43.5, 44.1, 44.5, 46, 47.2, 48.2]}
  style={{ maxWidth: 300 }}
/>
```

### JSON spec

The same thing as data, rendered with `<Insight spec={spec} />`:

```json
{
  "type": "stat-tile",
  "label": "Monthly active users",
  "value": 48210,
  "format": "compact",
  "delta": 0.083,
  "deltaLabel": "vs September",
  "trend": [38.1, 39.4, 39, 40.8, 42.2, 41.9, 43.5, 44.1, 44.5, 46, 47.2, 48.2],
  "style": { "maxWidth": 300 }
}
```

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `label` (required) | `string` |  | What it measures, sentence case. |
| `value` (required) | `number \| string` |  | The figure. Numbers are formatted with `format`. `progress`, `ring` and `unit` need a number. |
| `delta` | `number \| string` |  | Change against a baseline. Numbers render as signed percentages (0.12 is +12%). `comparison` computes it from `value` and `comparison` when omitted. |
| `deltaLabel` | `string` |  | What the delta is against, e.g. "vs last month". |
| `upIsGood` | `boolean` | `true` | Whether an increase is an improvement. Sets the delta colour; the arrow and sign always show the direction. |
| `context` | `string` |  | A line that states a comparison or reference for the number. |
| `variant` | `"plain" \| "borderless" \| "filled" \| "tinted" \| "outline-accent" \| "sparkline" \| "area" \| "bars" \| "dots" \| "progress" \| "ring" \| "comparison" \| "delta-first" \| "icon" \| "unit" \| "breakdown" \| "rank" \| "split" \| "compact" \| "hero"` | `"plain"` | The display. Grounds: `plain` (bordered card), `borderless`, `filled` (solid tone with contrasting ink), `tinted` (10% wash), `outline-accent` (a 2px rule on one edge). Trends, from `series`: `sparkline` (line), `area` (filled, edge to edge along the bottom, zero-based), `bars` (columns, zero-based), `dots`, `split` (figure left, line in a tinted panel right), `compact` (one line: label, small line, value, change). Goals, from `target` or `max`: `progress` (bar with the target marked), `ring`. Others: `comparison` (needs `comparison`: two labelled bars), `delta-first` (the change is the large figure), `icon` (needs `icon`: a tinted badge), `unit` (the count as repeated icons, up to 60), `breakdown` (needs `parts`: a segmented bar with a key), `rank` (needs `rank`: "3rd of 12" with a position strip), `hero` (a numeral of 40 to 96px). A variant whose data is missing renders as `plain`. |
| `surface` | `"plain" \| "borderless" \| "filled" \| "tinted" \| "outline-accent"` |  | The ground, independent of the display, so any variant can sit on any ground: `variant: "sparkline", surface: "filled"`. Default: the variant's own, otherwise `plain`. |
| `tone` | `"neutral" \| "accent" \| "positive" \| "negative" \| number` | `"accent"` | Colour of the graphic and of a filled or tinted ground. A number picks from the theme's categorical palette, 0-based. `neutral` is ink. |
| `size` | `"sm" \| "md" \| "lg"` | `"md"` | Type and padding scale: 22, 28 or 36px numerals with 12, 16 or 20px padding. The numeral shrinks to fit a narrow tile. |
| `align` | `"left" \| "center" \| "right"` | `"left"` | Text alignment. |
| `orientation` | `"vertical" \| "horizontal"` |  | Graphic under the figure or beside it, for `sparkline`, `bars`, `dots`, `ring` and `icon`. Default `vertical`, `horizontal` for `ring`. Falls back to vertical under about 250px (180px for `ring` and `icon`). |
| `series` | `number[]` |  | Past values in time order, oldest first, ending with the current value, in the units of `value`. A numeric `trend` array is used when `series` is omitted. |
| `target` | `number` |  | The goal for `value`, marked on `progress` and `ring`. |
| `targetLabel` | `string` | `"Target"` | Name for the target. |
| `max` | `number` |  | End of the scale for `progress` and `ring`, and the total count drawn by `unit`. Default: the target, or 1 for a share. |
| `comparison` | `number \| string` |  | The value compared with, for `comparison`: a previous period or a peer. |
| `comparisonLabel` | `string` | `"Before"` | Names the comparison value, e.g. "September". |
| `valueLabel` | `string` | `"Now"` | Names the current value in `comparison`, e.g. "December". |
| `parts` | `{ label: string; value: number }[]` |  | What the value is made of, for `breakdown`. Should sum to `value`. Past six parts the smallest fold into Other. |
| `icon` | `IconInput` |  | A built-in icon name or `path://...`, for `icon` and `unit`. `unit` defaults to `circle`. |
| `unitValue` | `number` | `1` | What one icon stands for in `unit`. A caption states it when it is not 1. |
| `rank` | `number` |  | Position in a ranking, 1 is first, for `rank`. |
| `rankOf` | `number` |  | Number of entries ranked. Up to 32 are drawn as one segment each. |
| `edge` | `"left" \| "top"` | `"left"` | Which edge carries the rule on an `outline-accent` surface. |
| `trend` | `Slot \| number[]` |  | A chart spec, a React element, or an array of numbers drawn as a sparkline. Works in every variant that does not draw `series` itself. |
| `trendPosition` | `"bottom" \| "right"` | `"bottom"` | Where the trend slot sits; `right` falls back to `bottom` in narrow tiles. |
| `format` | `FormatSpec` | `"auto"` | Number format for `value`, `target`, `max`, `comparison` and `series`. |
| `theme` | `ThemeInput` |  | A theme name such as `"ledger"`, or token overrides. A named theme paints its own ground behind the tile. |
| `frame` | `boolean` |  | Set false to stop a named theme painting its ground. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` |  | Extra content at the bottom of the tile. |

### Composition

- Composes: nothing (it is a primitive)
- Used by: [before-after](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/before-after.md), [kpi-grid](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/kpi-grid.md), [metric-breakdown](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/metric-breakdown.md), [section](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/section.md), [stat-row](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/stat-row.md), [trend-card](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/trend-card.md), [timeline-story](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/timeline-story.md)

## Step marker (`step-marker`)

> A numbered chapter or step heading ("01 — Electricity sources in 2015") for sequencing the sections of a story.

- Component: `StepMarker` (import from `insightcharts`)
- Spec type: `"step-marker"`
- Level: atom. Category: text.
- An HTML component: it takes only the props listed below, plus `theme`, `mode`, `className` and `style` where its source declares them. It does not take the common chart props.

### When to use

When a piece has three to seven ordered chapters or steps. Open each one with a marker so the reader can see the position in the sequence.

### Avoid

Unordered sections (use `headline` with `size: "section"`), or numbering a list of items inside a paragraph.

### Install

From npm (the component ships in the package):

```bash
npm install insightcharts echarts
```

Or copy the source into your project with the shadcn CLI, so you can edit it (the engine still comes from the `insightcharts` package):

```bash
npx shadcn@latest registry add @insightcharts=https://insightcharts.dev/r/{name}.json   # once per project
npx shadcn@latest add @insightcharts/step-marker
```

The file lands at `components/insightcharts/atoms/step-marker.tsx`. `@insightcharts/step-marker-demo` adds a ready-made example next to it.

### Usage

```tsx
import { StepMarker } from "insightcharts";

<StepMarker
  theme="mono"
  step={1}
  title="Electricity sources in 2015"
  text="Europe's electricity generation by source in 2015."
  size="lg"
/>
```

### JSON spec

The same thing as data, rendered with `<Insight spec={spec} />`:

```json
{
  "type": "step-marker",
  "theme": "mono",
  "step": 1,
  "title": "Electricity sources in 2015",
  "text": "Europe's electricity generation by source in 2015.",
  "size": "lg"
}
```

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `step` (required) | `number \| string` |  | Step number, zero-padded to two digits. Strings are shown as written. |
| `title` (required) | `string` |  | The chapter or step title. |
| `total` | `number` |  | Total steps; the marker then reads "02 / 05". |
| `text` | `string` |  | A sentence under the title. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` |  | JSX alternative to `text`. |
| `level` | `1 \| 2 \| 3 \| 4 \| 5 \| 6` | `2` | Heading level. |
| `size` | `"md" \| "lg"` | `"md"` | `lg` for chapter openers. |
| `layout` | `"inline" \| "stacked"` | `"inline"` | Number beside or above the title. Narrow containers always stack. |
| `rule` | `boolean` | `false` | Hairline above the marker. |
| `frame` | `boolean` |  | Paint a named theme's background behind the block, with padding and rounded corners. On by default for a named theme with its own surface; `false` turns it off. |

### Composition

- Composes: nothing (it is a primitive)
- Used by: [annotated-timeline](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/annotated-timeline.md), [section](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/section.md), [explainer](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/explainer.md), [visual-essay](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/visual-essay.md)

### More examples

#### With total and rule

```tsx
import { StepMarker } from "insightcharts";

<StepMarker
  step={2}
  total={5}
  title="Solar module costs fell 82% in eight years"
  text="Average module cost per watt in each year."
  rule
/>
```

#### Stacked

```tsx
import { StepMarker } from "insightcharts";

<StepMarker
  theme="poster"
  step={3}
  title="Hours in which midday solar generation exceeded demand on the grid, by month and country"
  layout="stacked"
  size="lg"
/>
```

#### Rule on a painted ground

```tsx
import { StepMarker } from "insightcharts";

<StepMarker
  theme="sunrise"
  step={4}
  total={5}
  title="Wind supplied 17% of Europe's electricity in 2024"
  text="Share of electricity generation by source, 2024."
  rule
/>
```

#### Letter step, title only

```tsx
import { StepMarker } from "insightcharts";

<StepMarker theme="forest" step="B" title="Factors excluded from the forecast" level={3} />
```

- Spec schema: https://insightcharts.dev/schema/insight-spec.json

## Strip plot (`strip-plot`)

> Shows every observation as a tick or dot along a value axis, one row per category.

- Component: `StripPlot` (import from `insightcharts`)
- Spec type: `"strip-plot"`
- Level: atom. Category: distribution.
- An ECharts chart built with `defineChart`: accepts every common chart prop (data, transform, title, highlight, annotations, ...).

### When to use

Comparing the spread and clustering of a numeric value across 2 to about 15 categories when there are few enough observations to show each one; many rows with few to a few hundred observations each.

### Avoid

A single group where the shape matters (use histogram or beeswarm-chart); when individual points must be identifiable or coloured (use beeswarm-chart); when only quartiles matter (use box-plot).

### Install

From npm (the component ships in the package):

```bash
npm install insightcharts echarts
```

Or copy the source into your project with the shadcn CLI, so you can edit it (the engine still comes from the `insightcharts` package):

```bash
npx shadcn@latest registry add @insightcharts=https://insightcharts.dev/r/{name}.json   # once per project
npx shadcn@latest add @insightcharts/strip-plot
```

The file lands at `components/insightcharts/atoms/strip-plot.tsx`. `@insightcharts/strip-plot-demo` adds a ready-made example next to it.

### Usage

```tsx
  { day: "Mon", minutes: 42 },
```

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `value` (required) | `string` |  | Numeric field positioning each mark. |
| `group` (required) | `string` |  | Category field: one row per distinct value. |
| `label` | `string` |  | Field naming each observation, for the tooltip. |
| `mark` | `"tick" \| "dot"` | `"tick"` | Thin vertical ticks (a barcode) or translucent dots. |
| `median` | `boolean` | `false` | Heavier tick at each row's median, with its value printed. |
| `sort` | `"none" \| "asc" \| "desc"` | `"none"` | Order rows by median. |
| `jitter` | `boolean` | `false` | Deterministic vertical spread for dots, to relieve overplotting. |

### Common props

Also accepts every prop in the "Common chart props" section of this file.

### Composition

- Composes: nothing (it is a primitive)
- Used by: no molecule or template yet

## Timeline chart (`timeline-chart`)

> Places events and spans on a time axis in labelled lanes, with each item named directly.

- Component: `TimelineChart` (import from `insightcharts`)
- Spec type: `"timeline-chart"`
- Level: atom. Category: trend.
- An ECharts chart built with `defineChart`: accepts every common chart prop (data, transform, title, highlight, annotations, ...).

### When to use

When things happened and how long they lasted: project phases, terms of office, product launches, the sequence of events in a story. Mix spans (start and end) with point milestones (start only).

### Avoid

A measured value changing over time (use line-chart, with annotations for the events); more than about 40 items (filter, or split into several timelines); durations to be compared precisely with no interest in when (use bar-chart).

### Install

From npm (the component ships in the package):

```bash
npm install insightcharts echarts
```

Or copy the source into your project with the shadcn CLI, so you can edit it (the engine still comes from the `insightcharts` package):

```bash
npx shadcn@latest registry add @insightcharts=https://insightcharts.dev/r/{name}.json   # once per project
npx shadcn@latest add @insightcharts/timeline-chart
```

The file lands at `components/insightcharts/atoms/timeline-chart.tsx`. `@insightcharts/timeline-chart-demo` adds a ready-made example next to it.

### Usage

```tsx
import { TimelineChart } from "insightcharts";

const data = [
  { mission: "Mercury", programme: "Crewed programmes", from: "1958-10", to: "1963-05" },
  { mission: "Gemini", programme: "Crewed programmes", from: "1961-12", to: "1966-11" },
  { mission: "Apollo", programme: "Crewed programmes", from: "1961-05", to: "1972-12" },
  { mission: "Skylab", programme: "Crewed programmes", from: "1973-05", to: "1974-02" },
  { mission: "Shuttle development", programme: "Crewed programmes", from: "1972-01", to: "1981-04" },
  { mission: "Glenn orbits Earth", programme: "Milestones", from: "1962-02-20" },
  { mission: "Apollo 1 fire", programme: "Milestones", from: "1967-01-27" },
  { mission: "First Moon landing", programme: "Milestones", from: "1969-07-20" },
  { mission: "Apollo-Soyuz", programme: "Milestones", from: "1975-07-15" },
  { mission: "First Shuttle flight", programme: "Milestones", from: "1981-04-12" },
];

<TimelineChart
  theme="editorial"
  data={data}
  name="mission"
  start="from"
  end="to"
  lane="programme"
  highlight={["Apollo", "First Moon landing"]}
  title="The Apollo programme ran from May 1961 to December 1972"
  subtitle="NASA human spaceflight programmes and milestones, 1958 to 1981"
  source="NASA History Office"
  note="Figures are approximate, for illustration"
/>
```

### JSON spec

The same thing as data, rendered with `<Insight spec={spec} />`:

```json

    { "mission": "Gemini", "programme": "Crewed programmes", "from": "1961-12", "to": "1966-11" },
    { "mission": "Apollo", "programme": "Crewed programmes", "from": "1961-05", "to": "1972-12" },
    { "mission": "Skylab", "programme": "Crewed programmes", "from": "1973-05", "to": "1974-02" },
    {
      "mission": "Shuttle development",
      "programme": "Crewed programmes",
      "from": "1972-01",
      "to": "1981-04"
    },
    { "mission": "Glenn orbits Earth", "programme": "Milestones", "from": "1962-02-20" },
    { "mission": "Apollo 1 fire", "programme": "Milestones", "from": "1967-01-27" },
    { "mission": "First Moon landing", "programme": "Milestones", "from": "1969-07-20" },
    { "mission": "Apollo-Soyuz", "programme": "Milestones", "from": "1975-07-15" },
    { "mission": "First Shuttle flight", "programme": "Milestones", "from": "1981-04-12" }
  ],
  "name": "mission",
  "start": "from",
  "end": "to",
  "lane": "programme",
  "highlight": ["Apollo", "First Moon landing"],
  "title": "The Apollo programme ran from May 1961 to December 1972",
  "subtitle": "NASA human spaceflight programmes and milestones, 1958 to 1981",
  "source": "NASA History Office",
  "note": "Figures are approximate, for illustration"
}
```

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` (required) | `string` |  | Label field: what the event or span is. |
| `start` (required) | `string` |  | Start field: ISO date, year or timestamp. |
| `end` | `string` |  | End field. Rows without an end are point milestones. |
| `lane` | `string` |  | Field that groups rows into labelled lanes. |
| `precision` | `"year" \| "month" \| "day"` |  | Date precision in tooltips. Default: chosen from the span of the data. |

### Common props

Also accepts every prop in the "Common chart props" section of this file.

### Composition

- Composes: nothing (it is a primitive)
- Used by: [timeline-story](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/timeline-story.md)

## Treemap (`treemap`)

> Shows parts of a whole as nested rectangles sized by value, optionally grouped into categories.

- Component: `Treemap` (import from `insightcharts`)
- Spec type: `"treemap"`
- Level: atom. Category: part-to-whole.
- An ECharts chart built with `defineChart`: accepts every common chart prop (data, transform, title, highlight, annotations, ...).

### When to use

Many parts (10 to 100) of very different sizes, or a two-level hierarchy, where the reader needs the largest parts rather than exact comparison: budgets, market capitalisation, export baskets.

### Avoid

Fewer than about 6 parts or values that need precise comparison (use bar-chart); 2 to 5 parts (use donut-chart or segmented-bar); values that can be negative (use bar-chart); change over time (use line-chart).

### Install

From npm (the component ships in the package):

```bash
npm install insightcharts echarts
```

Or copy the source into your project with the shadcn CLI, so you can edit it (the engine still comes from the `insightcharts` package):

```bash
npx shadcn@latest registry add @insightcharts=https://insightcharts.dev/r/{name}.json   # once per project
npx shadcn@latest add @insightcharts/treemap
```

The file lands at `components/insightcharts/atoms/treemap.tsx`. `@insightcharts/treemap-demo` adds a ready-made example next to it.

### Usage

```tsx
import { Treemap } from "insightcharts";

const data = [
  { sector: "Energy", source: "Electricity and heat", gt: 15.8 },
  { sector: "Energy", source: "Transport", gt: 8.4 },
  { sector: "Energy", source: "Manufacturing and construction", gt: 6.3 },
  { sector: "Energy", source: "Buildings", gt: 3 },
  { sector: "Energy", source: "Fugitive emissions", gt: 3.3 },
  { sector: "Agriculture", source: "Livestock and manure", gt: 3.5 },
  { sector: "Agriculture", source: "Soils and rice", gt: 2.4 },
  { sector: "Industry", source: "Cement", gt: 1.6 },
  { sector: "Industry", source: "Chemicals and other", gt: 1.6 },
  { sector: "Waste", source: "Landfill and wastewater", gt: 1.7 },
  { sector: "Land use", source: "Deforestation and land-use change", gt: 1.4 },
];

<Treemap
  theme="paper"
  data={data}
  group="sector"
  name="source"
  value="gt"
  format="{value} Gt"
  title="Energy produced 75% of global greenhouse gas emissions in 2021"
  subtitle="Global emissions by sector and source, billion tonnes of CO2 equivalent, 2021"
  source="Climate Watch, World Resources Institute"
  note="Rounded, approximate figures for illustration"
/>
```

### JSON spec

The same thing as data, rendered with `<Insight spec={spec} />`:

```json
{
  "theme": "paper",
  "type": "treemap",
  "data": [
    { "sector": "Energy", "source": "Electricity and heat", "gt": 15.8 },
    { "sector": "Energy", "source": "Transport", "gt": 8.4 },
    { "sector": "Energy", "source": "Manufacturing and construction", "gt": 6.3 },
    { "sector": "Energy", "source": "Buildings", "gt": 3 },
    { "sector": "Energy", "source": "Fugitive emissions", "gt": 3.3 },
    { "sector": "Agriculture", "source": "Livestock and manure", "gt": 3.5 },
    { "sector": "Agriculture", "source": "Soils and rice", "gt": 2.4 },
    { "sector": "Industry", "source": "Cement", "gt": 1.6 },
    { "sector": "Industry", "source": "Chemicals and other", "gt": 1.6 },
    { "sector": "Waste", "source": "Landfill and wastewater", "gt": 1.7 },
    { "sector": "Land use", "source": "Deforestation and land-use change", "gt": 1.4 }
  ],
  "group": "sector",
  "name": "source",
  "value": "gt",
  "format": "{value} Gt",
  "title": "Energy produced 75% of global greenhouse gas emissions in 2021",
  "subtitle": "Global emissions by sector and source, billion tonnes of CO2 equivalent, 2021",
  "source": "Climate Watch, World Resources Institute",
  "note": "Rounded, approximate figures for illustration"
}
```

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` (required) | `string` |  | Leaf name field: one tile per row. |
| `value` (required) | `string` |  | Value field: tile area. Non-positive values are dropped. |
| `group` | `string` |  | Parent field. Rows sharing a group are drawn together and share a colour. |
| `labels` | `boolean` | `true` | Print the value under the name where the tile is big enough. |
| `groupLabels` | `boolean` |  | Heading strip above each group. Default: on when `group` is set and not compact. |
| `names` | `Record<string, string>` |  | Display names for group keys. |

### Common props

Also accepts every prop in the "Common chart props" section of this file.

### Composition

- Composes: nothing (it is a primitive)
- Used by: [poster](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/poster.md), [atlas-poster](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/atlas-poster.md), [explainer](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/explainer.md), [flow-poster](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/flow-poster.md), [ranking-poster](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/ranking-poster.md)

## Unit blocks (`unit-blocks`)

> Shows the size of each group as a solid block of small icons, one icon per fixed number of units.

- Component: `UnitBlocks` (import from `insightcharts`)
- Spec type: `"unit-blocks"`
- Level: atom. Category: poster.
- An ECharts chart built with `defineChart`: accepts every common chart prop (data, transform, title, highlight, annotations, ...).

### When to use

Large counts of people or things in 2 to 12 groups, where the reader should see the crowd itself: 20,350 marathon finishers by age group, one figure per 10 runners.

### Avoid

Precise comparison of close values (use block-bar or bar-chart); fewer than about 30 icons per group (use pictogram-chart or icon-array-grid); shares of one whole (use waffle-chart).

### Install

From npm (the component ships in the package):

```bash
npm install insightcharts echarts
```

Or copy the source into your project with the shadcn CLI, so you can edit it (the engine still comes from the `insightcharts` package):

```bash
npx shadcn@latest registry add @insightcharts=https://insightcharts.dev/r/{name}.json   # once per project
npx shadcn@latest add @insightcharts/unit-blocks
```

The file lands at `components/insightcharts/atoms/unit-blocks.tsx`. `@insightcharts/unit-blocks-demo` adds a ready-made example next to it.

### Usage

```tsx
import { UnitBlocks } from "insightcharts";

const data = [
  { age: "Under 30", finishers: 4180 },
  { age: "30 to 39", finishers: 6920 },
  { age: "40 to 49", finishers: 5340 },
  { age: "50 to 59", finishers: 2760 },
  { age: "60 and over", finishers: 1150 },
];

<UnitBlocks
  theme="noir"
  data={data}
  name="age"
  value="finishers"
  unit={10}
  unitLabel="10 finishers"
  format="integer"
  title="6,920 of the 20,350 finishers were aged 30 to 39"
  subtitle="Finishers of the Lakeshore Marathon by age group, 2025"
  source="Illustrative data"
  note="Invented figures for a fictional race"
/>
```

### JSON spec

The same thing as data, rendered with `<Insight spec={spec} />`:

```json
{
  "theme": "noir",
  "type": "unit-blocks",
  "data": [
    { "age": "Under 30", "finishers": 4180 },
    { "age": "30 to 39", "finishers": 6920 },
    { "age": "40 to 49", "finishers": 5340 },
    { "age": "50 to 59", "finishers": 2760 },
    { "age": "60 and over", "finishers": 1150 }
  ],
  "name": "age",
  "value": "finishers",
  "unit": 10,
  "unitLabel": "10 finishers",
  "format": "integer",
  "title": "6,920 of the 20,350 finishers were aged 30 to 39",
  "subtitle": "Finishers of the Lakeshore Marathon by age group, 2025",
  "source": "Illustrative data",
  "note": "Invented figures for a fictional race"
}
```

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` (required) | `string` |  | Group field: one block of icons per row of data. |
| `value` (required) | `string` |  | Value field: the quantity each block counts out. |
| `unit` | `number` |  | Units per icon. Default: a round number that gives about 2,000 icons in total. |
| `unitLabel` | `string` |  | What one icon stands for, for the key line, e.g. "10 finishers". |
| `icon` | `IconName \| "path://..."` | `"person"` | Built-in icon name or a custom single SVG path. |
| `series` | `string` |  | Field that colours the blocks. Default: one colour per group, up to eight groups. |
| `layout` | `"packed" \| "columns"` | `"packed"` | `packed`: equal block heights, widths follow the counts. `columns`: equal widths, blocks grow upwards from a baseline. |
| `columns` | `number` |  | Blocks per line in the `columns` layout. Default: all, two on a phone. |
| `iconSize` | `number` |  | Icon height in px. Default: the largest that fits, chosen per chart. To put two charts on one scale, give both the same `unit` and `iconSize`: the icon size, the gaps and the worth of an icon are then identical and the chart takes the height it needs. |
| `sort` | `"none" \| "asc" \| "desc"` | `"none"` | Order of the blocks. |

### Common props

Also accepts every prop in the "Common chart props" section of this file.

### Composition

- Composes: nothing (it is a primitive)
- Used by: [count-poster](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/count-poster.md)

## Waffle chart (`waffle-chart`)

> Shows shares of a whole as counted cells in a grid, such as 37 in every 100.

- Component: `WaffleChart` (import from `insightcharts`)
- Spec type: `"waffle-chart"`
- Level: atom. Category: part-to-whole.
- An ECharts chart built with `defineChart`: accepts every common chart prop (data, transform, title, highlight, annotations, ...).

### When to use

One share ("37 in every 100") or a handful of categories that add up to a whole, where the reader should be able to count the units.

### Avoid

Comparing shares across several groups (use bar-chart with stack "percent"); more than about 6 categories or shares under 1% (use bar-chart); a compact inline part-to-whole (use segmented-bar).

### Install

From npm (the component ships in the package):

```bash
npm install insightcharts echarts
```

Or copy the source into your project with the shadcn CLI, so you can edit it (the engine still comes from the `insightcharts` package):

```bash
npx shadcn@latest registry add @insightcharts=https://insightcharts.dev/r/{name}.json   # once per project
npx shadcn@latest add @insightcharts/waffle-chart
```

The file lands at `components/insightcharts/atoms/waffle-chart.tsx`. `@insightcharts/waffle-chart-demo` adds a ready-made example next to it.

### Usage

```tsx
import { WaffleChart } from "insightcharts";

<WaffleChart
  theme="poster"
  data={[{ group: "Have never been online", share: 33 }]}
  name="group"
  value="share"
  total={100}
  restLabel="Use the internet"
  title="33% of the world's population had never used the internet in 2023"
  subtitle="Share of the global population, 2023. Each square is 1% of people"
  source="ITU Facts and Figures 2023"
  note="Figures are approximate, for illustration"
/>
```

### JSON spec

The same thing as data, rendered with `<Insight spec={spec} />`:

```json
{
  "theme": "poster",
  "type": "waffle-chart",
  "data": [{ "group": "Have never been online", "share": 33 }],
  "name": "group",
  "value": "share",
  "total": 100,
  "restLabel": "Use the internet",
  "title": "33% of the world's population had never used the internet in 2023",
  "subtitle": "Share of the global population, 2023. Each square is 1% of people",
  "source": "ITU Facts and Figures 2023",
  "note": "Figures are approximate, for illustration"
}
```

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `value` (required) | `string` |  | Value field. Each category's cells are its share of the whole. |
| `name` | `string` |  | Category field. Omit for a single share. |
| `total` | `number` |  | The whole. Default: the sum of the values. Set to 100 with one value to show a single share against an empty remainder. |
| `rows` | `number` | `10` | Grid rows. |
| `columns` | `number` | `10` | Grid columns. |
| `shape` | `"square" \| "circle"` | `"square"` | Cell shape. |
| `restLabel` | `string` |  | Label for the unfilled remainder when `total` exceeds the sum. |
| `names` | `Record<string, string>` |  | Display names for category keys. |

### Common props

Also accepts every prop in the "Common chart props" section of this file.

### Composition

- Composes: nothing (it is a primitive)
- Used by: [hero-figure](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/hero-figure.md), [poster](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/poster.md), [proportion-statement](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/proportion-statement.md), [small-multiple-grid](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/small-multiple-grid.md), [comparison-brief](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/comparison-brief.md), [social-card](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/social-card.md), [story-deck](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/story-deck.md), [timeline-story](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/timeline-story.md), [visual-essay](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/visual-essay.md)

### More examples

#### Several categories

```tsx

const data = [
  { source: "Coal", twh: 35.4 },
  { source: "Gas", twh: 22.5 },

  { source: "Nuclear", twh: 9.1 },
  { source: "Wind", twh: 7.8 },
  { source: "Solar", twh: 5.5 },
  { source: "Other", twh: 5.4 },
];

<WaffleChart
  data={data}
  name="source"
  value="twh"
  format="{value}%"
  title="Coal and gas generated 57.9% of the world's electricity in 2023"
  subtitle="Share of global electricity generation by source, 2023"
  source="Ember, Global Electricity Review 2024"
  note="Figures are approximate, for illustration"
/>
```

## Annotated timeline (`annotated-timeline`)

> A vertical sequence of dated events along a rail, each with a short explanation and, optionally, a small chart or figure.

- Component: `AnnotatedTimeline` (import from `insightcharts`)
- Spec type: `"annotated-timeline"`
- Level: molecule. Category: story.
- An HTML component: it takes only the props listed below, plus `theme`, `mode`, `className` and `style` where its source declares them. It does not take the common chart props.

### When to use

Telling how something unfolded when the events matter more than a continuous measure: a policy history, an incident, a product's milestones. Four to eight events; give a figure only to the ones where a number changed.

### Avoid

Events that should be read against a time scale, with gaps and overlaps to scale (use `timeline-chart`); a continuous series with a few annotated moments (use `line-chart` with `annotations`); ordered steps that are not dated (use `section` with `step`).

### Install

From npm (the component ships in the package):

```bash
npm install insightcharts echarts
```

Or copy the source into your project with the shadcn CLI, so you can edit it (the engine still comes from the `insightcharts` package):

```bash
npx shadcn@latest registry add @insightcharts=https://insightcharts.dev/r/{name}.json   # once per project
npx shadcn@latest add @insightcharts/annotated-timeline
```

The file lands at `components/insightcharts/molecules/annotated-timeline.tsx`. `@insightcharts/annotated-timeline-demo` adds a ready-made example next to it.

### Usage

```tsx
import { AnnotatedTimeline, BigNumber, Sparkline } from "insightcharts";

<AnnotatedTimeline
  theme="paper"
  title="The ECB raised its deposit rate from −0.5% to 4% between July 2022 and September 2023"
  subtitle="Euro area deposit facility rate and annual inflation, 2021 to 2024"
  events={[
    {
      date: "July 2021",
      title: "Inflation reaches 2.2%",
      text: "The ECB's target is 2%. The bank kept its deposit rate at −0.5%.",
    },
    {
      date: "July 2022",
      title: "The deposit rate rises from −0.5% to 0%",
      emphasis: true,
      text: "This was the ECB's first rate rise in eleven years. Inflation was 8.9%.",
      figure: <BigNumber value="8.9%" label="Annual inflation, July 2022" context="The target is 2%" />,
    },
    {
      date: "October 2022",
      title: "Inflation reaches 10.6%",
      text: "This was the highest monthly figure of 2022. The ECB raised rates by 0.75 points at each of two consecutive meetings.",
      figure: <Sparkline
        data={[
          { month: "2022-01", rate: 5.1 },
          { month: "2022-02", rate: 5.9 },
          { month: "2022-03", rate: 7.4 },
          { month: "2022-04", rate: 7.4 },
          { month: "2022-05", rate: 8.1 },
          { month: "2022-06", rate: 8.6 },
          { month: "2022-07", rate: 8.9 },
          { month: "2022-08", rate: 9.1 },
          { month: "2022-09", rate: 9.9 },
          { month: "2022-10", rate: 10.6 },
          { month: "2022-11", rate: 10.1 },
          { month: "2022-12", rate: 9.2 },
        ]}
        x="month"
        y="rate"
        format="{value}%"
        extremes
        showValue
        style={{ maxWidth: 260 }}
      />,
    },
    {
      date: "September 2023",
      title: "The deposit rate reaches 4%",
      text: "This was the tenth rise in a row. Inflation was 4.3%.",
    },
    {
      date: "June 2024",
      title: "The deposit rate is cut to 3.75%",
      emphasis: true,
      text: "The cut was 0.25 points. Inflation was 2.5%.",
    },
  ]}
  source="European Central Bank; Eurostat"
  note="Figures are approximate, for illustration"
/>
```
