### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `events` (required) | `{ date, title, text?, figure?, emphasis? }[]` |  | The events in reading order. `date` is shown as written; `figure` is a chart spec or element; `emphasis` fills the marker to mark the most important events. |
| `figurePosition` | `"below" \| "side"` | `"below"` | Where an event's figure sits; `side` falls back to `below` under 640px. |
| `level` | `2 \| 3 \| 4 \| 5 \| 6` | `3` | Heading level of the event titles. |
| `title` | `string` |  | The main fact with its number, or a plain label. |
| `subtitle` | `string` |  | Scope and period. |
| `source` | `string` |  | Shown under the timeline as "Source: ...". |
| `note` | `string` |  | Method note or caveat. |
| `theme` | `ThemeInput` |  | A built-in theme name (`editorial`, `ledger`, `noir`...) or a theme object, passed on to every event. A named theme with its own surface paints that surface behind the component. |
| `frame` | `boolean` |  | Paint the theme's surface behind the component. Default: on for a named theme with its own surface. |
| `mode` | `"auto" \| "system" \| "light" \| "dark"` | `"auto"` | Colour mode. |

### Composition

- Composes: [step-marker](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/step-marker.md), [prose](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/prose.md), [sparkline](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/sparkline.md), [big-number](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/big-number.md)
- Used by: [timeline-story](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/timeline-story.md)

```tsx
      figure: <BigNumber value="£7.20" label="Hourly rate, April 2016" />,
    },
    { date: "April 2021", title: "The age threshold falls to 23", text: "The rate was £8.91." },
    {
      date: "April 2024",
      title: "The rate rises to £11.44",
      emphasis: true,
      text: "The age threshold fell to 21. The rate was £10.42 in 2023.",
      figure: <BigNumber
        value="£11.44"
        label="Hourly rate, April 2024"
        delta="+9.8%"
        deltaLabel="vs 2023"
      />,
    },
    {
      date: "April 2025",
      title: "The rate rises to £12.21",
      text: "The rise was 6.7%.",
      figure: <BigNumber
        value="£12.21"
        label="Hourly rate, April 2025"
        delta="+6.7%"
        deltaLabel="vs 2024"
      />,
    },
  ]}
  source="Low Pay Commission"
/>
```

## Before and after (`before-after`)

> Two states of one measure side by side, as figures, stat tiles of any variant or small charts, with the change between them stated in the middle.

- Component: `BeforeAfter` (import from `insightcharts`)
- Spec type: `"before-after"`
- Level: molecule. Category: layout.
- An HTML component: it takes only the props listed below, plus `theme`, `mode`, `className` and `style` where its source declares them. It does not take the common chart props.

### When to use

A single measure at two moments or under two conditions: before and after a policy, control and treatment, last year and this. The change is computed from the two values unless you state it.

### Avoid

More than two states (use `line-chart` or `slope-chart`); many entities each with a before and after (use `dumbbell-chart` or `arrow-chart`); two unrelated figures (use `stat-row`).

### Install

From npm (the component ships in the package):

```bash
npm install insightcharts echarts
```

Or copy the source into your project with the shadcn CLI, so you can edit it (the engine still comes from the `insightcharts` package):

```bash
npx shadcn@latest registry add @insightcharts=https://insightcharts.dev/r/{name}.json   # once per project
npx shadcn@latest add @insightcharts/before-after
```

The file lands at `components/insightcharts/molecules/before-after.tsx`. `@insightcharts/before-after-demo` adds a ready-made example next to it.

### Usage

```tsx
import { BeforeAfter } from "insightcharts";

<BeforeAfter
  title="Solar module prices fell from $0.74 to $0.15 per watt between 2013 and 2023"
  subtitle="Average price of crystalline silicon modules, US dollars per watt"
  format={{ style: "currency", currency: "USD" }}
  before={{ heading: "2013", value: 0.74, label: "Per watt", context: "2013 average" }}
  after={{ heading: "2023", value: 0.15, label: "Per watt", context: "2023 average" }}
  deltaLabel="in ten years"
  upIsGood={false}
  source="IRENA Renewable Power Generation Costs 2023"
  note="Rounded, approximate figures for illustration"
/>
```

### JSON spec

The same thing as data, rendered with `<Insight spec={spec} />`:

```json
{
  "type": "before-after",
  "title": "Solar module prices fell from $0.74 to $0.15 per watt between 2013 and 2023",
  "subtitle": "Average price of crystalline silicon modules, US dollars per watt",
  "format": { "style": "currency", "currency": "USD" },
  "before": { "heading": "2013", "value": 0.74, "label": "Per watt", "context": "2013 average" },
  "after": { "heading": "2023", "value": 0.15, "label": "Per watt", "context": "2023 average" },
  "deltaLabel": "in ten years",
  "upIsGood": false,
  "source": "IRENA Renewable Power Generation Costs 2023",
  "note": "Rounded, approximate figures for illustration"
}
```

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `before` (required) | `{ heading?, value?, label?, context?, format?, chart?, variant?, surface?, tone?, series?, target?, targetLabel?, max?, parts?, icon?, unitValue?, rank?, rankOf?, orientation? }` |  | The first state: a figure, a chart slot, or both. The fields after `chart` apply when the states are tiles and are passed to `stat-tile`. |
| `after` (required) | `{ heading?, value?, label?, context?, format?, chart?, variant?, surface?, tone?, series?, target?, targetLabel?, max?, parts?, icon?, unitValue?, rank?, rankOf?, orientation? }` |  | The second state. |
| `variant` | `"plain" \| "tiles" \| StatTileVariant` | `"plain"` | `plain`: open `big-number` figures under a ruled heading. `tiles`: bordered `stat-tile` cards. Any `stat-tile` variant (`progress`, `ring`, `sparkline`, `area`, `bars`, `unit`, `breakdown`, `rank`, `icon`, `filled`, `tinted`, `hero`...) draws both states as that tile; a state's own `variant` overrides it. |
| `surface` | `"plain" \| "borderless" \| "filled" \| "tinted" \| "outline-accent"` |  | Tiles only: the ground of both tiles. |
| `emphasis` | `"after" \| "none"` | `"after"` | Tiles only: `after` draws the first state in neutral ink and the second in the accent; `none` draws both in the accent. A state's own `tone` overrides it. |
| `layout` | `"auto" \| "side" \| "stacked"` | `"auto"` | Side by side from 520px, or force one arrangement. |
| `deltaVariant` | `"text" \| "pill" \| "solid"` | `"pill"` | How the change between the states is set: passed to `delta`. |
| `arrow` | `boolean` | `true` | The arrow between the states. |
| `density` | `"dense" \| "default" \| "roomy"` | `"default"` | Spacing and tile scale (`sm`, `md`, `lg`). |
| `frame` | `boolean` |  | Set false to stop a named theme painting its ground. |
| `delta` | `number \| string` |  | The change stated between the two. Default: the relative change when both values are numbers. |
| `deltaLabel` | `string` |  | Words under the change, e.g. "in five years". |
| `deltaFormat` | `FormatSpec` | `signed percent` | Number format for a numeric `delta`. |
| `upIsGood` | `boolean` | `true` | Whether an increase is good news; decides the colour of the change. |
| `format` | `FormatSpec` | `"auto"` | Number format shared by both values. |
| `title` | `string` |  | The change stated plainly, with both values and the period. |
| `subtitle` | `string` |  | Measure and population. |
| `source` | `string` |  | Shown underneath as "Source: ...". |
| `note` | `string` |  | Method note or caveat. |
| `theme` | `ThemeInput` |  | A theme name such as `"editorial"`, or token overrides, passed on to both states. A named theme paints its own ground. |
| `mode` | `"auto" \| "system" \| "light" \| "dark"` | `"auto"` | Colour mode. |

### Composition

- Composes: [big-number](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/big-number.md), [stat-tile](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/stat-tile.md), [delta](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/delta.md), [bar-chart](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/bar-chart.md), [sparkline](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/sparkline.md)
- Used by: no molecule or template yet

## Chart with callout (`chart-callout`)

> A chart with a callout beside it that states the main fact. In narrow containers the callout goes underneath.

- Component: `ChartCallout` (import from `insightcharts`)
- Spec type: `"chart-callout"`
- Level: molecule. Category: layout.
- An HTML component: it takes only the props listed below, plus `theme`, `mode`, `className` and `style` where its source declares them. It does not take the common chart props.

### When to use

Whenever a chart needs its meaning stated in words next to it: the standard chart-plus-interpretation unit of a report. The chart's title states the main fact with its number. The callout adds a second fact, a cause or a caveat in plain words.

### Avoid

Repeating the chart title in the callout; long narration (put `prose` before the chart instead); a chart that is already a small tile (the callout would outweigh it).

### Install

From npm (the component ships in the package):

```bash
npm install insightcharts echarts
```

Or copy the source into your project with the shadcn CLI, so you can edit it (the engine still comes from the `insightcharts` package):

```bash
npx shadcn@latest registry add @insightcharts=https://insightcharts.dev/r/{name}.json   # once per project
npx shadcn@latest add @insightcharts/chart-callout
```

The file lands at `components/insightcharts/molecules/chart-callout.tsx`. `@insightcharts/chart-callout-demo` adds a ready-made example next to it.

### Usage

```tsx
import { ChartCallout, LineChart } from "insightcharts";

<ChartCallout
  theme="ledger"
  chart={<LineChart
    data={[
      { "2023": 4.4, "2024": 4.2, month: "Jan" },
      { "2023": 4.3, "2024": 4.3, month: "Feb" },
      { "2023": 4.4, "2024": 4.1, month: "Mar" },
      { "2023": 4.2, "2024": 3.6, month: "Apr" },
      { "2023": 4.3, "2024": 3.1, month: "May" },
      { "2023": 4.1, "2024": 2.9, month: "Jun" },
      { "2023": 4.2, "2024": 2.6, month: "Jul" },
      { "2023": 4.3, "2024": 2.4, month: "Aug" },
      { "2023": 4.1, "2024": 2.3, month: "Sep" },
      { "2023": 4.2, "2024": 2.2, month: "Oct" },
      { "2023": 4.3, "2024": 2.1, month: "Nov" },
      { "2023": 4.2, "2024": 2.1, month: "Dec" },
    ]}
    x="month"
    y={["2024", "2023"]}
    highlight="2024"
    contextLabels
    format="{value}%"
    zero
    height={280}
    title="Monthly churn fell from 4.2% to 2.1% in 2024"
    subtitle="Monthly customer churn, 2024 and 2023"
    source="Internal analytics"
    note="Illustrative data"
    annotations={[{ type: "line", axis: "x", value: "Mar", label: "New onboarding" }]}
  />}
  label="Takeaway"
  lead="Churn fell 2 points after March"
  body="Churn was 4.1% in March 2024, when the new onboarding launched. It was 2.1% in December 2024. It was 4.2% in December 2023."
/>
```

### JSON spec

The same thing as data, rendered with `<Insight spec={spec} />`:

```json
{
  "type": "chart-callout",
  "theme": "ledger",
  "chart": {
    "type": "line-chart",
    "data": [
      { "2023": 4.4, "2024": 4.2, "month": "Jan" },
      { "2023": 4.3, "2024": 4.3, "month": "Feb" },
      { "2023": 4.4, "2024": 4.1, "month": "Mar" },
      { "2023": 4.2, "2024": 3.6, "month": "Apr" },
      { "2023": 4.3, "2024": 3.1, "month": "May" },
      { "2023": 4.1, "2024": 2.9, "month": "Jun" },
      { "2023": 4.2, "2024": 2.6, "month": "Jul" },
      { "2023": 4.3, "2024": 2.4, "month": "Aug" },
      { "2023": 4.1, "2024": 2.3, "month": "Sep" },
      { "2023": 4.2, "2024": 2.2, "month": "Oct" },
      { "2023": 4.3, "2024": 2.1, "month": "Nov" },
      { "2023": 4.2, "2024": 2.1, "month": "Dec" }
    ],
    "x": "month",
    "y": ["2024", "2023"],
    "highlight": "2024",
    "contextLabels": true,
    "format": "{value}%",
    "zero": true,
    "height": 280,
    "title": "Monthly churn fell from 4.2% to 2.1% in 2024",
    "subtitle": "Monthly customer churn, 2024 and 2023",
    "source": "Internal analytics",
    "note": "Illustrative data",
    "annotations": [{ "type": "line", "axis": "x", "value": "Mar", "label": "New onboarding" }]
  },
  "label": "Takeaway",
  "lead": "Churn fell 2 points after March",
  "body": "Churn was 4.1% in March 2024, when the new onboarding launched. It was 2.1% in December 2024. It was 4.2% in December 2023."
}
```

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `chart` (required) | `Slot` |  | The chart: a spec or a React element. |
| `lead` | `string` |  | The main fact in a few words, with its number. Shown in bold. |
| `body` | `string` |  | One or two plain sentences that say what the fact means. |
| `tone` | `"neutral" \| "positive" \| "negative" \| "accent"` | `"accent"` | Sets the callout's icon and tint together. |
| `label` | `string` |  | Small label above the lead, e.g. "Takeaway" or "Caveat". |
| `side` | `"left" \| "right"` | `"right"` | Side of the chart the callout sits on. Under 640px it always goes underneath. |
| `variant` | `"plain" \| "soft" \| "outline"` | `"plain"` | `plain` separates the callout with a hairline; the others box it. |
| `align` | `"start" \| "center" \| "end"` | `"center"` | Vertical position of the callout beside the chart. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` |  | JSX alternative to `chart`. |
| `theme` | `ThemeInput` |  | A built-in theme name (`editorial`, `ledger`, `noir`...) or a theme object, passed on to the chart and callout. A named theme with its own surface paints that surface behind the component. |
| `frame` | `boolean` |  | Paint the theme's surface behind the component. Default: on for a named theme with its own surface. |
| `mode` | `"auto" \| "system" \| "light" \| "dark"` | `"auto"` | Colour mode. |

### Composition

- Composes: [callout](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/callout.md), [line-chart](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/line-chart.md), [bar-chart](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/bar-chart.md), [dumbbell-chart](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/dumbbell-chart.md), [slope-chart](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/slope-chart.md)
- Used by: [executive-brief](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/executive-brief.md), [visual-essay](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/visual-essay.md)

#### Positive, aligned to the top, science theme

```tsx
  theme="science"

  label="Result"
  lead="Kraków's annual PM2.5 fell from 31 to 19 µg/m³"
  body="All five cities recorded a lower annual mean in 2023 than in 2015. All five were above the WHO guideline of 5 µg/m³ in 2023."
  chart={<DumbbellChart
    data={[
      { city: "Kraków", y2015: 31, y2023: 19 },
      { city: "Milan", y2015: 29, y2023: 21 },
      { city: "Sofia", y2015: 26, y2023: 17 },
      { city: "Prague", y2015: 19, y2023: 13 },
      { city: "Vienna", y2015: 16, y2023: 11 },
    ]}
    category="city"
    from="y2015"
    to="y2023"
    names={{ y2015: "2015", y2023: "2023" }}
    format="{value}"
    sort="gap"
    highlight="Kraków"
    title="Annual PM2.5 fell in all five cities between 2015 and 2023"
    subtitle="Annual mean PM2.5 concentration, µg/m³, 2015 and 2023"
    source="European Environment Agency"
    note="Illustrative data"
  />}
/>
```

```tsx
    note="Illustrative data"
  />}
/>
```

## Chart tabs (`chart-tabs`)

> One chart frame with a segmented control that switches between several views of the same data, morphing between views that share a chart type.

- Component: `ChartTabs` (import from `insightcharts`)
- Spec type: `"chart-tabs"`
- Level: molecule. Category: layout.
- An HTML component: it takes only the props listed below, plus `theme`, `mode`, `className` and `style` where its source declares them. It does not take the common chart props.

### When to use

The same entities under two to five measures or scalings where each view changes the reading: total / per capita / change, absolute / share, linear / log. Give the frame a plain label as its title. Each view's `subtitle` names its measure.

### Avoid

Hiding the most important view behind a tab (show it first, or show both with `small-multiple-grid`); unrelated charts (give each its own figure); more than five views.

### Install

From npm (the component ships in the package):

```bash
npm install insightcharts echarts
```

Or copy the source into your project with the shadcn CLI, so you can edit it (the engine still comes from the `insightcharts` package):

```bash
npx shadcn@latest registry add @insightcharts=https://insightcharts.dev/r/{name}.json   # once per project
npx shadcn@latest add @insightcharts/chart-tabs
```

The file lands at `components/insightcharts/molecules/chart-tabs.tsx`. `@insightcharts/chart-tabs-demo` adds a ready-made example next to it.

### Usage

```tsx
import { BarChart, ChartTabs, registerComponents } from "insightcharts";

// Specs passed as data are resolved by name when rendered.
registerComponents({ BarChart });

<ChartTabs
  theme="mono"
  title="CO2 emissions of six large emitters, 2023"
  tabsPosition="below"
  chart={{
    type: "bar-chart",
    data: [
      { country: "China", total: 11.9, perCapita: 8.4, change: 0.38 },
      { country: "United States", total: 4.9, perCapita: 14.3, change: -0.13 },
      { country: "India", total: 3.1, perCapita: 2.1, change: 0.74 },
      { country: "Russia", total: 1.8, perCapita: 12.5, change: 0.1 },
      { country: "Japan", total: 1, perCapita: 8, change: -0.19 },
      { country: "Germany", total: 0.6, perCapita: 7.1, change: -0.28 },
    ],
    x: "country",
    y: "total",
    sort: "desc",
    orientation: "horizontal",
    height: 280,
    highlight: "China",
    format: "{value} Gt",
    subtitle: "CO2 emissions from fossil fuels, billion tonnes, 2023",
  }}
  views={[
    { label: "Total", id: "total" },
    {
      label: "Per capita",
      id: "per-capita",
      props: {
        y: "perCapita",
        highlight: "United States",
        format: "{value} t",
        subtitle: "CO2 emissions per person, tonnes, 2023",
      },
    },
    {
      label: "Change since 2010",
      id: "change",
      props: {
        y: "change",
        highlight: "India",
        format: "percent",
        subtitle: "Change in CO2 emissions, 2010 to 2023",
      },
    },
  ]}
  source="Global Carbon Budget 2024"
  note="Rounded, approximate figures for illustration"
/>
```

### JSON spec

The same thing as data, rendered with `<Insight spec={spec} />`:

```json
      { "country": "India", "total": 3.1, "perCapita": 2.1, "change": 0.74 },
      { "country": "Russia", "total": 1.8, "perCapita": 12.5, "change": 0.1 },
      { "country": "Japan", "total": 1, "perCapita": 8, "change": -0.19 },

    "orientation": "horizontal",
    "height": 280,

    "format": "{value} Gt",
    "subtitle": "CO2 emissions from fossil fuels, billion tonnes, 2023"
  },
  "views": [
    { "label": "Total", "id": "total" },
    {
      "label": "Per capita",
      "id": "per-capita",

        "y": "perCapita",
        "highlight": "United States",
```

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `chart` | `InsightSpec` |  | The base chart spec every view starts from: `{ type, data, ... }`. |
| `views` (required) | `{ label, id?, props?, chart? }[]` |  | Two to five views. `props` are merged over `chart`; or give a view its own complete `chart` slot. |
| `defaultView` | `string \| number` |  | The view shown first: an id, a label or an index. |
| `view` | `string \| number` |  | Controlled active view. |
| `onViewChange` | `(id, index) => void` |  | Called when the reader switches view. |
| `tabsLabel` | `string` | `"Chart view"` | Accessible name of the tab list. |
| `tabsPosition` | `"right" \| "below"` | `"right"` | Tabs beside the title or under it. Under 560px they always go underneath. |
| `title` | `string` |  | A plain label or fact that is true of every view. |
| `subtitle` | `string` |  | What the views share; each view's own `subtitle` names its measure. |
| `source` | `string` |  | Shown under the chart as "Source: ...". |
| `note` | `string` |  | Method note or caveat. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` |  | Extra content under the chart. |
| `theme` | `ThemeInput` |  | A built-in theme name (`editorial`, `ledger`, `noir`...) or a theme object, passed on to the chart. A named theme with its own surface paints that surface behind the component. |
| `frame` | `boolean` |  | Paint the theme's surface behind the component. Default: on for a named theme with its own surface. |
| `mode` | `"auto" \| "system" \| "light" \| "dark"` | `"auto"` | Colour mode. |

### Composition

- Composes: [bar-chart](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/bar-chart.md), [line-chart](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/line-chart.md)
- Used by: no molecule or template yet

## Comparison table (`comparison-table`)

> A table whose rows carry inline sparklines, deltas and in-cell bars beside their exact values, from rows and a column config.

- Component: `ComparisonTable` (import from `insightcharts`)
- Spec type: `"comparison-table"`
- Level: molecule. Category: layout.
- An HTML component: it takes only the props listed below, plus `theme`, `mode`, `className` and `style` where its source declares them. It does not take the common chart props.

### When to use

Comparing five to twenty entities on a level, a trend and a change at once: countries, products, teams. Readers look up their row. The sparkline and delta show how the value changed.

### Avoid

Plain lookups with no series (use `data-table`); one measure ranked (use `ranked-list` or `bar-chart`); trends the reader must compare precisely (use `small-multiples`). Each sparkline has its own scale, so it shows the direction of change and cannot be used to compare levels between rows.

### Install

From npm (the component ships in the package):

```bash
npm install insightcharts echarts
```

Or copy the source into your project with the shadcn CLI, so you can edit it (the engine still comes from the `insightcharts` package):

```bash
npx shadcn@latest registry add @insightcharts=https://insightcharts.dev/r/{name}.json   # once per project
npx shadcn@latest add @insightcharts/comparison-table
```

The file lands at `components/insightcharts/molecules/comparison-table.tsx`. `@insightcharts/comparison-table-demo` adds a ready-made example next to it.

### Usage

```tsx
import { ComparisonTable } from "insightcharts";

const data = [
  {
    "2019": 40.1,
    "2020": 44.2,
    "2021": 40.9,
    "2022": 44.5,
    "2023": 52.6,
    "2024": 58.9,
    country: "Germany",
    share: 58.9,
    twh: 498,
  },
  {
    "2019": 37.5,
    "2020": 44.1,
    "2021": 46.7,
    "2022": 42.2,
    "2023": 50.3,
    "2024": 56.8,
    country: "Spain",
    share: 56.8,
    twh: 264,
  },
  {
    "2019": 18.2,
    "2020": 26.1,
    "2021": 33,
    "2022": 40.1,
    "2023": 47.7,
    "2024": 52.4,
    country: "Netherlands",
    share: 52.4,
    twh: 121,
  },
  {
    "2019": 39.9,
    "2020": 41.7,
    "2021": 40.3,
    "2022": 35.6,
    "2023": 43.8,
    "2024": 49,
    country: "Italy",
    share: 49,
    twh: 264,
  },
  {
    "2019": 20.9,
    "2020": 24.2,
    "2021": 22.5,
    "2022": 24.4,
    "2023": 27,
    "2024": 28.3,
    country: "France",
    share: 28.3,
    twh: 536,
  },
  {
    "2019": 14.1,
    "2020": 17.2,
    "2021": 16.9,
    "2022": 20.6,
    "2023": 26.4,
    "2024": 29.5,
    country: "Poland",
    share: 29.5,
    twh: 167,
  },
];

<ComparisonTable
  title="The Netherlands' renewable share of electricity rose from 18.2% to 52.4% between 2019 and 2024"
  subtitle="Renewable share of electricity generation, selected EU countries, 2019 to 2024"
  data={data}
  columns={[
    { key: "country", label: "Country" },
    { key: "twh", label: "Generation, TWh", kind: "bar", format: "integer", hideBelow: 560 },
    { key: "share", label: "Share, 2024", format: "{value}%" },
    {
      key: "trend",
      label: "2019 to 2024",
      kind: "sparkline",
      fields: ["2019", "2020", "2021", "2022", "2023", "2024"],
      format: "{value}%",
    },
    {
      key: "change",
      label: "Change",
      kind: "delta",
      fields: ["2019", "2020", "2021", "2022", "2023", "2024"],
      change: "absolute",
      format: "{value} pts",
    },
  ]}
  sort={{ key: "share" }}
  highlight="Netherlands"
  source="Ember, European Electricity Review 2025"
  note="Rounded, illustrative"
/>
```

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `data` | `DataInput` |  | Wide data: one row per entity. Long data: one row per entity and period, with `groupBy`. Omit inside `<InsightData>`. |
| `transform` | `Transform \| Transform[]` |  | Applied before rows are grouped. |
| `columns` (required) | `(string \| { key, label?, kind?, fields?, agg?, change?, format?, upIsGood?, mark?, align?, width?, hideBelow?, sortable? })[]` |  | Columns in order; the first is the row header. `kind` is `text`, `number`, `sparkline`, `delta` or `bar`. For wide data give a sparkline or computed delta its series with `fields`; for long data they use the group's rows. |
| `groupBy` | `string` |  | Long data: the entity field. Rows sharing a value become one table row, in data order. |
| `highlight` | `string \| string[]` |  | Entities to emphasise, matched on the first column. |
| `sort` | `{ key, direction?: "asc" \| "desc" }` |  | Order rows by a column's value. Default direction: descending. With `sortable` this is the opening order. |
| `sortable` | `boolean` | `true` | Click or press Enter on a column header to sort by it (numbers largest first, text A to Z); a second press reverses and a third restores the original order. Sparkline columns do not sort; set `sortable: false` on a column to exclude it. |
| `limit` | `number` |  | Show only the first N rows. |
| `density` | `"comfortable" \| "compact"` | `"comfortable"` | Row padding. |
| `title` | `string` |  | The main fact with its number, or a plain label. Set as the table's `<caption>`. |
| `subtitle` | `string` |  | Units and period. |
| `source` | `string` |  | Shown under the table as "Source: ...". |
| `note` | `string` |  | Method note or caveat. |
| `theme` | `ThemeInput` |  | A built-in theme name (`editorial`, `ledger`, `noir`...) or a theme object, passed on to the sparklines and deltas. A named theme with its own surface paints that surface behind the component. |
| `frame` | `boolean` |  | Paint the theme's surface behind the component. Default: on for a named theme with its own surface. |
| `mode` | `"auto" \| "system" \| "light" \| "dark"` | `"auto"` | Colour mode. |

### Composition

- Composes: [sparkline](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/sparkline.md), [delta](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/delta.md)
- Used by: [scorecard](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/scorecard.md)

### More examples

```tsx
    { key: "country", label: "Country" },
    { key: "share", label: "Latest", format: "{value}%" },
    { key: "share", label: "Peak", agg: "max", format: "{value}%", hideBelow: 420 },
    { key: "share", label: "Trend", kind: "sparkline", mark: "bar", format: "{value}%" },
    { key: "share", label: "Since 2019", kind: "delta" },
  ]}
  note="Illustrative data"
/>
```

## Filter chips (`filter-chips`)

> The active crossfilter selections of the surrounding `InsightData`, shown as removable chips with a reset control.

- Component: `FilterChips` (import from `insightcharts`)
- Spec type: `"filter-chips"`
- Level: molecule. Category: layout.
- An HTML component: it takes only the props listed below, plus `theme`, `mode`, `className` and `style` where its source declares them. It does not take the common chart props.

### When to use

Inside any `<InsightData>` whose charts use `select`: put it above the charts so readers can see what is filtered, drop one value, or clear everything. `linked-charts` already includes it.

### Avoid

Outside `<InsightData>` it renders nothing unless you pass `selections` yourself. It is not a filter builder: selections are made by clicking marks in the charts.

### Install

From npm (the component ships in the package):

```bash
npm install insightcharts echarts
```

Or copy the source into your project with the shadcn CLI, so you can edit it (the engine still comes from the `insightcharts` package):

```bash
npx shadcn@latest registry add @insightcharts=https://insightcharts.dev/r/{name}.json   # once per project
npx shadcn@latest add @insightcharts/filter-chips
```

The file lands at `components/insightcharts/molecules/filter-chips.tsx`. `@insightcharts/filter-chips-demo` adds a ready-made example next to it.

### Usage

```tsx
import { FilterChips } from "insightcharts";

<FilterChips
  labels={{ region: "Region", source: "Source", year: "Year" }}
  selections={{
    "by-region": { field: "region", values: ["Asia", "Europe"] },
    "by-source": { field: "source", values: ["Solar"] },
    "by-year": { field: "year", range: [2020, 2024] },
  }}
/>
```

### JSON spec

The same thing as data, rendered with `<Insight spec={spec} />`:

```json
{
  "type": "filter-chips",
  "labels": { "region": "Region", "source": "Source", "year": "Year" },
  "selections": {
    "by-region": { "field": "region", "values": ["Asia", "Europe"] },
    "by-source": { "field": "source", "values": ["Solar"] },
    "by-year": { "field": "year", "range": [2020, 2024] }
  }
}
```

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `selections` | `Record<string, { field, values?, range? }>` |  | Selections to show when there is no surrounding `<InsightData>` (or to override it), keyed by owner. Uncontrolled unless `onSelectionsChange` is given. |
| `onSelectionsChange` | `(selections) => void` |  | Called when a chip is removed or the reset is pressed; makes `selections` controlled. |
| `labels` | `Record<string, string>` |  | Display names for field names, e.g. `{ region: "Region" }`. |
| `hint` | `string` |  | Shown while nothing is selected, e.g. "Click a bar to filter". |
| `resetLabel` | `string` | `"Reset"` | Text of the clear-all control. |
| `count` | `boolean` | `false` | Show "1,204 of 5,000 rows" at the end of the line. |
| `unit` | `string` | `"rows"` | Noun for the count, e.g. "orders". |
| `theme` | `ThemeInput` |  | A built-in theme name (`editorial`, `ledger`, `noir`...) or a theme object. A named theme with its own surface paints that surface behind the component. |
| `frame` | `boolean` |  | Paint the theme's surface behind the component. Default: on for a named theme with its own surface. |
| `mode` | `"auto" \| "system" \| "light" \| "dark"` | `"auto"` | Colour mode. |

### Composition

- Composes: nothing (it is a primitive)
- Used by: [linked-charts](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/linked-charts.md), [data-explorer](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/data-explorer.md)

### More examples

#### Nothing selected, with a hint, earth theme

```tsx
import { FilterChips } from "insightcharts";

<FilterChips theme="earth" selections={{}} hint="Click a bar to filter" />
```

#### A date range and two values, blueprint theme

```tsx
import { FilterChips } from "insightcharts";

<FilterChips
  theme="blueprint"
  labels={{ month: "Month", line: "Line" }}
  resetLabel="Clear all"
  selections={{
    "by-month": { field: "month", range: ["2024-03-01", "2024-09-01"] },
    "by-line": { field: "line", values: ["Northern", "Circle"] },
  }}
/>
```

#### One value, ledger theme

```tsx
import { FilterChips } from "insightcharts";

<FilterChips
  theme="ledger"
  labels={{ plan: "Plan" }}
  selections={{ "by-plan": { field: "plan", values: ["Enterprise"] } }}
/>
```

- Source: https://github.com/insightcharts/insightcharts/blob/main/packages/insightcharts/src/molecules/filter-chips.tsx
- Spec schema: https://insightcharts.dev/schema/insight-spec.json
- Choosing a form: https://insightcharts.dev/llms/guides/choosing-a-form.md
- All components: https://insightcharts.dev/llms.txt

## Hero figure (`hero-figure`)

> The opening exhibit of a piece: kicker, headline and deck above one large chart, with a source line underneath.

- Component: `HeroFigure` (import from `insightcharts`)
- Spec type: `"hero-figure"`
- Level: molecule. Category: story.
- An HTML component: it takes only the props listed below, plus `theme`, `mode`, `className` and `style` where its source declares them. It does not take the common chart props.

### When to use

At the very top of a data story or a one-page report. The headline states the main fact with its number. The chart shows that fact.

### Avoid

Giving the chart its own `title` (the headline is the title; use the chart's `subtitle` for the measure). A second hero on the same page: later sections use `section` or `chart-callout`.

### Install

From npm (the component ships in the package):

```bash
npm install insightcharts echarts
```

Or copy the source into your project with the shadcn CLI, so you can edit it (the engine still comes from the `insightcharts` package):

```bash
npx shadcn@latest registry add @insightcharts=https://insightcharts.dev/r/{name}.json   # once per project
npx shadcn@latest add @insightcharts/hero-figure
```

The file lands at `components/insightcharts/molecules/hero-figure.tsx`. `@insightcharts/hero-figure-demo` adds a ready-made example next to it.

### Usage

```tsx
import { HeroFigure, LineChart } from "insightcharts";

<HeroFigure
  theme="editorial"
  kicker="Energy transition"
  title="Solar supplied 11.1% of EU electricity in 2024"
  deck="Coal's share fell from 24.6% in 2015 to 9.8% in 2024."
  byline="By Ana Ruiz"
  date="2025-01-23"
  chart={<LineChart
    data={[
      { year: "2015", Solar: 2.9, Coal: 24.6, Wind: 9.2, Gas: 15.6 },
      { year: "2016", Solar: 3, Coal: 22, Wind: 9.5, Gas: 18.4 },
      { year: "2017", Solar: 3.4, Coal: 20.6, Wind: 11, Gas: 19.7 },
      { year: "2018", Solar: 3.7, Coal: 19.2, Wind: 11.4, Gas: 18.3 },
      { year: "2019", Solar: 4.2, Coal: 15, Wind: 13, Gas: 21 },
      { year: "2020", Solar: 5, Coal: 13, Wind: 14.4, Gas: 20.1 },
      { year: "2021", Solar: 5.4, Coal: 14.7, Wind: 13.3, Gas: 18.8 },
      { year: "2022", Solar: 7, Coal: 15.8, Wind: 15.1, Gas: 19.6 },
      { year: "2023", Solar: 9.1, Coal: 12.3, Wind: 17.5, Gas: 16.8 },
      { year: "2024", Solar: 11.1, Coal: 9.8, Wind: 17.4, Gas: 15.7 },
    ]}
    x="year"
    y={["Solar", "Coal", "Wind", "Gas"]}
    highlight={["Solar", "Coal"]}
    contextLabels
    format="{value}%"
    zero
    height={380}
    subtitle="Share of EU electricity generation by source, 2015 to 2024"
  />}
  source={{ name: "Ember, European Electricity Review 2025", url: "https://ember-energy.org" }}
  note="Figures are approximate, for illustration"
  period="2015 to 2024"
/>
```

```json
      { "year": "2017", "Solar": 3.4, "Coal": 20.6, "Wind": 11, "Gas": 19.7 },
      { "year": "2018", "Solar": 3.7, "Coal": 19.2, "Wind": 11.4, "Gas": 18.3 },
      { "year": "2019", "Solar": 4.2, "Coal": 15, "Wind": 13, "Gas": 21 },
      { "year": "2020", "Solar": 5, "Coal": 13, "Wind": 14.4, "Gas": 20.1 },
      { "year": "2021", "Solar": 5.4, "Coal": 14.7, "Wind": 13.3, "Gas": 18.8 },
      { "year": "2022", "Solar": 7, "Coal": 15.8, "Wind": 15.1, "Gas": 19.6 },
      { "year": "2023", "Solar": 9.1, "Coal": 12.3, "Wind": 17.5, "Gas": 16.8 },
      { "year": "2024", "Solar": 11.1, "Coal": 9.8, "Wind": 17.4, "Gas": 15.7 }
    ],
    "x": "year",
    "y": ["Solar", "Coal", "Wind", "Gas"],

  "note": "Figures are approximate, for illustration",
  "period": "2015 to 2024"

```

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `title` (required) | `string` |  | The main fact, as one plain sentence with its number. |
| `kicker` | `string` |  | Small label above the title: the series or topic. |
| `deck` | `string` |  | One plain sentence under the title that adds a second fact. |
| `byline` | `string` |  | Author line, e.g. "By Ana Ruiz". |
| `date` | `string` |  | Publication date. ISO dates are formatted for the locale. |
| `chart` (required) | `Slot` |  | The hero chart: a spec or a React element, without its own title. |
| `source` | `string \| { name, url? } \| (string \| { name, url? })[]` |  | Where the data comes from. Entries with a `url` are linked. |
| `period` | `string` |  | The period the data covers. |
| `note` | `string` |  | Caveats the reader should know. |
| `align` | `"left" \| "center"` | `"left"` | Headline alignment. |
| `level` | `1 \| 2 \| 3 \| 4 \| 5 \| 6` | `1` | Heading level of the title. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` |  | JSX alternative to `chart`. |
| `theme` | `ThemeInput` |  | A built-in theme name (`editorial`, `ledger`, `noir`...) or a theme object, passed on to the headline, chart and source note. A named theme with its own surface paints that surface behind the component. |
| `frame` | `boolean` |  | Paint the theme's surface behind the component. Default: on for a named theme with its own surface. |
| `mode` | `"auto" \| "system" \| "light" \| "dark"` | `"auto"` | Colour mode. |

### Composition

- Composes: [headline](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/headline.md), [source-note](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/source-note.md), [line-chart](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/line-chart.md), [big-number](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/big-number.md), [dumbbell-chart](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/dumbbell-chart.md), [waffle-chart](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/waffle-chart.md)
- Used by: no molecule or template yet

## KPI grid (`kpi-grid`)

> A responsive grid of trend cards drawn from one dataset: each metric shows its latest value, its change and a graphic, in one `stat-tile` variant or a deliberate mix of them.

- Component: `KpiGrid` (import from `insightcharts`)
- Spec type: `"kpi-grid"`
- Level: molecule. Category: layout.
- An HTML component: it takes only the props listed below, plus `theme`, `mode`, `className` and `style` where its source declares them. It does not take the common chart props.

### When to use

The top of a dashboard or a monthly report: three to eight metrics tracked over the same periods. Pass one table with a column per metric.

### Avoid

Figures without a series behind them (use `stat-row`); comparing the metrics with each other on one scale (use `line-chart` or `small-multiples`); more than eight cards.

### Install

From npm (the component ships in the package):

```bash
npm install insightcharts echarts
```

Or copy the source into your project with the shadcn CLI, so you can edit it (the engine still comes from the `insightcharts` package):

```bash
npx shadcn@latest registry add @insightcharts=https://insightcharts.dev/r/{name}.json   # once per project
npx shadcn@latest add @insightcharts/kpi-grid
```

The file lands at `components/insightcharts/molecules/kpi-grid.tsx`. `@insightcharts/kpi-grid-demo` adds a ready-made example next to it.

### Usage

```tsx
import { KpiGrid } from "insightcharts";

const data = [
  { month: "2024-01-01", users: 38100, mrr: 412000, churn: 4.2, response: 4.1 },
  { month: "2024-02-01", users: 39400, mrr: 428000, churn: 4, response: 3.9 },
  { month: "2024-03-01", users: 39000, mrr: 431000, churn: 3.9, response: 3.8 },
  { month: "2024-04-01", users: 40800, mrr: 455000, churn: 3.6, response: 3.2 },
  { month: "2024-05-01", users: 42200, mrr: 470000, churn: 3.1, response: 3.4 },
  { month: "2024-06-01", users: 41900, mrr: 476000, churn: 2.9, response: 2.9 },
  { month: "2024-07-01", users: 43500, mrr: 498000, churn: 2.6, response: 2.7 },
  { month: "2024-08-01", users: 44100, mrr: 511000, churn: 2.4, response: 2.6 },
  { month: "2024-09-01", users: 44500, mrr: 524000, churn: 2.3, response: 2.4 },
  { month: "2024-10-01", users: 46000, mrr: 548000, churn: 2.2, response: 2.3 },
  { month: "2024-11-01", users: 47200, mrr: 566000, churn: 2.1, response: 2.2 },
  { month: "2024-12-01", users: 48200, mrr: 589000, churn: 2.1, response: 2.2 },
];

<KpiGrid
  title="Monthly active users rose from 38,100 to 48,200 in 2024"
  subtitle="Four product metrics by month, 2024. Change is measured against January."
  data={data}
  x="month"
  metrics={[
    { y: "users", label: "Monthly active users", format: "compact" },
    { y: "mrr", label: "Recurring revenue", format: "currency:USD" },
    { y: "churn", label: "Monthly churn", format: "{value}%", change: "absolute", upIsGood: false },
    { y: "response", label: "Median first response", format: "{value} h", upIsGood: false },
  ]}
  source="Internal analytics"
  note="Illustrative data"
/>
```

### JSON spec

The same thing as data, rendered with `<Insight spec={spec} />`:

```json
{
  "type": "kpi-grid",
  "title": "Monthly active users rose from 38,100 to 48,200 in 2024",
  "subtitle": "Four product metrics by month, 2024. Change is measured against January.",
  "data": [
    { "month": "2024-01-01", "users": 38100, "mrr": 412000, "churn": 4.2, "response": 4.1 },
```

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `data` | `DataInput` |  | One dataset in time order: a row per period, a column per metric. Omit inside `<InsightData>`. |
| `transform` | `Transform \| Transform[]` |  | Applied once, before the cards read the rows. |
| `x` | `string` |  | Period field shared by every metric. |
| `metrics` (required) | `{ y, label, format?, upIsGood?, compare?, change?, deltaFormat?, deltaLabel?, context?, value?, delta?, kind?, variant?, surface?, tone?, size?, align?, orientation?, icon?, target?, targetLabel?, max?, parts?, rank?, rankOf?, unitValue?, showTrend? }[]` |  | One card per metric; each takes the props of `trend-card`, including its own `variant`, `surface`, `tone` and `size`. |
| `variant` | `StatTileVariant` |  | The display of every card: any `stat-tile` variant (`sparkline`, `area`, `bars`, `dots`, `split`, `compact`, `progress`, `ring`, `comparison`, `delta-first`, `icon`, `breakdown`, `rank`, `hero`, `filled`, `tinted`, `borderless`, `outline-accent`). Omit for the original cards with an interactive sparkline. |
| `variants` | `StatTileVariant[]` |  | A display per card, by position, so one grid mixes them on purpose: `["split", "area", "bars", "progress"]`. A metric's own `variant` wins; cards past the end use `variant`. |
| `surface` | `"plain" \| "borderless" \| "filled" \| "tinted" \| "outline-accent"` |  | The ground of every card. |
| `tone` | `"neutral" \| "accent" \| "positive" \| "negative" \| number \| "series"` |  | Tone of every card. `series` gives each card the next categorical colour. |
| `layout` | `"cards" \| "dividers"` | `"cards"` | Separate cards, or open tiles with hairlines between them. |
| `featured` | `boolean` | `false` | The first card spans two columns and is set one size larger. |
| `density` | `"dense" \| "default" \| "roomy"` | `"default"` | Spacing and type scale: cards are `sm`, `md` or `lg`, with 8, 12 or 16px between them. |
| `frame` | `boolean` |  | Set false to stop a named theme painting its ground. |
| `compare` | `"first" \| "previous" \| number` | `"first"` | Baseline for every card's change; a metric can override it. |
| `change` | `"percent" \| "absolute"` | `"percent"` | Relative change, or the difference between the two values; a metric can override it. An absolute change of a percentage metric is shown in percentage points ("−2.1 pts"). |
| `deltaFormat` | `FormatSpec` |  | Format for absolute changes, e.g. `"{value} pp"` or `"signed"`; a metric can override it. Default: points for percentage formats, otherwise the metric's own `format`. |
| `columns` | `number` |  | Preferred columns. Default: up to four, reduced to fit cards of at least 200px. |
| `title` | `string` |  | The main fact with its number, or a plain label. |
| `subtitle` | `string` |  | Population and period. |
| `source` | `string` |  | Shown under the grid as "Source: ...". |
| `note` | `string` |  | Method note or caveat. |
| `theme` | `ThemeInput` |  | A theme name such as `"ledger"`, or token overrides, passed on to every card. A named theme paints its own ground. |
| `mode` | `"auto" \| "system" \| "light" \| "dark"` | `"auto"` | Colour mode. |

### Composition

- Composes: [trend-card](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/trend-card.md), [stat-tile](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/stat-tile.md)
- Used by: [scorecard](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/scorecard.md)

#### Dividers instead of cards, editorial

```tsx
import { KpiGrid } from "insightcharts";

const data = [
  { year: "2017", solar: 1.9, wind: 5.6, coal: 38.2, gas: 22.9 },
  { year: "2018", solar: 2.4, wind: 6.1, coal: 37.9, gas: 23 },
  { year: "2019", solar: 2.9, wind: 6.9, coal: 36.4, gas: 23.5 },
  { year: "2020", solar: 3.6, wind: 7.8, coal: 35.1, gas: 23.4 },
  { year: "2021", solar: 4.4, wind: 8.4, coal: 36, gas: 22.8 },
  { year: "2022", solar: 5.6, wind: 9.3, coal: 35.6, gas: 22.2 },
  { year: "2023", solar: 7.1, wind: 10.1, coal: 34.9, gas: 22.4 },
  { year: "2024", solar: 9.2, wind: 10.9, coal: 33.8, gas: 22.1 },
];

<KpiGrid
  theme="editorial"
  title="Solar supplied 9.2% of electricity in 2024"
  subtitle="Share of generation by source, 2017 to 2024, with the change since 2017"

  layout="dividers"
  variant="sparkline"

    { y: "solar", label: "Solar", format: "{value}%" },

    { y: "coal", label: "Coal", format: "{value}%", tone: "neutral", upIsGood: false },
  ]}
  note="Illustrative data"
/>
```

## Linked charts (`linked-charts`)

> Two to four charts over one shared dataset in a responsive grid: clicking a mark in one filters the others, with the active filters shown as removable chips.

- Component: `LinkedCharts` (import from `insightcharts`)
- Spec type: `"linked-charts"`
- Level: molecule. Category: layout.
- An HTML component: it takes only the props listed below, plus `theme`, `mode`, `className` and `style` where its source declares them. It does not take the common chart props.

### When to use

Exploration of one table along several dimensions: by region, by category and over time. Pass row-level data once; each chart aggregates it with its own `transform`, sets `select: true` and omits `data`.

### Avoid

A report that states one fixed fact (use `chart-callout` or `scrolly-chart`); charts over unrelated datasets (they cannot filter each other); more than four charts.

### Install

From npm (the component ships in the package):

```bash
npm install insightcharts echarts
```

Or copy the source into your project with the shadcn CLI, so you can edit it (the engine still comes from the `insightcharts` package):

```bash
npx shadcn@latest registry add @insightcharts=https://insightcharts.dev/r/{name}.json   # once per project
npx shadcn@latest add @insightcharts/linked-charts
```

The file lands at `components/insightcharts/molecules/linked-charts.tsx`. `@insightcharts/linked-charts-demo` adds a ready-made example next to it.

### Usage

```tsx
      x="region"

    />,
    <DonutChart
      id="by-source"
      name="source"
      value="twh"
      select
      format="compact"
      centerLabel="TWh"
      height={200}
      title="By source"
      transform={{ type: "aggregate", groupBy: "source", measures: { twh: { op: "sum", field: "twh" } } }}
    />,
    <BarChart
      id="by-year"
      x="year"
      y="twh"
      series="source"
      stack
      orientation="vertical"
      sort="none"
      select="year"
      format="compact"
      height={240}
      title="By year"
      transform={{
        type: "aggregate",
        groupBy: ["year", "source"],
        measures: { twh: { op: "sum", field: "twh" } },
      }}
    />,
  ]}
  source="Ember, Global Electricity Review 2025"
  note="Regional figures rounded, illustrative"
/>
```

```json
      "select": "year",
      "format": "compact",
      "height": 240,
      "title": "By year",
      "transform": {
        "type": "aggregate",
        "groupBy": ["year", "source"],
        "measures": { "twh": { "op": "sum", "field": "twh" } }
      }
    }
  ],
  "source": "Ember, Global Electricity Review 2025",
  "note": "Regional figures rounded, illustrative"
}
```

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `data` (required) | `DataInput` |  | The shared, row-level dataset. |
| `transform` | `Transform \| Transform[]` |  | Applied once to the shared data. |
| `charts` | `Slot[]` |  | Two to four chart specs or elements. Give each `select: true` (or a field name) and a stable `id`, and leave out `data`. |
| `columns` | `number` |  | Preferred columns. Default two; fewer when charts would be narrower than `minChartWidth`. |
| `minChartWidth` | `number` | `260` | Narrowest a chart may get before the grid drops a column. |
| `filters` | `boolean` | `true` | Show the filter line (`filter-chips`). |
| `hint` | `string` | `"Click a mark to filter the other charts"` | Shown in the filter line while nothing is selected. |
| `labels` | `Record<string, string>` |  | Display names for the fields in the chips. |
| `count` | `boolean` | `false` | Show the filtered row count at the end of the filter line. |
| `unit` | `string` | `"rows"` | Noun for the count. |
| `selections` | `Record<string, Selection>` |  | Controlled selections, keyed by chart id. |
| `onSelectionsChange` | `(selections) => void` |  | Called when the selections change. |
| `title` | `string` |  | Heading for the group. |
| `subtitle` | `string` |  | Measure, population and period shared by the charts. |
| `source` | `string` |  | Shown under the grid as "Source: ...". |
| `note` | `string` |  | Method note or caveat. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` |  | JSX alternative to `charts`. |
| `before` | `Slot \| Slot[]` |  | Content rendered inside the shared store above the grid: figures, text, a custom component that calls `useInsightData()`, or a spec that omits `data` (e.g. `stat-row`, `data-table`). It sees the same filtered rows as the charts. |
| `after` | `Slot \| Slot[]` |  | Content rendered inside the shared store below the grid, e.g. a detail table of the filtered rows. |
| `gap` | `number` | `24` | Space in px between the `before` slot, the grid and the `after` slot. |
| `theme` | `ThemeInput` |  | A built-in theme name (`editorial`, `ledger`, `noir`...) or a theme object, passed on to every chart. A named theme with its own surface paints that surface behind the component. |
| `frame` | `boolean` |  | Paint the theme's surface behind the component. Default: on for a named theme with its own surface. |
| `mode` | `"auto" \| "system" \| "light" \| "dark"` | `"auto"` | Colour mode. |

### Composition

- Composes: [filter-chips](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/filter-chips.md), [bar-chart](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/bar-chart.md), [line-chart](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/line-chart.md)
- Used by: [data-explorer](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/data-explorer.md)

## Metric breakdown (`metric-breakdown`)

> A headline number with its composition underneath: one segmented bar and a key giving each part's value and share.

- Component: `MetricBreakdown` (import from `insightcharts`)
- Spec type: `"metric-breakdown"`
- Level: molecule. Category: layout.
- An HTML component: it takes only the props listed below, plus `theme`, `mode`, `className` and `style` where its source declares them. It does not take the common chart props.

### When to use

A total that the reader will immediately want split: a budget by department, revenue by product line, emissions by sector. Two to six parts that add up to the number above them.

### Avoid

Parts that do not sum to the headline; more than about six parts (use `bar-chart`); composition compared across groups or over time (use `bar-chart` with `stack: "percent"` or `area-chart`).

### Install

From npm (the component ships in the package):

```bash
npm install insightcharts echarts
```

Or copy the source into your project with the shadcn CLI, so you can edit it (the engine still comes from the `insightcharts` package):

```bash
npx shadcn@latest registry add @insightcharts=https://insightcharts.dev/r/{name}.json   # once per project
npx shadcn@latest add @insightcharts/metric-breakdown
```

The file lands at `components/insightcharts/molecules/metric-breakdown.tsx`. `@insightcharts/metric-breakdown-demo` adds a ready-made example next to it.

### Usage

```tsx
import { MetricBreakdown } from "insightcharts";

const data = [
  { sector: "Energy supply", mt: 862 },
  { sector: "Transport", mt: 804 },
  { sector: "Industry", mt: 701 },
  { sector: "Buildings", mt: 437 },
  { sector: "Agriculture", mt: 378 },
  { sector: "Waste", mt: 109 },
];

<MetricBreakdown
  label="Greenhouse gas emissions, EU-27, 2022"
  context="Million tonnes of CO2 equivalent. 31% below the 1990 level."
  data={data}
  name="sector"
  value="mt"
  format="integer"
  source="European Environment Agency"
  note="Rounded, approximate figures for illustration"
/>
```

### JSON spec

The same thing as data, rendered with `<Insight spec={spec} />`:

```json
{
  "type": "metric-breakdown",
  "label": "Greenhouse gas emissions, EU-27, 2022",
  "context": "Million tonnes of CO2 equivalent. 31% below the 1990 level.",
  "data": [
    { "sector": "Energy supply", "mt": 862 },
    { "sector": "Transport", "mt": 804 },
    { "sector": "Industry", "mt": 701 },
    { "sector": "Buildings", "mt": 437 },
    { "sector": "Agriculture", "mt": 378 },
    { "sector": "Waste", "mt": 109 }
  ],
  "name": "sector",
  "value": "mt",
  "format": "integer",
  "source": "European Environment Agency",
  "note": "Rounded, approximate figures for illustration"
}
```

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `label` (required) | `string` |  | What the headline number measures. |
| `data` | `DataInput` |  | One row per part. Omit inside `<InsightData>`. |
| `transform` | `Transform \| Transform[]` |  | Applied before the parts are summed. |
| `name` (required) | `string` |  | Field naming each part. |
| `value` (required) | `string` |  | Field with each part's value. |
| `total` | `number \| string` |  | The headline number. Default: the sum of the parts. |
| `context` | `string` |  | The line under the headline number. |
| `delta` | `number \| string` |  | Change in the headline number. Numbers render as signed percentages. |
| `deltaLabel` | `string` |  | What the delta is against. |
| `upIsGood` | `boolean` | `true` | Whether an increase is good news. |
| `size` | `"hero" \| "stat"` | `"stat"` | `hero` when this opens a piece. |
| `show` | `"both" \| "value" \| "share"` | `"both"` | What the key prints beside each part. |
| `sort` | `"none" \| "desc"` | `"none"` | Order parts by size; the bar and the key follow. |
| `names` | `Record<string, string>` |  | Display names for part keys. |
| `format` | `FormatSpec` | `"auto"` | Number format for the headline and the parts. |
| `source` | `string` |  | Shown underneath as "Source: ...". |
| `note` | `string` |  | Method note or caveat. |
| `variant` | `"plain" \| "filled" \| "tinted" \| "with-icon" \| "with-ring" \| "with-trend"` | `"plain"` | How the headline number is dressed: passed to `big-number`. |
| `icon` | `IconInput` |  | Icon for the headline when `variant` is `with-icon`. |
| `tone` | `"neutral" \| "accent" \| "positive" \| "negative" \| number` |  | Tone of a filled or tinted headline. |
| `display` | `"key" \| "inline" \| "meters" \| "tiles"` | `"key"` | How the parts are shown: a list with values and shares, one wrapped line, a `progress-meter` per part scaled to the total, or a `stat-tile` per part. |
| `tileVariant` | `StatTileVariant` | `"progress"` | The tile display when `display` is `tiles`: `progress`, `ring`, `filled`, `tinted`, `plain`... Each tile gets the part's value, the total as `max` and the part's categorical colour. |
| `tileSurface` | `"plain" \| "borderless" \| "filled" \| "tinted" \| "outline-accent"` |  | The ground of each tile when `display` is `tiles`. |
| `layout` | `"stacked" \| "side"` | `"stacked"` | `side` puts the headline left and the parts right from 600px. |
| `columns` | `number` |  | Columns for the key, meters or tiles. Default: by width. |
| `bar` | `boolean` | `true` | Set false to leave out the segmented bar, e.g. with `meters` or `tiles`. |
| `dividers` | `boolean` | `true` | Hairlines between key rows. |
| `density` | `"dense" \| "default" \| "roomy"` | `"default"` | Spacing between the bar, the key rows and the tiles. |
| `frame` | `boolean` |  | Set false to stop a named theme painting its ground. |
| `theme` | `ThemeInput` |  | A theme name such as `"earth"`, or token overrides, passed on to the number and the bar. A named theme paints its own ground. |
| `mode` | `"auto" \| "system" \| "light" \| "dark"` | `"auto"` | Colour mode. |

### Composition

- Composes: [big-number](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/big-number.md), [segmented-bar](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/segmented-bar.md), [progress-meter](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/progress-meter.md), [stat-tile](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/stat-tile.md)
- Used by: no molecule or template yet

## Poster (`poster`)

> The sheet an infographic is composed on. It paints a full-bleed ground from a poster theme, forces one theme and colour mode on everything inside, and lays out a masthead, a grid of panels and a footer. It can save the whole sheet as one PNG.

- Component: `Poster` (import from `insightcharts`)
- Spec type: `"poster"`
- Level: molecule. Category: poster.
- An HTML component: it takes only the props listed below, plus `theme`, `mode`, `className` and `style` where its source declares them. It does not take the common chart props.

### When to use

Use it as the outer frame of any infographic: one dominant graphic with a few supporting panels, on a painted ground. Give it a poster theme (`noir`, `magenta`, `dusk`, `paper`, `ocean`, `forest`, `blueprint`, `sunrise`) and put a chart or figure spec in each panel. Put the one fact in `title` and keep panel headings short. It reflows to one column under 600px.

### Avoid

Long reading text or more than about six panels (use `report-page` or `visual-essay`). A single fact at a fixed social size (use `social-card`). Charts that need axes, gridlines and dense labels to be read, because a poster ground suits large flat marks with their values printed on them.

### Install

From npm (the component ships in the package):

```bash
npm install insightcharts echarts
```

Or copy the source into your project with the shadcn CLI, so you can edit it (the engine still comes from the `insightcharts` package):

```bash
npx shadcn@latest registry add @insightcharts=https://insightcharts.dev/r/{name}.json   # once per project
npx shadcn@latest add @insightcharts/poster
```

The file lands at `components/insightcharts/molecules/poster.tsx`. `@insightcharts/poster-demo` adds a ready-made example next to it.

### Usage

```tsx
import { BarChart, BigNumber, DonutChart, PictogramChart, Poster } from "insightcharts";

<Poster
  theme="noir"
  kicker="Transport"
  title="Riverton's bike-share scheme carried 4.2 million trips in 2025"
  subtitle="Trips, bikes and reasons for riding in the city's public bike-share scheme, January to December 2025."
  panels={[
    {
      span: 4,
      valign: "center",
      content: <BigNumber
        size="hero"
        value="4.2 million"
        label="Trips in 2025"
        context="3.4 million in 2024"
      />,
    },
    {
      span: 8,
      title: "Old Town had 1,150 of the scheme's 3,000 bikes",
      content: <PictogramChart
        data={[
          { district: "Old Town", bikes: 1150 },

        name="district"

      />,

    },
    {

          { day: "Mon", trips: 610 },

          { day: "Thu", trips: 662 },

        x="day"

        sort="none"
        highlight="Wed"

        height={260}
      />,
    },
    {
      span: 5,

        data={[
          { purpose: "Commuting", share: 46 },

          { purpose: "Other", share: 9 },
        ]}
        name="purpose"
        value="share"
        format="{value}%"
        centerValue="46%"
        centerLabel="Commuting"
        height={260}
      />,
    },
  ]}
  sources={["Riverton Transport Office", "Riverton rider survey 2025"]}
  note="Riverton is an invented city. All figures are illustrative."
  credit="InsightCharts"
/>
```

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `title` | `string` |  | The poster's one fact, as a plain sentence with its number. Set large and light in the theme's display face. |
| `kicker` | `string` |  | Small label above the title: the topic or series. |
| `subtitle` | `string` |  | One or two lines under the title: the measure, population and period. |
| `panels` (required) | `PosterPanel[]` |  | The blocks, in reading order. Each is `{ content, title?, subtitle?, span?, rowSpan?, source?, note?, align?, valign?, bleed?, id? }`. `content` is a component spec or rendered content. `span` is in units of `columns` (default: full width). `bleed` runs the content to the poster's left and right edges. |
| `columns` | `number` | `12` | Columns of the layout grid: a 12-unit grid, or a simple count such as 2 or 3. Under 600px every panel is full width; from 600 to 760px the grid has two columns. |
| `gap` | `number` |  | Space between panels in px. Default 40 (28 under 600px). |
| `padding` | `number` |  | Space between the poster's edge and its content in px. Default 56 (36 under 900px, 20 under 600px). |
| `maxWidth` | `number \| string` | `1200` | Widest the poster is drawn. It is centred in wider containers. |
| `aspect` | `number \| string` |  | Fixed shape as width / height: `0.75`, `"3:4"`, `"16:9"`. The poster still grows when its content needs more height, and the ratio is dropped under 600px. |
| `theme` | `PosterThemeName \| string \| ThemeInput` | `"noir"` | A poster theme name, any other theme name, or a theme object. It is passed on to everything inside. |
| `mode` | `"light" \| "dark" \| "auto" \| "system"` | `"light"` | Colour mode of the poster and everything in it. A poster does not follow the page unless you set `auto`. Only `paper` has a different dark variant. |
| `background` | `string` |  | CSS background of the sheet, a colour or a gradient. Default: the poster theme's ground. Keep it close to the theme's `surface`, which charts use for the gaps between marks. |
| `rules` | `"none" \| "solid" \| "dotted"` | `"dotted"` | Lines under the masthead, between rows of panels and above the footer. |
| `sources` | `string \| string[]` |  | Where the data comes from, shown in the footer. |
| `note` | `string` |  | Caveat shown in the footer, e.g. "Illustrative data". |
| `credit` | `string` |  | Who made the poster, shown at the right of the footer. |
| `titleAlign` | `"left" \| "center"` | `"left"` | Alignment of the masthead. |
| `level` | `1 \| 2 \| 3 \| 4 \| 5` | `2` | Heading level of the title. Panel headings are one level down. |
| `download` | `boolean` | `false` | Show a "Download PNG" control under the poster. The image is the whole sheet, drawn from the DOM onto a canvas, without the control. |
| `exportWidth` | `number` | `2400` | Width of the downloaded PNG in pixels. |
| `filename` | `string` |  | File name without extension. Defaults to a slug of the title. |
| `downloadLabel` | `string` | `"Download PNG"` | Label of the download control. |
| `onExport` | `(blob: Blob) => void` |  | Called with the PNG after a download. |

### Composition

- Composes: [big-number](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/big-number.md), [pictogram-chart](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/pictogram-chart.md), [bar-chart](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/bar-chart.md), [donut-chart](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/donut-chart.md), [treemap](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/treemap.md), [waffle-chart](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/waffle-chart.md), [segmented-bar](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/segmented-bar.md), [icon-stat](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/icon-stat.md)
- Used by: [atlas-poster](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/atlas-poster.md), [count-poster](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/count-poster.md), [flow-poster](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/flow-poster.md), [matrix-poster](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/matrix-poster.md), [network-poster](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/network-poster.md), [profile-poster](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/profile-poster.md), [radial-poster](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/radial-poster.md), [ranking-poster](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/ranking-poster.md), [scale-poster](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/scale-poster.md), [timeline-poster](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/timeline-poster.md)

## Proportion statement (`proportion-statement`)

> A share stated as a countable sentence ("37 in every 100…"): a waffle grid or a row of icons beside the statement in large type, with the number emphasised.

- Component: `ProportionStatement` (import from `insightcharts`)
- Spec type: `"proportion-statement"`
- Level: molecule. Category: story.
- An HTML component: it takes only the props listed below, plus `theme`, `mode`, `className` and `style` where its source declares them. It does not take the common chart props.

### When to use

One proportion that is easier to read as a count of people or units than as a percentage. Round to a small whole first: 1 in 4 with icons, 37 in every 100 with a waffle.

### Avoid

Several shares side by side (use `bar-chart`, or `waffle-chart` with categories); a precise percentage where the decimals matter (use `big-number`); totals above 100.

### Install

From npm (the component ships in the package):

```bash
npm install insightcharts echarts
```

Or copy the source into your project with the shadcn CLI, so you can edit it (the engine still comes from the `insightcharts` package):

```bash
npx shadcn@latest registry add @insightcharts=https://insightcharts.dev/r/{name}.json   # once per project
npx shadcn@latest add @insightcharts/proportion-statement
```

The file lands at `components/insightcharts/molecules/proportion-statement.tsx`. `@insightcharts/proportion-statement-demo` adds a ready-made example next to it.

### Usage

```tsx
import { ProportionStatement } from "insightcharts";

<ProportionStatement
  theme="sunrise"
  value={33}
  total={100}
  text="people in the world have never used the internet."
  detail="That was about 2.6 billion people in 2023."
  source="ITU Facts and Figures 2023"
  note="Figures are approximate, for illustration"
/>
```

### JSON spec

The same thing as data, rendered with `<Insight spec={spec} />`:

```json
{
  "type": "proportion-statement",
  "theme": "sunrise",
  "value": 33,
  "total": 100,
  "text": "people in the world have never used the internet.",
  "detail": "That was about 2.6 billion people in 2023.",
  "source": "ITU Facts and Figures 2023",
  "note": "Figures are approximate, for illustration"
}
```

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `value` (required) | `number` |  | How many of the whole are counted. |
| `total` | `number` | `100` | The whole. |
| `figure` | `string` |  | The emphasised words. Default: "{value} in every {total}", or "{value} in {total}" up to 20. |
| `text` (required) | `string` |  | The rest of the sentence, read straight after the figure. |
| `visual` | `"waffle" \| "icons"` |  | Grid of cells or row of glyphs. Default: icons up to a total of 20, waffle above. |
| `icon` | `"circle" \| "person" \| "square"` | `"person"` | Glyph for the `icons` visual. |
| `shape` | `"square" \| "circle"` | `"square"` | Cell shape for the `waffle` visual. |
| `side` | `"left" \| "right"` | `"left"` | Side the visual sits on; under 520px it goes on top. |
| `detail` | `string` |  | A second, quieter sentence under the statement. |
| `source` | `string` |  | Shown under the statement as "Source: ...". |
| `note` | `string` |  | Method note or caveat. |
| `theme` | `ThemeInput` |  | A built-in theme name (`editorial`, `ledger`, `noir`...) or a theme object, passed on to the visual. A named theme with its own surface paints that surface behind the component. |
| `frame` | `boolean` |  | Paint the theme's surface behind the component. Default: on for a named theme with its own surface. |
| `mode` | `"auto" \| "system" \| "light" \| "dark"` | `"auto"` | Colour mode. |

### Composition

- Composes: [waffle-chart](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/waffle-chart.md), [icon-stat](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/icon-stat.md)
- Used by: [explainer](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/explainer.md)

### More examples

#### Icons, 1 in 4

```tsx

  value={1}
  total={4}
  text="households could not cover an unexpected bill of €500 without borrowing."

  note="Figures are approximate, for illustration"
/>
```

```tsx

  theme="ocean"

  total={10}

  detail="Battery-electric models were 89% of registrations in 2024. They were 82% in 2023."

  note="Figures are approximate, for illustration"
/>
```

#### Waffle with circles, poster theme

## Quote with figure (`quote-figure`)

> A pull-quote paired with the statistic or small chart that backs it up, side by side and stacking in narrow containers.

- Component: `QuoteFigure` (import from `insightcharts`)
- Spec type: `"quote-figure"`
- Level: molecule. Category: story.
- An HTML component: it takes only the props listed below, plus `theme`, `mode`, `className` and `style` where its source declares them. It does not take the common chart props.

### When to use

A quotation shown next to the number it refers to: an interview finding with its survey figure, an executive's statement with the metric. One per section.

### Avoid

A quote with no evidence (use `pull-quote`); a figure that needs axes to read (use `chart-callout` and put the quote in prose); unattributed quotations.

### Install

From npm (the component ships in the package):

```bash
npm install insightcharts echarts
```

Or copy the source into your project with the shadcn CLI, so you can edit it (the engine still comes from the `insightcharts` package):

```bash
npx shadcn@latest registry add @insightcharts=https://insightcharts.dev/r/{name}.json   # once per project
npx shadcn@latest add @insightcharts/quote-figure
```

The file lands at `components/insightcharts/molecules/quote-figure.tsx`. `@insightcharts/quote-figure-demo` adds a ready-made example next to it.

### Usage

```tsx
import { QuoteFigure, Sparkline } from "insightcharts";

<QuoteFigure
  theme="magenta"
  quote="Solar met more than half of demand on 41% of summer afternoons in 2024. We do not have enough storage for the midday surplus yet."
  attribution="Marta Keller"
  role="Grid planner, quoted in the 2024 system adequacy review"
  stat={{
    value: 0.41,
    format: "percent",
    label: "Summer afternoons when solar met over half of demand",
    context: "It was 6% of afternoons in 2019",
  }}
  figure={<Sparkline
    data={[
      { year: "2019", share: 6 },
      { year: "2020", share: 9 },
      { year: "2021", share: 14 },
      { year: "2022", share: 22 },
      { year: "2023", share: 31 },
      { year: "2024", share: 41 },
    ]}
    x="year"
    y="share"
    format="{value}%"
    area
  />}
  source="National grid operator, hourly generation data"
  note="Illustrative data"
/>
```

### JSON spec

The same thing as data, rendered with `<Insight spec={spec} />`:

```json
{
  "type": "quote-figure",
  "theme": "magenta",
  "quote": "Solar met more than half of demand on 41% of summer afternoons in 2024. We do not have enough storage for the midday surplus yet.",
  "attribution": "Marta Keller",
  "role": "Grid planner, quoted in the 2024 system adequacy review",
  "stat": {
    "value": 0.41,
    "format": "percent",
    "label": "Summer afternoons when solar met over half of demand",
    "context": "It was 6% of afternoons in 2019"
  },
  "figure": {
    "type": "sparkline",
    "data": [
      { "year": "2019", "share": 6 },
      { "year": "2020", "share": 9 },
      { "year": "2021", "share": 14 },
      { "year": "2022", "share": 22 },
      { "year": "2023", "share": 31 },
      { "year": "2024", "share": 41 }
    ],
    "x": "year",
    "y": "share",
    "format": "{value}%",
    "area": true
  },
  "source": "National grid operator, hourly generation data",
  "note": "Illustrative data"
}
```

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `quote` (required) | `string` |  | The words quoted, without quotation marks. |
| `attribution` | `string` |  | Who said it. |
| `role` | `string` |  | Their role, or where it was said. |
| `cite` | `string` |  | Source URL, linked from the attribution. |
| `stat` | `{ value, label, context?, delta?, deltaLabel?, upIsGood?, format? }` |  | The statistic that backs the quote up; takes the props of `big-number`. |
| `figure` | `Slot` |  | A small chart or figure instead of, or under, the statistic: a spec or a React element. |
| `side` | `"left" \| "right"` | `"right"` | Side the evidence sits on; under 640px it goes underneath. |
| `source` | `string` |  | Shown underneath as "Source: ...". |
| `note` | `string` |  | Method note or caveat. |
| `theme` | `ThemeInput` |  | A built-in theme name (`editorial`, `ledger`, `noir`...) or a theme object, passed on to the quote and the figure. A named theme with its own surface paints that surface behind the component. |
| `frame` | `boolean` |  | Paint the theme's surface behind the component. Default: on for a named theme with its own surface. |
| `mode` | `"auto" \| "system" \| "light" \| "dark"` | `"auto"` | Colour mode. |

### Composition

- Composes: [pull-quote](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/pull-quote.md), [big-number](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/big-number.md), [sparkline](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/sparkline.md), [progress-meter](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/progress-meter.md)
- Used by: no molecule or template yet

## Ranked list (`ranked-list`)

> A ranking as a list: position, name, value and a thin in-row bar, with an optional change indicator and highlighted rows.

- Component: `RankedList` (import from `insightcharts`)
- Spec type: `"ranked-list"`
- Level: molecule. Category: layout.
- An HTML component: it takes only the props listed below, plus `theme`, `mode`, `className` and `style` where its source declares them. It does not take the common chart props.

### When to use

A top-N list where the names matter as much as the values: league tables, best and worst performers, leaderboards with a movement column. It keeps long names readable and works in a narrow column.

### Avoid

Precise visual comparison of many values or more than about 15 rows (use `bar-chart`); several measures per entity (use `data-table` or `comparison-table`); rank changing over time (use `bump-chart`).

### Install

From npm (the component ships in the package):

```bash
npm install insightcharts echarts
```

Or copy the source into your project with the shadcn CLI, so you can edit it (the engine still comes from the `insightcharts` package):

```bash
npx shadcn@latest registry add @insightcharts=https://insightcharts.dev/r/{name}.json   # once per project
npx shadcn@latest add @insightcharts/ranked-list
```

The file lands at `components/insightcharts/molecules/ranked-list.tsx`. `@insightcharts/ranked-list-demo` adds a ready-made example next to it.

### Usage

```tsx
import { RankedList } from "insightcharts";

const data = [
  { city: "Copenhagen", country: "Denmark", share: 49, change: 0.04 },
  { city: "Amsterdam", country: "Netherlands", share: 35, change: 0.01 },
  { city: "Utrecht", country: "Netherlands", share: 34, change: 0.02 },
  { city: "Münster", country: "Germany", share: 31, change: 0 },
  { city: "Antwerp", country: "Belgium", share: 26, change: 0.05 },
  { city: "Malmö", country: "Sweden", share: 25, change: -0.01 },
  { city: "Bordeaux", country: "France", share: 13, change: 0.06 },
  { city: "Paris", country: "France", share: 11, change: 0.07 },
];

<RankedList
  title="11% of commuting trips in Paris are made by bicycle"
  subtitle="Share of commuting trips made by bicycle, selected European cities, with change since 2019"
  data={data}
  name="city"
  detail="country"
  value="share"
  format="{value}%"
  change="change"
  highlight="Paris"
  source="City mobility surveys"
  note="Illustrative data"
/>
```

### JSON spec

The same thing as data, rendered with `<Insight spec={spec} />`:

```json
{
  "type": "ranked-list",
  "title": "11% of commuting trips in Paris are made by bicycle",
  "subtitle": "Share of commuting trips made by bicycle, selected European cities, with change since 2019",
  "data": [
    { "city": "Copenhagen", "country": "Denmark", "share": 49, "change": 0.04 },
    { "city": "Amsterdam", "country": "Netherlands", "share": 35, "change": 0.01 },
    { "city": "Utrecht", "country": "Netherlands", "share": 34, "change": 0.02 },
    { "city": "Münster", "country": "Germany", "share": 31, "change": 0 },
    { "city": "Antwerp", "country": "Belgium", "share": 26, "change": 0.05 },
    { "city": "Malmö", "country": "Sweden", "share": 25, "change": -0.01 },
    { "city": "Bordeaux", "country": "France", "share": 13, "change": 0.06 },
    { "city": "Paris", "country": "France", "share": 11, "change": 0.07 }
  ],
  "name": "city",
  "detail": "country",
  "value": "share",
  "format": "{value}%",
  "change": "change",
  "highlight": "Paris",
  "source": "City mobility surveys",
  "note": "Illustrative data"
}
```

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `data` | `DataInput` |  | One row per entity. Omit inside `<InsightData>`. |
| `transform` | `Transform \| Transform[]` |  | Applied before ranking. |
| `name` (required) | `string` |  | Field naming each entity. |
| `value` (required) | `string` |  | Field with the value that ranks them. Bars start at zero. |
| `change` | `string` |  | Field with a change shown at the end of each row: a number (0.12 is +12%) or a string. |
| `changeFormat` | `FormatSpec` | `signed percent` | Format for numeric changes, e.g. `"signed"` for places moved. |
| `upIsGood` | `boolean` | `true` | Whether a positive change is good news. |
| `detail` | `string` |  | Field with a short secondary line under each name. |
| `sort` | `"desc" \| "asc" \| "none"` | `"desc"` | Order by value; `none` keeps the data order. |
| `limit` | `number` |  | Show only the first N rows after sorting. |
| `highlight` | `string \| string[]` |  | Entity names to emphasise. The other bars are drawn in grey. |
| `bar` | `boolean` | `true` | Draw the in-row bar. |
| `max` | `number` |  | Value at which a bar is full. Default: the largest value shown. |
| `format` | `FormatSpec` | `"auto"` | Number format for the values. |
| `title` | `string` |  | The main fact with its number, or a plain label. |
| `subtitle` | `string` |  | Measure, population and period. |
| `source` | `string` |  | Shown under the list as "Source: ...". |
| `note` | `string` |  | Method note or caveat. |
| `theme` | `ThemeInput` |  | A built-in theme name (`editorial`, `ledger`, `noir`...) or a theme object. A named theme with its own surface paints that surface behind the component. |
| `frame` | `boolean` |  | Paint the theme's surface behind the component. Default: on for a named theme with its own surface. |
| `mode` | `"auto" \| "system" \| "light" \| "dark"` | `"auto"` | Colour mode. |

### Composition

- Composes: [delta](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/delta.md)
- Used by: [scorecard](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/scorecard.md)
