## Scrolly chart (`scrolly-chart`)

> A scroll-driven story from JSON: one base chart spec and a list of steps, each with narration and a patch of chart props applied while that step is active.

- Component: `ScrollyChart` (import from `insightcharts`)
- Spec type: `"scrolly-chart"`
- Level: molecule. Category: story.
- An HTML component: it takes only the props listed below, plus `theme`, `mode`, `className` and `style` where its source declares them. It does not take the common chart props.

### When to use

Walking a reader through one chart in stages: show everything, highlight the subject, change the measure, add the annotation. Make ONE change per step (the highlight, the data or the encoding) so the reader can see what changed.

### Avoid

Steps that change several things at once, or that swap to an unrelated chart (start a new `section` instead). More than about seven steps. A fact that one view can show (use `chart-callout`). In documents that will be printed or embedded in a short frame, set `scrollMode: "steps"`.

### Install

From npm (the component ships in the package):

```bash
npm install insightcharts echarts
```

Or copy the source into your project with the shadcn CLI, so you can edit it (the engine still comes from the `insightcharts` package):

```bash
npx shadcn@latest registry add @insightcharts=https://insightcharts.dev/r/{name}.json   # once per project
npx shadcn@latest add @insightcharts/scrolly-chart
```

The file lands at `components/insightcharts/molecules/scrolly-chart.tsx`. `@insightcharts/scrolly-chart-demo` adds a ready-made example next to it.

### Usage

```tsx
import { BarChart, ScrollyChart, registerComponents } from "insightcharts";

// Specs passed as data are resolved by name when rendered.
registerComponents({ BarChart });

<ScrollyChart
  theme="earth"
  chart={{
    type: "bar-chart",
    data: [
      { source: "Coal", y2015: 24.6, y2024: 9.8 },
      { source: "Gas", y2015: 15.8, y2024: 15.7 },
      { source: "Nuclear", y2015: 27.1, y2024: 23.7 },
      { source: "Wind", y2015: 9.2, y2024: 17.4 },
      { source: "Hydro", y2015: 12, y2024: 13.2 },
      { source: "Solar", y2015: 2.9, y2024: 11.1 },
    ],
    x: "source",
    y: "y2015",
    sort: "none",
    orientation: "horizontal",
    format: "{value}%",
    height: 300,
    title: "EU electricity generation by source, 2015",
    subtitle: "Share of EU electricity generation, %",
    source: "Ember, European Electricity Review 2025",
    note: "Rounded, approximate figures for illustration",
  }}
  steps={[
    {
      id: "baseline",
      label: "2015",
      content: "In 2015 **nuclear and coal** together supplied 51.7% of the EU's electricity.",
    },
    {
      id: "coal",
      content: "Coal supplied 24.6% in 2015. Only nuclear supplied more.",
      highlight: "Coal",
    },
    {
      id: "today",
      label: "2024",
      content: "In 2024 coal supplied 9.8%.",
      highlight: "Coal",
      y: "y2024",
      title: "EU electricity generation by source, 2024",
    },
    {
      id: "solar",
      content: "**Solar** supplied 11.1% in 2024. It supplied 2.9% in 2015.",
      highlight: "Solar",
      y: "y2024",
      title: "Solar supplied 11.1% of EU electricity in 2024",
    },
  ]}
  stepHeight="70vh"
  stickyTop={16}
/>
```

### JSON spec

The same thing as data, rendered with `<Insight spec={spec} />`:

```json

  "theme": "earth",
  "chart": {
    "type": "bar-chart",
    "data": [
      { "source": "Coal", "y2015": 24.6, "y2024": 9.8 },
      { "source": "Gas", "y2015": 15.8, "y2024": 15.7 },
      { "source": "Nuclear", "y2015": 27.1, "y2024": 23.7 },
      { "source": "Wind", "y2015": 9.2, "y2024": 17.4 },
      { "source": "Hydro", "y2015": 12, "y2024": 13.2 },
      { "source": "Solar", "y2015": 2.9, "y2024": 11.1 }
    ],
    "x": "source",
    "y": "y2015",
    "sort": "none",
    "orientation": "horizontal",
    "format": "{value}%",
    "height": 300,
    "title": "EU electricity generation by source, 2015",
    "subtitle": "Share of EU electricity generation, %",
    "source": "Ember, European Electricity Review 2025",
    "note": "Rounded, approximate figures for illustration"
  },
  "steps": [
    {
      "id": "baseline",
      "label": "2015",
      "content": "In 2015 **nuclear and coal** together supplied 51.7% of the EU's electricity."
    },
    {
      "id": "coal",
      "content": "Coal supplied 24.6% in 2015. Only nuclear supplied more.",
      "highlight": "Coal"
    },
    {
```

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `chart` (required) | `InsightSpec` |  | The base chart spec: `{ type, data, x, y, ... }`. Give it a `title`; steps may replace it. |
| `steps` (required) | `{ content, id?, label?, ...chart props }[]` |  | The steps in order. `content` is a short paragraph that says plainly what the chart now shows (`**bold**` works). Every other key is a chart prop merged over `chart` for that step: `highlight`, `transform`, `annotations`, `x`, `y`, `title`… Use `null` to remove a base prop. Change one thing per step. |
| `cumulative` | `boolean` | `false` | Each step's patch builds on the previous steps instead of on the base spec alone. |
| `scrollMode` | `"auto" \| "scroll" \| "swipe" \| "steps"` | `"auto"` | `scroll` pins the chart while steps scroll past; `swipe` makes steps swipeable cards; `steps` shows previous/next buttons; `auto` uses scroll, or swipe on narrow touch screens. (Named `scrollMode` because `mode` is the colour mode.) |
| `side` | `"left" \| "right"` | `"left"` | Side of the text column in scroll mode. Narrow containers overlay the text on the chart. |
| `stickyTop` | `number \| string` | `0` | Offset from the top of the viewport at which the chart pins; set it to the height of a fixed header. |
| `stepHeight` | `string` | `"80vh"` | Scroll distance per step, as a CSS length. |
| `onStepChange` | `(index) => void` |  | Called when the active step changes. |
| `title` | `string` |  | Heading above the whole story. |
| `subtitle` | `string` |  | Line under the heading. |
| `source` | `string` |  | Shown after the last step as "Source: ...". Prefer the chart's own `source`, which stays visible. |
| `note` | `string` |  | Method note or caveat. |
| `theme` | `ThemeInput` |  | A built-in theme name (`editorial`, `ledger`, `noir`...) or a theme object, passed on to the chart and the step cards. A named theme with its own surface paints that surface behind the component. |
| `frame` | `boolean` |  | Paint the theme's surface behind the component. Default: on for a named theme with its own surface. |
| `mode` | `"auto" \| "system" \| "light" \| "dark"` | `"auto"` | Colour mode. |

### Composition

- Composes: [prose](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/prose.md), [bar-chart](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/bar-chart.md), [line-chart](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/line-chart.md)
- Used by: [visual-essay](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/visual-essay.md)

### More examples

#### Steps mode (buttons), cumulative patches, noir theme

```tsx

<ScrollyChart
  theme="noir"
  scrollMode="steps"
  cumulative
  chart={{
    type: "bar-chart",
    data: [
      { source: "Coal", y2015: 24.6, y2024: 9.8 },
      { source: "Gas", y2015: 15.8, y2024: 15.7 },
      { source: "Nuclear", y2015: 27.1, y2024: 23.7 },
      { source: "Wind", y2015: 9.2, y2024: 17.4 },
      { source: "Hydro", y2015: 12, y2024: 13.2 },
      { source: "Solar", y2015: 2.9, y2024: 11.1 },
    ],
    x: "source",
    y: "y2015",
    sort: "none",
    orientation: "horizontal",
    format: "{value}%",
    height: 300,
    title: "EU electricity generation by source, 2015",
    subtitle: "Share of EU electricity generation, %",
    source: "Ember, European Electricity Review 2025",
    note: "Rounded, approximate figures for illustration",
  }}
  steps={[
    { content: "The chart shows each source's share in 2015." },
    { content: "**Coal** is highlighted. It supplied 24.6% in 2015.", highlight: "Coal" },
    {
      content: "The chart now shows 2024. Coal is still highlighted because the patches accumulate.",
      y: "y2024",
      title: "EU electricity generation by source, 2024",
    },
    {
      content: "The highlight is removed. The sources are sorted by their 2024 share.",
      highlight: null,
      sort: "desc",
    },
  ]}
/>
```

## Section (`section`)

> A story section: a numbered step marker or a headline, introductory prose, then one or more exhibits in a responsive one- to three-column grid.

- Component: `Section` (import from `insightcharts`)
- Spec type: `"section"`
- Level: molecule. Category: story.
- An HTML component: it takes only the props listed below, plus `theme`, `mode`, `className` and `style` where its source declares them. It does not take the common chart props.

### When to use

The building block of a longer piece. Each section states one fact with its number in the title, explains it in a paragraph and shows it in one to three exhibits. Use `step` when the sections are read in order.

### Avoid

The opening of a piece (use `hero-figure`); a single chart with one callout (use `chart-callout` directly); more than three exhibits in one section (split it).

### Install

From npm (the component ships in the package):

```bash
npm install insightcharts echarts
```

Or copy the source into your project with the shadcn CLI, so you can edit it (the engine still comes from the `insightcharts` package):

```bash
npx shadcn@latest registry add @insightcharts=https://insightcharts.dev/r/{name}.json   # once per project
npx shadcn@latest add @insightcharts/section
```

The file lands at `components/insightcharts/molecules/section.tsx`. `@insightcharts/section-demo` adds a ready-made example next to it.

### Usage

```tsx
import { BarChart, LineChart, Section } from "insightcharts";

<Section
  theme="ocean"
  step={2}
  total={4}
  title="First-quarter churn was 2.0% for customers who joined after March"
  intro="Monthly churn fell from 4.2% in January to 2.1% in December 2024. The new onboarding launched in March. Customers who joined after March had first-quarter churn of **2.0%**. Customers who joined before March had 4.1%."
  columns={2}
  body={[
    <LineChart
      data={[
        { month: "2024-01-01", rate: 4.2 },
        { month: "2024-02-01", rate: 4.3 },
        { month: "2024-03-01", rate: 4.1 },
        { month: "2024-04-01", rate: 3.6 },
        { month: "2024-05-01", rate: 3.1 },
        { month: "2024-06-01", rate: 2.9 },
        { month: "2024-07-01", rate: 2.6 },
        { month: "2024-08-01", rate: 2.4 },
        { month: "2024-09-01", rate: 2.3 },
        { month: "2024-10-01", rate: 2.2 },
        { month: "2024-11-01", rate: 2.1 },
        { month: "2024-12-01", rate: 2.1 },
      ]}
      x="month"
      y="rate"
      format="{value}%"
      zero
      height={240}
      title="Monthly churn fell from 4.2% to 2.1% in 2024"
      subtitle="Monthly customer churn, 2024"
      annotations={[{ type: "line", axis: "x", value: "2024-03-01", label: "New onboarding" }]}
    />,
    <BarChart
      data={[{ cohort: "Before March", churn: 4.1 }, { cohort: "After March", churn: 2 }]}
      x="cohort"
      y="churn"
      format="{value}%"
      height={240}
      highlight="After March"
      title="First-quarter churn was 4.1% for customers who joined before March"
      subtitle="First-quarter churn by sign-up cohort, 2024"
    />,
  ]}
  outro="The next section covers the first 90 days after sign-up."
/>
```

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `title` | `string` |  | The section's main fact, as one plain sentence with its number. |
| `step` | `number \| string` |  | Step number: turns the heading into a numbered chapter marker ("02 — ..."). |
| `total` | `number` |  | Total steps, shown as "02 / 05". |
| `kicker` | `string` |  | Small label above an unnumbered heading. |
| `deck` | `string` |  | One plain sentence under the heading that adds a second fact. |
| `intro` | `string \| string[]` |  | Introductory narration. Supports `**bold**`, `*italic*` and links. |
| `body` | `Slot \| Slot[]` |  | The exhibits: one slot or several, each a spec or a React element. |
| `columns` | `1 \| 2 \| 3` | `1` | Columns for the body at full width; reduced under 720px and 520px. |
| `outro` | `string \| string[]` |  | Closing narration under the body. |
| `rule` | `boolean` | `false` | Hairline above the section. |
| `level` | `1 \| 2 \| 3 \| 4 \| 5 \| 6` | `2` | Heading level. |
| `id` | `string` |  | Anchor id for deep links. |
| `spacing` | `"compact" \| "comfortable"` | `"comfortable"` | Vertical rhythm between heading, intro and body. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` |  | JSX alternative to `body`; each child becomes a grid item. |
| `theme` | `ThemeInput` |  | A built-in theme name (`editorial`, `ledger`, `noir`...) or a theme object, passed on to everything inside. A named theme with its own surface paints that surface behind the component. |
| `frame` | `boolean` |  | Paint the theme's surface behind the component. Default: on for a named theme with its own surface. |
| `mode` | `"auto" \| "system" \| "light" \| "dark"` | `"auto"` | Colour mode. |

### Composition

- Composes: [step-marker](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/step-marker.md), [headline](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/headline.md), [prose](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/prose.md), [line-chart](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/line-chart.md), [bar-chart](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/bar-chart.md), [area-chart](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/area-chart.md), [stat-tile](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/stat-tile.md)
- Used by: no molecule or template yet

## Small multiple grid (`small-multiple-grid`)

> Repeats any chart spec once per value of a facet field, each panel with its own filtered rows and a title, in a grid that follows the container width.

- Component: `SmallMultipleGrid` (import from `insightcharts`)
- Spec type: `"small-multiple-grid"`
- Level: molecule. Category: layout.
- An HTML component: it takes only the props listed below, plus `theme`, `mode`, `className` and `style` where its source declares them. It does not take the common chart props.

### When to use

Faceting a chart form the `small-multiples` atom does not draw: stacked bars, scatter plots, donuts, waffles, dumbbells, histograms. Also when each panel should be a full chart with its own tooltip and axis.

### Avoid

Line, area or bar facets that must share one value scale: use the `small-multiples` atom, which draws every panel in one chart on a common axis. Here each panel scales to its own rows unless the spec fixes the axis (for example `option: { xAxis: { max: 70 } }`), so say so in the subtitle or fix it. More than about twelve panels.

### Install

From npm (the component ships in the package):

```bash
npm install insightcharts echarts
```

Or copy the source into your project with the shadcn CLI, so you can edit it (the engine still comes from the `insightcharts` package):

```bash
npx shadcn@latest registry add @insightcharts=https://insightcharts.dev/r/{name}.json   # once per project
npx shadcn@latest add @insightcharts/small-multiple-grid
```

The file lands at `components/insightcharts/molecules/small-multiple-grid.tsx`. `@insightcharts/small-multiple-grid-demo` adds a ready-made example next to it.

### Usage

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `data` | `DataInput` |  | Rows for every panel together. Omit inside `<InsightData>`. |
| `transform` | `Transform \| Transform[]` |  | Applied before the rows are split by `facet`. |
| `facet` (required) | `string` |  | Field whose values each get a panel. |
| `chart` (required) | `InsightSpec \| (facet, rows) => ReactNode` |  | The chart repeated in every panel: a spec without `data` and without a `title`, or a render function from JSX. |
| `columns` | `number` |  | Preferred columns. Default: up to four, reduced to fit `minPanelWidth`. |
| `minPanelWidth` | `number` | `200` | Narrowest a panel may get before the grid drops a column. |
| `order` | `"data" \| "asc" \| "desc" \| string[]` | `"data"` | Panel order: data order, alphabetical, or an explicit list of facet values. |
| `panelHeight` | `number` | `160` | Plot height of each panel when the spec sets none. |
| `highlight` | `string \| string[]` |  | Passed to every panel as its `highlight`, so the same entity is emphasised everywhere. |
| `emphasis` | `string \| string[]` |  | Facet values whose panel titles are emphasised. |
| `legend` | `(string \| { label, color?, index?, shape?, muted? })[]` |  | One shared colour key above the panels (`legend-key` items, in series order). Set `legend: false` in the chart spec so panels do not repeat it. |
| `names` | `Record<string, string>` |  | Display names for facet values. |
| `level` | `2 \| 3 \| 4 \| 5 \| 6` | `4` | Heading level of the panel titles. |
| `title` | `string` |  | The main fact with its number, or a plain label. |
| `subtitle` | `string` |  | Measure, population, period, and whether the panels share a scale. |
| `source` | `string` |  | Shown under the grid as "Source: ...". |
| `note` | `string` |  | Method note or caveat. |
| `theme` | `ThemeInput` |  | A built-in theme name (`editorial`, `ledger`, `noir`...) or a theme object, passed on to every panel. A named theme with its own surface paints that surface behind the component. |
| `frame` | `boolean` |  | Paint the theme's surface behind the component. Default: on for a named theme with its own surface. |
| `mode` | `"auto" \| "system" \| "light" \| "dark"` | `"auto"` | Colour mode. |

### Composition

- Composes: [legend-key](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/legend-key.md), [bar-chart](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/bar-chart.md), [waffle-chart](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/waffle-chart.md), [dumbbell-chart](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/dumbbell-chart.md)
- Used by: [visual-essay](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/visual-essay.md)

## Stat row (`stat-row`)

> Two to five key figures in one row, as open numbers separated by hairlines or as stat tiles of any variant, collapsing to two columns and then one as the container narrows.

- Component: `StatRow` (import from `insightcharts`)
- Spec type: `"stat-row"`
- Level: molecule. Category: layout.
- An HTML component: it takes only the props listed below, plus `theme`, `mode`, `className` and `style` where its source declares them. It does not take the common chart props.

### When to use

The opening summary of a report or dashboard: the two to five most important numbers. Give every figure a delta or a context line, and order them by importance.

### Avoid

More than five figures (use `kpi-grid`), a single lead number (use `big-number` with `size: "hero"`), or figures that need their history shown (use `kpi-grid`, or `variant: "tiles"` with a `trend`).

### Install

From npm (the component ships in the package):

```bash
npm install insightcharts echarts
```

Or copy the source into your project with the shadcn CLI, so you can edit it (the engine still comes from the `insightcharts` package):

```bash
npx shadcn@latest registry add @insightcharts=https://insightcharts.dev/r/{name}.json   # once per project
npx shadcn@latest add @insightcharts/stat-row
```

The file lands at `components/insightcharts/molecules/stat-row.tsx`. `@insightcharts/stat-row-demo` adds a ready-made example next to it.

### Usage

```tsx
import { StatRow } from "insightcharts";

<StatRow
  title="Renewables supplied 31.7% of the world's electricity in 2024"
  subtitle="Global electricity generation, 2024"
  items={[
    {
      value: 0.317,
      format: "percent",
      label: "Share from renewables",
      delta: "+1.9 pts",
      deltaLabel: "vs 2023",
    },
    { value: 2131, label: "Solar generation, TWh", delta: 0.29, deltaLabel: "vs 2023" },
    { value: 2494, label: "Wind generation, TWh", delta: 0.079, deltaLabel: "vs 2023" },
    {
      value: 0.409,
      format: "percent",
      label: "Share from all clean sources",
      context: "Above 40% for the first time since the 1940s",
    },
  ]}
  source="Ember, Global Electricity Review 2025"
  note="Figures are approximate, for illustration"
/>
```

### JSON spec

The same thing as data, rendered with `<Insight spec={spec} />`:

```json
{
  "type": "stat-row",
  "title": "Renewables supplied 31.7% of the world's electricity in 2024",
  "subtitle": "Global electricity generation, 2024",
  "items": [
    {
      "value": 0.317,
      "format": "percent",
      "label": "Share from renewables",
      "delta": "+1.9 pts",
      "deltaLabel": "vs 2023"
    },
    { "value": 2131, "label": "Solar generation, TWh", "delta": 0.29, "deltaLabel": "vs 2023" },
    { "value": 2494, "label": "Wind generation, TWh", "delta": 0.079, "deltaLabel": "vs 2023" },
    {
      "value": 0.409,
      "format": "percent",
      "label": "Share from all clean sources",
      "context": "Above 40% for the first time since the 1940s"
    }
  ],
  "source": "Ember, Global Electricity Review 2025",
  "note": "Figures are approximate, for illustration"
}
```

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `items` (required) | `{ value, label, context?, delta?, deltaLabel?, upIsGood?, format?, trend?, variant?, surface?, tone?, size?, align?, series?, target?, targetLabel?, max?, comparison?, comparisonLabel?, valueLabel?, parts?, icon?, unitValue?, rank?, rankOf?, orientation?, edge? }[]` |  | Two to five figures, most important first. In `plain` each takes the props of `big-number`; otherwise each takes the props of `stat-tile`, and an item's own `variant`, `surface`, `tone` and `size` override the row's. |
| `variant` | `"plain" \| "tiles" \| StatTileVariant` | `"plain"` | `plain`: open `big-number` figures divided by hairlines. `tiles`: bordered `stat-tile` cards. Any `stat-tile` variant (`sparkline`, `area`, `bars`, `dots`, `progress`, `ring`, `comparison`, `delta-first`, `icon`, `unit`, `breakdown`, `rank`, `split`, `compact`, `hero`, `filled`, `tinted`, `borderless`, `outline-accent`) draws every item as that tile. Setting `variant` on any item also switches the row to tiles. |
| `surface` | `"plain" \| "borderless" \| "filled" \| "tinted" \| "outline-accent"` |  | Tiles only: the ground of every tile. |
| `tone` | `"neutral" \| "accent" \| "positive" \| "negative" \| number \| "series"` |  | Tone of every tile. `series` gives each tile the next categorical colour, for figures that name different entities. |
| `layout` | `"cards" \| "dividers"` | `"cards"` | Tiles only: separate cards, or open tiles with hairlines between them. |
| `columns` | `number` |  | Preferred number of columns. Default: one row when every figure has room. |
| `featured` | `boolean` | `false` | The first figure spans two columns and is set one size larger. |
| `density` | `"dense" \| "default" \| "roomy"` | `"default"` | Spacing and type scale: tiles are `sm`, `md` or `lg`. |
| `align` | `"left" \| "center"` | `"left"` | Text alignment of every figure. |
| `frame` | `boolean` |  | Set false to stop a named theme painting its ground. |
| `format` | `FormatSpec` | `"auto"` | Number format for every figure that does not set its own. |
| `title` | `string` |  | The main fact with its number, or a plain label. |
| `subtitle` | `string` |  | Population and period the figures share. |
| `source` | `string` |  | Shown under the row as "Source: ...". |
| `note` | `string` |  | Method note or caveat. |
| `theme` | `ThemeInput` |  | A theme name such as `"ledger"`, or token overrides, passed on to every figure. A named theme paints its own ground. |
| `mode` | `"auto" \| "system" \| "light" \| "dark"` | `"auto"` | Colour mode, passed on to every figure. |

### Composition

- Composes: [big-number](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/big-number.md), [stat-tile](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/stat-tile.md)
- Used by: [data-explorer](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/data-explorer.md), [executive-brief](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/executive-brief.md), [report-page](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/report-page.md), [visual-essay](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/visual-essay.md)

## Trend card (`trend-card`)

> A KPI card computed from a series: the latest value, its change against a baseline in the same data, and a trend graphic, in any `stat-tile` variant.

- Component: `TrendCard` (import from `insightcharts`)
- Spec type: `"trend-card"`
- Level: molecule. Category: layout.
- An HTML component: it takes only the props listed below, plus `theme`, `mode`, `className` and `style` where its source declares them. It does not take the common chart props.

### When to use

A metric whose recent history matters as much as its level: users, revenue, response time. Pass the series and field names; the figure, the change and the sparkline all come from the same rows, so they cannot disagree.

### Avoid

A number with no history (use `big-number` or `stat-tile`); several metrics from one dataset (use `kpi-grid`); a series the reader must read values from (use `line-chart`).

### Install

From npm (the component ships in the package):

```bash
npm install insightcharts echarts
```

Or copy the source into your project with the shadcn CLI, so you can edit it (the engine still comes from the `insightcharts` package):

```bash
npx shadcn@latest registry add @insightcharts=https://insightcharts.dev/r/{name}.json   # once per project
npx shadcn@latest add @insightcharts/trend-card
```

The file lands at `components/insightcharts/molecules/trend-card.tsx`. `@insightcharts/trend-card-demo` adds a ready-made example next to it.

### Usage

```tsx
import { TrendCard } from "insightcharts";

const data = [
  { month: "2024-01-01", users: 38100 },
  { month: "2024-02-01", users: 39400 },
  { month: "2024-03-01", users: 39000 },
  { month: "2024-04-01", users: 40800 },
  { month: "2024-05-01", users: 42200 },
  { month: "2024-06-01", users: 41900 },
  { month: "2024-07-01", users: 43500 },
  { month: "2024-08-01", users: 44100 },
  { month: "2024-09-01", users: 44500 },
  { month: "2024-10-01", users: 46000 },
  { month: "2024-11-01", users: 47200 },
  { month: "2024-12-01", users: 48210 },
];

<TrendCard
  label="Monthly active users"
  data={data}
  x="month"
  y="users"
  format="compact"
  style={{ maxWidth: 300 }}
/>
```

### JSON spec

The same thing as data, rendered with `<Insight spec={spec} />`:

```json
{
  "type": "trend-card",
  "label": "Monthly active users",
  "data": [
    { "month": "2024-01-01", "users": 38100 },
    { "month": "2024-02-01", "users": 39400 },
    { "month": "2024-03-01", "users": 39000 },
    { "month": "2024-04-01", "users": 40800 },
    { "month": "2024-05-01", "users": 42200 },
    { "month": "2024-06-01", "users": 41900 },
    { "month": "2024-07-01", "users": 43500 },
    { "month": "2024-08-01", "users": 44100 },
    { "month": "2024-09-01", "users": 44500 },
    { "month": "2024-10-01", "users": 46000 },
    { "month": "2024-11-01", "users": 47200 },
    { "month": "2024-12-01", "users": 48210 }
  ],
  "x": "month",
  "y": "users",
  "format": "compact",
  "style": { "maxWidth": 300 }
}
```

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `label` (required) | `string` |  | What the figure measures, sentence case. |
| `data` | `DataInput` |  | Rows in time order, one per period. Omit inside `<InsightData>`. |
| `transform` | `Transform \| Transform[]` |  | Applied to the rows before anything is computed. |
| `y` (required) | `string` |  | Value field: the series drawn and the source of the figure and its change. |
| `x` | `string` |  | Period field, used to name the baseline and in the sparkline tooltip. |
| `value` | `number \| string` |  | The figure shown. Default: the last row's `y`. |
| `delta` | `number \| string` |  | The change shown. Default: computed from the series according to `compare`. |
| `compare` | `"first" \| "previous" \| number` | `"first"` | Baseline for the computed change: first row, previous row, or a number of rows back (12 for year-on-year in monthly data). |
| `change` | `"percent" \| "absolute"` | `"percent"` | Relative change, or the difference between the two values (use for rates and shares). An absolute change of a percentage is shown in percentage points. |
| `deltaFormat` | `FormatSpec` |  | Format for a computed absolute change, e.g. `"{value} pp"` or `"signed"`. Default: points ("+1.9 pts") when `format` is a percentage, otherwise `format`. |
| `deltaLabel` | `string` |  | What the change is against. Default: "since {first period}" when `x` is given. |
| `upIsGood` | `boolean` | `true` | Whether an increase is good news; decides the delta colour. |
| `context` | `string` |  | A line under the figure that gives it meaning. |
| `format` | `FormatSpec` | `"auto"` | Number format for the figure and the sparkline tooltip. |
| `kind` | `"line" \| "bar"` | `"line"` | Sparkline form: a line for a trend, bars for discrete counts. |
| `area` | `boolean` | `false` | Light fill under the line; the scale then includes zero. |
| `trendPosition` | `"bottom" \| "right"` | `"bottom"` | Where the sparkline sits; `right` falls back to `bottom` in narrow cards. |
| `variant` | `StatTileVariant` |  | The tile display: any `stat-tile` variant (`sparkline`, `area`, `bars`, `dots`, `split`, `compact`, `progress`, `ring`, `comparison`, `delta-first`, `icon`, `breakdown`, `rank`, `unit`, `hero`, `filled`, `tinted`, `borderless`, `outline-accent`, `plain`). The series is passed as the tile's `series`; `comparison` takes the baseline value and both period names from the rows. Omit for the original card with an interactive `sparkline` atom (tooltip on hover). |
| `showTrend` | `boolean` | `true` | With a `variant` that does not draw the series itself (`filled`, `icon`, `hero`, `delta-first`...), a line is drawn at the bottom; set false to leave it off. |
| `surface` | `"plain" \| "borderless" \| "filled" \| "tinted" \| "outline-accent"` |  | The tile's ground, with any `variant`. |
| `tone` | `"neutral" \| "accent" \| "positive" \| "negative" \| number` |  | Colour of the tile's graphic or ground; a number picks a categorical colour, 0-based. |
| `size` | `"sm" \| "md" \| "lg"` | `"md"` | Tile scale. |
| `align` | `"left" \| "center" \| "right"` |  | Text alignment. |
| `orientation` | `"vertical" \| "horizontal"` |  | Graphic under or beside the figure, as in `stat-tile`. |
| `icon` | `IconInput` |  | Icon for the `icon` and `unit` variants. |
| `target` | `number` |  | Goal for the `progress` and `ring` variants. |
| `targetLabel` | `string` | `"Target"` | Name for the target. |
| `max` | `number` |  | End of the scale for `progress` and `ring`; total count for `unit`. |
| `parts` | `{ label: string; value: number }[]` |  | Composition of the latest value, for `breakdown`. |
| `rank` | `number` |  | Position for the `rank` variant. |
| `rankOf` | `number` |  | Entries ranked. |
| `unitValue` | `number` |  | What one icon stands for in `unit`. |
| `edge` | `"left" \| "top"` |  | Edge of the rule on an `outline-accent` surface. |
| `frame` | `boolean` |  | Set false to stop a named theme painting its ground. |
| `theme` | `ThemeInput` |  | A theme name such as `"ledger"`, or token overrides, passed on to the tile. A named theme paints its own ground. |
| `mode` | `"auto" \| "system" \| "light" \| "dark"` | `"auto"` | Colour mode. |

### Composition

- Composes: [stat-tile](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/stat-tile.md), [sparkline](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/sparkline.md)
- Used by: [kpi-grid](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/kpi-grid.md)

## Atlas poster (`atlas-poster`)

> A landscape spread of up to eleven small illustrations of one subject, each a different graphic form, in three bands of unequal panels: a statement in large type, spokes round an icon and a network of circles; a smooth trend with its peak labelled, nested squares and a slope chart; a pill ranking, a treemap, a tile map and sized circles; and a closing row of icon statements.

- Component: `AtlasPoster` (import from `insightcharts`)
- Spec type: `"atlas-poster"`
- Level: template. Category: infographic.
- An HTML component: it takes only the props listed below, plus `theme`, `mode`, `className` and `style` where its source declares them. It does not take the common chart props.

### When to use

Use it when one subject has many small facts of different kinds (shares, places, a trend, a change, a ranking, a map) and none of them should dominate: a crop, an industry, a service, a country's internet. Fill at least eight regions. Give every panel a short heading that states its one number. Every region is optional, and each band shares its width among the panels that are present.

### Avoid

One dominant fact or graphic (use `count-poster`, `flow-poster` or `ranking-poster`). The same measures across several entities (use `matrix-poster`). Fewer than six panels (use `poster` and place them yourself). A phone-first piece: the spread becomes one long column under 600px.

### Install

From npm (the component ships in the package):

```bash
npm install insightcharts echarts
```

Or copy the source into your project with the shadcn CLI, so you can edit it (the engine still comes from the `insightcharts` package):

```bash
npx shadcn@latest registry add @insightcharts=https://insightcharts.dev/r/{name}.json   # once per project
npx shadcn@latest add @insightcharts/atlas-poster
```

The file lands at `components/insightcharts/templates/atlas-poster.tsx`. `@insightcharts/atlas-poster-demo` adds a ready-made example next to it.

### Usage

```tsx
import { AtlasPoster } from "insightcharts";

<AtlasPoster
  theme="forest"
  kicker="Food"
  title="Norland's orchards picked 2.4 million tonnes of apples in 2025"
  subtitle="Harvest, regions, varieties, prices and exports of the apple crop."
  statement={{
    value: "2.4m",
```

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `statement` | `{ value, label, context?, icon? }` |  | Band 1, left: the subject's main number in large light type, in the accent colour. |
| `spokes` | `{ data, name, value, icon?, centerLabel?, highlight?, title?, ...radial-spokes props } \| Slot` |  | Band 1, middle: 4 to 12 attributes as spokes round a centre icon (`radial-spokes`). |
| `network` | `{ data, name, value, links, highlight?, tag?, title?, ...bubble-network props } \| Slot` |  | Band 1, right: named places or things as circles sized by value and joined by lines (`bubble-network`). |
| `trend` | `{ data, x, y, peak?, format?, title?, ...area-chart props } \| Slot` |  | Band 2, wide: one measure over an ordered dimension as a smooth filled curve (`area-chart`). The highest point is labelled with its value and position; `peak` replaces that label, and `peak: false` removes it. |
| `area` | `{ data, name, value, ratio?, title?, ...proportional-area props } \| Slot` |  | Band 2: two or three quantities as squares nested from one corner, with a bracket stating the ratio (`proportional-area`, `layout: "nested"`). |
| `slope` | `{ data, series, y: [from, to], names?, highlight?, title?, ...slope-chart props } \| Slot` |  | Band 2: each entity at two dates, joined by a line and labelled at the end (`slope-chart`). |
| `rank` | `{ data, name, value, highlight?, title?, ...pill-rank props } \| Slot` |  | Band 3: a ranking of 4 to 6 rows as centred pills (`pill-rank`). Pass a `bar-chart` spec for bars instead. |
| `parts` | `{ data, name, value, title?, ...treemap props } \| Slot` |  | Band 3: the parts of one whole as tiles (`treemap`). |
| `map` | `{ data, region, value, code?, geo?, title?, ...choropleth-map props } \| Slot` |  | Band 3: a tile map shaded by value (`choropleth-map`). Give every row `col` and `row`, the tile's place in the grid, and the template builds the squares; `code` names the field printed on each tile. Pass `geo` to use your own GeoJSON. |
| `circles` | `{ data, name, value, unit?, title?, ...stat-circles props } \| Slot` |  | Band 3: two to four magnitudes as sized circles (`stat-circles`). |
| `stats` | `{ count, total?, text, icon?, value? }[]` |  | Closing row: up to three "3 in 10" statements, each a row of icons with some filled (`icon-stat`). |
| `title` (required) | `string` |  | The poster's one fact, as a plain sentence with its number. |
| `kicker` | `string` |  | Small label above the title: the topic. |
| `subtitle` | `string` |  | One line under the title: the measure, population and period. |
| `theme` | `PosterThemeName \| string \| ThemeInput` | `"forest"` | Poster theme: `noir`, `magenta`, `dusk`, `ocean`, `forest`, `blueprint`, `sunrise`, `paper`, any other theme name, or a theme object. |
| `mode` | `"light" \| "dark" \| "auto" \| "system"` | `"light"` | Colour mode of the poster and everything in it. A poster paints its own ground and does not follow the page unless you set `auto`. Only `paper` has a different dark variant. |
| `download` | `boolean` | `false` | Show a "Download PNG" control under the poster that saves the whole poster as one image. |
| `maxWidth` | `number \| string` | `1440` | Widest the poster is drawn. It is centred in wider containers. |
| `linked` | `boolean` | `false` | Make the marks clickable. Clicking a mark in one graphic highlights the same name in every other graphic that has it, and filters the graphics that read the shared `data`. Click it again, or the empty ground of that graphic, to clear. |
| `data` | `DataInput` |  | Rows shared by every region whose config leaves out its own `data`. With `linked`, a click filters those regions. |
| `sources` | `string \| string[]` |  | Where the data comes from, shown in the footer. |
| `note` | `string` |  | Caveat shown in the footer, e.g. "Illustrative data". |
| `credit` | `string` |  | Who made the poster, shown at the right of the footer. |
| `level` | `1 \| 2 \| 3 \| 4 \| 5` | `2` | Heading level of the title. Panel headings are one level down. |

### Composition

- Composes: [poster](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/poster.md), [radial-spokes](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/radial-spokes.md), [bubble-network](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/bubble-network.md), [area-chart](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/area-chart.md), [proportional-area](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/proportional-area.md), [slope-chart](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/slope-chart.md), [pill-rank](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/pill-rank.md), [treemap](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/treemap.md), [choropleth-map](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/choropleth-map.md), [stat-circles](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/stat-circles.md), [icon-stat](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/icon-stat.md)
- Used by: no molecule or template yet

### More examples

#### Dusk, a space programme, ten panels, with download

```tsx
import { AtlasPoster } from "insightcharts";

<AtlasPoster
  theme="dusk"
  download
  kicker="Space"
  title="The Norland Space Agency put 42 satellites into orbit in 2025"
  subtitle="Satellites, launches, ground stations, costs and budget of one national space programme."
  statement={{ value: "42", label: "Satellites launched in 2025", context: "38 in 2024", icon: "satellite" }}
  spokes={{
    data: [
      { purpose: "Earth observation", n: 14 },
      { purpose: "Communications", n: 11 },
      { purpose: "Navigation", n: 6 },
      { purpose: "Weather", n: 5 },
      { purpose: "Science", n: 4 },
      { purpose: "Technology tests", n: 2 },
    ],
    name: "purpose",
    value: "n",
    icon: "satellite",
    highlight: "Earth observation",
    title: "14 of the satellites observe the Earth",
  }}
  network={{
    data: [
      { station: "Skarvik", passes: 96 },
      { station: "Holm Pass", passes: 64 },
      { station: "Sundby", passes: 48 },
      { station: "Tarn Head", passes: 31 },
      { station: "Aldern", passes: 22 },
    ],
    name: "station",
    value: "passes",
    links: [
      { from: "Skarvik", to: "Holm Pass" },
      { from: "Skarvik", to: "Sundby" },
      { from: "Skarvik", to: "Tarn Head" },
      { from: "Skarvik", to: "Aldern" },
      { from: "Sundby", to: "Aldern" },
    ],
    highlight: "Skarvik",
    tag: "Control centre",
    title: "Skarvik tracked 96 satellite passes a day",
    subtitle: "Passes tracked per day by ground station. Lines are data links.",
  }}
  trend={{
    data: [
      { year: "2013", n: 3 },
      { year: "2014", n: 4 },
      { year: "2015", n: 4 },
      { year: "2016", n: 6 },
      { year: "2017", n: 9 },
      { year: "2018", n: 8 },
      { year: "2019", n: 13 },
      { year: "2020", n: 17 },
      { year: "2021", n: 24 },
      { year: "2022", n: 31 },
      { year: "2023", n: 46 },
      { year: "2024", n: 38 },
      { year: "2025", n: 42 },
    ],
    x: "year",
    y: "n",
    format: "integer",
    title: "The agency launched 46 satellites in 2023",
    subtitle: "Satellites put into orbit per year, 2013 to 2025",
  }}
  area={{
    data: [{ year: "2025", t: 60 }, { year: "2015", t: 4 }],
    name: "year",
    value: "t",
    format: "{value} t",
    ratio: "{ratio}x the mass",
    title: "60 tonnes reached orbit in 2025",
    subtitle: "Mass put into orbit per year, tonnes",
  }}
  slope={{
    data: [
      { rocket: "Small launcher", y2015: 41, y2025: 18 },
      { rocket: "Medium launcher", y2015: 22, y2025: 7 },
      { rocket: "Shared ride", y2015: 15, y2025: 4 },
    ],
    series: "rocket",
    y: ["y2015", "y2025"],
    names: { y2015: "2015", y2025: "2025" },
    highlight: "Shared ride",
    format: "€{value}k",
    title: "A shared ride cost €4,000 a kilogram in 2025",
    subtitle: "Launch price per kilogram, thousand euros",
  }}
  rank={{
    data: [
      { programme: "Launch services", m: 310 },
      { programme: "Earth observation", m: 240 },
      { programme: "Communications", m: 150 },
      { programme: "Science missions", m: 90 },
      { programme: "Ground stations", m: 60 },
    ],
    name: "programme",
    value: "m",
    format: "€{value}m",
    highlight: "Launch services",
    title: "Launch services cost €310 million",
  }}
  parts={{
    data: [
      { builder: "Agency workshops", n: 18 },
      { builder: "Universities", n: 13 },
      { builder: "Industry", n: 11 },
    ],
    name: "builder",
    value: "n",
    highlight: "Universities",
    title: "Universities built 13 of the 42 satellites",
  }}
  circles={{
    data: [
      { kind: "kg, relay satellite", kg: 4200 },
      { kind: "kg, weather satellite", kg: 1100 },
      { kind: "kg, cubesat", kg: 12 },
    ],
    name: "kind",
    value: "kg",
    format: "integer",
    title: "A relay satellite weighs 4,200 kg",
  }}
  stats={[
    { icon: "rocket", count: 9, total: 10, text: "launches reached their planned orbit." },
    { icon: "satellite", count: 3, total: 10, text: "satellites were built by universities." },
  ]}
  sources="Norland Space Agency annual report 2025"
  note="The Norland Space Agency is invented. All figures are illustrative."
  credit="InsightCharts"
/>
```

#### Sunrise, a country's internet, linked

```tsx
import { AtlasPoster } from "insightcharts";

<AtlasPoster
  theme="sunrise"
  linked
  kicker="The internet"
  title="94% of Norland's households were online in 2025"
  subtitle="Use, traffic, networks and speeds of the internet in one country."
  statement={{
    value: "94%",
    label: "Households with an internet connection in 2025",
    context: "81% in 2015",
    icon: "laptop",
  }}
  spokes={{
    data: [
      { use: "Messaging", share: 81 },
      { use: "Video", share: 64 },
      { use: "News", share: 52 },
      { use: "Shopping", share: 31 },
      { use: "Banking", share: 28 },
      { use: "Learning", share: 12 },
      { use: "Games", share: 24 },
    ],
    name: "use",
    value: "share",
    format: "{value}%",
    icon: "phone",
    highlight: "Messaging",
    title: "81% of adults sent a message online every day",
  }}
  network={{
    data: [
      { site: "Norvik", mw: 180 },
      { site: "Castren", mw: 120 },
      { site: "Sundby", mw: 75 },
      { site: "Eastmark", mw: 40 },
      { site: "Aldern", mw: 25 },
      { site: "Skarvik", mw: 15 },
    ],
    name: "site",
    value: "mw",
    links: [
      { from: "Norvik", to: "Castren" },
      { from: "Norvik", to: "Sundby" },
      { from: "Norvik", to: "Skarvik" },
      { from: "Norvik", to: "Aldern" },
      { from: "Castren", to: "Eastmark" },
      { from: "Sundby", to: "Eastmark" },
    ],
    highlight: "Norvik",
    tag: "Main exchange",
    format: "{value} MW",
    title: "Norvik's data centres drew 180 MW",
    subtitle: "Data-centre power by site, megawatts. Lines are trunk fibre routes.",
```

## Comparison brief (`comparison-brief`)

> A compared with B on one page. It has a headline that states the result, the headline figures mirrored either side of their labels, one hero exhibit that shows both sides, paired exhibits on a shared scale, a verdict callout and a source note.

- Component: `ComparisonBrief` (import from `insightcharts`)
- Spec type: `"comparison-brief"`
- Level: template. Category: layout.
- An HTML component: it takes only the props listed below, plus `theme`, `mode`, `className` and `style` where its source declares them. It does not take the common chart props.

### When to use

Use it for two things a reader has to choose between or compare, such as two countries, two products or a before and an after. Write the result with its number in the headline. Put the four or five most important measures in `figures`. Use a two-series line, dumbbell, slope or `before-after` as the hero. In each pair, use the same chart form and the same scale for both sides. The `subject` side takes the accent colour everywhere and the other side stays grey.

### Avoid

Three or more things (use a `comparison-table` or `small-multiple-grid` inside a `report-page`). One thing over time with nothing to compare it with (use `timeline-story`). Paired charts on different scales, because readers compare bar lengths across the pair.

### Install

From npm (the component ships in the package):

```bash
npm install insightcharts echarts
```

Or copy the source into your project with the shadcn CLI, so you can edit it (the engine still comes from the `insightcharts` package):

```bash
npx shadcn@latest registry add @insightcharts=https://insightcharts.dev/r/{name}.json   # once per project
npx shadcn@latest add @insightcharts/comparison-brief
```

The file lands at `components/insightcharts/templates/comparison-brief.tsx`. `@insightcharts/comparison-brief-demo` adds a ready-made example next to it.

### Usage

```tsx
import { BarChart, ComparisonBrief, LineChart, SegmentedBar } from "insightcharts";

<ComparisonBrief
  theme="earth"
  kicker="Home heating"
  title="With the £7,500 grant, a heat pump repays its extra £500 cost in 4 years"
  deck="After the grant a heat pump costs £3,500 to buy and fit. A gas boiler costs £3,000. The heat pump costs £855 a year to run. The boiler costs £980."
  a={{ name: "Heat pump", detail: "Air source, 7 kW" }}
  b={{ name: "Gas boiler", detail: "Condensing combi, 30 kW" }}
  figures={[
    {
      label: "Cost to buy and fit, after grant",
      a: 3500,
      b: 3000,
      format: { style: "currency", currency: "GBP", maximumFractionDigits: 0 },
      better: "lower",
    },
    { label: "Running cost per year", a: 855, b: 980, format: "currency:GBP", better: "lower" },
    { label: "CO2 per year, tonnes", a: 0.6, b: 2.3, format: "decimal:1", better: "lower" },
    {
      label: "Heat out per unit of energy in",
      a: 3.2,
      b: 0.9,
      format: "decimal:1",
      better: "higher",
    },
    { label: "Expected life, years", a: 20, b: 15, better: "higher" },
  ]}
  hero={<LineChart
    data={[
      { year: "0", saving: -500 },
      { year: "1", saving: -375 },
      { year: "2", saving: -250 },
      { year: "3", saving: -125 },
      { year: "4", saving: 0 },
      { year: "5", saving: 125 },
      { year: "6", saving: 250 },
      { year: "7", saving: 375 },
      { year: "8", saving: 500 },
      { year: "9", saving: 625 },
      { year: "10", saving: 750 },
      { year: "11", saving: 875 },
      { year: "12", saving: 1000 },
      { year: "13", saving: 1125 },
      { year: "14", saving: 1250 },
      { year: "15", saving: 1375 },
    ]}
    x="year"
    y="saving"
    format={{ style: "currency", currency: "GBP", maximumFractionDigits: 0, signDisplay: "exceptZero" }}
    area
    title="After 15 years the heat pump has cost £1,375 less than the boiler"
    subtitle="Cumulative saving of a heat pump over a gas boiler in pounds, by years since installation. Includes purchase after the £7,500 grant, energy and servicing"
    annotations={[
      {
        type: "line",
        axis: "y",
        value: 0,
        label: "Same cost as the boiler",
        dashed: false,
        emphasis: true,
      },
      { type: "point", x: "4", y: 0, label: "Break-even", position: "top" },
    ]}
  />}
  heroText="Without the grant the heat pump costs £11,000 to buy and fit. That is £8,000 more than the boiler. A saving of £125 a year would take 64 years to repay it."
  pairs={[
    {
      title: "The January energy bill is £120 for the heat pump and £139 for the boiler",
      text: "Estimated monthly energy cost for heating and hot water. Both charts use the same scale. The heat pump's bill is lower in all 12 months.",
      a: <BarChart
        data={[
          { month: "Jan", cost: 120 },
          { month: "Feb", cost: 108 },
          { month: "Mar", cost: 86 },
          { month: "Apr", cost: 57 },
          { month: "May", cost: 34 },
          { month: "Jun", cost: 24 },
          { month: "Jul", cost: 21 },
          { month: "Aug", cost: 22 },
          { month: "Sep", cost: 32 },
          { month: "Oct", cost: 56 },
          { month: "Nov", cost: 83 },
          { month: "Dec", cost: 112 },
        ]}
        x="month"
        y="cost"
        orientation="vertical"
        sort="none"
        labels={false}
        format="currency:GBP"
        height={200}
        option={{ yAxis: { max: 140 } }}
      />,
      b: <BarChart
        data={[
          { month: "Jan", cost: 139 },
          { month: "Feb", cost: 124 },
          { month: "Mar", cost: 101 },
          { month: "Apr", cost: 69 },
          { month: "May", cost: 43 },
          { month: "Jun", cost: 33 },
          { month: "Jul", cost: 30 },
          { month: "Aug", cost: 31 },
          { month: "Sep", cost: 41 },
          { month: "Oct", cost: 65 },
          { month: "Nov", cost: 94 },
          { month: "Dec", cost: 130 },
        ]}
        x="month"
        y="cost"
        orientation="vertical"
        sort="none"
        labels={false}
        format="currency:GBP"
        height={200}
        highlight="none"
        option={{ yAxis: { max: 140 } }}
      />,
    },
    {
      title: "Cost over 15 years by part",
      text: "Energy is £11,325 of the heat pump's £16,325. It is £13,500 of the boiler's £17,700.",
      a: <SegmentedBar
        data={[
          { part: "Purchase and fitting", gbp: 3500 },
          { part: "Energy", gbp: 11325 },
          { part: "Servicing", gbp: 1500 },
        ]}
        name="part"
        value="gbp"
        format="currency:GBP"
      />,
      b: <SegmentedBar
        data={[
          { part: "Purchase and fitting", gbp: 3000 },
          { part: "Energy", gbp: 13500 },
          { part: "Servicing", gbp: 1200 },
        ]}
        name="part"
        value="gbp"
        format="currency:GBP"
      />,
    },
  ]}
  verdict={{
    lead: "Choose the heat pump if you get the grant and will stay at least 5 years",
    body: "Without the grant the boiler is cheaper. The figures assume electricity and gas prices stay at their Q4 2024 levels.",
  }}
  sources={["Energy regulator price cap, Q4 2024", "Installer quotes collected by the author"]}
  method="A house using 11,500 kWh of heat a year. Heat pump seasonal efficiency is 3.2. Boiler efficiency is 90%. Prices held flat in real terms."
  note="Illustrative data"
/>
```

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `title` (required) | `string` |  | The result of the comparison, as one plain sentence with the number in it. |
| `kicker` | `string` |  | Small label above the title. |
| `deck` | `string` |  | One-sentence standfirst. |
| `byline` | `string` |  | Author line. |
| `date` | `string` |  | Publication date. |
| `a` (required) | `string \| { name, detail? }` |  | Side A, shown on the left. |
| `b` (required) | `string \| { name, detail? }` |  | Side B, shown on the right. |
| `subject` | `"a" \| "b" \| "none"` | `"a"` | The side the piece is about. It takes the accent colour; the other stays grey. Match it with `highlight` in the charts. |
| `figures` | `{ label, a, b, format?, better?: "higher" \| "lower" }[]` |  | Headline measures. Numeric values get mirrored bars scaled within each row; `better` sets the stronger value bolder. |
| `hero` | `Slot` |  | The exhibit that shows both sides at once. Default height 360px. |
| `heroText` | `string` |  | One or two sentences under the hero. |
| `pairs` | `{ title, text?, a: Slot, b: Slot }[]` |  | Paired exhibits under one heading. A is on the left and B on the right; they stack in narrow containers. Use the same form and scale for both. |
| `verdict` | `{ lead?, body?, label?, tone? }` |  | The closing recommendation, shown as a callout. |
| `sources` | `string \| { name, url? } \| (string \| { name, url? })[]` |  | Where the data comes from, shown in the closing source note. Entries with a `url` are linked. |
| `period` | `string` |  | The period the data covers. |
| `method` | `string` |  | How the numbers were produced: definitions, adjustments, exclusions. |
| `note` | `string` |  | Caveats the reader should know, e.g. "Illustrative data". |
| `credit` | `string` |  | Who made the piece. |
| `level` | `1 \| 2 \| 3 \| 4 \| 5 \| 6` | `1` | Heading level of the title; section headings follow one level down. |
| `maxWidth` | `number \| string` |  | Widest the piece may get. It is centred in wider containers. |
| `theme` | `ThemeInput` |  | A built-in theme name (`"editorial"`, `"ledger"`, `"noir"`...) or a theme object, passed on to everything inside. A named theme with its own surface paints that surface behind the whole piece. |
| `frame` | `boolean` |  | Paint the theme's surface behind the piece, with page padding. Default: on when `theme` is a named theme with its own surface. Set false when the host already paints it. |
| `mode` | `"auto" \| "system" \| "light" \| "dark"` | `"auto"` | Colour mode, passed on to everything inside. |

### Composition

- Composes: [headline](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/headline.md), [prose](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/prose.md), [callout](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/callout.md), [source-note](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/source-note.md), [line-chart](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/line-chart.md), [bar-chart](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/bar-chart.md), [segmented-bar](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/segmented-bar.md), [waffle-chart](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/waffle-chart.md)
- Used by: no molecule or template yet

### More examples

#### Transport: a stacked hero and a pair of waffles

```tsx
import { BarChart, ComparisonBrief, WaffleChart } from "insightcharts";

<ComparisonBrief
  theme="poster"
  kicker="London to Edinburgh"
  title="Flying from London to Edinburgh is 35 minutes faster than the train, door to door"
  deck="The plane takes 275 minutes and the train 310. The flight itself lasts 80 minutes. The plane emits 140 kg of CO2 per passenger. The train emits 13 kg."
  a="Train"
  b="Plane"
  figures={[
    { label: "Door to door, minutes", a: 310, b: 275, better: "lower" },
    { label: "CO2 per passenger, kg", a: 13, b: 140, better: "lower" },
    {
      label: "Typical fare booked two weeks ahead",
      a: 78,
      b: 92,
      format: "currency:GBP",
      better: "lower",
    },
    { label: "Minutes you can spend working", a: 240, b: 50, better: "higher" },
  ]}
  hero={<BarChart
    data={[
      {
        mode: "Train",
        "Getting there": 25,
        "Waiting and boarding": 15,
        "In transit": 260,
        Onward: 10,
      },
      {
        mode: "Plane",
        "Getting there": 55,
        "Waiting and boarding": 95,
        "In transit": 80,
        Onward: 45,
      },
    ]}
    x="mode"
    y={["Getting there", "Waiting and boarding", "In transit", "Onward"]}
    stack
    orientation="horizontal"
    sort="none"
    format="{value} min"
    title="80 of the plane's 275 minutes are spent in the air"
    subtitle="Minutes per stage, city centre to city centre"
    source="Timetables and airport guidance, weekday morning departures"
  />}
  pairs={[
    {
      title: "240 of the train's 310 minutes can be spent working",
      text: "On the plane it is 50 of 275 minutes. Each square is 1% of the journey.",
      a: <WaffleChart
        data={[{ part: "Working time", minutes: 240 }]}
        name="part"
        value="minutes"
        total={310}
        restLabel="Other time"
        format="{value} min"
        aspect={1.6}
      />,
      b: <WaffleChart
        data={[{ part: "Working time", minutes: 50 }]}
        name="part"
        value="minutes"
        total={275}
        restLabel="Other time"
        format="{value} min"
        aspect={1.6}
        highlight="none"
      />,
    },
  ]}
  verdict={{
    lead: "Take the train unless you need the 35 minutes",
    body: "The train fare is £78 and the plane fare is £92. The train gives 240 minutes of working time. The plane gives 50.",
    tone: "positive",
  }}
  sources={["Operator timetables", "Government greenhouse gas conversion factors"]}
  note="Illustrative fares and times"
/>
```

## Count poster (`count-poster`)

> A poster that counts at scale. Blocks of thousands of unit icons fill most of the sheet, a second band counts reference groups with the same icon at the same size in a muted colour, and a bottom row holds three small graphics: squares sized by area with a ratio bracket, thick bars with the numbers inside, and shares as nested outlines or filled silhouettes.

- Component: `CountPoster` (import from `insightcharts`)
- Spec type: `"count-poster"`
- Level: template. Category: infographic.
- An HTML component: it takes only the props listed below, plus `theme`, `mode`, `className` and `style` where its source declares them. It does not take the common chart props.

### When to use

Use it when the subject is a large count of people or things in 2 to 6 groups and the reader should see the crowd: pupils by stage, trees planted by species, vehicles built by model. Give `hero` the groups and `reference` one to three quantities to compare them with. Both bands use the same `unit`, `icon` and icon size, so their areas compare. State the total in the title.

### Avoid

Counts under a few hundred (use `pictogram-chart` in a `poster`). Shares of one whole as the main point (use `waffle-chart` or `treemap`). A ranking of many named things (use `ranking-poster`). A flow from sources to destinations (use `flow-poster`).

### Install

From npm (the component ships in the package):

```bash
npm install insightcharts echarts
```

Or copy the source into your project with the shadcn CLI, so you can edit it (the engine still comes from the `insightcharts` package):

```bash
npx shadcn@latest registry add @insightcharts=https://insightcharts.dev/r/{name}.json   # once per project
npx shadcn@latest add @insightcharts/count-poster
```

The file lands at `components/insightcharts/templates/count-poster.tsx`. `@insightcharts/count-poster-demo` adds a ready-made example next to it.

### Usage

```tsx
import { CountPoster } from "insightcharts";

<CountPoster
  theme="noir"
  kicker="Education"
  title="Norland's schools taught 1.84 million pupils in 2025"
  subtitle="Pupils enrolled in state schools by stage, autumn term 2025."
  unit={1000}
  unitLabel="1,000 people"
  icon="person"
  hero={{
    data: [
      { stage: "Primary", pupils: 820000 },
      { stage: "Lower secondary", pupils: 460000 },
      { stage: "Upper secondary", pupils: 390000 },
      { stage: "Vocational", pupils: 170000 },
    ],
    name: "stage",
    value: "pupils",
    title: "820,000 pupils were in primary school",
  }}
  reference={{
    data: [
      { group: "Teachers", people: 142000 },
      { group: "Support staff", people: 61000 },
      { group: "Pupils who left without a certificate", people: 38000 },
    ],
    name: "group",
    value: "people",
    title: "142,000 teachers taught them",
  }}
  area={{
    data: [
      { school: "Largest secondary school", pupils: 3640 },
      { school: "Median primary school", pupils: 280 },
    ],
    name: "school",
    value: "pupils",
    title: "The largest school had 3,640 pupils",
  }}
  bars={{
    data: [
      { year: "2000", m: 1.42 },
      { year: "2005", m: 1.51 },
      { year: "2010", m: 1.6 },
      { year: "2015", m: 1.69 },
      { year: "2020", m: 1.77 },
      { year: "2025", m: 1.84 },
    ],
    name: "year",
    value: "m",
    format: "{value}m",
    title: "Enrolment was 1.42 million in 2000",
  }}
  shares={{
    data: [
      { year: "2013", share: 6 },
      { year: "2017", share: 19 },
      { year: "2021", share: 44 },
      { year: "2025", share: 68 },
    ],
    name: "year",
    value: "share",
    highlight: "2025",
    wholeLabel: "All pupils",
    title: "68% of pupils had a school laptop in 2025",
  }}
  sources="Norland Ministry of Education, school census 2025"
  note="Norland is an invented country. All figures are illustrative."
  credit="InsightCharts"
/>
```

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `hero` (required) | `{ data, name, value, title?, subtitle?, source?, ...unit-blocks props } \| Slot` |  | The hero band: one block of unit icons per row, drawn by `unit-blocks`. A full spec or element replaces it. |
| `unit` | `number` |  | Units one icon stands for, in both bands. Default: a round number that gives the hero about 2,000 icons. |
| `unitLabel` | `string` |  | What one icon stands for, e.g. "1,000 pupils". Printed as the key of both bands. |
| `icon` | `IconName \| "path://..."` | `"person"` | Icon of both bands. |
| `format` | `FormatSpec` | `"integer"` | How to print the counts. |
| `reference` | `{ data, name, value, title?, ... } \| Slot` |  | The second band: reference groups counted with the same icon at the same size, painted in the theme's context grey (`unit-blocks`). |
| `area` | `{ data, name, value, ratio?, title?, ... } \| Slot` |  | Bottom left: two to four values as squares sized by area, with a bracket stating how many times the largest is the smallest (`proportional-area`). `ratio` defaults to `"{ratio}x larger"`. |
| `bars` | `{ data, name, value, title?, ... } \| Slot` |  | Bottom middle: 3 to 8 values as thick rounded bars with the numbers inside (`block-bar`). |
| `shares` | `{ data, name, value, icon?, title?, ... } \| Slot` |  | Bottom right: shares of one whole. With `icon` each share is a silhouette filled to its level (`shape-fill`); without, the shares are outlines nested in one square (`nested-shares`). |
| `title` (required) | `string` |  | The poster's one fact, as a plain sentence with its number. |
| `kicker` | `string` |  | Small label above the title: the topic. |
| `subtitle` | `string` |  | One line under the title: the measure, population and period. |
| `theme` | `PosterThemeName \| string \| ThemeInput` | `"noir"` | Poster theme: `noir`, `magenta`, `dusk`, `ocean`, `forest`, `blueprint`, `sunrise`, `paper`, any other theme name, or a theme object. |
| `mode` | `"light" \| "dark" \| "auto" \| "system"` | `"light"` | Colour mode of the poster and everything in it. A poster paints its own ground and does not follow the page unless you set `auto`. Only `paper` has a different dark variant. |
| `download` | `boolean` | `false` | Show a "Download PNG" control under the poster that saves the whole poster as one image. |
| `maxWidth` | `number \| string` | `1100` | Widest the poster is drawn. It is centred in wider containers. |
| `linked` | `boolean` | `false` | Make the marks clickable. Clicking a mark in one graphic highlights the same name in every other graphic that has it, and filters the graphics that read the shared `data`. Click it again, or the empty ground of that graphic, to clear. |
| `data` | `DataInput` |  | Rows shared by every region whose config leaves out its own `data`. With `linked`, a click filters those regions. |
| `sources` | `string \| string[]` |  | Where the data comes from, shown in the footer. |
| `note` | `string` |  | Caveat shown in the footer, e.g. "Illustrative data". |
| `credit` | `string` |  | Who made the poster, shown at the right of the footer. |
| `level` | `1 \| 2 \| 3 \| 4 \| 5` | `2` | Heading level of the title. Panel headings are one level down. |

### Composition

- Composes: [poster](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/poster.md), [unit-blocks](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/unit-blocks.md), [proportional-area](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/proportional-area.md), [block-bar](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/block-bar.md), [nested-shares](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/nested-shares.md), [shape-fill](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/shape-fill.md)
- Used by: no molecule or template yet

## Data explorer (`data-explorer`)

> A set of linked charts over one shared dataset that filter each other. It has a headline, a sentence of instructions with filter chips, a row of figures that recompute from the filtered rows, two to four charts and an optional detail table. It opens on selections the author chooses.

- Component: `DataExplorer` (import from `insightcharts`)
- Spec type: `"data-explorer"`
- Level: template. Category: story.
- An HTML component: it takes only the props listed below, plus `theme`, `mode`, `className` and `style` where its source declares them. It does not take the common chart props.

### When to use

Use it when readers will want to filter the data themselves after seeing the main finding. State the finding with its number in the headline. Set `initialSelections` so the piece opens on the view the headline describes. Use the figures and the `finding` callout to give the numbers for that view. Keep to one dataset and two to four small, plain charts. Readers click the charts to filter, so keep them all the same size.

### Avoid

A fixed message that needs no exploration (use `executive-brief` or `visual-essay`). Charts over unrelated datasets, which cannot filter each other. More than four charts or five figures.

### Install

From npm (the component ships in the package):

```bash
npm install insightcharts echarts
```

Or copy the source into your project with the shadcn CLI, so you can edit it (the engine still comes from the `insightcharts` package):

```bash
npx shadcn@latest registry add @insightcharts=https://insightcharts.dev/r/{name}.json   # once per project
npx shadcn@latest add @insightcharts/data-explorer
```

The file lands at `components/insightcharts/templates/data-explorer.tsx`. `@insightcharts/data-explorer-demo` adds a ready-made example next to it.

```tsx
  theme="science"
  kicker="City bike share · June"
  title="Casual riders' trips averaged 24.6 minutes in June, against 12.0 for members"
  deck="70% of casual trips were at weekends. 40% started in Riverside. The view below is filtered to casual riders."
  instructions="Click a bar to filter the other charts and the figures. Click it again to clear."
  finding={{
    lead: "Casual riders made 1.43 million of the 3.65 million trips in June",
    body: "520,000 of them were at weekend middays. Members made 34% of their trips at weekends.",
  }}
  data={data}
  unit="trips"
  figuresVariant="outline-accent"
  labels={{ rider: "Rider", daypart: "Time of day", district: "District", day: "Day" }}
  initialSelections={{ "by-rider": { field: "rider", values: ["Casual"] } }}
  figures={[
    { label: "Trips, thousands", field: "trips", format: "integer" },
    { label: "Average trip length, minutes", field: "minutes", per: "trips", format: "decimal:1" },
    {
      label: "Share taken at weekends",
      field: "trips",
      where: { field: "day", value: "Weekend" },
      per: "trips",
      format: "percent",
    },
    {
      label: "Share starting in Riverside",
      field: "trips",
      where: { field: "district", value: "Riverside" },
      per: "trips",
      format: "percent",
    },
  ]}
  charts={[
    <DonutChart
      id="by-rider"
      name="rider"
      value="trips"
      select
      format="integer"
      height={220}
      title="Rider"
      subtitle="Trips, thousands"
      transform={{ type: "aggregate", groupBy: "rider", measures: { trips: { op: "sum", field: "trips" } } }}
    />,
    <BarChart
      id="by-day"
      x="day"
      y="trips"
      select
      sort="none"
      orientation="horizontal"
      format="integer"
      title="Day"
      subtitle="Trips, thousands"
      transform={{ type: "aggregate", groupBy: "day", measures: { trips: { op: "sum", field: "trips" } } }}
    />,
    <BarChart
      id="by-daypart"
      x="daypart"
      y="trips"
      select
      sort="none"
      orientation="vertical"
      format="integer"
      height={220}
      title="Time of day"
      subtitle="Trips, thousands"
      transform={{ type: "aggregate", groupBy: "daypart", measures: { trips: { op: "sum", field: "trips" } } }}
    />,
    <LollipopChart
      id="by-district"
      x="district"
      y="trips"
      select
      sort="desc"
      format="integer"
      title="Start district"
      subtitle="Trips, thousands"
      transform={{ type: "aggregate", groupBy: "district", measures: { trips: { op: "sum", field: "trips" } } }}
    />,
  ]}
  table={{
    caption: "Selected trips by start district and time of day",
    transform: [
      {
        type: "aggregate",
        groupBy: ["district", "daypart"],
        measures: { trips: { op: "sum", field: "trips" }, minutes: { op: "sum", field: "minutes" } },
      },
      { type: "derive", as: "length", op: "divide", fields: ["minutes", "trips"] },
      { type: "sort", by: "trips", order: "desc" },
      { type: "limit", n: 6 },
    ],
    columns: [
      { key: "district", label: "District" },
      { key: "daypart", label: "Time of day" },
      { key: "trips", label: "Trips, thousands", format: "integer", bar: true, width: "34%" },
      { key: "length", label: "Average minutes", format: "decimal:1" },
    ],
  }}
  sources="City bike-share operator, trip records"
  period="June 2024"
  method="A trip is a hire of more than one minute. Morning is 6 to 10am, evening 4 to 8pm."
  note="Illustrative data"
/>
```
