### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `title` (required) | `string` |  | What the starting view shows, as one plain sentence with the number in it. |
| `kicker` | `string` |  | Small label above the title. |
| `deck` | `string` |  | One-sentence standfirst. |
| `byline` | `string` |  | Author line. |
| `date` | `string` |  | Publication date. |
| `instructions` | `string` |  | One sentence saying what can be clicked and what happens. Shown in the filter line. |
| `finding` | `{ lead?, body?, label? }` |  | A callout saying what to look for in the starting view. |
| `data` (required) | `DataInput` |  | The shared, row-level dataset: rows, CSV text, a URL or a loader. |
| `transform` | `Transform \| Transform[]` |  | Applied once to the shared data. |
| `charts` (required) | `Slot[]` |  | Two to four chart specs. Give each a stable `id`, `select: true` (or a field name) and its own aggregating `transform`; leave out `data`. |
| `initialSelections` | `Record<string, { field, values?, range? }>` |  | Selections the piece opens with, keyed by chart `id`. A button restores them after the reader changes the filter. |
| `figures` | `{ label, field?, op?, where?: { field, value }, per?, format?, context? }[]` |  | Figures recomputed from the filtered rows: `op` over `field` (default sum; count without a field), optionally restricted by `where` and divided by the sum of `per` for a rate or share. While a filter is active each shows the all-rows value as context. |
| `figuresVariant` | `StatRowProps["variant"]` | `"plain"` | How the figures are displayed: any `variant` of `stat-row`, e.g. `tiles`, `tinted` or `outline-accent`. Extra fields on a figure (`tone`, `surface`, `icon`...) are passed to its `stat-row` item. |
| `table` | `{ transform?, columns?, caption?, sort?, highlight?, ... }` |  | A detail table of the filtered rows: the props of `data-table` without `rows`, plus a `transform` applied first. |
| `labels` | `Record<string, string>` |  | Display names for fields in the filter chips. |
| `unit` | `string` | `"rows"` | Noun for what the figures total, used in figure context ("3,650 across all trips"). |
| `count` | `boolean` | `false` | Show the filtered row count beside the chips. |
| `rowUnit` | `string` | `"rows"` | Noun for one row of `data` in that count. |
| `columns` | `number` |  | Preferred chart columns. |
| `restoreLabel` | `string` | `"Back to the starting view"` | Label of the button that restores `initialSelections`. |
| `sources` | `string \| { name, url? } \| (string \| { name, url? })[]` |  | Where the data comes from, shown in the closing source note. Entries with a `url` are linked. |
| `period` | `string` |  | The period the data covers. |
| `method` | `string` |  | How the numbers were produced: definitions, adjustments, exclusions. |
| `note` | `string` |  | Caveats the reader should know, e.g. "Illustrative data". |
| `credit` | `string` |  | Who made the piece. |
| `level` | `1 \| 2 \| 3 \| 4 \| 5 \| 6` | `1` | Heading level of the title; section headings follow one level down. |
| `maxWidth` | `number \| string` |  | Widest the piece may get. It is centred in wider containers. |
| `theme` | `ThemeInput` |  | A built-in theme name (`"editorial"`, `"ledger"`, `"noir"`...) or a theme object, passed on to everything inside. A named theme with its own surface paints that surface behind the whole piece. |
| `frame` | `boolean` |  | Paint the theme's surface behind the piece, with page padding. Default: on when `theme` is a named theme with its own surface. Set false when the host already paints it. |
| `mode` | `"auto" \| "system" \| "light" \| "dark"` | `"auto"` | Colour mode, passed on to everything inside. |

### Composition

- Composes: [headline](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/headline.md), [callout](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/callout.md), [filter-chips](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/filter-chips.md), [stat-row](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/stat-row.md), [linked-charts](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/linked-charts.md), [data-table](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/data-table.md), [source-note](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/source-note.md), [bar-chart](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/bar-chart.md), [donut-chart](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/donut-chart.md), [lollipop-chart](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/lollipop-chart.md), [segmented-bar](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/segmented-bar.md)
- Used by: no molecule or template yet

### More examples

#### Education: rates rather than totals, two starting filters

```tsx
import { BarChart, DataExplorer, LollipopChart } from "insightcharts";

const data = [
  { phase: "Primary", meals: "Eligible", term: "Autumn", sessions: 410, missed: 31.16 },
  { phase: "Primary", meals: "Eligible", term: "Spring", sessions: 410, missed: 34.44 },
  { phase: "Primary", meals: "Eligible", term: "Summer", sessions: 410, missed: 33.21 },
  { phase: "Primary", meals: "Not eligible", term: "Autumn", sessions: 1320, missed: 60.72 },
  { phase: "Primary", meals: "Not eligible", term: "Spring", sessions: 1320, missed: 68.64 },
  { phase: "Primary", meals: "Not eligible", term: "Summer", sessions: 1320, missed: 64.68 },
  { phase: "Secondary", meals: "Eligible", term: "Autumn", sessions: 300, missed: 39.3 },
  { phase: "Secondary", meals: "Eligible", term: "Spring", sessions: 300, missed: 43.8 },
  // ... 10 more rows
];

<DataExplorer
  theme="ocean"
  kicker="School attendance · 2023/24"
  title="Secondary pupils on free school meals missed 14.5% of sessions in 2023/24"
  deck="The rate for all pupils was 7.2%. For secondary pupils on free school meals it was 13.1% in the autumn term and 15.8% in the summer term."
  instructions="Click a bar to filter the other charts and the figures. The bars show absence rates, not totals."
  data={data}
  unit="pupil groups"
  figuresVariant="tiles"
  labels={{ phase: "School type", meals: "Free school meals", term: "Term" }}
  initialSelections={{
    "by-phase": { field: "phase", values: ["Secondary"] },
    "by-meals": { field: "meals", values: ["Eligible"] },
  }}
  figures={[
    {
      label: "Absence rate",
      field: "missed",
      per: "sessions",
      format: { style: "percent", maximumFractionDigits: 1 },
    },
    { label: "Sessions missed, thousands", field: "missed", format: "decimal:1" },
    { label: "Sessions possible, thousands", field: "sessions", format: "integer" },
  ]}
  charts={[
    <BarChart
      id="by-phase"
      x="phase"
      y="rate"
      select
      sort="none"
      orientation="horizontal"
      format={{ style: "percent", maximumFractionDigits: 1 }}
      title="School type"
      subtitle="Absence rate"
      transform={[
        {
          type: "aggregate",
          groupBy: "phase",
          measures: { missed: { op: "sum", field: "missed" }, sessions: { op: "sum", field: "sessions" } },
        },
        { type: "derive", as: "rate", op: "divide", fields: ["missed", "sessions"] },
      ]}
    />,
    <BarChart
      id="by-meals"
      x="meals"
      y="rate"
      select
      sort="none"
      orientation="horizontal"
      format={{ style: "percent", maximumFractionDigits: 1 }}
      title="Free school meals"
      subtitle="Absence rate"
      transform={[
        {
          type: "aggregate",
          groupBy: "meals",
          measures: { missed: { op: "sum", field: "missed" }, sessions: { op: "sum", field: "sessions" } },
        },
        { type: "derive", as: "rate", op: "divide", fields: ["missed", "sessions"] },
      ]}
    />,
    <LollipopChart
      id="by-term"
      x="term"
      y="rate"
      select
      sort="none"
      format={{ style: "percent", maximumFractionDigits: 1 }}
      title="Term"
      subtitle="Absence rate"
      transform={[
        {
          type: "aggregate",
          groupBy: "term",
          measures: { missed: { op: "sum", field: "missed" }, sessions: { op: "sum", field: "sessions" } },
        },
        { type: "derive", as: "rate", op: "divide", fields: ["missed", "sessions"] },
      ]}
    />,
  ]}
  sources="Local authority attendance returns"
  period="School year 2023/24"
  method="A session is half a school day. The absence rate is sessions missed, authorised or not, as a share of sessions possible."
  note="Illustrative data"
/>
```

#### Customer support: default theme, three chart forms and a table

```tsx
import { BarChart, DataExplorer, DonutChart, SegmentedBar } from "insightcharts";

const data = [
  { channel: "Email", plan: "Free", area: "Billing", tickets: 310, hours: 4340 },
  { channel: "Email", plan: "Free", area: "Login", tickets: 420, hours: 5880 },
  { channel: "Email", plan: "Free", area: "Sync", tickets: 150, hours: 3150 },
  { channel: "Email", plan: "Free", area: "Reports", tickets: 60, hours: 840 },
  { channel: "Email", plan: "Paid", area: "Billing", tickets: 260, hours: 3640 },
  { channel: "Email", plan: "Paid", area: "Login", tickets: 140, hours: 1960 },
  { channel: "Email", plan: "Paid", area: "Sync", tickets: 330, hours: 6930 },
  { channel: "Email", plan: "Paid", area: "Reports", tickets: 170, hours: 2380 },
  // ... 12 more rows
];

<DataExplorer
  kicker="Support desk · Q3 2024"
  title="Sync tickets took 12.2 hours to resolve on average in Q3, against 9.9 for all tickets"
  deck="78% of sync tickets came from paid plans. Sync tickets sent by email took 21.0 hours. The view below is filtered to sync tickets."
  instructions="Click a mark to filter the other charts, the figures and the table. Click it again to clear."
  finding={{
    lead: "Sync was 1,110 of the 3,690 tickets in Q3",
    body: "480 of them arrived by email and took 21.0 hours on average. The 500 that arrived by chat took 4.5 hours.",
  }}
  data={data}
  unit="tickets"
  figuresVariant="tinted"
  labels={{ area: "Product area", channel: "Channel", plan: "Plan" }}
  initialSelections={{ "by-area": { field: "area", values: ["Sync"] } }}
  figures={[
    { label: "Tickets", field: "tickets", format: "integer" },
    { label: "Average hours to resolve", field: "hours", per: "tickets", format: "decimal:1" },
    {
      label: "Share from paid plans",
      field: "tickets",
      where: { field: "plan", value: "Paid" },
      per: "tickets",
      format: "percent",
    },
    {
      label: "Share sent by email",
      field: "tickets",
      where: { field: "channel", value: "Email" },
      per: "tickets",
      format: "percent",
    },
  ]}
  charts={[
    <BarChart
      id="by-area"
      x="area"
      y="tickets"
      select
      sort="desc"
      orientation="horizontal"
      format="integer"
      title="Product area"
      subtitle="Tickets"
      transform={{ type: "aggregate", groupBy: "area", measures: { tickets: { op: "sum", field: "tickets" } } }}
    />,
    <DonutChart
      id="by-channel"
      name="channel"
      value="tickets"
      select
      format="integer"
      height={220}
      title="Channel"
      subtitle="Tickets"
      transform={{
        type: "aggregate",
        groupBy: "channel",
        measures: { tickets: { op: "sum", field: "tickets" } },
      }}
    />,
    <SegmentedBar
      id="by-plan"
      name="plan"
      value="tickets"
      select
      format="integer"
      title="Plan"
      subtitle="Tickets"
      transform={{ type: "aggregate", groupBy: "plan", measures: { tickets: { op: "sum", field: "tickets" } } }}
    />,
  ]}
  table={{
    caption: "Selected tickets by channel and plan",
    transform: [
      {
        type: "aggregate",
        groupBy: ["channel", "plan"],
        measures: { tickets: { op: "sum", field: "tickets" }, hours: { op: "sum", field: "hours" } },
      },
      { type: "derive", as: "each", op: "divide", fields: ["hours", "tickets"] },
      { type: "sort", by: "tickets", order: "desc" },
    ],
    columns: [
      { key: "channel", label: "Channel" },
      { key: "plan", label: "Plan" },
      { key: "tickets", label: "Tickets", format: "integer", bar: true, width: "34%" },
      { key: "each", label: "Average hours", format: "decimal:1" },
    ],
  }}
  sources="Support desk ticket export"
  period="July to September 2024"
  method="Hours to resolve run from the first message to the ticket being closed, including nights and weekends."
  note="Illustrative data"
/>
```

## Executive brief (`executive-brief`)

> A one-page summary. It has a headline that states the main finding with its number, a deck, a row of three or four key figures, one hero chart with a takeaway callout, two smaller supporting exhibits, a short list of actions and a source note.

- Component: `ExecutiveBrief` (import from `insightcharts`)
- Spec type: `"executive-brief"`
- Level: template. Category: layout.
- An HTML component: it takes only the props listed below, plus `theme`, `mode`, `className` and `style` where its source declares them. It does not take the common chart props.

### When to use

Use it when a decision-maker will spend about a minute on the page. State the main finding with its number and period in the headline. The headline and the hero chart should be enough for a reader who stops there. The figures, supporting exhibits and actions add detail. Use one accent colour for the subject (`highlight`) and leave everything else grey. Mark the cause on the hero as an annotation. The proportions suit a printed page.

### Avoid

More than one hero or more than three supporting exhibits (use `report-page`). A recurring set of numbers with no single finding (use `scorecard`). A story told in several steps (use `visual-essay`).

### Install

From npm (the component ships in the package):

```bash
npm install insightcharts echarts
```

Or copy the source into your project with the shadcn CLI, so you can edit it (the engine still comes from the `insightcharts` package):

```bash
npx shadcn@latest registry add @insightcharts=https://insightcharts.dev/r/{name}.json   # once per project
npx shadcn@latest add @insightcharts/executive-brief
```

The file lands at `components/insightcharts/templates/executive-brief.tsx`. `@insightcharts/executive-brief-demo` adds a ready-made example next to it.

### Usage

```tsx
import { DumbbellChart, ExecutiveBrief, LineChart, SlopeChart } from "insightcharts";

<ExecutiveBrief
  theme="ledger"
  kicker="Retention review · Q4 2024"
  title="Monthly churn fell from 4.2% to 2.1% in 2024"
  deck="The new onboarding shipped in March. Accounts that joined before March still churn at 3.8% a month."
  byline="Growth analytics"
  date="2025-01-14"
  figures={{
    variant: "tiles",
    items: [
      {
        surface: "outline-accent",
        edge: "top",
        value: "2.1%",
        label: "Monthly churn, December",
        delta: "−2.1 pts",
        deltaLabel: "vs January",
        upIsGood: false,
      },
      {
        surface: "outline-accent",
        edge: "top",
        value: 0.61,
        format: "percent",
        label: "New accounts finishing setup in week one",
        delta: "+19 pts",
        deltaLabel: "vs January",
      },
      {
        surface: "outline-accent",
        edge: "top",
        value: 1.12,
        format: "percent",
        label: "Net revenue retention",
        context: "Top quartile for the sector is 110%",
      },
      {
        surface: "outline-accent",
        edge: "top",
        value: "$1.9m",
        label: "Annual revenue retained",
        context: "Compared with churn staying at the January rate of 4.2%",
      },
    ],
  }}
  hero={<LineChart
    data={[
      { month: "2024-01-01", churn: 4.2, prior: 4.4 },
      { month: "2024-02-01", churn: 4.3, prior: 4.3 },
      { month: "2024-03-01", churn: 4.1, prior: 4.4 },
      { month: "2024-04-01", churn: 3.6, prior: 4.2 },
      { month: "2024-05-01", churn: 3.1, prior: 4.3 },
      { month: "2024-06-01", churn: 2.9, prior: 4.1 },
      { month: "2024-07-01", churn: 2.6, prior: 4.2 },
      { month: "2024-08-01", churn: 2.4, prior: 4.3 },
      { month: "2024-09-01", churn: 2.3, prior: 4.1 },
      { month: "2024-10-01", churn: 2.2, prior: 4.2 },
      { month: "2024-11-01", churn: 2.1, prior: 4.3 },
      { month: "2024-12-01", churn: 2.1, prior: 4.2 },
    ]}
    x="month"
    y={["churn", "prior"]}
    names={{ churn: "2024", prior: "2023" }}
    highlight="churn"
    contextLabels
    format="{value}%"
    zero
    title="Monthly churn fell from 4.1% in March to 2.1% in December"
    subtitle="Share of paying accounts cancelling each month, 2024 and the same months of 2023"
    annotations={[
      { type: "line", axis: "x", value: "2024-03-01", label: "New onboarding ships" },
      { type: "band", axis: "y", from: 2, to: 2.5, label: "Target range" },
    ]}
    source="Billing system"
  />}
  takeaway={{
    lead: "Churn was between 2.1% and 2.4% from August to December",
    body: "The new onboarding shipped in March. Churn was between 4.1% and 4.4% in every month of 2023.",
  }}
  supporting={[
    <DumbbellChart
      data={[
        { plan: "Starter", jan: 6.1, dec: 2.9 },
        { plan: "Team", jan: 4, dec: 2 },
        { plan: "Business", jan: 2.4, dec: 1.6 },
        { plan: "Enterprise", jan: 0.9, dec: 0.8 },
      ]}
      category="plan"
      from="jan"
      to="dec"
      names={{ jan: "January", dec: "December" }}
      format="{value}%"
      sort="none"
      highlight="Starter"
      title="Starter plan churn fell from 6.1% to 2.9%"
      subtitle="Monthly churn by plan, January and December 2024"
    />,
    <SlopeChart
      data={[
        { reason: "Setup not finished", before: 38, after: 14 },
        { reason: "Too expensive", before: 22, after: 27 },
        { reason: "Missing a feature", before: 17, after: 24 },
        { reason: "Went to a rival", before: 13, after: 19 },
        { reason: "Company closed", before: 10, after: 16 },
      ]}
      series="reason"
      y={["before", "after"]}
      names={{ before: "Q1", after: "Q4" }}
      format="{value}%"
      highlight="Setup not finished"
      height={260}
      title="“Setup not finished” fell from 38% to 14% of cancellations"
      subtitle="Share of cancellations by stated reason, Q1 and Q4 2024"
    />,
  ]}
  actions={[
    {
      title: "Offer the guided setup to the 2,400 accounts that joined before March",
      text: "These accounts churn at 3.8% a month.",
      owner: "Lifecycle · by end of February",
    },
    {
      title: "Make the setup checklist the default on the Team plan",
      text: "The checklist is opt-in on Team today. Team churn was 2.0% in December.",
      owner: "Product · Q1",
    },
    {

      text: "That will give 12 months of data since the new onboarding shipped.",
      owner: "Growth analytics",
    },
  ]}
  sources={["Billing system", "Product analytics warehouse"]}
  period="January to December 2024, monthly"
  method="Churn is the share of accounts paying at the start of a month that cancel during it. Downgrades are not counted."
  note="Illustrative data"
/>
```

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `title` (required) | `string` |  | The main finding, as one plain sentence with the number and the period in it. |
| `kicker` | `string` |  | Small label above the title: the report series or team. |
| `deck` | `string` |  | One to three short sentences. Each states one more fact. |
| `byline` | `string` |  | Author line, shown as written. |
| `date` | `string` |  | Publication date. ISO dates are formatted for the locale. |
| `figures` | `StatRowItem[] \| StatRowProps` |  | Three or four key figures, most important first. A list of `{ value, label, context?, delta?, deltaLabel?, upIsGood?, format? }`, or the props of `stat-row` (`{ items, variant, ... }`) to choose how they are drawn. |
| `hero` (required) | `Slot` |  | The hero exhibit: a chart spec or element whose `title` states one fact with its number. Gets a height of 340px (260px on phones) unless it sets one. |
| `takeaway` | `{ lead?, body?, label?, tone? }` |  | The callout beside the hero. `lead` is one short sentence stating the main fact. `body` gives the supporting numbers. |
| `supporting` | `Slot[]` |  | Two (at most three) smaller exhibits shown side by side; they stack in narrow containers. Default height 220px. |
| `actions` | `(string \| { title, text?, owner? })[]` |  | Recommended actions, numbered. Two to four. |
| `actionsTitle` | `string` | `"What to do"` | Heading of the actions list. |
| `sources` | `string \| { name, url? } \| (string \| { name, url? })[]` |  | Where the data comes from, shown in the closing source note. Entries with a `url` are linked. |
| `period` | `string` |  | The period the data covers. |
| `method` | `string` |  | How the numbers were produced: definitions, adjustments, exclusions. |
| `note` | `string` |  | Caveats the reader should know, e.g. "Illustrative data". |
| `credit` | `string` |  | Who made the piece. |
| `level` | `1 \| 2 \| 3 \| 4 \| 5 \| 6` | `1` | Heading level of the title; section headings follow one level down. |
| `maxWidth` | `number \| string` |  | Widest the piece may get. It is centred in wider containers. |
| `theme` | `ThemeInput` |  | A built-in theme name (`"editorial"`, `"ledger"`, `"noir"`...) or a theme object, passed on to everything inside. A named theme with its own surface paints that surface behind the whole piece. |
| `frame` | `boolean` |  | Paint the theme's surface behind the piece, with page padding. Default: on when `theme` is a named theme with its own surface. Set false when the host already paints it. |
| `mode` | `"auto" \| "system" \| "light" \| "dark"` | `"auto"` | Colour mode, passed on to everything inside. |

### Composition

- Composes: [headline](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/headline.md), [stat-row](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/stat-row.md), [chart-callout](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/chart-callout.md), [prose](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/prose.md), [source-note](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/source-note.md), [line-chart](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/line-chart.md), [dumbbell-chart](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/dumbbell-chart.md), [slope-chart](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/slope-chart.md), [bar-chart](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/bar-chart.md), [heatmap](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/heatmap.md), [diverging-bar-chart](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/diverging-bar-chart.md)
- Used by: no molecule or template yet

## Explainer (`explainer`)

> A vertical infographic in one narrow column. It opens with a big number or a proportion statement (`hook`), then the hero exhibit, then numbered sections with one exhibit each, a conclusion with an optional link, and sources.

- Component: `Explainer` (import from `insightcharts`)
- Spec type: `"explainer"`
- Level: template. Category: story.
- An HTML component: it takes only the props listed below, plus `theme`, `mode`, `className` and `style` where its source declares them. It does not take the common chart props.

### When to use

Use it to explain one subject to a general audience in a single narrow column. The column also works as a tall image or on a phone screen. State the main finding with its number in the headline and repeat the main number in `hook`. Make the hero exhibit the largest thing on the page. Give each numbered section one heading, one exhibit and one sentence with its main number. Write each section so it can be read without the others. Keep one accent colour on the subject (`highlight`) throughout.

### Avoid

Findings that need caveats and separate interpretation (use `report-page`). A chart that has to change step by step (use `visual-essay` with a scrolly block). More than five sections, because readers stop before the end.

### Install

From npm (the component ships in the package):

```bash
npm install insightcharts echarts
```

Or copy the source into your project with the shadcn CLI, so you can edit it (the engine still comes from the `insightcharts` package):

```bash
npx shadcn@latest registry add @insightcharts=https://insightcharts.dev/r/{name}.json   # once per project
npx shadcn@latest add @insightcharts/explainer
```

The file lands at `components/insightcharts/templates/explainer.tsx`. `@insightcharts/explainer-demo` adds a ready-made example next to it.

### Usage

```tsx
import { BarChart, DonutChart, Explainer, IconStat, PictogramChart } from "insightcharts";

<Explainer
  theme="sunrise"
  kicker="Food and climate"
  title="Households threw away 631 million tonnes of food in 2022"
  deck="That is 60% of the 1.05 billion tonnes of food wasted worldwide. Food service wasted 290 million tonnes and retail 131 million."
  hook={{
    value: 19,
    total: 100,
    text: "tonnes of food that reach shops, restaurants and homes are thrown away.",
    detail: "That was 1.05 billion tonnes in 2022.",
  }}
  hero={<DonutChart
    data={[
      { sector: "Households", mt: 631 },
      { sector: "Food service", mt: 290 },
      { sector: "Retail", mt: 131 },
    ]}
    name="sector"
    value="mt"
    format="{value} Mt"
    centerLabel="Million tonnes wasted"
    centerValue="1,052"
    height={340}
    title="Households produced 60% of the world's food waste in 2022"
    subtitle="Food waste by sector, million tonnes (Mt), 2022"
    source="UNEP Food Waste Index Report 2024"
    note="Figures are approximate, for illustration"
  />}
  heroText="Food service produced 290 million tonnes, or 28%. Retail produced 131 million tonnes, or 12%."
  sections={[
    {
      title: "Household food waste by income group",
      text: "Households in high-income countries waste 81 kg of food per person a year. In upper-middle-income countries the figure is 88 kg. In lower-middle-income countries it is 86 kg.",
      exhibit: <PictogramChart
        data={[
          { group: "High income", kg: 81 },
          { group: "Upper-middle", kg: 88 },
          { group: "Lower-middle", kg: 86 },
        ]}
        name="group"
        value="kg"
        unit={10}
        unitLabel="10 kg of food"
        icon="apple"
        format="{value} kg"
        subtitle="Household food waste per person per year, by country income group"
      />,
      takeaway: "The three income groups are within 7 kg per person of each other.",
    },
    {
      title: "Lost and wasted food causes 4.4 billion tonnes of emissions a year",
      text: "Growing, transporting and chilling food uses land, fertiliser and fuel. Food releases methane when it rots. Lost and wasted food causes 8 to 10% of global greenhouse gas emissions.",
      exhibit: <BarChart
        data={[
          { emitter: "China", gt: 13 },
          { emitter: "United States", gt: 6 },
          { emitter: "Wasted food", gt: 4.4 },
          { emitter: "India", gt: 3.9 },
          { emitter: "European Union", gt: 3.4 },
        ]}
        x="emitter"
        y="gt"
        sort="desc"
        orientation="horizontal"
        highlight="Wasted food"
        format="{value} Gt"
        subtitle="Annual greenhouse gas emissions, billion tonnes of CO2 equivalent. Wasted food includes losses before retail"
      />,
      takeaway: "Only China and the United States emit more than lost and wasted food.",
    },
    {
      title: "733 million people faced hunger in 2023",
      exhibit: <IconStat
        icon="person"
        tone="negative"
        count={1}
        total={11}
        columns={11}
        text="people in the world faced hunger in 2023."
      />,
    },
  ]}
  conclusion={{
    title: "The UN target is to halve food waste by 2030",
    text: "Britain and Japan publish household food waste figures. Britain has cut household waste by 18% and Japan by 31%.",
    points: [
      "Measure household food waste and publish the figure every year.",
      "State on packaging that “best before” refers to quality and “use by” refers to safety.",
      "Plan meals before shopping and freeze food that will not be eaten in time.",
    ],
    action: {
      label: "Read the UNEP report",
      href: "https://www.unep.org/resources/publication/food-waste-index-report-2024",
    },
  }}
  sources={[
    {
      name: "UNEP Food Waste Index Report 2024",
      url: "https://www.unep.org/resources/publication/food-waste-index-report-2024",
    },
    "FAO, State of Food Security and Nutrition in the World 2024",
    "Emissions figures rounded from national inventories",
  ]}
  note="Figures are approximate, for illustration"
  period="2022 (waste), 2023 (hunger and emissions)"
  method="Food waste is measured at retail, food service and household level and includes inedible parts. Losses on farms and in transport are counted separately."
/>
```

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `title` (required) | `string` |  | The main finding, as one plain sentence with the number and the period in it. |
| `kicker` | `string` |  | Small label above the title. |
| `deck` | `string` |  | One-sentence standfirst. |
| `byline` | `string` |  | Author line. |
| `date` | `string` |  | Publication date. |
| `hook` | `{ value, total?, text?, figure?, visual?, icon?, detail?, label?, context?, format?, variant?, tone?, series?, target?, max? } \| Slot` |  | The opening number. With `text` it renders a `proportion-statement` ("19 in every 100 ..."); with `label` a hero `big-number`, which also takes that atom's `variant` (`filled`, `tinted`, `with-icon`, `with-ring`, `with-trend`), `tone`, `icon`, `series`, `target` and `max`. A spec or element is rendered as given. |
| `hero` | `Slot` |  | The main exhibit. Its `title` states one fact with its number. Default height 360px. |
| `heroText` | `string` |  | One or two sentences under the hero. Each states one more fact. |
| `sections` | `{ title, text?, exhibit?, takeaway?, id? }[]` |  | Numbered sections. Each has a heading, one exhibit and a `takeaway` sentence with its main number. |
| `screenful` | `boolean` | `false` | Give every section at least the height of the viewport and centre its content, so each fills a screen. |
| `conclusion` | `{ title, text?, points?, action?: { label, href } }` |  | The closing block: a heading, text, a list of actions and an optional link. |
| `sources` | `string \| { name, url? } \| (string \| { name, url? })[]` |  | Where the data comes from, shown in the closing source note. Entries with a `url` are linked. |
| `period` | `string` |  | The period the data covers. |
| `method` | `string` |  | How the numbers were produced: definitions, adjustments, exclusions. |
| `note` | `string` |  | Caveats the reader should know, e.g. "Illustrative data". |
| `credit` | `string` |  | Who made the piece. |
| `level` | `1 \| 2 \| 3 \| 4 \| 5 \| 6` | `1` | Heading level of the title; section headings follow one level down. |
| `maxWidth` | `number \| string` |  | Widest the piece may get. It is centred in wider containers. |
| `theme` | `ThemeInput` |  | A built-in theme name (`"editorial"`, `"ledger"`, `"noir"`...) or a theme object, passed on to everything inside. A named theme with its own surface paints that surface behind the whole piece. |
| `frame` | `boolean` |  | Paint the theme's surface behind the piece, with page padding. Default: on when `theme` is a named theme with its own surface. Set false when the host already paints it. |
| `mode` | `"auto" \| "system" \| "light" \| "dark"` | `"auto"` | Colour mode, passed on to everything inside. |

### Composition

- Composes: [headline](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/headline.md), [big-number](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/big-number.md), [proportion-statement](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/proportion-statement.md), [step-marker](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/step-marker.md), [prose](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/prose.md), [callout](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/callout.md), [source-note](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/source-note.md), [bar-chart](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/bar-chart.md), [donut-chart](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/donut-chart.md), [pictogram-chart](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/pictogram-chart.md), [icon-stat](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/icon-stat.md), [line-chart](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/line-chart.md), [segmented-bar](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/segmented-bar.md), [treemap](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/treemap.md), [lollipop-chart](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/lollipop-chart.md)
- Used by: no molecule or template yet

## Flow poster (`flow-poster`)

> A portrait poster of where something comes from and where it goes, in three stacked bands painted in one colour: the producers as large labelled tiles, the leading producer's output fanning out as ribbons to an aligned column of destinations, and the destinations as bubbles on a scale of how much each depends on that producer.

- Component: `FlowPoster` (import from `insightcharts`)
- Spec type: `"flow-poster"`
- Level: template. Category: infographic.
- An HTML component: it takes only the props listed below, plus `theme`, `mode`, `className` and `style` where its source declares them. It does not take the common chart props.

### When to use

Use it when one producer leads and the reader should follow its output: ports and the buyers of one port's catch, regions and the users of one region's electricity, terminals and the routes out of the largest. Give `producers` 4 to 10 rows, `flow` 4 to 12 destinations of the leading producer, and `scale` the same destinations with a share (position) and a size. Keep the destination names identical in `flow` and `scale` so `linked` can join them.

### Avoid

Flows through more than one stage or between many sources and many destinations (use `sankey-chart` in a `poster`). A count of people or things (use `count-poster`). Many measures of the same entities (use `matrix-poster`).

### Install

From npm (the component ships in the package):

```bash
npm install insightcharts echarts
```

Or copy the source into your project with the shadcn CLI, so you can edit it (the engine still comes from the `insightcharts` package):

```bash
npx shadcn@latest registry add @insightcharts=https://insightcharts.dev/r/{name}.json   # once per project
npx shadcn@latest add @insightcharts/flow-poster
```

The file lands at `components/insightcharts/templates/flow-poster.tsx`. `@insightcharts/flow-poster-demo` adds a ready-made example next to it.

### Usage

```tsx
import { FlowPoster } from "insightcharts";

<FlowPoster
  theme="magenta"
  kicker="Fishing"
  title="Six ports on the Verran Coast landed 412,000 tonnes of fish in 2025"
  subtitle="Landings by port, the buyers of Port Alda's catch, and how much each buyer relies on Port Alda. Thousand tonnes (kt)."
  format="{value} kt"
  producers={{
    data: [
      { port: "Port Alda", kt: 148 },
      { port: "Skerry", kt: 96 },
      { port: "Marrow Bay", kt: 71 },
      { port: "Tolven", kt: 52 },
      { port: "Hask", kt: 28 },
      { port: "Lund", kt: 17 },
    ],
    name: "port",
    value: "kt",
    title: "Port Alda landed 148,000 of the 412,000 tonnes",
  }}
  flow={{
    data: [
      { buyer: "Canneries", kt: 46 },
      { buyer: "Fresh markets", kt: 34 },
      { buyer: "Frozen export", kt: 29 },
      { buyer: "Fishmeal plants", kt: 21 },
      { buyer: "Restaurants", kt: 11 },
      { buyer: "Smokehouses", kt: 7 },
    ],
    name: "buyer",
    value: "kt",
    trunk: "Port Alda",
    title: "Canneries bought 46,000 tonnes of Port Alda's catch",
  }}
  scale={{
    data: [
      { buyer: "Canneries", fromAlda: 56, kt: 82 },
      { buyer: "Fresh markets", fromAlda: 35, kt: 96 },
      { buyer: "Frozen export", fromAlda: 23, kt: 124 },
      { buyer: "Fishmeal plants", fromAlda: 34, kt: 61 },
      { buyer: "Restaurants", fromAlda: 29, kt: 38 },
      { buyer: "Smokehouses", fromAlda: 64, kt: 11 },
    ],
    name: "buyer",
    value: "fromAlda",
    size: "kt",
    sizeFormat: "{value} kt",
    scaleLabel: "From Port Alda",
    title: "Smokehouses bought 64% of their fish from Port Alda",
    subtitle: "Share of each buyer's fish landed at Port Alda (position) and all the fish it bought (area)",
  }}
  sources="Verran Coast Fisheries Board landing returns"
  note="The Verran Coast is an invented place. All figures are illustrative."
  credit="InsightCharts"
/>
```

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `producers` (required) | `{ data, name, value, title?, subtitle?, source?, ...treemap props } \| Slot` |  | Top band: the producers as tiles sized by output (`treemap`). The leading one is painted in the accent. |
| `lead` | `string` |  | The producer the flow starts from. Default: the largest row of `producers`. It names the block the ribbons leave. |
| `flow` (required) | `{ data, name, value, trunk?, tagged?, tagLabel?, title?, ...fan-flow props } \| Slot` |  | Middle band: one ribbon per destination, as thick as its value, ending at a column of names, values and shares (`fan-flow`). |
| `scale` | `{ data, name, value, size, scaleLabel?, sizeFormat?, title?, ...bubble-scale props } \| Slot` |  | Bottom band: one bubble per destination, placed by `value` on a 0 to 100 scale and sized by `size` (`bubble-scale`). Set `domain` and `ticks` for a scale that is not a percentage. |
| `format` | `FormatSpec` |  | How to print the quantities of the top and middle bands, e.g. `"{value} kt"`. |
| `title` (required) | `string` |  | The poster's one fact, as a plain sentence with its number. |
| `kicker` | `string` |  | Small label above the title: the topic. |
| `subtitle` | `string` |  | One line under the title: the measure, population and period. |
| `theme` | `PosterThemeName \| string \| ThemeInput` | `"magenta"` | Poster theme: `noir`, `magenta`, `dusk`, `ocean`, `forest`, `blueprint`, `sunrise`, `paper`, any other theme name, or a theme object. |
| `mode` | `"light" \| "dark" \| "auto" \| "system"` | `"light"` | Colour mode of the poster and everything in it. A poster paints its own ground and does not follow the page unless you set `auto`. Only `paper` has a different dark variant. |
| `download` | `boolean` | `false` | Show a "Download PNG" control under the poster that saves the whole poster as one image. |
| `maxWidth` | `number \| string` | `920` | Widest the poster is drawn. It is centred in wider containers. |
| `linked` | `boolean` | `false` | Make the marks clickable. Clicking a mark in one graphic highlights the same name in every other graphic that has it, and filters the graphics that read the shared `data`. Click it again, or the empty ground of that graphic, to clear. |
| `data` | `DataInput` |  | Rows shared by every region whose config leaves out its own `data`. With `linked`, a click filters those regions. |
| `sources` | `string \| string[]` |  | Where the data comes from, shown in the footer. |
| `note` | `string` |  | Caveat shown in the footer, e.g. "Illustrative data". |
| `credit` | `string` |  | Who made the poster, shown at the right of the footer. |
| `level` | `1 \| 2 \| 3 \| 4 \| 5` | `2` | Heading level of the title. Panel headings are one level down. |

### Composition

- Composes: [poster](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/poster.md), [treemap](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/treemap.md), [fan-flow](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/fan-flow.md), [bubble-scale](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/bubble-scale.md)
- Used by: no molecule or template yet

## Matrix poster (`matrix-poster`)

> One wide landscape graphic that compares 4 to 12 entities on five to seven measures: two measures as S-curves between parallel scales on the left, joined to a table on the right in which every other number is drawn as dots, squares, icons, a ring, a circle or a bar. Both halves share one row order and one colour per entity.

- Component: `MatrixPoster` (import from `insightcharts`)
- Spec type: `"matrix-poster"`
- Level: template. Category: infographic.
- An HTML component: it takes only the props listed below, plus `theme`, `mode`, `className` and `style` where its source declares them. It does not take the common chart props.

### When to use

Use it for profiles of a handful of comparable things with measures in different units: cities, species, products, stations, teams. Pass one row per entity with every measure in it. Put the two measures whose relationship matters in `curve` and the rest in `columns`, choosing a counted glyph (`dots`, `blocks`, `icons`) for small whole numbers, `ring` for shares, `bar` or `circle` for magnitudes. Leave `highlight` out to give every entity its own colour, derived from the theme when its palette is smaller than the number of entities; set it to draw one or two entities in colour and the rest in grey.

### Avoid

One measure across entities (use `pill-rank` or `bar-chart`). More than 12 entities (use `data-table` or `heatmap`). A subject with a total and its parts (use `ranking-poster` or `flow-poster`). A phone-first piece: the table stacks into cards under 600px and the poster becomes long.

### Install

From npm (the component ships in the package):

```bash
npm install insightcharts echarts
```

Or copy the source into your project with the shadcn CLI, so you can edit it (the engine still comes from the `insightcharts` package):

```bash
npx shadcn@latest registry add @insightcharts=https://insightcharts.dev/r/{name}.json   # once per project
npx shadcn@latest add @insightcharts/matrix-poster
```

The file lands at `components/insightcharts/templates/matrix-poster.tsx`. `@insightcharts/matrix-poster-demo` adds a ready-made example next to it.

### Usage

```tsx
import { MatrixPoster } from "insightcharts";

<MatrixPoster
  theme="paper"
  kicker="Cities"
  title="A one-bedroom flat in Avenmouth rented for €1,640 a month in 2025"
  subtitle="Eight cities of Norland compared on rent, pay and five measures of daily life, 2025."
  rows={[
    {
      city: "Avenmouth",
      rent: 1640,
      pay: 3900,
      transit: 38,
      parks: 14,
      lanes: 212,
      cafes: 23,
      sun: 148,
    },
    {
      city: "Brackley Bay",
      rent: 1480,
      pay: 3300,
      transit: 22,
      parks: 9,
      lanes: 96,
      cafes: 17,
      sun: 201,
    },
    {
      city: "Castren",
      rent: 1310,
      pay: 3600,
      transit: 41,
      parks: 17,
      lanes: 184,
      cafes: 19,
      sun: 132,
    },
    {
      city: "Dunmore",
      rent: 1150,
      pay: 2900,
      transit: 27,
      parks: 11,
      lanes: 120,
      cafes: 12,
      sun: 165,
    },
    {
      city: "Eastwick",
      rent: 980,
      pay: 3100,
      transit: 33,
      parks: 21,
      lanes: 240,
      cafes: 15,
      sun: 121,
    },
    {
      city: "Fenhallow",
      rent: 860,
      pay: 2500,
      transit: 18,
      parks: 8,
      lanes: 54,
      cafes: 9,
      sun: 176,
    },
    {
      city: "Greyport",
      rent: 740,
      pay: 2700,
      transit: 24,
      parks: 12,
      lanes: 88,
      cafes: 11,
      sun: 190,
    },
    { city: "Hallin", rent: 610, pay: 2200, transit: 12, parks: 6, lanes: 31, cafes: 7, sun: 210 },
  ]}
  name="city"
  nameLabel="City"
  curve={{
    left: "rent",
    right: "pay",
    leftLabel: "Rent, € a month",
    rightLabel: "Median pay, € a month",
    format: "integer",
    title: "Median pay in Avenmouth was €3,900 a month",
  }}
  columns={[
    { field: "transit", label: "Trips by public transport", glyph: "ring", format: "{value}%" },
    { field: "parks", label: "Parks per 100,000 people", glyph: "dots" },
    { field: "lanes", label: "Cycle lanes, km", glyph: "bar" },
    { field: "cafes", label: "Cafés per 10,000 people", glyph: "blocks" },
    { field: "sun", label: "Sunny days a year", glyph: "circle" },
  ]}
  table={{ title: "Eastwick had 240 km of cycle lanes" }}
  sources="Norland Statistics Office, city indicators 2025"
  note="Norland and its cities are invented. All figures are illustrative."
  credit="InsightCharts"
/>
```

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rows` (required) | `Row[]` |  | One object per entity, holding the name and every measure. |
| `name` | `string` |  | Field holding the entity name. Default: the first key of the first row. |
| `nameLabel` | `string` |  | Heading of the table's name column. |
| `curve` (required) | `{ left, right, leftLabel?, rightLabel?, leftFormat?, rightFormat?, leftTop?, rightTop?, title?, subtitle?, source?, ...curve-rank props }` |  | Left graphic: the two measures joined by one S-curve per entity (`curve-rank`). The poster's rows are ordered by `left`, largest first. |
| `columns` (required) | `{ field, label?, glyph?, unit?, format?, max?, icon? }[]` |  | Right graphic: the glyph columns of the table, in order (`glyph-table`). Three to five read well beside the curves. |
| `table` | `{ title?, subtitle?, source?, note? }` |  | Short heading and source line over and under the table. |
| `order` | `string[]` |  | Entity names in display order, for both graphics. Default: largest first on the curve's left measure. |
| `highlight` | `string \| string[]` |  | Entities drawn in colour while every other one turns grey. Without it each entity has its own colour in both graphics. |
| `title` (required) | `string` |  | The poster's one fact, as a plain sentence with its number. |
| `kicker` | `string` |  | Small label above the title: the topic. |
| `subtitle` | `string` |  | One line under the title: the measure, population and period. |
| `theme` | `PosterThemeName \| string \| ThemeInput` | `"paper"` | Poster theme: `noir`, `magenta`, `dusk`, `ocean`, `forest`, `blueprint`, `sunrise`, `paper`, any other theme name, or a theme object. |
| `mode` | `"light" \| "dark" \| "auto" \| "system"` | `"light"` | Colour mode of the poster and everything in it. A poster paints its own ground and does not follow the page unless you set `auto`. Only `paper` has a different dark variant. |
| `download` | `boolean` | `false` | Show a "Download PNG" control under the poster that saves the whole poster as one image. |
| `maxWidth` | `number \| string` | `1400` | Widest the poster is drawn. It is centred in wider containers. |
| `linked` | `boolean` | `false` | Make the marks clickable. Clicking a mark in one graphic highlights the same name in every other graphic that has it, and filters the graphics that read the shared `data`. Click it again, or the empty ground of that graphic, to clear. |
| `sources` | `string \| string[]` |  | Where the data comes from, shown in the footer. |
| `note` | `string` |  | Caveat shown in the footer, e.g. "Illustrative data". |
| `credit` | `string` |  | Who made the poster, shown at the right of the footer. |
| `level` | `1 \| 2 \| 3 \| 4 \| 5` | `2` | Heading level of the title. Panel headings are one level down. |

## Network poster (`network-poster`)

> A poster of who is connected to whom: a full-width arc diagram with one arc per connection, as thick as its value (`arc-diagram`), a strip of two to four large figures, and a bottom row where the same entities return as circles joined by lines (`bubble-network`) and as a ranking of centred pills (`pill-rank`).

- Component: `NetworkPoster` (import from `insightcharts`)
- Spec type: `"network-poster"`
- Level: template. Category: infographic.
- An HTML component: it takes only the props listed below, plus `theme`, `mode`, `className` and `style` where its source declares them. It does not take the common chart props.

### When to use

Use it when the connections between 5 to about 20 named things are the subject: ferry crossings between harbours, joint papers between institutes, freight between rail yards. Give `hero` one row per connection and the `order` the entities sit in, `map` the entities with a size and optional hand-placed `x` and `y`, and `rank` one measure of each entity. With `linked`, a click on an entity in any of the three highlights it in the other two.

### Avoid

A flow from sources to destinations in one direction (use `flow-poster` or `sankey-chart`). More than about 20 entities or 40 connections, because the arcs cover each other. Entities with no meaningful order and few links (use `bubble-network` in a `poster`). Parts of one subject (use `radial-poster`).

### Install

From npm (the component ships in the package):

```bash
npm install insightcharts echarts
```

Or copy the source into your project with the shadcn CLI, so you can edit it (the engine still comes from the `insightcharts` package):

```bash
npx shadcn@latest registry add @insightcharts=https://insightcharts.dev/r/{name}.json   # once per project
npx shadcn@latest add @insightcharts/network-poster
```

The file lands at `components/insightcharts/templates/network-poster.tsx`. `@insightcharts/network-poster-demo` adds a ready-made example next to it.

### Usage

```tsx
import { NetworkPoster } from "insightcharts";

<NetworkPoster
  theme="dusk"
  linked
  kicker="Ferries"
  title="Skerry Isles ferries carried 1.66 million passengers on 12 routes in 2025"
  subtitle="Passengers carried between pairs of harbours, thousands, both directions, 2025."
  hero={{
    data: [
      { a: "Port Aven", b: "Brae", k: 412 },
      { a: "Port Aven", b: "Storholm", k: 268 },
      { a: "Port Aven", b: "Little Skerry", k: 96 },
      { a: "Brae", b: "Storholm", k: 187 },
      { a: "Brae", b: "Tarn Head", k: 74 },
      { a: "Storholm", b: "Tarn Head", k: 153 },
      { a: "Storholm", b: "Ness", k: 121 },
      { a: "Tarn Head", b: "Ness", k: 88 },
      { a: "Ness", b: "Outer Holm", k: 43 },
      { a: "Little Skerry", b: "Brae", k: 52 },
      { a: "Port Aven", b: "Ness", k: 139 },
      { a: "Storholm", b: "Outer Holm", k: 31 },
    ],
    from: "a",
    to: "b",
    value: "k",
    order: ["Port Aven", "Little Skerry", "Brae", "Storholm", "Tarn Head", "Ness", "Outer Holm"],
    colorBy: "series",
    format: "{value}k",
    title: "412,000 passengers crossed between Port Aven and Brae",
  }}
  figures={[
    { value: "412k", label: "passengers on the busiest route", context: "Port Aven to Brae" },
    { value: "31k", label: "passengers on the quietest route", context: "Storholm to Outer Holm" },
    { value: "4", label: "of the 12 routes call at Port Aven" },
  ]}
  map={{
    data: [
      { harbour: "Port Aven", k: 915, x: 12, y: 62 },
      { harbour: "Little Skerry", k: 148, x: 22, y: 18 },
      { harbour: "Brae", k: 725, x: 38, y: 40 },
      { harbour: "Storholm", k: 760, x: 56, y: 80 },
      { harbour: "Tarn Head", k: 315, x: 66, y: 22 },
      { harbour: "Ness", k: 391, x: 84, y: 46 },
      { harbour: "Outer Holm", k: 74, x: 93, y: 82 },
    ],
    name: "harbour",
    value: "k",
    x: "x",
    y: "y",
    links: [
      { from: "Port Aven", to: "Brae" },
      { from: "Port Aven", to: "Storholm" },
      { from: "Port Aven", to: "Little Skerry" },
      { from: "Brae", to: "Storholm" },
      { from: "Brae", to: "Tarn Head" },
      { from: "Storholm", to: "Tarn Head" },
      { from: "Storholm", to: "Ness" },
      { from: "Tarn Head", to: "Ness" },
      { from: "Ness", to: "Outer Holm" },
      { from: "Little Skerry", to: "Brae" },
      { from: "Port Aven", to: "Ness" },
      { from: "Storholm", to: "Outer Holm" },
    ],
    format: "{value}k",
    highlight: "Port Aven",
    tag: "Busiest harbour",
    title: "915,000 passengers used Port Aven",
    subtitle: "Passengers through each harbour, thousands. Positions are approximate.",
  }}
  rank={{
    data: [
      { harbour: "Port Aven", sailings: 46 },
      { harbour: "Storholm", sailings: 38 },
      { harbour: "Brae", sailings: 33 },
      { harbour: "Ness", sailings: 21 },
      { harbour: "Tarn Head", sailings: 16 },
      { harbour: "Little Skerry", sailings: 8 },
      { harbour: "Outer Holm", sailings: 4 },
    ],
    name: "harbour",
    value: "sailings",
    title: "Port Aven had 46 sailings a day",
    subtitle: "Scheduled departures per day, summer 2025.",
  }}
  sources="Skerry Isles Ferries, annual traffic return 2025"
  note="The Skerry Isles are invented. All figures are illustrative."
  credit="InsightCharts"
/>
```

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `hero` (required) | `{ data, from, to, value?, order?, colorBy?, arcLabels?, orientation?, format?, highlight?, title?, ... } \| Slot` |  | The hero: one arc per pair of connected entities, drawn by `arc-diagram`. Rows joining the same pair are summed. A full spec or element replaces it. |
| `figures` | `{ value: string; label: string; context?: string; icon?: string; tag?: string }[]` |  | Two to four large figures in a strip under the hero. |
| `map` | `{ data, name, value, links?, x?, y?, layout?, tag?, highlight?, format?, title?, ... } \| Slot` |  | Bottom left: the entities as circles sized by `value` and joined by `links: { from, to, value? }[]` (`bubble-network`). `x` and `y` (0 to 100) place the circles by hand. |
| `rank` | `{ data, name, value, highlight?, compare?, format?, title?, ... } \| Slot` |  | Bottom right: the entities ranked by one measure as centred pills (`pill-rank`). With only one of `map` and `rank`, that one takes the full width. |
| `title` (required) | `string` |  | The poster's one fact, as a plain sentence with its number. |
| `kicker` | `string` |  | Small label above the title: the topic. |
| `subtitle` | `string` |  | One line under the title: the measure, population and period. |
| `theme` | `PosterThemeName \| string \| ThemeInput` | `"dusk"` | Poster theme: `noir`, `magenta`, `dusk`, `ocean`, `forest`, `blueprint`, `sunrise`, `paper`, any other theme name, or a theme object. |
| `mode` | `"light" \| "dark" \| "auto" \| "system"` | `"light"` | Colour mode of the poster and everything in it. A poster paints its own ground and does not follow the page unless you set `auto`. Only `paper` has a different dark variant. |
| `download` | `boolean` | `false` | Show a "Download PNG" control under the poster that saves the whole poster as one image. |
| `maxWidth` | `number \| string` | `1100` | Widest the poster is drawn. It is centred in wider containers. |
| `linked` | `boolean` | `false` | Make the marks clickable. Clicking a mark in one graphic highlights the same name in every other graphic that has it, and filters the graphics that read the shared `data`. Click it again, or the empty ground of that graphic, to clear. |
| `data` | `DataInput` |  | Rows shared by every region whose config leaves out its own `data`. With `linked`, a click filters those regions. |
| `sources` | `string \| string[]` |  | Where the data comes from, shown in the footer. |
| `note` | `string` |  | Caveat shown in the footer, e.g. "Illustrative data". |
| `credit` | `string` |  | Who made the poster, shown at the right of the footer. |
| `level` | `1 \| 2 \| 3 \| 4 \| 5` | `2` | Heading level of the title. Panel headings are one level down. |

### Composition

- Composes: [poster](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/poster.md), [arc-diagram](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/arc-diagram.md), [bubble-network](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/bubble-network.md), [pill-rank](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/pill-rank.md)
- Used by: no molecule or template yet

### More examples

#### Noir, joint papers, a hub layout, with download

```tsx
import { NetworkPoster } from "insightcharts";

<NetworkPoster
  theme="noir"
  download
  kicker="Research"
  title="Six Norland institutes published 369 joint papers in 2025"
  subtitle="Papers with authors at two of the six institutes, by pair, 2025."
  hero={{
    data: [
      { a: "Marlow", b: "Halden", papers: 84 },
      { a: "Marlow", b: "Orrin", papers: 61 },
      { a: "Marlow", b: "Carrow", papers: 37 },
      { a: "Halden", b: "Orrin", papers: 52 },
      { a: "Halden", b: "Kestrel", papers: 29 },
      { a: "Orrin", b: "Carrow", papers: 44 },
      { a: "Orrin", b: "Aldern", papers: 18 },
      { a: "Carrow", b: "Kestrel", papers: 23 },
      { a: "Kestrel", b: "Aldern", papers: 12 },
      { a: "Marlow", b: "Aldern", papers: 9 },
    ],
    from: "a",
    to: "b",
    value: "papers",
    order: ["Marlow", "Halden", "Orrin", "Carrow", "Kestrel", "Aldern"],
    colorBy: "none",
    highlight: "Marlow",
    title: "Marlow and Halden shared 84 papers",
  }}
  figures={[
    { value: "191", label: "of the 369 papers had a Marlow author" },
    { value: "84", label: "papers were shared by Marlow and Halden" },
    { value: "39", label: "papers had an Aldern author" },
  ]}
  map={{
    data: [
      { institute: "Marlow", staff: 640 },
      { institute: "Halden", staff: 510 },
      { institute: "Orrin", staff: 470 },
      { institute: "Carrow", staff: 290 },
      { institute: "Kestrel", staff: 180 },
      { institute: "Aldern", staff: 95 },
    ],
    name: "institute",
    value: "staff",
    layout: "hub",
    links: [
      { from: "Marlow", to: "Halden", value: 84 },
      { from: "Marlow", to: "Orrin", value: 61 },
      { from: "Marlow", to: "Carrow", value: 37 },
      { from: "Halden", to: "Orrin", value: 52 },
      { from: "Halden", to: "Kestrel", value: 29 },
      { from: "Orrin", to: "Carrow", value: 44 },
      { from: "Orrin", to: "Aldern", value: 18 },
      { from: "Carrow", to: "Kestrel", value: 23 },
      { from: "Kestrel", to: "Aldern", value: 12 },
      { from: "Marlow", to: "Aldern", value: 9 },
    ],
    highlight: "Marlow",
    tag: "640 researchers",
    linkLabels: false,
    title: "Marlow employed 640 researchers",
    subtitle: "Research staff at each institute. Line width is the number of joint papers.",
  }}
  rank={{
    data: [
      { institute: "Marlow", staff: 640 },
      { institute: "Halden", staff: 510 },
      { institute: "Orrin", staff: 470 },
      { institute: "Carrow", staff: 290 },
      { institute: "Kestrel", staff: 180 },
      { institute: "Aldern", staff: 95 },
    ],
    name: "institute",
    value: "staff",
    highlight: "Marlow",
    title: "Aldern employed 95 researchers",
  }}
  sources="Norland Research Council, publication register 2025"
  note="The institutes are invented. All figures are illustrative."
  credit="InsightCharts"
/>
```

#### Forest, five rail yards, arcs and figures only

```tsx
import { NetworkPoster } from "insightcharts";

<NetworkPoster
  theme="forest"
  kicker="Rail freight"
  title="Halden's five rail yards exchanged 1,670 wagons a week in 2025"
  subtitle="Wagons moved between pairs of yards per week, both directions, average for 2025."
  hero={{
    data: [
      { a: "Northgate", b: "Mill Lane", wagons: 310 },
      { a: "Northgate", b: "Quarry Junction", wagons: 190 },
      { a: "Mill Lane", b: "Quarry Junction", wagons: 240 },
      { a: "Mill Lane", b: "Harbour East", wagons: 420 },
      { a: "Quarry Junction", b: "Harbour East", wagons: 160 },
      { a: "Harbour East", b: "Southfield", wagons: 280 },
      { a: "Northgate", b: "Southfield", wagons: 70 },
    ],
    from: "a",
    to: "b",
    value: "wagons",
    order: ["Northgate", "Mill Lane", "Quarry Junction", "Harbour East", "Southfield"],
    colorBy: "series",
    title: "Mill Lane and Harbour East exchanged 420 wagons a week",
  }}
  figures={[
    { value: "420", label: "wagons a week on the busiest pair" },
    { value: "70", label: "wagons a week between Northgate and Southfield" },
  ]}
  sources="Halden Rail Freight, yard movements 2025"
  note="The Halden yards are invented. All figures are illustrative."
  credit="InsightCharts"
/>
```

## Profile poster (`profile-poster`)

> A poster that describes one subject from four sides: the subject as one large silhouette filled to a share (`shape-fill`), two to four large figures, its place among other things on one scale (`scale-ladder`), and a table that sets it beside its peers with every number drawn as a small form (`glyph-table`).

- Component: `ProfilePoster` (import from `insightcharts`)
- Spec type: `"profile-poster"`
- Level: template. Category: infographic.
- An HTML component: it takes only the props listed below, plus `theme`, `mode`, `className` and `style` where its source declares them. It does not take the common chart props.

### When to use

Use it for a fact sheet about one named thing: a vehicle, a reservoir, a building, a machine, a species. Give `portrait` one row with the share that defines the subject and the `icon` that stands for it, `figures` the numbers a reader should take away, `scale` the subject among 4 to 10 reference points, and `table` the subject beside 2 to 6 peers. Highlight the subject in `scale` and `table`. On a sheet at least 960px wide the silhouette, the figures and the scale stand in three columns.

### Avoid

Several subjects of equal weight (use `glyph-table` in a `poster`, or `ranking-poster`). A subject whose parts are the point (use `radial-poster`). A subject with no defining share: leave `portrait` to a full spec such as `stat-circles`, or use `scale-poster` when the scale is the whole subject. Change over time (use `timeline-poster`).

### Install

From npm (the component ships in the package):

```bash
npm install insightcharts echarts
```

Or copy the source into your project with the shadcn CLI, so you can edit it (the engine still comes from the `insightcharts` package):

```bash
npx shadcn@latest registry add @insightcharts=https://insightcharts.dev/r/{name}.json   # once per project
npx shadcn@latest add @insightcharts/profile-poster
```

The file lands at `components/insightcharts/templates/profile-poster.tsx`. `@insightcharts/profile-poster-demo` adds a ready-made example next to it.

### Usage

```tsx
import { ProfilePoster } from "insightcharts";

<ProfilePoster
  theme="blueprint"
  kicker="Public transport"
  title="The Line 9 electric bus ended a working day with 34% of its charge"
  subtitle="One 12-metre battery bus on Marlow's Line 9, average of 60 working days in 2025."
  portrait={{
    data: [{ state: "Charge left at 23:00", charge: 34 }],
    name: "state",
    value: "charge",
    icon: "bus",
    title: "Charge left at the end of the day",
  }}
  figures={[
    { value: "204 km", label: "driven on a working day" },
    { value: "310 km", label: "of range on a full charge" },
    { value: "4 h", label: "to recharge overnight at the depot" },
  ]}
  scale={{
    data: [
      { vehicle: "Electric scooter", km: 35, icon: "bolt" },
      { vehicle: "Electric bike", km: 70, icon: "bike" },
      { vehicle: "Delivery van", km: 210, icon: "truck" },
      { vehicle: "Line 9 bus", km: 310, icon: "bus" },
      { vehicle: "Family car", km: 420, icon: "car" },
      { vehicle: "Long-haul truck", km: 520, icon: "truck" },
    ],
    name: "vehicle",
    value: "km",
    iconField: "icon",
    min: 0,
    max: 600,
    format: "{value} km",
    scaleLabel: "Range, km",
    highlight: "Line 9 bus",
    title: "Range of six electric vehicles",
  }}
  table={{
    rows: [
      { vehicle: "Line 9 bus", seats: 41, cost: 0.21, co2: 14, noise: 62 },
      { vehicle: "Diesel bus", seats: 43, cost: 0.58, co2: 71, noise: 78 },
      { vehicle: "Tram", seats: 64, cost: 0.17, co2: 9, noise: 70 },
    ],
    name: "vehicle",
    nameLabel: "Vehicle",
    highlight: "Line 9 bus",
    title: "The Line 9 bus emitted 14 g of CO2 per passenger-kilometre",
    columns: [
      { field: "seats", label: "Seats", glyph: "icons", icon: "person", unit: 5 },
      { field: "cost", label: "Energy cost per km", glyph: "bar", format: "€{value}", max: 0.6 },
      { field: "co2", label: "CO2 per passenger-km", glyph: "circle", format: "{value} g" },
      { field: "noise", label: "Noise at 10 m", glyph: "bar", format: "{value} dB", max: 80 },
    ],
  }}
  sources="Marlow Transit depot telemetry, 2025"
  note="Marlow Transit and the Line 9 bus are invented. All figures are illustrative."
  credit="InsightCharts"
/>
```

```json
    "highlight": "Line 9 bus",
    "title": "The Line 9 bus emitted 14 g of CO2 per passenger-kilometre",
    "columns": [
      { "field": "seats", "label": "Seats", "glyph": "icons", "icon": "person", "unit": 5 },
      {
        "field": "cost",
        "label": "Energy cost per km",
        "glyph": "bar",
        "format": "€{value}",
        "max": 0.6
      },
      { "field": "co2", "label": "CO2 per passenger-km", "glyph": "circle", "format": "{value} g" },
      {
        "field": "noise",
        "label": "Noise at 10 m",
        "glyph": "bar",
        "format": "{value} dB",
        "max": 80
      }
    ]
  },
  "sources": "Marlow Transit depot telemetry, 2025",
  "note": "Marlow Transit and the Line 9 bus are invented. All figures are illustrative.",
  "credit": "InsightCharts"
}
```

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `portrait` (required) | `{ data, name, value, icon, max?, format?, title?, ... } \| Slot` |  | The portrait: one silhouette filled from the bottom to the share in its row, with the number beside it, drawn by `shape-fill`. `format` defaults to `"{value}%"`. A full spec or element replaces it. |
| `figures` | `{ value: string; label: string; context?: string; icon?: string; tag?: string }[]` |  | Two to four large figures about the subject. In the three-column layout they stand between the silhouette and the scale; otherwise they run in a strip. |
| `scale` | `{ data, name, value, iconField?, direction?, scale?, min?, max?, zones?, scaleLabel?, highlight?, format?, title?, ... } \| Slot` |  | The subject among 4 to 10 other things on one scale (`scale-ladder`). It is drawn as tall as the silhouette. |
| `table` | `{ rows, name, columns, nameLabel?, highlight?, order?, title?, ... } \| Slot` |  | The subject beside its peers, one row each, with a glyph per measure (`glyph-table`). `columns` is `{ field, label?, glyph?, unit?, format?, max?, icon? }[]`. |
| `title` (required) | `string` |  | The poster's one fact, as a plain sentence with its number. |
| `kicker` | `string` |  | Small label above the title: the topic. |
| `subtitle` | `string` |  | One line under the title: the measure, population and period. |
| `theme` | `PosterThemeName \| string \| ThemeInput` | `"blueprint"` | Poster theme: `noir`, `magenta`, `dusk`, `ocean`, `forest`, `blueprint`, `sunrise`, `paper`, any other theme name, or a theme object. |
| `mode` | `"light" \| "dark" \| "auto" \| "system"` | `"light"` | Colour mode of the poster and everything in it. A poster paints its own ground and does not follow the page unless you set `auto`. Only `paper` has a different dark variant. |
| `download` | `boolean` | `false` | Show a "Download PNG" control under the poster that saves the whole poster as one image. |
| `maxWidth` | `number \| string` | `1100` | Widest the poster is drawn. It is centred in wider containers. |
| `linked` | `boolean` | `false` | Make the marks clickable. Clicking a mark in one graphic highlights the same name in every other graphic that has it, and filters the graphics that read the shared `data`. Click it again, or the empty ground of that graphic, to clear. |
| `data` | `DataInput` |  | Rows shared by every region whose config leaves out its own `data`. With `linked`, a click filters those regions. |
| `sources` | `string \| string[]` |  | Where the data comes from, shown in the footer. |
| `note` | `string` |  | Caveat shown in the footer, e.g. "Illustrative data". |
| `credit` | `string` |  | Who made the poster, shown at the right of the footer. |
| `level` | `1 \| 2 \| 3 \| 4 \| 5` | `2` | Heading level of the title. Panel headings are one level down. |

### Composition

- Composes: [poster](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/poster.md), [shape-fill](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/shape-fill.md), [scale-ladder](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/scale-ladder.md), [glyph-table](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/glyph-table.md)
- Used by: no molecule or template yet

## Radial poster (`radial-poster`)

> A poster with one subject in the middle of the sheet: a wheel of spokes round an icon (`radial-spokes`), two to four large figures standing either side of it, and a bottom row with the same subject's surroundings on concentric rings (`orbit-chart`) and a ranking as centred pills (`pill-rank`).

- Component: `RadialPoster` (import from `insightcharts`)
- Spec type: `"radial-poster"`
- Level: template. Category: infographic.
- An HTML component: it takes only the props listed below, plus `theme`, `mode`, `className` and `style` where its source declares them. It does not take the common chart props.

### When to use

Use it when the poster is about the 4 to 12 parts, causes, effects or scores of one thing: what a household's water goes on, the species one tree supports, where one home's energy goes. Give `hero` the spokes and an `icon` for the centre, state the total in the title, and use `figures` for the two to four numbers a reader should take away.

### Avoid

Parts of a whole that must be compared precisely (use `bar-chart` in a `poster`). Positions on one scale (use `scale-poster`). Change over time (use `timeline-poster`). Connections between many things (use `network-poster`). Large counts shown as crowds (use `count-poster`).

### Install

From npm (the component ships in the package):

```bash
npm install insightcharts echarts
```

Or copy the source into your project with the shadcn CLI, so you can edit it (the engine still comes from the `insightcharts` package):

```bash
npx shadcn@latest registry add @insightcharts=https://insightcharts.dev/r/{name}.json   # once per project
npx shadcn@latest add @insightcharts/radial-poster
```

The file lands at `components/insightcharts/templates/radial-poster.tsx`. `@insightcharts/radial-poster-demo` adds a ready-made example next to it.

### Usage

```tsx
import { RadialPoster } from "insightcharts";

<RadialPoster
  theme="magenta"
  kicker="Water"
  title="A person on Verne Street used 142 litres of water a day in 2025"
  subtitle="Litres of mains water per person per day by use, 212 metered homes, 2025."
  hero={{
    data: [
      { use: "Shower", litres: 44 },
      { use: "Toilet", litres: 31 },
      { use: "Washing machine", litres: 19 },
      { use: "Kitchen tap", litres: 17 },
      { use: "Garden", litres: 12 },
      { use: "Dishwasher", litres: 9 },
      { use: "Bath", litres: 6 },
      { use: "Other", litres: 4 },
    ],
    name: "use",
    value: "litres",
    icon: "drop",
    format: "{value} L",
    highlight: "Shower",
  }}
  figures={[
    { value: "44 L", label: "went on showers", context: "31% of the daily total" },
    { value: "9 min", label: "was the average length of a shower" },
    { value: "6 L", label: "went on baths" },
    { value: "€1.12", label: "was the cost of one person's water for a day" },
  ]}
  rings={{
    data: [
      { fixture: "Bath", room: "Bathroom", litres: 80 },
      { fixture: "Shower, 8 min", room: "Bathroom", litres: 64 },
      { fixture: "Toilet flush", room: "Bathroom", litres: 6 },
      { fixture: "Washing machine", room: "Kitchen", litres: 50 },
      { fixture: "Dishwasher", room: "Kitchen", litres: 12 },
      { fixture: "Washing-up bowl", room: "Kitchen", litres: 8 },
      { fixture: "Hose, 10 min", room: "Garden", litres: 150 },
      { fixture: "Watering can", room: "Garden", litres: 10 },
    ],
    name: "fixture",
    ring: "room",
    value: "litres",
    format: "{value} L",
    icon: "house",
    ringLabel: "One ring per room",
    sizeLabel: "litres per use",
    highlight: "Hose, 10 min",
    title: "Ten minutes with a hose used 150 litres",
    height: 460,
  }}
  rank={{
    data: [
      { district: "Harbour", litres: 168 },
      { district: "Old Town", litres: 155 },
      { district: "Verne Street", litres: 142 },
      { district: "Northgate", litres: 136 },
      { district: "Riverside", litres: 129 },
      { district: "Mill Lane", litres: 117 },
    ],
    name: "district",
    value: "litres",
    format: "{value} L",
    highlight: "Verne Street",
    title: "Verne Street ranked third of six districts",
  }}
  sources="Verne Street metering study 2025"
  note="Verne Street and its figures are invented. All figures are illustrative."
  credit="InsightCharts"
/>
```

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `hero` (required) | `{ data, name, value, icon?, centerLabel?, shape?, sweep?, max?, highlight?, format?, title?, ... } \| Slot` |  | The hero: one spoke per row round a centre disc, drawn by `radial-spokes`. A full spec or element replaces it. |
| `figures` | `{ value: string; label: string; context?: string; icon?: string; tag?: string }[]` |  | Two to four large figures. On a sheet at least 960px wide they stand in two columns either side of the hero; on a narrower one they run in a row under it. |
| `rings` | `{ data, name, ring, value?, rings?, ringLabel?, sizeLabel?, icon?, centerLabel?, title?, ... } \| Slot` |  | Bottom left: named things on concentric rings, one ring per category, level or period (`orbit-chart`). |
| `rank` | `{ data, name, value, highlight?, compare?, format?, title?, ... } \| Slot` |  | Bottom right: a ranking as centred pills (`pill-rank`). With only one of `rings` and `rank`, that one takes the full width. |
| `title` (required) | `string` |  | The poster's one fact, as a plain sentence with its number. |
| `kicker` | `string` |  | Small label above the title: the topic. |
| `subtitle` | `string` |  | One line under the title: the measure, population and period. |
| `theme` | `PosterThemeName \| string \| ThemeInput` | `"magenta"` | Poster theme: `noir`, `magenta`, `dusk`, `ocean`, `forest`, `blueprint`, `sunrise`, `paper`, any other theme name, or a theme object. |
| `mode` | `"light" \| "dark" \| "auto" \| "system"` | `"light"` | Colour mode of the poster and everything in it. A poster paints its own ground and does not follow the page unless you set `auto`. Only `paper` has a different dark variant. |
| `download` | `boolean` | `false` | Show a "Download PNG" control under the poster that saves the whole poster as one image. |
| `maxWidth` | `number \| string` | `1100` | Widest the poster is drawn. It is centred in wider containers. |
| `linked` | `boolean` | `false` | Make the marks clickable. Clicking a mark in one graphic highlights the same name in every other graphic that has it, and filters the graphics that read the shared `data`. Click it again, or the empty ground of that graphic, to clear. |
| `data` | `DataInput` |  | Rows shared by every region whose config leaves out its own `data`. With `linked`, a click filters those regions. |
| `sources` | `string \| string[]` |  | Where the data comes from, shown in the footer. |
| `note` | `string` |  | Caveat shown in the footer, e.g. "Illustrative data". |
| `credit` | `string` |  | Who made the poster, shown at the right of the footer. |
| `level` | `1 \| 2 \| 3 \| 4 \| 5` | `2` | Heading level of the title. Panel headings are one level down. |

## Ranking poster (`ranking-poster`)

> A poster of one subject by the numbers, in four rows: two figures in large type or as filled silhouettes, two treemaps side by side, a full-width ranking of centred pills with one row highlighted, and packed circles with icons beside a column of sized circles and a closing figure.

- Component: `RankingPoster` (import from `insightcharts`)
- Spec type: `"ranking-poster"`
- Level: template. Category: infographic.
- An HTML component: it takes only the props listed below, plus `theme`, `mode`, `className` and `style` where its source declares them. It does not take the common chart props.

### When to use

Use it for a profile of one event, place or organisation that has a headline total, two ways to split it, a ranking of 6 to 12 named things and a few supporting magnitudes: a festival, a race, a nature reserve, a library service. Put the total in the title and repeat it as the first figure. Highlight the ranking row the heading is about.

### Avoid

A subject whose point is a count of people or things (use `count-poster`). Several entities compared on the same measures (use `matrix-poster`). Eight or more small graphics on one subject (use `atlas-poster`). A ranking alone (use `pill-rank` in a `poster`).

### Install

From npm (the component ships in the package):

```bash
npm install insightcharts echarts
```

Or copy the source into your project with the shadcn CLI, so you can edit it (the engine still comes from the `insightcharts` package):

```bash
npx shadcn@latest registry add @insightcharts=https://insightcharts.dev/r/{name}.json   # once per project
npx shadcn@latest add @insightcharts/ranking-poster
```

The file lands at `components/insightcharts/templates/ranking-poster.tsx`. `@insightcharts/ranking-poster-demo` adds a ready-made example next to it.

### Usage

```tsx
import { RankingPoster } from "insightcharts";

<RankingPoster
  theme="dusk"
  kicker="Music"
  title="The Solvik Festival sold 184,000 tickets in 2025"
  subtitle="Tickets, crowds and spending at a three-day music festival, 11 to 13 July 2025."
  figures={[
    { value: "184,000", label: "Tickets sold in 2025", context: "171,000 in 2024" },
    {
      data: [{ day: "Friday", share: 84 }, { day: "Saturday", share: 100 }, { day: "Sunday", share: 91 }],
      name: "day",
      value: "share",
      icon: "group",
      title: "Saturday sold 100% of its 64,000 places",
    },
  ]}
  breakdowns={[
    {
      data: [
```
