### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `figures` | `({ value, label, context?, icon? } \| { data, name, value, icon, title?, ...shape-fill props } \| Slot)[]` |  | Top row, up to two. A statement `{ value, label }` is set in large light type (the first in the accent colour); a config with `data` draws silhouettes filled to their level (`shape-fill`). |
| `breakdowns` | `({ data, name, value, title?, ...treemap props } \| Slot)[]` |  | Second row, up to two: the subject's total split two ways, as treemaps side by side. |
| `ranking` (required) | `{ data, name, value, highlight?, compare?, compareLabel?, title?, ...pill-rank props } \| Slot` |  | Third row, full width: a ranking as centred pills with the value at the left and the rank at the right (`pill-rank`). `highlight` names the row drawn in the accent. |
| `pack` | `{ data, name, value, icon?, group?, title?, ...circle-pack props } \| Slot` |  | Bottom left: parts as packed circles (`circle-pack`). `icon` is one icon name or a map from circle name to icon. |
| `circles` | `{ data, name, value, unit?, title?, ...stat-circles props } \| Slot` |  | Bottom right: two to four related magnitudes as circles standing on one baseline (`stat-circles`). |
| `figure` | `{ value, label, context?, icon? }` |  | Bottom right, under the circles: one closing figure in large type. |
| `format` | `FormatSpec` |  | How to print values in the regions that set no `format` of their own. |
| `title` (required) | `string` |  | The poster's one fact, as a plain sentence with its number. |
| `kicker` | `string` |  | Small label above the title: the topic. |
| `subtitle` | `string` |  | One line under the title: the measure, population and period. |
| `theme` | `PosterThemeName \| string \| ThemeInput` | `"dusk"` | Poster theme: `noir`, `magenta`, `dusk`, `ocean`, `forest`, `blueprint`, `sunrise`, `paper`, any other theme name, or a theme object. |
| `mode` | `"light" \| "dark" \| "auto" \| "system"` | `"light"` | Colour mode of the poster and everything in it. A poster paints its own ground and does not follow the page unless you set `auto`. Only `paper` has a different dark variant. |
| `download` | `boolean` | `false` | Show a "Download PNG" control under the poster that saves the whole poster as one image. |
| `maxWidth` | `number \| string` | `1100` | Widest the poster is drawn. It is centred in wider containers. |
| `linked` | `boolean` | `false` | Make the marks clickable. Clicking a mark in one graphic highlights the same name in every other graphic that has it, and filters the graphics that read the shared `data`. Click it again, or the empty ground of that graphic, to clear. |
| `data` | `DataInput` |  | Rows shared by every region whose config leaves out its own `data`. With `linked`, a click filters those regions. |
| `sources` | `string \| string[]` |  | Where the data comes from, shown in the footer. |
| `note` | `string` |  | Caveat shown in the footer, e.g. "Illustrative data". |
| `credit` | `string` |  | Who made the poster, shown at the right of the footer. |
| `level` | `1 \| 2 \| 3 \| 4 \| 5` | `2` | Heading level of the title. Panel headings are one level down. |

### Composition

- Composes: [poster](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/poster.md), [shape-fill](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/shape-fill.md), [treemap](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/treemap.md), [pill-rank](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/pill-rank.md), [circle-pack](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/circle-pack.md), [stat-circles](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/stat-circles.md)
- Used by: no molecule or template yet

## Report page (`report-page`)

> A section of an analytical report laid out as a document. It has a title block, a summary, numbered findings, then method, limitations and sources. Each finding has one exhibit, an observation and a separately labelled interpretation with a confidence rating and a caveat.

- Component: `ReportPage` (import from `insightcharts`)
- Spec type: `"report-page"`
- Level: template. Category: layout.
- An HTML component: it takes only the props listed below, plus `theme`, `mode`, `className` and `style` where its source declares them. It does not take the common chart props.

### When to use

Use it for readers who will check the reasoning, as in evaluations, research notes, audits and experiment write-ups. State the main finding with its number in the title. Put all the main findings and the recommendation in the summary. Write each finding title as one fact with its number, and give it an exhibit that shows that fact. Put what the data shows in `observation` and what you infer from it in `interpretation`. End with method, limitations and sources.

### Avoid

A decision-maker who wants only the result (use `executive-brief`). A general audience (use `explainer` or `visual-essay`). Findings without an exhibit. Put those in the summary.

### Install

From npm (the component ships in the package):

```bash
npm install insightcharts echarts
```

Or copy the source into your project with the shadcn CLI, so you can edit it (the engine still comes from the `insightcharts` package):

```bash
npx shadcn@latest registry add @insightcharts=https://insightcharts.dev/r/{name}.json   # once per project
npx shadcn@latest add @insightcharts/report-page
```

The file lands at `components/insightcharts/templates/report-page.tsx`. `@insightcharts/report-page-demo` adds a ready-made example next to it.

### Usage

```tsx
import { BarChart, ProgressMeter, ReportPage } from "insightcharts";

<ReportPage
  theme="paper"
  kicker="Small-group tutoring programme · Year 1 evaluation"
  title="Tutored pupils gained 2.9 more scaled-score points in maths than matched pupils"
  deck="The difference in reading was 0.5 points. 31% of tutored pupils were eligible for free school meals against a funding target of 50%."
  byline="Evaluation team"
  date="2025-02-20"
  summary="Pupils offered tutoring gained **2.9 more scaled-score points in maths** over the year than matched pupils who were not. That is about three months of additional learning. The difference in reading was 0.5 points and could be chance. Pupils who attended fewer than 12 sessions gained less than 1 point over their matches. 58% of pupils attended 12 or more. We recommend continuing the maths strand. Attendance should be the main delivery target. The way pupils are selected should change."
  figures={{
    variant: "tiles",
    items: [
      {
        variant: "comparison",
        value: 8.1,
        comparison: 5.2,
        valueLabel: "Tutored",
        comparisonLabel: "Comparison",
        delta: "+2.9 points",
        format: "decimal:1",
        label: "Mean gain in maths, scaled-score points",
      },
      {
        variant: "ring",
        value: 0.58,
        max: 1,
        format: "percent",
        label: "Tutored pupils attending 12 or more sessions",
        context: "20 sessions were offered",
      },
      {
        variant: "progress",
        value: 0.31,
        max: 1,
        target: 0.5,
        targetLabel: "Funding target",
        format: "percent",
        label: "Tutored pupils eligible for free school meals",
      },
    ],
  }}
  findings={[
    {
      title: "Tutored pupils gained 8.1 points in maths against 5.2 for comparison pupils",
      exhibit: <BarChart
        data={[
          { subject: "Maths", Tutored: 8.1, Comparison: 5.2 },
          { subject: "Reading", Tutored: 5.9, Comparison: 5.4 },
        ]}
        x="subject"
        y={["Tutored", "Comparison"]}
        orientation="horizontal"
        sort="none"
        format="decimal:1"
        subtitle="Mean gain in scaled score, autumn 2023 to summer 2024"
        source="Standardised assessments, 42 schools"
      />,
      observation: "The difference in maths was 2.9 points (95% interval 1.6 to 4.2). In reading tutored pupils gained 5.9 points and comparison pupils 5.4. That difference was 0.5 points (−0.7 to 1.7).",
      interpretation: "The maths difference is unlikely to be chance. Trials of similar programmes found effects of about the same size. We do not conclude that reading tutoring failed, because half the reading tutors were recruited after January.",
      confidence: "medium",
      caveat: "Pupils were matched on prior attainment and background. They were not randomised. Unmeasured differences, such as parental engagement, could account for part of the difference.",
    },
    {
      title: "Pupils who attended 18 or more sessions gained 4.4 points over their matches",
      exhibit: <BarChart
        data={[
          { sessions: "Under 6", effect: 0.2 },
          { sessions: "6–11", effect: 0.9 },
          { sessions: "12–17", effect: 3.1 },
          { sessions: "18+", effect: 4.4 },
        ]}
        x="sessions"
        y="effect"
        orientation="vertical"
        sort="none"
        format={{ signDisplay: "exceptZero", maximumFractionDigits: 1 }}
        height={260}
        subtitle="Maths gain over comparison pupils, scaled-score points, by sessions attended (of 20 offered)"
      />,
      observation: "Pupils who attended fewer than 6 sessions gained 0.2 points more than their matches. Those who attended 6 to 11 gained 0.9 points more. 42% of tutored pupils attended fewer than 12 sessions.",
      interpretation: "A gain that rises with attendance is consistent with a real effect. Pupils who attend more may also differ in ways that raise attainment. The effect of extra sessions is therefore probably smaller than the bars show.",
      confidence: "low",
    },
    {
      title: "31% of tutored pupils were eligible for free school meals against a target of 50%",
      exhibit: <ProgressMeter
        label="Tutored pupils eligible for free school meals"
        value={0.31}
        max={1}
        showMax={false}
        target={0.5}
        targetLabel="Funding target"
        format="percent"
        context="984 of 3,180 pupils. In the same schools, 38% of all pupils are eligible."
      />,
      observation: "984 of the 3,180 tutored pupils were eligible for free school meals. The funding agreement specifies 50%. 38% of all pupils in the participating schools are eligible.",
      interpretation: "Schools selected pupils by teacher nomination. Nomination appears to favour pupils just below the expected standard over the most disadvantaged. The schools have enough eligible pupils to meet the target, so we think the selection rules cause the shortfall.",
      confidence: "high",
    },
  ]}
  method="We compared 3,180 tutored pupils in 42 schools with 3,180 pupils in the same schools and year groups, matched one to one on prior attainment, free-school-meal eligibility, special educational needs and attendance in the previous year. Outcomes are scaled scores on the standardised assessments schools already use. Intervals are 95% and account for clustering by school."
  limitations={[
    "Matching cannot rule out differences we did not measure. A randomised design is planned for year two.",
    "Attendance was recorded by tutors and may be overstated.",
    "One year of outcomes does not show whether the gain lasts.",
  ]}
  sources={["School assessment returns", "Tutor session logs", "National pupil database extract"]}
  period="September 2023 to July 2024"
  note="Illustrative data"
/>
```

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `title` (required) | `string` |  | The report's main finding, as one plain sentence with the number in it. |
| `kicker` | `string` |  | The report series or section, e.g. "Evaluation report · Section 3". |
| `deck` | `string` |  | One-sentence standfirst. |
| `byline` | `string` |  | Author line. |
| `date` | `string` |  | Publication date. |
| `summary` | `string \| string[]` |  | One paragraph with the main findings, their numbers and the recommendation. Supports `**bold**`. |
| `summaryTitle` | `string` | `"Summary"` | Heading of the summary. |
| `figures` | `StatRowItem[] \| StatRowProps` |  | Two to four key figures shown under the summary. A list of `{ value, label, context?, delta?, ... }`, or the props of `stat-row` (`{ items, variant, ... }`) to choose how they are drawn. |
| `findings` | `{ title, exhibit?, observation?, interpretation?, confidence?: "high" \| "medium" \| "low", caveat?, id? }[]` |  | Numbered findings. `observation` is what the data shows; `interpretation` is what the authors infer, with an optional confidence rating and caveat. |
| `observationLabel` | `string` | `"What the data shows"` | Label over each observation. |
| `interpretationLabel` | `string` | `"What we think it means"` | Label over each interpretation. |
| `method` | `string \| string[]` |  | How the analysis was done, as its own section. |
| `limitations` | `string[]` |  | What the analysis cannot show. |
| `sources` | `string \| { name, url? } \| (string \| { name, url? })[]` |  | Where the data comes from, shown in the closing source note. Entries with a `url` are linked. |
| `period` | `string` |  | The period the data covers. |
| `note` | `string` |  | Caveats the reader should know, e.g. "Illustrative data". |
| `credit` | `string` |  | Who made the piece. |
| `level` | `1 \| 2 \| 3 \| 4 \| 5 \| 6` | `1` | Heading level of the title; section headings follow one level down. |
| `maxWidth` | `number \| string` |  | Widest the piece may get. It is centred in wider containers. |
| `theme` | `ThemeInput` |  | A built-in theme name (`"editorial"`, `"ledger"`, `"noir"`...) or a theme object, passed on to everything inside. A named theme with its own surface paints that surface behind the whole piece. |
| `frame` | `boolean` |  | Paint the theme's surface behind the piece, with page padding. Default: on when `theme` is a named theme with its own surface. Set false when the host already paints it. |
| `mode` | `"auto" \| "system" \| "light" \| "dark"` | `"auto"` | Colour mode, passed on to everything inside. |

### Composition

- Composes: [headline](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/headline.md), [prose](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/prose.md), [stat-row](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/stat-row.md), [source-note](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/source-note.md), [bar-chart](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/bar-chart.md), [progress-meter](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/progress-meter.md), [line-chart](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/line-chart.md), [dumbbell-chart](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/dumbbell-chart.md), [histogram](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/histogram.md), [diverging-bar-chart](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/diverging-bar-chart.md)
- Used by: no molecule or template yet

### More examples

#### Product analytics: an experiment write-up

```tsx
import { BarChart, LineChart, ReportPage } from "insightcharts";

<ReportPage
  theme="mono"
  kicker="Experiment PRC-114 · pricing page"
  title="The annual-first pricing page converted 3.4% of visitors against 3.1% for the control"
  byline="Growth analytics"
  date="2025-05-06"
  summary="Over six weeks the annual-first pricing page converted **3.4% of visitors**. The control converted 3.1%. 52% of new customers on the annual-first page chose annual billing, against 29% in the control. We recommend shipping the annual-first page. Track refund requests for two more months before counting the revenue."
  findings={[
    {
      title: "The annual-first page converted more visitors than the control in weeks 2 to 6",
      exhibit: <LineChart
        data={[
          { week: "Week 1", Control: 3.1, "Annual-first": 3 },
          { week: "Week 2", Control: 3.2, "Annual-first": 3.3 },
          { week: "Week 3", Control: 3, "Annual-first": 3.4 },
          { week: "Week 4", Control: 3.1, "Annual-first": 3.5 },
          { week: "Week 5", Control: 3.2, "Annual-first": 3.5 },
          { week: "Week 6", Control: 3.1, "Annual-first": 3.6 },
        ]}
        x="week"
        y={["Annual-first", "Control"]}
        highlight="Annual-first"
        format="{value}%"
        height={260}
        subtitle="Share of pricing-page visitors starting a paid plan, by week of first visit"
      />,
      observation: "The six-week mean was 3.38% for the annual-first page and 3.12% for the control. That is a relative lift of 8.5%. Each arm had 61,000 visitors.",
      interpretation: "The difference did not shrink after week 2, so we do not think it is a novelty effect. We are confident the annual-first page converts better. We are less sure of the size of the lift.",
      confidence: "high",
    },
    {
      title: "52% of new customers on the annual-first page chose annual billing",
      exhibit: <BarChart
        data={[
          { arm: "Control", Monthly: 71, Annual: 29 },
          { arm: "Annual-first", Monthly: 48, Annual: 52 },
        ]}
        x="arm"
        y={["Monthly", "Annual"]}
        stack="percent"
        orientation="horizontal"
        sort="none"
        highlight="Annual"
        format="{value}%"
        subtitle="Billing period chosen by new paying customers"
      />,
      observation: "52% of new customers in the annual-first arm chose annual billing. In the control 29% did.",
      interpretation: "More cash is collected up front. Annual customers who would have cancelled a monthly plan may ask for a refund instead. The effect on revenue will not be known until the 60-day refund window closes.",
      confidence: "medium",
      caveat: "Refunds within 60 days are not yet observable for weeks four to six.",
    },
  ]}
  method="Visitors were assigned at random by account cookie, 50/50, from 17 March to 27 April 2025. The primary metric, paid conversion within seven days, was registered before launch."
  limitations={[
    "Enterprise leads, who do not use the pricing page, are excluded.",
    "The test ran outside the January budget season, when annual plans usually sell better.",
  ]}
  sources={["Experiment platform", "Billing system"]}
  note="Illustrative data"
/>
```

## Scale poster (`scale-poster`)

> A tall poster that is one illustrated scale: a full-height `scale-ladder` with icons, leader-labelled items and named zones, and a narrow side column of large figures and one small graphic, each set level with the part of the scale it describes.

- Component: `ScalePoster` (import from `insightcharts`)
- Spec type: `"scale-poster"`
- Level: template. Category: infographic.
- An HTML component: it takes only the props listed below, plus `theme`, `mode`, `className` and `style` where its source declares them. It does not take the common chart props.

### When to use

Use it when the positions of 6 to about 16 named things on one scale are the whole subject: depths, altitudes, temperatures, distances, ages. Give the scale's rows and zones in `scale`, up to five `figures` with the scale position each belongs to, and optionally a `side` graphic of two to four magnitudes. Beside the scale the figures line up with their positions; under 760px they move below it.

### Avoid

Comparing sizes rather than positions (use `ranking-poster` or `count-poster`); change over time (use `timeline-poster`); more than about 16 items, because the labels run together; several unrelated graphics (use `poster` and lay the panels out yourself).

### Install

From npm (the component ships in the package):

```bash
npm install insightcharts echarts
```

Or copy the source into your project with the shadcn CLI, so you can edit it (the engine still comes from the `insightcharts` package):

```bash
npx shadcn@latest registry add @insightcharts=https://insightcharts.dev/r/{name}.json   # once per project
npx shadcn@latest add @insightcharts/scale-poster
```

The file lands at `components/insightcharts/templates/scale-poster.tsx`. `@insightcharts/scale-poster-demo` adds a ready-made example next to it.

### Usage

```tsx
import { ScalePoster } from "insightcharts";

<ScalePoster
  theme="ocean"
  kicker="Oceans"
  title="The Meridian Deep survey logged 12 sightings between 8 m and 3,750 m"
  subtitle="Depth of each sighting on one research dive, metres below the surface."
  scale={{
    data: [
      { sighting: "Survey ship hull", m: 8, icon: "ship" },
      { sighting: "Kelp canopy", m: 120, icon: "leaf" },
      { sighting: "Sardine shoal", m: 310, icon: "fish" },
      { sighting: "Lanternfish layer", m: 560, icon: "fish" },
      { sighting: "Swordfish", m: 820, icon: "fish" },
      { sighting: "Coral mound", m: 1150, icon: "tree" },
      { sighting: "Sperm whale", m: 1480, icon: "wave" },
      { sighting: "Anglerfish", m: 1900, icon: "fish" },
      { sighting: "Sensor array", m: 2300, icon: "satellite" },
      { sighting: "Dumbo octopus", m: 2750, icon: "star" },
      { sighting: "Sea cucumbers", m: 3200, icon: "circle" },
      { sighting: "Seabed lander", m: 3750, icon: "pin" },
    ],
    name: "sighting",
    value: "m",
    iconField: "icon",
    direction: "down",
    min: 0,
    max: 4000,
    format: "{value} m",
    scaleLabel: "Depth, metres",
    zones: [
      { from: 0, to: 200, label: "Sunlit" },
      { from: 200, to: 1000, label: "Twilight zone" },
      { from: 1000, to: 4000, label: "Dark zone" },
    ],
  }}
  figures={[
    { at: 200, value: "1%", label: "of surface light is left" },
    { at: 1000, value: "4°C", label: "water temperature" },
    { at: 3000, value: "376 atm", label: "pressure at the lander, 3,750 m down" },
  ]}
  side={{
    data: [
      { zone: "species in the sunlit zone", species: 148 },
      { zone: "species in the twilight zone", species: 61 },
      { zone: "species in the dark zone", species: 23 },
    ],
    name: "zone",
    value: "species",
    title: "Species logged",
    height: 250,
  }}
  sideAt={1900}
  sources="Meridian Deep survey log"
  note="The Meridian Deep survey is invented. All figures are illustrative."
  credit="InsightCharts"
/>
```

```json
    "name": "zone",
    "value": "species",
    "title": "Species logged",
    "height": 250
  },
  "sideAt": 1900,
  "sources": "Meridian Deep survey log",
  "note": "The Meridian Deep survey is invented. All figures are illustrative.",
  "credit": "InsightCharts"
}
```

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `scale` (required) | `ScaleLadderConfig \| Slot` |  | The scale. A compact `scale-ladder` config: `{ data, name, value, iconField?, icon?, direction?, scale?, min?, max?, ticks?, zones?, scaleLabel?, format?, highlight? }`. Or a full spec, which replaces the ladder. |
| `figures` | `{ at: number; value: string; label: string; context?: string; icon?: string }[]` |  | Large figures for the side column. `at` is the position on the scale the figure belongs to; beside the scale the figure is set level with it under a dotted rule. |
| `side` | `StatCirclesConfig \| Slot` |  | One small graphic in the side column. A compact `stat-circles` config: `{ data, name, value, unit?, format?, title?, subtitle? }`. Or a full spec. |
| `sideAt` | `number` |  | Position on the scale where the `side` graphic starts. Default: under the last figure. |
| `height` | `number` |  | Height of the scale in px. Default: 68px per item, at least 920 (760 when stacked). |
| `title` (required) | `string` |  | The poster's one fact, as a plain sentence with its number. |
| `kicker` | `string` |  | Small label above the title: the topic. |
| `subtitle` | `string` |  | One line under the title: the measure, population and period. |
| `theme` | `PosterThemeName \| string \| ThemeInput` | `"ocean"` | Poster theme: `noir`, `magenta`, `dusk`, `ocean`, `forest`, `blueprint`, `sunrise`, `paper`, any other theme name, or a theme object. |
| `mode` | `"light" \| "dark" \| "auto" \| "system"` | `"light"` | Colour mode of the poster and everything in it. A poster paints its own ground and does not follow the page unless you set `auto`. Only `paper` has a different dark variant. |
| `download` | `boolean` | `false` | Show a "Download PNG" control under the poster that saves the whole poster as one image. |
| `maxWidth` | `number \| string` | `980` | Widest the poster is drawn. It is centred in wider containers. |
| `linked` | `boolean` | `false` | Make the marks clickable. Clicking a mark in one graphic highlights the same name in every other graphic that has it, and filters the graphics that read the shared `data`. Click it again, or the empty ground of that graphic, to clear. |
| `data` | `DataInput` |  | Rows shared by every region whose config leaves out its own `data`. With `linked`, a click filters those regions. |
| `sources` | `string \| string[]` |  | Where the data comes from, shown in the footer. |
| `note` | `string` |  | Caveat shown in the footer, e.g. "Illustrative data". |
| `credit` | `string` |  | Who made the poster, shown at the right of the footer. |
| `level` | `1 \| 2 \| 3 \| 4 \| 5` | `2` | Heading level of the title. Panel headings are one level down. |

### Composition

- Composes: [poster](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/poster.md), [scale-ladder](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/scale-ladder.md), [stat-circles](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/stat-circles.md)
- Used by: no molecule or template yet

## Scorecard (`scorecard`)

> A recurring report. It has a masthead with the report name and period, a headline that states the main change, a KPI grid with changes and sparklines, a ranked list beside one or two trend charts, an optional comparison table, short notes and a source note.

- Component: `Scorecard` (import from `insightcharts`)
- Spec type: `"scorecard"`
- Level: template. Category: layout.
- An HTML component: it takes only the props listed below, plus `theme`, `mode`, `className` and `style` where its source declares them. It does not take the common chart props.

### When to use

Use it for weekly or monthly numbers. Keep the layout the same in every edition so readers know where each number is. Change the headline each edition to state the main change with its number. The headline and the KPI row should be enough for a reader who stops there. The ranking, trends and notes add detail. Highlight the one row or series the headline is about and leave the rest grey.

### Avoid

A one-off finding (use `executive-brief`). Readers who need to filter the data themselves (use `data-explorer`). More than six KPIs.

### Install

From npm (the component ships in the package):

```bash
npm install insightcharts echarts
```

Or copy the source into your project with the shadcn CLI, so you can edit it (the engine still comes from the `insightcharts` package):

```bash
npx shadcn@latest registry add @insightcharts=https://insightcharts.dev/r/{name}.json   # once per project
npx shadcn@latest add @insightcharts/scorecard
```

The file lands at `components/insightcharts/templates/scorecard.tsx`. `@insightcharts/scorecard-demo` adds a ready-made example next to it.

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `title` (required) | `string` |  | The main change this period, as one plain sentence with the number in it. |
| `kicker` | `string` |  | The name of the report, e.g. "Store scorecard". Shown in the masthead. |
| `reportPeriod` | `string` |  | The period reported, e.g. "October 2024". Shown opposite the report name. |
| `deck` | `string` |  | One-sentence standfirst. |
| `byline` | `string` |  | Author line. |
| `date` | `string` |  | Publication date. |
| `kpis` | `{ data, x, metrics, compare?, change?, columns? }` |  | The headline metrics: the props of `kpi-grid`. One time-ordered dataset, one card per metric. |
| `ranking` | `{ data, name, value, change?, highlight?, title?, ... } \| Slot` |  | A ranking: the props of `ranked-list`, or any spec or element. |
| `trends` | `Slot[]` |  | One or two trend exhibits, shown beside the ranking in wide containers. |
| `table` | `{ data, columns, highlight?, sort?, title?, ... } \| Slot` |  | A comparison across entities: the props of `comparison-table`, or any spec or element. |
| `notes` | `(string \| { title, text? })[]` |  | Short notes on what changed in the period. Each states one fact with its number. |
| `notesTitle` | `string` | `"Notes"` | Heading of the notes. |
| `sources` | `string \| { name, url? } \| (string \| { name, url? })[]` |  | Where the data comes from, shown in the closing source note. Entries with a `url` are linked. |
| `period` | `string` |  | The period the data covers. |
| `method` | `string` |  | How the numbers were produced: definitions, adjustments, exclusions. |
| `note` | `string` |  | Caveats the reader should know, e.g. "Illustrative data". |
| `credit` | `string` |  | Who made the piece. |
| `level` | `1 \| 2 \| 3 \| 4 \| 5 \| 6` | `1` | Heading level of the title; section headings follow one level down. |
| `maxWidth` | `number \| string` |  | Widest the piece may get. It is centred in wider containers. |
| `theme` | `ThemeInput` |  | A built-in theme name (`"editorial"`, `"ledger"`, `"noir"`...) or a theme object, passed on to everything inside. A named theme with its own surface paints that surface behind the whole piece. |
| `frame` | `boolean` |  | Paint the theme's surface behind the piece, with page padding. Default: on when `theme` is a named theme with its own surface. Set false when the host already paints it. |
| `mode` | `"auto" \| "system" \| "light" \| "dark"` | `"auto"` | Colour mode, passed on to everything inside. |

### Composition

- Composes: [headline](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/headline.md), [kpi-grid](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/kpi-grid.md), [ranked-list](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/ranked-list.md), [comparison-table](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/comparison-table.md), [prose](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/prose.md), [source-note](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/source-note.md), [line-chart](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/line-chart.md), [bar-chart](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/bar-chart.md), [bullet-chart](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/bullet-chart.md)
- Used by: no molecule or template yet

## Social card (`social-card`)

> A graphic that states one fact, at a fixed aspect ratio (1:1, 4:5, 16:9 or 9:16). It has a kicker, a headline, one exhibit, a source and a credit, painted on the theme surface. A button downloads the whole card as a PNG.

- Component: `SocialCard` (import from `insightcharts`)
- Spec type: `"social-card"`
- Level: template. Category: layout.
- An HTML component: it takes only the props listed below, plus `theme`, `mode`, `className` and `style` where its source declares them. It does not take the common chart props.

### When to use

Use it for one finding that will be shared in a feed, a slide or a chat thread with no text around it. State the fact with its number in the headline. Use one simple exhibit, such as one highlighted bar, one line or one number. Put the source and your name on the card, because it will be shared without the page. Use 1:1 or 4:5 for feeds, 16:9 for slides and link previews, 9:16 for stories.

### Avoid

More than one fact or more than one exhibit (use `story-deck` for a sequence, `executive-brief` for a page). Charts that need a legend, small labels or hovering to read, because a shared image is not interactive. An exhibit with its own `title`, because the card's headline is the title.

### Install

From npm (the component ships in the package):

```bash
npm install insightcharts echarts
```

Or copy the source into your project with the shadcn CLI, so you can edit it (the engine still comes from the `insightcharts` package):

```bash
npx shadcn@latest registry add @insightcharts=https://insightcharts.dev/r/{name}.json   # once per project
npx shadcn@latest add @insightcharts/social-card
```

The file lands at `components/insightcharts/templates/social-card.tsx`. `@insightcharts/social-card-demo` adds a ready-made example next to it.

### Usage

```tsx
import { BarChart, SocialCard } from "insightcharts";

<SocialCard
  theme="magenta"
  aspect="1:1"
  kicker="Climate"
  title="The world was 1.6°C warmer in 2024 than in 1850 to 1900"
  exhibit={<BarChart
    data={[
      { year: "2015", c: 1.17 },
      { year: "2016", c: 1.31 },
      { year: "2017", c: 1.22 },
      { year: "2018", c: 1.14 },
      { year: "2019", c: 1.26 },
      { year: "2020", c: 1.31 },
      { year: "2021", c: 1.14 },
      { year: "2022", c: 1.18 },
      { year: "2023", c: 1.48 },
      { year: "2024", c: 1.6 },
    ]}
    x="year"
    y="c"
    orientation="vertical"
    sort="none"
    highlight="2024"
    format="{value}°C"
    labels={false}
    subtitle="Global average temperature above the 1850 to 1900 level"
    annotations={[{ type: "line", axis: "y", value: 1.5, label: "Paris Agreement limit" }]}
  />}
  source="Copernicus Climate Change Service, ERA5 (rounded)"
  note="Figures are approximate, for illustration"
  credit="InsightCharts"
/>
```

```json
  "exhibit": {
    "type": "bar-chart",
    "data": [
      { "year": "2015", "c": 1.17 },
      { "year": "2016", "c": 1.31 },
      { "year": "2017", "c": 1.22 },
      { "year": "2018", "c": 1.14 },
      { "year": "2019", "c": 1.26 },
      { "year": "2020", "c": 1.31 },
      { "year": "2021", "c": 1.14 },
      { "year": "2022", "c": 1.18 },
      { "year": "2023", "c": 1.48 },
      { "year": "2024", "c": 1.6 }
    ],
    "x": "year",
    "y": "c",
    "orientation": "vertical",
    "sort": "none",
    "highlight": "2024",
    "format": "{value}°C",
    "labels": false,
    "subtitle": "Global average temperature above the 1850 to 1900 level",
    "annotations": [{ "type": "line", "axis": "y", "value": 1.5, "label": "Paris Agreement limit" }]
  },
  "source": "Copernicus Climate Change Service, ERA5 (rounded)",
  "note": "Figures are approximate, for illustration",
  "credit": "InsightCharts"

```

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `title` (required) | `string` |  | The card's one fact, as a plain sentence with the number in it. |
| `kicker` | `string` |  | Small label above the title. |
| `deck` | `string` |  | One short line under the title: the measure, or the number in words. |
| `exhibit` | `Slot` |  | The one exhibit. A chart spec is given the height left in the card (any `height` you set wins); leave out its `title`. |
| `source` | `string` |  | Where the data comes from, shown as "Source: ...". |
| `note` | `string` |  | Caveat shown after the source, e.g. "Illustrative data". |
| `credit` | `string` |  | Who made it: a name, handle or publication. |
| `aspect` | `"1:1" \| "4:5" \| "16:9" \| "9:16"` | `"1:1"` | Shape of the card. |
| `tone` | `"surface" \| "inverse"` | `"surface"` | `inverse` paints the card in the opposite colour mode. |
| `downloadable` | `boolean` | `true` | Show the download button under the card. The image is the whole card, drawn from the DOM onto a canvas. |
| `exportWidth` | `number` | `1080` | Width of the downloaded PNG in pixels (1920 for 16:9). |
| `filename` | `string` |  | File name without extension. Defaults to a slug of the title. |
| `downloadLabel` | `string` | `"Download PNG"` | Label of the download button. |
| `maxWidth` | `number` |  | Widest the card is drawn on screen, in px. Default 540 (520 for 4:5, 720 for 16:9, 400 for 9:16). In narrower containers the whole card is scaled down, like an image, so its composition never changes. |
| `onExport` | `(blob: Blob) => void` |  | Called with the PNG after a download. |
| `level` | `1 \| 2 \| 3 \| 4 \| 5 \| 6` | `2` | Heading level of the title. |
| `theme` | `ThemeInput` |  | A built-in theme name (`"magenta"`, `"noir"`, `"editorial"`...) or a theme object, passed on to the exhibit. A named theme with its own surface paints the card in that surface; the download button stays in the page's theme. |
| `mode` | `"auto" \| "system" \| "light" \| "dark"` | `"auto"` | Colour mode. |

### Composition

- Composes: [bar-chart](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/bar-chart.md), [big-number](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/big-number.md), [waffle-chart](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/waffle-chart.md), [area-chart](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/area-chart.md), [source-note](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/source-note.md)
- Used by: no molecule or template yet


#### 9:16, transport, a proportion instead of a chart

```tsx

  theme="ocean"

  title="58% of car journeys in England are under five miles"
  deck="Each square is 1% of car journeys."

    data={[{ group: "Under five miles", share: 58 }]}
    name="group"
    value="share"
    total={100}
    restLabel="Five miles or more"
    legend={false}
    aspect={1}
  />}
  source="National Travel Survey"
  note="Rounded, approximate figures for illustration"
  credit="@datadesk"
/>
```

## Story deck (`story-deck`)

> A sequence of full-frame cards (title, stat, chart, quote, closing) that the reader swipes or steps through. Each card states one fact. It has an optional fixed aspect ratio, a keyboard-accessible pager and a stacked layout for print.

- Component: `StoryDeck` (import from `insightcharts`)
- Spec type: `"story-deck"`
- Level: template. Category: story.
- An HTML component: it takes only the props listed below, plus `theme`, `mode`, `className` and `style` where its source declares them. It does not take the common chart props.

### When to use

Use it for a short sequence read on a phone, such as a “year in review”. Each card should be readable in a couple of seconds. State the main fact with its number on the title card. Put one fact on each later card, as a number or as one chart with one highlighted mark under a headline that states the fact. Use five to ten cards. End with a closing card and the sources. Charts in cards should have few data points and direct labels, with no legend.

### Avoid

Findings that need two exhibits in view at once (use `executive-brief`). A single shareable image (use `social-card`). Dense charts or long paragraphs, because a card has little room. One chart that changes step by step (use `scrolly-chart` in `steps` mode).

### Install

From npm (the component ships in the package):

```bash
npm install insightcharts echarts
```

Or copy the source into your project with the shadcn CLI, so you can edit it (the engine still comes from the `insightcharts` package):

```bash
npx shadcn@latest registry add @insightcharts=https://insightcharts.dev/r/{name}.json   # once per project
npx shadcn@latest add @insightcharts/story-deck
```

The file lands at `components/insightcharts/templates/story-deck.tsx`. `@insightcharts/story-deck-demo` adds a ready-made example next to it.

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `cards` (required) | `Card[]` |  | The cards in order. Each has a `kind`: `title` `{ title, deck?, byline? }`; `stat` `{ value, label, context?, delta?, deltaLabel?, upIsGood?, format?, text?, variant?, icon?, series?, target?, max? }`, where `variant` is any `big-number` display (`with-icon`, `with-ring`, `with-trend`, `filled`, `tinted`); `chart` `{ title, chart, text? }`; `quote` `{ quote, attribution?, role? }`; `closing` `{ title, text?, points?, action?: { label, href } }`. Any card takes `kicker`, `tone: "surface" \| "inverse" \| "accent"` and `id`. |
| `label` | `string` |  | Accessible name of the deck. Defaults to the first card's title. |
| `aspect` | `"auto" \| "9:16" \| "4:5" \| "1:1" \| "16:9"` | `"4:5"` | Shape of every card. `auto` lets cards take the height their content needs. `16:9` falls back to `4:5` in containers under 520px. |
| `layout` | `"pager" \| "stack"` | `"pager"` | `pager` shows one card at a time (swipe, buttons, dots, arrow keys, Home/End). `stack` lists every card in a column. |
| `startAt` | `number` | `0` | Card shown first (zero-based). |
| `onCardChange` | `(index: number) => void` |  | Called when the visible card changes. |
| `maxWidth` | `number` |  | Widest a card is drawn, in px. Default 440 (400 for 9:16, 520 for 1:1, 840 for 16:9). Type and spacing scale with the card. |
| `previousLabel` | `string` | `"Previous"` | Label of the previous button. |
| `nextLabel` | `string` | `"Next"` | Label of the next button. |
| `sources` | `string \| { name, url? } \| (string \| { name, url? })[]` |  | Where the data comes from, shown in the closing source note. Entries with a `url` are linked. |
| `period` | `string` |  | The period the data covers. |
| `method` | `string` |  | How the numbers were produced: definitions, adjustments, exclusions. |
| `note` | `string` |  | Caveats the reader should know, e.g. "Illustrative data". |
| `credit` | `string` |  | Who made the piece. |
| `level` | `1 \| 2 \| 3 \| 4 \| 5 \| 6` | `1` | Heading level of the title; section headings follow one level down. |
| `theme` | `ThemeInput` |  | A built-in theme name (`"dusk"`, `"magenta"`, `"paper"`...) or a theme object, passed on to everything in the cards. A named theme with its own surface paints each card in that surface; the pager and the source note stay in the page's theme. |
| `mode` | `"auto" \| "system" \| "light" \| "dark"` | `"auto"` | Colour mode, passed on to everything inside. |

### Composition

- Composes: [big-number](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/big-number.md), [prose](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/prose.md), [pull-quote](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/pull-quote.md), [source-note](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/source-note.md), [bar-chart](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/bar-chart.md), [line-chart](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/line-chart.md), [radial-bar-chart](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/radial-bar-chart.md), [waffle-chart](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/waffle-chart.md)
- Used by: no molecule or template yet

## Timeline poster (`timeline-poster`)

> A poster of change over a run of periods: a full-width ribbon of bands whose thickness is each entity's value and whose order is its rank (`ribbon-chart`), a strip of two to four dated figures under it, and a bottom row with one measure per period as thick bars (`block-bar`) and one share at several dates as nested outlines (`nested-shares`).

- Component: `TimelinePoster` (import from `insightcharts`)
- Spec type: `"timeline-poster"`
- Level: template. Category: infographic.
- An HTML component: it takes only the props listed below, plus `theme`, `mode`, `className` and `style` where its source declares them. It does not take the common chart props.

### When to use

Use it when the subject is how 4 to 8 named things grew, shrank and changed places over 4 to 10 periods: electricity by source, library loans by format, commuters by mode. Give `hero` the periods and entities, `milestones` the dated numbers a reader should take away, `bars` one measure of the whole at each period and `shares` one share at a few dates. State the latest value in the title.

### Avoid

A single series over time (use `line-chart` or `area-chart` in a `poster`). Events with start and end dates (use `timeline-chart` or the `timeline-story` template). More than 8 entities or 10 periods, because the bands get too thin to label. Positions on one scale (use `scale-poster`). Parts of one subject at one date (use `radial-poster`).

### Install

From npm (the component ships in the package):

```bash
npm install insightcharts echarts
```

Or copy the source into your project with the shadcn CLI, so you can edit it (the engine still comes from the `insightcharts` package):

```bash
npx shadcn@latest registry add @insightcharts=https://insightcharts.dev/r/{name}.json   # once per project
npx shadcn@latest add @insightcharts/timeline-poster
```

The file lands at `components/insightcharts/templates/timeline-poster.tsx`. `@insightcharts/timeline-poster-demo` adds a ready-made example next to it.

### Usage

```tsx
import { TimelinePoster } from "insightcharts";

<TimelinePoster
  theme="sunrise"
  kicker="Electricity"
  title="Wind supplied 8.6 TWh of Orrin Island's electricity in 2025"
  subtitle="Electricity generated on Orrin Island by source, terawatt-hours, every second year from 2015 to 2025."
  hero={{
    data: [
      { year: "2015", Coal: 9.2, Gas: 6.1, Hydro: 2.2, Wind: 1.4, Solar: 0.3 },
      { year: "2017", Coal: 8, Gas: 6.4, Hydro: 2.3, Wind: 2.6, Solar: 0.6 },
      { year: "2019", Coal: 6.1, Gas: 6, Hydro: 2.1, Wind: 4.3, Solar: 1.3 },
      { year: "2021", Coal: 4, Gas: 5.4, Hydro: 2.4, Wind: 5.9, Solar: 2.4 },
      { year: "2023", Coal: 2.3, Gas: 4.7, Hydro: 2.2, Wind: 7.4, Solar: 3.7 },
      { year: "2025", Coal: 1.1, Gas: 4, Hydro: 2.3, Wind: 8.6, Solar: 4.9 },
    ],
    x: "year",
    y: ["Coal", "Gas", "Hydro", "Wind", "Solar"],
    colorBy: "series",
    title: "Coal supplied 9.2 TWh in 2015",
  }}
  milestones={[
    { at: "2017", value: "62", label: "turbines started at the Skerry wind farm" },
    { at: "2021", value: "5.9 TWh", label: "came from wind", context: "Gas supplied 5.4 TWh" },
    { at: "2025", value: "1.1 TWh", label: "came from coal", context: "9.2 TWh in 2015" },
  ]}
  bars={{
    data: [
      { year: "2015", g: 520 },
      { year: "2017", g: 455 },
      { year: "2019", g: 370 },
      { year: "2021", g: 290 },
      { year: "2023", g: 215 },
      { year: "2025", g: 160 },
    ],
    name: "year",
    value: "g",
    format: "{value} g",
    marker: { after: "2017", label: "Skerry wind farm opened" },
    title: "A kilowatt-hour emitted 160 g of CO2 in 2025",
    subtitle: "Grams of CO2 per kilowatt-hour generated.",
  }}
  shares={{
    data: [
      { year: "2015", share: 9 },
      { year: "2019", share: 28 },
      { year: "2021", share: 41 },
      { year: "2025", share: 65 },
    ],
    name: "year",
    value: "share",
    highlight: "2025",
    wholeLabel: "All electricity generated",
    title: "Wind and solar supplied 65% of electricity in 2025",
  }}
  sources="Orrin Island Grid Office, annual generation statistics"
  note="Orrin Island is an invented place. All figures are illustrative."
  credit="InsightCharts"
/>
```

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `hero` (required) | `{ data, x, y, series?, values?, labels?, colorBy?, format?, highlight?, title?, ... } \| Slot` |  | The hero: one band per entity across the periods, drawn by `ribbon-chart`. Wide rows take `y` as a list of columns; long rows take `y` and `series`. A full spec or element replaces it. |
| `milestones` | `{ at: string; value: string; label: string; context?: string; icon?: string }[]` |  | Two to four dated figures in a strip under the hero, in time order. `at` is the period, printed in small capitals over the figure. |
| `bars` | `{ data, name, value, marker?, detail?, format?, title?, ... } \| Slot` |  | Bottom left: one measure at each period as thick bars with the numbers inside (`block-bar`). `marker: { after, label }` draws a dotted line after one period to mark an event. |
| `shares` | `{ data, name, value, wholeLabel?, highlight?, format?, title?, ... } \| Slot` |  | Bottom right: one share at 2 to 8 dates as outlines nested in one square (`nested-shares`). `format` defaults to `"{value}%"`. With only one of `bars` and `shares`, that one takes the full width. |
| `title` (required) | `string` |  | The poster's one fact, as a plain sentence with its number. |
| `kicker` | `string` |  | Small label above the title: the topic. |
| `subtitle` | `string` |  | One line under the title: the measure, population and period. |
| `theme` | `PosterThemeName \| string \| ThemeInput` | `"sunrise"` | Poster theme: `noir`, `magenta`, `dusk`, `ocean`, `forest`, `blueprint`, `sunrise`, `paper`, any other theme name, or a theme object. |
| `mode` | `"light" \| "dark" \| "auto" \| "system"` | `"light"` | Colour mode of the poster and everything in it. A poster paints its own ground and does not follow the page unless you set `auto`. Only `paper` has a different dark variant. |
| `download` | `boolean` | `false` | Show a "Download PNG" control under the poster that saves the whole poster as one image. |
| `maxWidth` | `number \| string` | `1100` | Widest the poster is drawn. It is centred in wider containers. |
| `linked` | `boolean` | `false` | Make the marks clickable. Clicking a mark in one graphic highlights the same name in every other graphic that has it, and filters the graphics that read the shared `data`. Click it again, or the empty ground of that graphic, to clear. |
| `data` | `DataInput` |  | Rows shared by every region whose config leaves out its own `data`. With `linked`, a click filters those regions. |
| `sources` | `string \| string[]` |  | Where the data comes from, shown in the footer. |
| `note` | `string` |  | Caveat shown in the footer, e.g. "Illustrative data". |
| `credit` | `string` |  | Who made the poster, shown at the right of the footer. |
| `level` | `1 \| 2 \| 3 \| 4 \| 5` | `2` | Heading level of the title. Panel headings are one level down. |

### Composition

- Composes: [poster](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/poster.md), [ribbon-chart](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/ribbon-chart.md), [block-bar](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/block-bar.md), [nested-shares](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/nested-shares.md)
- Used by: no molecule or template yet

## Timeline story (`timeline-story`)

> A story told in date order. It has a headline, one overview exhibit of the whole period (a timeline chart or an annotated line), dated chapters along a rail, a closing paragraph and a source note. Each chapter has a short text and an optional small exhibit.

- Component: `TimelineStory` (import from `insightcharts`)
- Spec type: `"timeline-story"`
- Level: template. Category: story.
- An HTML component: it takes only the props listed below, plus `theme`, `mode`, `className` and `style` where its source declares them. It does not take the common chart props.

### When to use

Use it when the reader needs the events in date order to understand a change. State the change over the whole period in the headline, with the numbers and dates. Mark the main events on the overview exhibit as annotations. Give each chapter one event. Add a small figure to a chapter only when it has a number to show. Mark the two or three most important events with `emphasis`.

### Avoid

Events with no measure that runs through the period (use a plain `annotated-timeline`). A comparison of two states with nothing in between (use `comparison-brief`). More than eight chapters. Merge minor events into the text of the chapter before or after.

### Install

From npm (the component ships in the package):

```bash
npm install insightcharts echarts
```

Or copy the source into your project with the shadcn CLI, so you can edit it (the engine still comes from the `insightcharts` package):

```bash
npx shadcn@latest registry add @insightcharts=https://insightcharts.dev/r/{name}.json   # once per project
npx shadcn@latest add @insightcharts/timeline-story
```

The file lands at `components/insightcharts/templates/timeline-story.tsx`. `@insightcharts/timeline-story-demo` adds a ready-made example next to it.

### Usage

```tsx
import { BarChart, LineChart, StatTile, TimelineStory } from "insightcharts";

<TimelineStory
  theme="forest"
  kicker="Energy"
  title="Coal generated 39% of Britain's electricity in 2012 and 0.6% in 2024"
  deck="The first public coal power station opened in 1882. The last coal plant closed on 30 September 2024."
  byline="By the data desk"
  date="2024-10-01"
  timeline={<LineChart
    data={[
      { year: "1990-01-01", share: 65, wind: 0 },
      { year: "1994-01-01", share: 50, wind: 0 },
      { year: "1998-01-01", share: 35, wind: 0.2 },
      { year: "2002-01-01", share: 32, wind: 0.4 },
      { year: "2006-01-01", share: 38, wind: 1 },
      { year: "2010-01-01", share: 28, wind: 3 },
      { year: "2012-01-01", share: 39, wind: 6 },
      { year: "2013-01-01", share: 36, wind: 8 },
      { year: "2014-01-01", share: 30, wind: 9 },
      { year: "2015-01-01", share: 22, wind: 12 },
      { year: "2016-01-01", share: 9, wind: 11 },
      { year: "2017-01-01", share: 7, wind: 15 },
      { year: "2018-01-01", share: 5, wind: 17 },
      { year: "2019-01-01", share: 2, wind: 20 },
      { year: "2020-01-01", share: 2, wind: 24 },
      { year: "2021-01-01", share: 2, wind: 21 },
      { year: "2022-01-01", share: 1.5, wind: 27 },
      { year: "2023-01-01", share: 1, wind: 29 },
      { year: "2024-01-01", share: 0.6, wind: 30 },
    ]}
    x="year"
    y={["share", "wind"]}
    names={{ share: "Coal", wind: "Wind" }}
    format="{value}%"
    zero
    title="Coal's share of generation fell from 65% in 1990 to 0.6% in 2024"
    subtitle="Share of Great Britain's electricity generated from coal and from wind, 1990 to 2024"
    annotations={[
      { type: "band", axis: "x", from: "1990-01-01", to: "1998-01-01", label: "Gas plants built" },
      { type: "line", axis: "x", value: "2013-01-01", label: "Carbon price floor" },
      { type: "point", x: "2012-01-01", y: 39, label: "39% in 2012", position: "top" },
    ]}
    source="Department for Energy Security and Net Zero and National Grid ESO (rounded)"
    note="Figures are approximate, for illustration"
  />}
  intro="Coal's share fell in two periods. It fell from 65% to 35% between 1990 and 1998, when generators built gas plants. It fell from 39% to 9% between 2012 and 2016, after the carbon price floor was introduced."
  chapters={[
    {
      date: "1882",
      title: "The first public coal power station opens in London",
      text: "Thomas Edison's company built the plant at Holborn Viaduct. It supplied street lamps and nearby buildings.",
    },
    {
      date: "1990s",
      title: "Coal's share falls from 65% to 35% between 1990 and 1998",
      text: "Privatised generators built gas plants, which were cheaper and quicker to build than coal plants. Coal's share was between 28% and 39% from 1998 to 2013.",
    },
    {
      date: "April 2013",
      title: "The carbon price floor takes effect",
      emphasis: true,
      text: "The floor set a minimum price on power-station emissions. The rate doubled in 2015. Coal's share fell from 22% in 2015 to 9% in 2016.",
      exhibit: <BarChart
        data={[
          { year: "2012", share: 39 },
          { year: "2013", share: 36 },
          { year: "2014", share: 30 },
          { year: "2015", share: 22 },
          { year: "2016", share: 9 },
        ]}
        x="year"
        y="share"
        orientation="vertical"
        sort="none"
        highlight="2016"
        format="{value}%"
        height={170}
        subtitle="Coal share of generation, 2012 to 2016"
      />,
    },
    {
      date: "21 April 2017",
      title: "The first full day without coal since 1882",
      text: "Britain had 1 coal-free day in 2017. It had 180 in 2020.",
      exhibit: <BarChart
        data={[
          { year: "2017", days: 1 },
          { year: "2018", days: 21 },
          { year: "2019", days: 83 },
          { year: "2020", days: 180 },
        ]}
        x="year"
        y="days"
        orientation="vertical"
        sort="none"
        highlight="2020"
        height={170}
        subtitle="Coal-free days per year"
      />,
    },
    {
      date: "30 September 2024",
      title: "Ratcliffe-on-Soar, the last coal plant, shuts down",
      emphasis: true,
      text: "The plant had run since 1968. In 2024 wind generated 30% of the country's electricity and gas generated 26%.",
      exhibit: <StatTile
        variant="comparison"
        surface="borderless"
        upIsGood={false}
        value={0.6}
        comparison={39}
        valueLabel="2024"
        comparisonLabel="2012"
        format="{value}%"
        label="Coal share of generation"
        context="Britain was the first G7 country to end coal power"
      />,
    },
  ]}
  closing="Coal generated 0.6% of Britain's electricity in 2024, all of it before 30 September. Gas generated 26%."
  sources={["Digest of UK Energy Statistics", "National Grid ESO"]}
  period="1990 to 2024"
  note="Annual shares are rounded. Intermediate years before 2012 are interpolated for the chart. Figures are approximate, for illustration."
/>
```

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `title` (required) | `string` |  | The change over the whole period, as one plain sentence with the numbers and dates in it. |
| `kicker` | `string` |  | Small label above the title. |
| `deck` | `string` |  | One-sentence standfirst. |
| `byline` | `string` |  | Author line. |
| `date` | `string` |  | Publication date. |
| `timeline` | `Slot` |  | The overview exhibit: a `timeline-chart` spec, or a `line-chart` with the events as `annotations`. Default height 360px for line charts. |
| `intro` | `string \| string[]` |  | A paragraph between the overview and the chapters. |
| `chaptersTitle` | `string` |  | Heading over the chapters. |
| `chapters` (required) | `{ date, title, text?, exhibit?, emphasis? }[]` |  | The dated chapters, oldest first. `date` is shown as written; `exhibit` is a small chart or figure; `emphasis` fills the marker for a major event. |
| `exhibitPosition` | `"below" \| "side"` | `"side"` | Where a chapter's exhibit sits; `side` falls back to `below` under 640px. |
| `closing` | `string \| string[]` |  | A closing paragraph that states the latest figures. |
| `sources` | `string \| { name, url? } \| (string \| { name, url? })[]` |  | Where the data comes from, shown in the closing source note. Entries with a `url` are linked. |
| `period` | `string` |  | The period the data covers. |
| `method` | `string` |  | How the numbers were produced: definitions, adjustments, exclusions. |
| `note` | `string` |  | Caveats the reader should know, e.g. "Illustrative data". |
| `credit` | `string` |  | Who made the piece. |
| `level` | `1 \| 2 \| 3 \| 4 \| 5 \| 6` | `1` | Heading level of the title; section headings follow one level down. |
| `maxWidth` | `number \| string` |  | Widest the piece may get. It is centred in wider containers. |
| `theme` | `ThemeInput` |  | A built-in theme name (`"editorial"`, `"ledger"`, `"noir"`...) or a theme object, passed on to everything inside. A named theme with its own surface paints that surface behind the whole piece. |
| `frame` | `boolean` |  | Paint the theme's surface behind the piece, with page padding. Default: on when `theme` is a named theme with its own surface. Set false when the host already paints it. |
| `mode` | `"auto" \| "system" \| "light" \| "dark"` | `"auto"` | Colour mode, passed on to everything inside. |

### Composition

- Composes: [headline](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/headline.md), [prose](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/prose.md), [annotated-timeline](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/annotated-timeline.md), [source-note](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/source-note.md), [line-chart](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/line-chart.md), [timeline-chart](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/timeline-chart.md), [bar-chart](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/bar-chart.md), [big-number](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/big-number.md), [stat-tile](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/stat-tile.md), [waffle-chart](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/waffle-chart.md)
- Used by: no molecule or template yet

## Visual essay (`visual-essay`)

> A long article read by scrolling. It has a headline, then an ordered list of blocks in a reading column, then a source note. The blocks are prose, figures, charts with a callout, scrolly sequences, pull quotes, stat rows, small multiples and chapter breaks. Exhibits can be wider than the column.

- Component: `VisualEssay` (import from `insightcharts`)
- Spec type: `"visual-essay"`
- Level: template. Category: story.
- An HTML component: it takes only the props listed below, plus `theme`, `mode`, `className` and `style` where its source declares them. It does not take the common chart props.

### When to use

Use it for a finding that takes several charts and some text to explain. State the main finding with its number in the headline. Put the main figure within the first screen. Alternate text and charts, with two or three short paragraphs before each exhibit. In a scrolly block change one thing per step, such as the highlight, the year or an annotation. Use one accent colour for the subject in every chart.

### Avoid

A summary for someone who will not scroll (use `executive-brief`). Reference material read out of order (use `report-page`). More than one or two scrolly blocks. Use one only where the chart changes between steps.

### Install

From npm (the component ships in the package):

```bash
npm install insightcharts echarts
```

Or copy the source into your project with the shadcn CLI, so you can edit it (the engine still comes from the `insightcharts` package):

```bash
npx shadcn@latest registry add @insightcharts=https://insightcharts.dev/r/{name}.json   # once per project
npx shadcn@latest add @insightcharts/visual-essay
```

The file lands at `components/insightcharts/templates/visual-essay.tsx`. `@insightcharts/visual-essay-demo` adds a ready-made example next to it.

### Usage

```tsx

          variant: "bars",

          variant: "bars",
```

### JSON spec

The same thing as data, rendered with `<Insight spec={spec} />`:

```json
{
  "type": "visual-essay",
  "theme": "editorial",
```

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `title` (required) | `string` |  | The essay's main finding, as one plain sentence with the number and the period in it. |
| `kicker` | `string` |  | Small label above the title. |
| `deck` | `string` |  | One-sentence standfirst. |
| `byline` | `string` |  | Author line. |
| `date` | `string` |  | Publication date. ISO dates are formatted for the locale. |
| `blocks` (required) | `(Block \| Slot)[]` |  | The story in reading order. Each block has a `kind`: `prose` `{ text, lead? }`; `figure` `{ chart, caption? }`; `callout` `{ chart, lead, body, label?, tone?, side? }`; `scrolly` `{ chart, steps, cumulative?, scrollMode?, side?, stepHeight? }` (the props of `scrolly-chart`); `quote` `{ quote, attribution?, role? }`; `stats` `{ items, variant?, title? }` (the props of `stat-row`); `multiples` `{ facet, ... }` (props of `small-multiples`, or of `small-multiple-grid` when it has a `chart`); `break` `{ title, step?, total?, text? }`. Any block takes `width: "text" \| "wide" \| "full"` and an `id`. A bare chart spec is treated as a wide figure. |
| `measure` | `number` | `680` | Width of the reading column in px. |
| `textSize` | `"md" \| "lg"` |  | Body text size. Default 18px, 16px in narrow containers. |
| `sources` | `string \| { name, url? } \| (string \| { name, url? })[]` |  | Where the data comes from, shown in the closing source note. Entries with a `url` are linked. |
| `period` | `string` |  | The period the data covers. |
| `method` | `string` |  | How the numbers were produced: definitions, adjustments, exclusions. |
| `note` | `string` |  | Caveats the reader should know, e.g. "Illustrative data". |
| `credit` | `string` |  | Who made the piece. |
| `level` | `1 \| 2 \| 3 \| 4 \| 5 \| 6` | `1` | Heading level of the title; section headings follow one level down. |
| `maxWidth` | `number \| string` |  | Widest the piece may get. It is centred in wider containers. |
| `theme` | `ThemeInput` |  | A built-in theme name (`"editorial"`, `"ledger"`, `"noir"`...) or a theme object, passed on to everything inside. A named theme with its own surface paints that surface behind the whole piece. |
| `frame` | `boolean` |  | Paint the theme's surface behind the piece, with page padding. Default: on when `theme` is a named theme with its own surface. Set false when the host already paints it. |
| `mode` | `"auto" \| "system" \| "light" \| "dark"` | `"auto"` | Colour mode, passed on to everything inside. |

### Composition

- Composes: [headline](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/headline.md), [prose](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/prose.md), [pull-quote](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/pull-quote.md), [step-marker](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/step-marker.md), [small-multiples](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/small-multiples.md), [chart-callout](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/chart-callout.md), [scrolly-chart](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/scrolly-chart.md), [small-multiple-grid](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/small-multiple-grid.md), [stat-row](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/stat-row.md), [source-note](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/source-note.md), [line-chart](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/line-chart.md), [bar-chart](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/bar-chart.md), [waffle-chart](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/waffle-chart.md), [dumbbell-chart](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/dumbbell-chart.md), [heatmap](https://insightcharts.dev/llms/heatmap.md)
- Used by: no molecule or template yet

### More examples

#### Transport: a shorter essay without a scrolly

```tsx
import { LineChart, VisualEssay, WaffleChart } from "insightcharts";

<VisualEssay
  theme="earth"
  kicker="Cities"
  title="Cycling accounts for 11.2% of trips in Paris and cars for 4.3%"
  deck="Bicycle counts in 2024 were 3.2 times the 2015 level. The city made 50 km of temporary pandemic cycle lanes permanent."
  byline="By the transport desk"
  date="2025-04-02"
  textSize="md"
  blocks={[
    {
      kind: "prose",
      lead: true,
      text: "Permanent counters in Paris recorded 3.2 times as many bicycles in 2024 as in 2015. The count rose 47% between 2019 and 2020.",
    },
    {
      kind: "figure",
      chart: <LineChart
        data={[
          { year: "2015", index: 100 },
          { year: "2016", index: 104 },
          { year: "2017", index: 108 },
          { year: "2018", index: 118 },
          { year: "2019", index: 154 },
          { year: "2020", index: 226 },
          { year: "2021", index: 241 },
          { year: "2022", index: 262 },
          { year: "2023", index: 288 },
          { year: "2024", index: 317 },
        ]}
        x="year"
        y="index"
        zero
        title="Bicycle counts in Paris in 2024 were 3.2 times the 2015 level"
        subtitle="Bicycle counts at permanent counters, index (2015 = 100)"
        annotations={[
          { type: "line", axis: "x", value: "2020", label: "Temporary lanes open" },
          { type: "point", x: "2024", y: 317, label: "3.2 times\nthe 2015 level", position: "left" },
        ]}
        source="City of Paris counter data (rounded, illustrative)"
      />,
    },
    {
      kind: "prose",
      text: "The index rose from 154 in 2019 to 226 in 2020, when the city opened 50 km of temporary lanes. The city kept those lanes and built 130 km more. The index reached 317 in 2024.",
    },
    {
      kind: "quote",
      quote: "Counts went up on the streets where we built protected lanes. They stayed up after the lockdowns ended.",
      attribution: "A city transport planner",
    },
    {
      kind: "callout",
      chart: <WaffleChart
        data={[
          { mode: "Walking", share: 53.5 },
          { mode: "Public transport", share: 30 },
          { mode: "Cycling", share: 11.2 },
          { mode: "Car", share: 4.3 },
          { mode: "Other", share: 1 },
        ]}
        name="mode"
        value="share"
        total={100}
        format="{value}%"
        title="Cycling's share of trips within Paris is 2.6 times the car's"
        subtitle="Share of trips within Paris by main mode, 2023"
        source="Institut Paris Region mobility survey"
      />,
      lead: "Walking accounts for 53.5% of trips within Paris",
      body: "Public transport accounts for 30.0%. Cycling accounts for 11.2% and cars for 4.3%.",
      tone: "neutral",
    },
    {
      kind: "prose",
      text: "These shares are for trips within the city. In the suburbs the car accounts for one trip in three.",
    },
  ]}
  sources={["City of Paris open data", "Institut Paris Region"]}
  period="2015 to 2024"
  note="Counter index is illustrative. Mode shares are approximate, for illustration."
/>
```

#### Health: sleep survey on a poster ground

```tsx
import { BarChart, DumbbellChart, Heatmap, VisualEssay } from "insightcharts";

<VisualEssay
  theme="dusk"
  kicker="Sleep survey 2024"
  title="Adults slept 6 hours 48 minutes on weeknights in 2024"
  deck="They slept 7 hours 52 minutes at weekends. 31% slept less than 6 hours on weeknights."
  byline="By the health desk"
  date="2025-02-18"
  textSize="md"
  blocks={[
    {
      kind: "prose",
      lead: true,
      text: "The survey asked 12,400 adults when they fell asleep and woke up on each of 14 nights. The average weeknight was **6 hours 48 minutes**. Health guidance recommends at least 7 hours.",
    },
    {
      kind: "figure",
      chart: <BarChart
        data={[
          { band: "Under 5 hours", share: 9 },
          { band: "5 to 6 hours", share: 22 },
          { band: "6 to 7 hours", share: 34 },
          { band: "7 to 8 hours", share: 24 },
          { band: "8 to 9 hours", share: 8 },
          { band: "9 hours or more", share: 3 },
        ]}
        x="band"
        y="share"
        sort="none"
        orientation="vertical"
        format="{value}%"
        highlight={["Under 5 hours", "5 to 6 hours"]}
        title="31% of adults slept less than 6 hours on weeknights"
        subtitle="Share of adults by average weeknight sleep, 2024"
        source="National sleep survey 2024"
      />,
    },
    {
      kind: "prose",
      text: "9% of adults slept less than 5 hours on weeknights. 35% slept 7 hours or more.",
    },
    {
      kind: "callout",
      chart: <DumbbellChart
        data={[
          { age: "18 to 29", weeknight: 6.5, weekend: 8.3 },
          { age: "30 to 44", weeknight: 6.6, weekend: 7.9 },
          { age: "45 to 59", weeknight: 6.8, weekend: 7.7 },
          { age: "60 and over", weeknight: 7.3, weekend: 7.6 },
        ]}
        category="age"
        from="weeknight"
        to="weekend"
        names={{ weeknight: "Weeknights", weekend: "Weekends" }}
        format="{value} h"
        sort="none"
        highlight="18 to 29"
        title="Adults aged 18 to 29 slept 1.8 hours longer at weekends"
        subtitle="Average hours of sleep by age group, weeknights and weekends, 2024"
        source="National sleep survey 2024"
      />,
      label: "By age",
      lead: "Adults aged 60 and over slept 0.3 hours longer at weekends",
      body: "They slept 7.3 hours on weeknights. That is the longest of the four age groups.",
      tone: "neutral",
    },
    {
      kind: "stats",
      items: [
        {
          value: "6h 48m",
          label: "Average sleep on weeknights",
          delta: "−9 min",
          deltaLabel: "vs 2019",
        },
        { value: "7h 52m", label: "Average sleep at weekends" },
        {
          value: "31%",
          label: "Adults sleeping less than 6 hours on weeknights",
          delta: "+4 pts",
          deltaLabel: "vs 2019",
          upIsGood: false,
        },
      ],
    },
    {
      kind: "figure",
      chart: <Heatmap
        data={[
          { night: "Weeknights", hour: "9pm", share: 6 },
          { night: "Weeknights", hour: "10pm", share: 24 },
          { night: "Weeknights", hour: "11pm", share: 52 },
          { night: "Weeknights", hour: "12am", share: 78 },
          { night: "Weeknights", hour: "1am", share: 91 },
          { night: "Weeknights", hour: "2am", share: 95 },
          { night: "Weeknights", hour: "3am", share: 96 },
          { night: "Weeknights", hour: "4am", share: 94 },
          { night: "Weeknights", hour: "5am", share: 85 },
          { night: "Weeknights", hour: "6am", share: 58 },
          { night: "Weeknights", hour: "7am", share: 23 },
          { night: "Weeknights", hour: "8am", share: 8 },
          { night: "Weekends", hour: "9pm", share: 3 },
          { night: "Weekends", hour: "10pm", share: 13 },
          { night: "Weekends", hour: "11pm", share: 34 },
          { night: "Weekends", hour: "12am", share: 61 },
          { night: "Weekends", hour: "1am", share: 82 },
          { night: "Weekends", hour: "2am", share: 92 },
          { night: "Weekends", hour: "3am", share: 95 },
          { night: "Weekends", hour: "4am", share: 95 },
          { night: "Weekends", hour: "5am", share: 93 },
          { night: "Weekends", hour: "6am", share: 84 },
          { night: "Weekends", hour: "7am", share: 63 },
          { night: "Weekends", hour: "8am", share: 37 },
        ]}
        x="hour"
        y="night"
        value="share"
        format="{value}%"
        labels
        title="52% of adults were asleep at 11pm on weeknights"
        subtitle="Share of adults asleep at each clock hour, weeknights and weekends, 2024"
        source="National sleep survey 2024"
      />,
      caption: "At 7am, 23% of adults were asleep on weeknights and 63% at weekends.",
    },
    {
      kind: "quote",
      quote: "I go to bed at the same time on Saturday as on Tuesday. I get up two hours later.",
      attribution: "Survey respondent, aged 27",
    },
    {
      kind: "prose",
      text: "Average weeknight sleep was 6 hours 57 minutes in the 2019 survey. The share sleeping less than 6 hours was 27% in 2019.",
    },
  ]}
  sources="National sleep survey 2024"
  period="14 nights per respondent, March to May 2024"
  method="Sleep is the time between self-reported falling asleep and waking. Weeknights are Sunday to Thursday nights."
  note="Illustrative data. The quotation is illustrative."
/>
```
